# cicilang -- the rules of the code, by topic

This file states the rules of the code as they hold now, by topic: the gates, each pass, what runs and what is not
done. One bullet is one rule: what the code does, the predicates that do it, the standard's clause where one
applies, the fixture that gates it, and why. The bullet ends with the version that made the rule or last changed it.
`CLAUDE.md` states the owner's rules and how the work is done; `HISTORY.md` keeps the record of every step. A step
that changes a rule edits the rule here, in its topic, and writes its entry in `HISTORY.md`. These topics were
`CLAUDE.md`'s until 0.204.

## Contents

- Build, prove and the gates
- The driver and the commands

## Build, prove and the gates

### Building

- `CICILI=~/Projects/GitHub/cicili COCOLOG=~/Projects/GitHub/cocolog sh module/build.sh` builds `library/cicilang.so`.
  It links cocolog's `lib/sdk.cicili` into `module/`, writes `module/ccl_uninames.h` and `module/ccl_xid.h` (0.221),
  transpiles `module/cicilang.cicili` with Cicili (SBCL, `cicili.lisp --release`), and compiles the C with the compiler
  that cocolog's `tools/cc/env.sh` picks. (0.103)
- `sh module/build-llvm.sh` builds `library/ccl_llvm.so` over llvm-c. `LLVM=` names Homebrew's LLVM (the default) or
  Debian's and Ubuntu's `/usr/lib/llvm-NN`. It links `-lLLVM-C` where `libLLVM-C.*` is in `llvm-config --libdir`, else
  `-lLLVM`, with an rpath to that directory: the library's name is read off the disk, never assumed. (0.87)
- `perl module/gen-uninames.pl > library/ccl_uninames.pl` makes the `\N{NAME}` table from Perl's `Unicode::UCD`.
  Never edit the table by hand. (0.104)
- `perl module/gen-xid.pl > library/ccl_xid.pl` makes THE IDENTIFIER'S CHARACTERS PAST ASCII and the white space past
  ASCII, `ccl_xid(Set, Lo, Hi)` (the Lexers topic): XID_Start and XID_Continue from Perl's `Unicode::UCD`, Unicode
  15.0.0, with Unicode 15.1's additions and clang's mathematical notation profile, C11's Annex D and C99's from the
  generator's own lists, 1738 facts. Never edit the table by hand; `module/build.sh` spells `module/ccl_xid.h` from it,
  and the flow gate loads it, not charted. (0.221)
- `sh module/gen-bidrt.sh` makes `library/ccl_bidrt.pl`, the decimal conversions of a 128-bit integer: cicilang
  compiles `module/bidrt.c` (C23, `-O1`, the IR text) and `module/gen-bidrt.pl` writes one fact per function and per
  declaration. Run it after a change to `bidrt.c` or to what the lowering emits for it; never edit the table by hand.
  (0.137)

### The chain

- `sh test/gates.sh` runs the flow gate (`test/flow.sh`) FIRST, then the reader, compile, driver and objects gates,
  the proof and the cross gate one after another, then the library read (`test/libcxx.sh`), then the C++ gate
  (`test/cpp.sh`): nine gates. Each prints `== NAME: GREEN in N s` or `== NAME: RED (exit N) in N s`. The first RED
  stops the chain, by its exit status, never by a log read. A full pass prints `ALL GREEN`. The flow gate is first
  because it runs nothing and takes a minute: a mis-edit that it can see (a call that nothing answers, a name given
  twice) stops the chain there, where the C++ gate met it after an hour. (0.105, 0.144)
- THE CHAIN RUNS OVER A LIBC++: `LLVM=/usr/lib/llvm-18 sh test/gates.sh` and `LLVM=/usr/lib/llvm-21 sh test/gates.sh` (or the
  last two gates alone at 21: `test/libcxx.sh`, `test/cpp.sh`; the C gates do not read libc++). The tree is read and linked
  (`ccl_cxx_dirs`); without `$LLVM` the newest installed one is, libc++ 22 on the Ubuntu box, which no gate has run. The
  library read wipes the HOME's summaries (`LX_HOME`), so give each pass a HOME of its own to keep both warm (the summaries
  are keyed by the header's path, so two trees never clash). (0.122, 0.126)
- `GATES_JOBS` (default 4) sets `FLOW_JOBS`, `LX_JOBS` and `CPP_JOBS`, the lanes of the three parallel phases. (0.105,
  0.144)
- By hand: build, then `test/flow.sh`, `test/reader.sh`, `test/compile.sh`, `test/driver.sh`, `test/objects.sh`,
  `proof/run.sh`, `test/cross.sh`; then `test/libcxx.sh` before `test/cpp.sh`. (0.105, 0.144)
- A gate prints `SKIP` and exits 0 when it finds no `$COCOLOG/cocolog` or no `library/cicilang.so`, and the chain
  prints GREEN for it; the flow gate also without cocolog's `library/flow/chart.pl` and `tables.pl` (`make modules`
  writes the tables). A SKIP is no GREEN line: build first. (from the start, 0.144)
- Only the three parallel phases have caps of their own. The four small gates and the proof run under an outside cap,
  as every cocolog run does. (0.105, 0.144)
- `test/config.sh`, sourced by every gate, puts this checkout's `library/` at the front of `COCOLOG_LIBRARY` and keeps
  the caller's path behind it. It sets `CICILANG_KB` to `~/.cicilang/KB` unless the caller set it, and stamps that
  store (`ccl_kb_prepare`). (M4)
- The reader and compile gates run over `--embed "$CICILANG_KB"`, and the driver gate over it through `bin/cicilang`.
  The C++ gate, the library read, the census, the flow gate and `test/why.sh` run `--local`. The objects gate runs
  `--local`, with a store of its own for an instance that outlives its process. (M4, M5, 0.144)
- A gate program is loaded by `ensure_loaded/1` from a `query` (`reader_main`, `compile_main`, `cpp_main`,
  `readhdr_main`, `census_main`, `fg_findings_main`, `cw_main`), never by `cocolog --embed ... run FILE goal`, which
  consults FILE into the store. (from the start)

### The flow gate: test/flow.sh

- `test/flow.sh` (0.144) reads every file of the library with cocolog's `library(flow/chart)` and RUNS NOTHING. A chart
  starts at one call pattern, so `test/flow.pl`'s `fg_roots_main/2` writes a copy of each file with a root,
  `'$fg_all'/N`, that calls each predicate the file defines with free arguments: 3538 predicates in the ten files at
  0.161 (3938 in all at 0.167, 4003 at 0.173, 4038 at 0.175, 4048 at 0.178, 4066 at 0.179, 4074 at 0.180, 4092 at 0.181,
  4094 at 0.182, 4101 at 0.185, 4109 at 0.186, 4128 at 0.187, 4151 at 0.188; each step's in HISTORY.md), and since
  0.161 the 220 of the nine gate programs, `test/reader.pl`, `compile.pl`, `cpp.pl`, `readhdr.pl`, `census.pl`,
  `libcxx.pl`, `flow.pl`,
  `why.pl` and `prof.pl` (`TFILES`), each charted with the compiler and the flow and process libraries loaded, nothing
  stubbed (no gate program is a library file); their first chart found a predicate split by another's clauses
  (`census_main/0`) and a call of `print_message/2`, which cocolog does not have, in the recovery of a `catch/3` in
  `readhdr.pl` and
  `libcxx.pl`: a read that raised would have raised again there, an existence error where the FAIL line stands. Each
  copy is charted with the rest of the compiler loaded (`flow_graph/3`'s `load(Files)`), and the file itself is stubbed
  out of the library path (an empty file of its name first on `COCOLOG_LIBRARY`), so that its clauses are read once. A
  helper of the gate takes the prefix `fg_`: cocolog has one namespace, and a helper named `flow_trim/2` joined
  `library/flow/read.pl`'s own and failed the chart far from the cause. Since cocolog 1.11.4 the chart refuses by name a
  file IT READS that defines a predicate of the flow library; the gate's own Prolog is loaded by the query, not read by
  the chart, so the prefix still guards it. (0.144, 0.146)
- The chart is given the two modules' Cicili sources as `modules([...])` (cocolog 1.11.4; `flow_graph/3` in
  `fg_findings_main/5`). It reads each `("name" N cfun)` dispatch row of a module as a C predicate, with the modes of
  the module's header line (`;;;; name(+A, -B)`; `module/cicilang.cicili` names five, `module/ccl_llvm.cicili` four),
  and it follows the libraries their Prolog halves load (`ccl_include`, `ccl_ir`, `ccl_build`, `ccl_driver` and what
  those load) for what the compiler declares AS IT RUNS: `dynamic/1` of a written name, an assert of a written head,
  and a call of a declarer of its own with a written name (`cpp_reset/1`), so that a call of the desugaring's
  registries (`'$cpp_cls'/2` ...) is a dynamic predicate's, not an unknown procedure. 0.144 wrote both itself, the
  rows of the C predicates and a `:- dynamic` line for each of the 73 tables (`fg_modules_main/2`,
  `fg_dynamic_main/2`): without them 1221 of the 1291 findings of `ccl_cpp.pl` were unknown procedures. On 1.11.4 the
  two ways give the same findings, key for key, and the gate's own are gone. (0.144, 0.146)
- One job a file in the memory-gated pool (`ccl_pool`; `FLOW_JOBS` 4, `FLOW_LAUNCH_MB` 9000, `FLOW_HARD_MB` 14000),
  the longest first by `~/.cicilang/flow-times`, each under `FLOW_SECS` (900 s): `ccl_cpp.pl` 47 s, `ccl_ir.pl` 46 s,
  `ccl_driver.pl` 33 s, `test/compile.pl` 32 s, `ccl_syntax.pl` 30 s, the others under 22 s; the gate 74 s and 2795 MB
  over its four lanes at 0.172 (71 s at 0.171, 68 s at 0.168, 78 s at 0.167, 75 s at 0.166, 82 s at 0.164, 92 s at 0.161; 55 s over the
  library alone at 0.144). A
  file that is not charted is RED.
  (0.144, 0.161)
- `fg_findings_main/5` writes `flow_findings/2`'s findings but the root's, a line each: the kind, the severity, the
  predicate, the line, the column and the text. The kinds: `unknown_procedure` (a call that nothing answers, with the
  nearest name: `ir_inz/1 is defined nowhere ... did you mean ir_ins/1?`; a warning, not an error, under a `catch/3`
  that takes its existence error), `instantiation` (a variable free on every path into a builtin that needs it bound),
  `left_recursion`, `unreachable_clause` (a clause that a cut or a fact before it makes dead, for the call pattern),
  `det_promise`, `discontiguous`, `defined_twice` (`CLAUDE.md`'s split rule, How the code is written). Five defects
  seeded in a copy of the library -- a misspelled call, a second definition, a dead clause, a free variable into `is/2`,
  a left recursion -- were each named at their file, line and column, each once, in 47 s at 0.144 and in 52 s by the
  gate of 0.146. (0.144, 0.146)
- THE VERDICT: a finding is keyed without its line, since it moves with every edit above it: `KIND SEVERITY FILE
  PREDICATE` for `discontiguous` and `defined_twice`, the callee added for an unknown procedure, the text with every
  number made `N` for the rest; and EACH KEY ONCE, since a predicate charted for two call patterns says one thing twice
  and how many patterns the chart sees changes with the chart (1.11.4 saw a third pattern of `ccl_sum_bigs_/3`). The
  severity is in the key: a call that nothing answers is a warning under a `catch/3` that takes its error, and the same
  call without the catch is an error again. The keys must be `test/flow.expect`'s: a NEW one is RED and printed at its
  place (`FILE:LINE:COL: SEVERITY: PREDICATE: TEXT`, each place once); one that the expect file holds and the run did
  not meet is RED too, so that a finding fixed leaves the file in the same step and a later edit cannot bring it back
  unseen. `FLOW_UPDATE=1` writes the expect file from the run, after every new line is read; `FLOW_KEEP=DIR` keeps the
  copies, the logs and each file's findings. (0.144, 0.146)
- `test/flow.expect` at 0.160 holds one key -- the 124 `discontiguous` splits of 0.146, all true, are gone with the
  regroup of 0.160 -- a warning, the call of `'$ccl_sum_big'/3` in `ccl_sum_bigs_/3`, a table that a summary's `.big.pl`
  file defines when `ensure_loaded/1` loads it at run time, under a `catch/3` that takes its existence error. The seven
  false findings of 0.144 are gone on cocolog 1.11.4, which answered the report of them: `format(atom(A), ...)` binds A
  (`ir_fp_nan/1`, `ir_neg_zero/1`), text made from text binds every argument (`cpp_dbg_op_spell/2`, whose W
  `atomic_list_concat/3`'s split binds), and the call under the catch is the warning above. (0.144, 0.146, 0.160)

### The C gates

- The reader gate. `test/reader.pl` runs 94 numbered checks, `k1` to `k94`, in one process over the user's store. It
  then reads five of Cicili's C files whole (`test/c/main.c`, `shared.c`, `macro.c`, `example/cimath.c`,
  `example/numpy_example.c`); a missing one is a SKIP. `test/reader.sh` adds a second process, which must read
  `hello.c` with its headers from the store in under 10 s. (0.93)
- Reader checks that guard rules of other sections: `k16` (a cached read equals a fresh one), `k59` and `k65`
  (`0xFFul`, `1u << 4`), `k81` (the tie), `k82` (`#cocolog`), `k83` (`pp.c` with `pp_defs.h`), `k84` (the native lexer
  gives the DCG's tokens on `test/c/lexer.c` and on real files), `k85` (the native lexer is in use), `k86` (the user's
  macros), `k87` to `k91` (C23 and C17 at their levels), `k92` (`__int128` is a type word, `test/c/run/int128.c`), `k93` (a float read back from the store is the one read
  fresh, the largest double and a 17-digit one among them, `test/c/floats.c`; 0.132), `k94` (an identifier's characters
  past ASCII by the language and its level, the two lexers token for token; 0.221). (0.93, 0.117, 0.221)
- The compile gate. `test/compile.pl`, one process over the user's store, reads, checks, lowers, compiles at `-O1` and
  links every `test/c/run/*.c` at its `NAME.std` level (`c_level`). It expects every `test/c/safe/*.c` refused.
  `test/compile.sh` runs each binary as `NAME arg1 arg2` against `NAME.expect`, and compares each refusal with
  `safe/NAME.expect`. There are 156 run and 61 safe fixtures at 0.221. (M2, M3, 0.57, 0.221)
- The driver gate. `test/driver.sh` makes 48 checks of `bin/cicilang` over the user's store (the two decimal checks are
  skipped where no gcc with decimal floating types is installed), the variadic calls of every kind both ways against
  clang among them (`test/c/link/va_*.c`, 0.131), and Apple's arm64 expansion of `va_arg` of an aggregate against
  clang's, both retargeted to this host (`test/c/link/va_darwin.c`, 0.160). They cover what `-o`, `-c`, `-S`,
  `-emit-llvm`, `-shared`, `-I`, `-ast-dump`, `-fsyntax-only`, `-g` and `-gline-tables-only` make (read back by
  `llvm-dwarfdump`, from `$PATH` or `$LLVM/bin`: the statements' lines and the file's name; each row's column one that
  clang's line table has for that line, ten of them, 0.161; the variables, a struct's members and an enum's enumerators,
  their names sorted; no variable under `-gline-tables-only`; a C++ static data member declared in its class, its
  definition naming that declaration, through `cicilang++ -g -c`, 0.133; under `-fdebug-macro` a file's and its header's
  macros at their lines, as clang's object has them, and the predefined ones at line 0, 0.134; a destructor at its
  scope's closing brace, on a return and at the end, 0.139), and the diagnostics in clang's shape (`#warning` printed,
  `#error` with exit 1, and since 0.205 a false static assertion among a struct's members, `static assertion failed:
  ...` with exit 1). The text of `-E` compiled by clang makes the program the source makes, its floats exact (0.143:
  `__DBL_MAX__`, `1.5e308`, 17 digits, a subnormal, an infinity), its long double literals too (0.154: `__LDBL_MAX__`,
  `__LDBL_MIN__`, `__LDBL_DENORM_MIN__`, `0.1L`, a hex one, `0.1Li`). They find `@ccl_drain_node` in `btree.c`'s IR, and
  pass structs by value both ways against clang-built code (`test/c/link/abi_main.c`, `abi_helper.c`; seven lines at
  0.117, the last two for the SysV register budget, `budget_*` built by clang and `bud_*` by cicilang), and vectors by
  value both ways (0.162; `test/c/link/vec_main.c`, `vec_helper.c`: 8- and 16-byte vectors, a struct of one, nine of
  them, a variadic call). The store must serve `hello.c` in under 10 s and redo only the changed one of two files. The
  gate follows the host: `_main:` and `.dylib` on Darwin, `main:` and `.so` elsewhere. The decimal floating types cross
  the ABI against gcc-built code both ways (`test/c/link/dec_main.c`, `dec_helper.c`: values, structs by value, a
  variadic call; clang has no decimal types), and twelve long double constants converted to decimal types fold to gcc's
  bits (`test/c/link/decld.c`, 0.154). Since 0.221 four more: an identifier's characters past ASCII by the level (C17's
  euro sign and middle dot, C23's and C99's refusals in clang's words), `__STDC_VERSION__` at C99, C11, C17 and C23, an
  `#undef NDEBUG` before `<assert.h>` under `-DNDEBUG` asserting again, and the C++ IR cache (a rebuild served, a
  changed file lowered again). (M4, 0.93, 0.128, 0.129, 0.154, 0.160, 0.221)
- The objects gate. `test/objects.sh` makes 29 checks of the objects layer, an instance that outlives its process
  among them. (from the start)
- The cross gate (0.131). `test/cross.sh` builds every `test/c/run/*.c` with `cicilang --target=aarch64-linux-gnu` and
  with `clang --target=aarch64-linux-gnu`, runs both under `qemu-aarch64 -L /usr/aarch64-linux-gnu` and compares them:
  that machine's output is the reference, not this one's `.expect` (plain char and `wchar_t` are unsigned there, `long
  double` an IEEE quad). A fixture in the language's own forms, which clang does not read, is held to its `.expect`.
  Then five checks against `aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc`: structs by value both ways (`test/c/link/abi_*.c`), variadic calls
  of every AAPCS64 kind both ways (`test/c/link/va_*.c`: an int, a long, a double, a long double, an HFA of doubles and
  of floats, a struct past 16 bytes, an eight-byte struct, a 16-aligned `__int128` struct, the general and the SIMD
  registers run out) and vectors by value both ways (0.162, `test/c/link/vec_*.c`). It SKIPs without `qemu-aarch64`,
  `aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc` and the sysroot (Debian and Ubuntu: `qemu-user`, `gcc-aarch64-linux-gnu`,
  `libc6-dev-arm64-cross`) or without clang. `ldconst.c` holds the quad's literals to clang's there. (0.131, 0.154)
- C++ FOR THAT MACHINE (0.161): where its libc++ is under the sysroot -- the tree cicilang++ reads, `$LLVM` or the
  newest `/usr/lib/llvm-NN`, at `/usr/aarch64-linux-gnu` plus that path, where Debian's and Ubuntu's arm64 packages put
  it when extracted there (`dpkg-deb -x` of `libc++-18-dev`, `libc++1-18`, `libc++abi-18-dev`, `libc++abi1-18`,
  `libunwind-18` and `libunwind-18-dev`: apt installs no package of another architecture without multiarch) -- the cross
  gate builds 25 C++ fixtures with `cicilang++ --target=aarch64-linux-gnu` and with clang++ over that same libc++, runs
  both under qemu and compares them, then three checks against clang++'s code on that machine, the C++ gate's own:
  classes by value, pointers to member functions both ways, and a by-value parameter destroyed by the caller both ways
  (0.207; `test/cpp/link/`). Each C++ build has a time and a memory cap of its own (`CROSS_SECS` 1800, `CROSS_MB` 2800:
  its summaries are the target's, cold in every chain); without the tree the part is a SKIP line. 87 C fixtures (85 at
  0.167) and 5 checks at 0.179, 24 C++ fixtures (`vector.cpp` since 0.162; 25 since 0.215, `gnuasm.cpp`) and 2 checks at
  0.167 (3 since 0.207), 703 s in 0.164's chain, peak 535 MB, the C++ part cold (its summaries are that machine's own,
  read afresh in every chain's fresh HOME); 151 s in 0.166's, 150 s in 0.167's, 143 s in 0.168's, 139 s in 0.171's and
  145 s in 0.172's, peaks 437 MB, 436 MB, 365 MB, 387 MB and 390 MB, over a HOME that 0.165's chain had warmed. (0.131,
  0.161, 0.207, 0.215)
- The proof. `proof/run.sh` has clang turn `proof/forty2.ll` into a binary that prints `cicilang reaches C` and exits
  42. (M0)

### The library read and the warm: test/libcxx.sh

- `test/libcxx.sh` is one cold parallel pass. It wipes `$WARMHOME/.cicilang/cpp` (`LX_HOME`, else `$HOME`). It reads
  each asserted header at its level whole, each in its own `--local` process (`test/readhdr.pl`'s `readhdr_main`,
  with `CCL_HDR`, `CCL_STD`, `CCL_MIN`). It checks the item count against the list's minimum, a floor under libc++ 18's
  counts, and leaves the summaries written for the C++ gate. (0.105)
- The 23 asserted reads: `vector`, `string`, `iostream`, `map`, `set`, `unordered_map`, `unordered_set`, `optional`,
  `memory`, `functional`, `tuple` at C++17; `compare`, `vector`, `string`, `iostream`, `set`, `map`, `unordered_map`,
  `unordered_set`, `ranges` at C++20; `optional` and `string` at C++23; `optional` at C++26. A header at a level is a
  check of its own. (0.109)
- The same pass warms every other `#include <…>` of `test/cpp/*.cpp`, `test/cpp/run/*.cpp` and
  `$CICILI/test/cpp/*.cpp` (`ccl_union`), by a `-fsyntax-only` build (`ccl_warm`) at the including file's `.flags`
  level, else C++17, but an asserted one, its key `header@level` matched WHOLE (0.180: `ostream@17` is a substring of
  `iostream@17`, so `<ostream>` at C++17 was never warmed, and `libdiamond.cpp` flattened it cold in the C++ gate of
  every chain over a fresh HOME, 147 s at 0.179's where it builds in 12 to 16 s warm). A missing Cicili checkout is
  named, because `<sstream>` and `<stdexcept>` then stay cold. `<algorithm>` and `<array>` are only warmed: nothing
  asserts their counts. A file whose `.flags` names `-fno-rtti` or `-fno-exceptions` has its headers warmed under that
  flag too, its key `header@level@-fno-rtti` (0.191, `-fno-exceptions` since 0.193: such a summary is keyed apart, the
  C++ summary cache). A header in a directory, `<sys/wait.h>`, names its warm's files with `_` for each `/` (0.200: they
  named a directory that is not there, the build read no file and wrote no verdict, and the header stayed cold without a
  word). (0.92, 0.105, 0.180, 0.191, 0.193, 0.200)
- `LX_SECS` (2400 s) caps each read and each warm through `timeout -s KILL`. A read with no verdict is
  `FAIL <h> at C++N: the read did not finish`. A failed warm, `FAILED to flatten`, counts as a failure. A pool killed
  at its hard cap is RED. (0.105)
- The phase IS the warm. A summary is keyed by the reader version and its deps' times, so a separate read under a
  fresh HOME was the same cold read done twice. `test/warm.sh` is a shim that runs it; `test/libcxx.pl`, the old
  one-process form (`at(H, Std)`), runs in no gate. (0.105)
- `test/census.sh` names where the reader stops: `sh test/census.sh '<vector>'` under a fresh HOME, or
  `sh test/census.sh flat.cpp` over the output of `cicilang++ -E`, read as the library's (no global macros) at
  `CCL_CENSUS_STD=N`. It prints WHOLE or PARTIAL, the stop and farthest lines with their tokens, and the AST's functors
  counted. (0.44, 0.99)

### The C++ gate: test/cpp.sh

- `test/cpp.sh` runs in this order: `test/cpp.pl` in one `--local` process; four checks of the command; every
  `test/cpp/run/*.cpp` as a pool job (836 at 0.221); `classes.cpp` and `templates.cpp` built and run; the refusals, each
  at the level its `test/cpp/NAME.flags` names, else C++17 (0.164). (0.105, 0.164)
- `test/cpp.pl` runs 47 numbered checks, `c1` to `c47`, then reads Cicili's six C++ files whole (`test/cpp/objects.cpp`,
  `emit_report.cpp`, `specialise.cpp`, `syntax.cpp`, `torch.cpp`, `torch-fragment.cpp`). `c34` checks the Itanium
  mangler on nine symbols, with no class registered. `unit_at(Std, Name, U)` sets `'$ccl_std'` for one read: `c22` to
  `c28` read `cxx20.cpp`, `c29` to `c33` `cxx23.cpp`, and `c35`, `c36` the run fixtures `cxx20cmp.cpp`, `cxx23b.cpp`,

  under load is not. `CPP_JOBS=1` makes the gate serial. A HOME whose cache was copied from another tree or another HOME
  is not warm (the summary cache topic, 0.217). (0.105, 0.217)
- `ccl_fixture NAME` builds with `NAME.flags`, capped at `CPP_FIXTURE_SECS` (2400 s) by `ccl_capped`. Past the cap,
  `ccl_kill_tree` kills the tree, and the verdict line itself reads `FAIL NAME.cpp: TIMEOUT after N s`, so no diff
  hides it. It runs the binary on `NAME.stdin` or `/dev/null`, compares with `NAME.expect`, and writes its verdict to
  `$RES/NAME.res`. (0.93, 0.94, 0.105)

  up, below), and its account -- the calls the error was raised through, the branch that raised it, then the failed
  call down the path that got furthest -- joins the verdict, under the diff. It costs two more builds of each such
  fixture, and none for a fixture that built and printed a wrong output. Over a copy of the library with one defect
