### The pool: test/parlib.sh

- `ccl_pool NMAX LAUNCH_MB HARD_MB` reads one shell line per job from its standard input. It starts a job only while
  fewer than NMAX run and the summed RSS of every `cocolog … query` and `cocolog … run` on the box (`ccl_cocolog_rss`)
  is under LAUNCH_MB. It gates on memory because cocolog has no garbage collector and a build peaks in gigabytes. A
  run is counted since 0.148: `library(flow/debug)`'s probes and replays under `CPP_WHY=1` are `cocolog run`s, in
  process groups of their own. (0.105, 0.148)
- Past HARD_MB the pool kills every cocolog query and run on the box with `pkill -9` and returns 1, a RED. The
  defaults are 4 jobs, 9000 MB and 14000 MB: `CPP_JOBS`, `CPP_LAUNCH_MB`, `CPP_HARD_MB` in `test/cpp.sh`, the `LX_`
  ones in `test/libcxx.sh` and the `FLOW_` ones in `test/flow.sh`. (0.105, 0.144, 0.148)
- The pool tracks its children by PID with `kill -0`, because dash has no `jobs -r`. It matches `[c]ocolog`, never
  its own shell. Every job runs with `< /dev/null`: the pool's input is the job list, and a build once swallowed the
  lines queued behind it. (0.105, 0.106)
- The jobs run longest first. `ccl_lpt_order FILE` sorts lines by the recorded seconds of their first word, the
  unknown keys first. `ccl_time_record FILE KEY SECS` appends a line, and the last line per key wins. Only a passing
  build's, a good read's or a good chart's seconds are recorded, in `~/.cicilang/fixture-times` (`CPP_TIMES`),
  `~/.cicilang/header-times` (`LX_TIMES`) and `~/.cicilang/flow-times` (`FLOW_TIMES`). (0.105, 0.106, 0.144)

### Fixtures and their companion files

- `NAME.expect` is clang's or clang++'s output for the same program, then the `exit N` that the gate appends. For C it
  holds the binary's standard output and error; for C++, the build's own output (empty when clean), then the binary's
  standard output. `btree`'s comes from the C mirror `bench/btree/btree_cicilang.c`. Compare by hand the same way.
  (M2, 0.93)
- `NAME.flags` gives a C++ fixture its level (`-std=c++20`, `-std=c++23`, `-std=c++26`), a refusal of `test/cpp/` too
  (0.164); without one it builds at C++17. It may name `-fno-rtti` beside the level (0.191: `nortti.cpp` and three
  refusals), or `-fno-exceptions` (0.193: `noexcgrow.cpp` and two refusals). `NAME.std` gives a C fixture its level
  (`-std=c23`); an ISO level (`-std=c17`, `-std=c23`) is an ISO mode, `'$ccl_iso'`, and before C23 it turns trigraphs
  on, as `bin/cicilang` does (`c_level` in `test/compile.pl`). (0.42, 0.57, 0.108, 0.214)
- `NAME.stdin` is the input of a fixture that reads (`stdcin`, `stdcinld`, `stdget`, `stdgetline`, `stdistream`,
  `stdistream2`, `stdws`, `stdtie`); the others read `/dev/null`. (0.75, 0.115, 0.136)
- `NAME.needs` holds a preprocessor condition over the library's own macros. `ccl_needs_met` runs a four-line file
  that includes `<version>` through `cicilang++ -E` with the fixture's flags, and looks for a marker. When the box's
  library fails it, the verdict is `skip NAME.cpp: needs ...`, never a RED. Two exist: `stdoptionalref.needs`
  (`__cpp_lib_optional >= 202506L`, since 0.123: libc++ 21.1.8 has no `optional<T &>`, it came with libc++ 22) and
  `joinwith.needs` (`__cpp_lib_ranges_join_with >= 202202L`, since 0.133: libc++ 18 has no `views::join_with`). (0.95,
  0.107, 0.123, 0.133)
- `test/c/safe/NAME.expect` holds the refusal, `ownership(Kind,Name)`. (M3)
- Inputs beside the fixtures are no fixtures: `test/c/run/pp_defs.h`, `fileconst.h` (`fileconst.c`, 0.195), `embed.txt`,
  `empty.txt`; `test/cpp/run/bag.h`
  (`bag.cpp`, `member.cpp`), `hunit.h` (`headerunit.cpp`, `hdrinline.cpp`), `basem.cppm` and `mathm.cppm`
  (`modules.cpp`), `embed26.txt` (`cxx26.cpp`); `test/cpp/hidem.cppm` (`modhidden.cpp`). (0.93, 0.108, 0.110)
- A binary runs only if this run built it. Each gate builds into a fresh temporary directory; `test/cpp.sh` runs on
  a build status of 0, and `test/compile.sh` on its `built NAME` line. (from the start, 0.89)
- A check is its own clause, `kN :- check(Name, Goal).`, with a unique number, never a fact driven by `findall/3`:
  two clauses of one name both run on backtracking. Each check runs inside `\+ \+`, so a process peaks at its biggest
  check, not at the sum. (from the start, 0.46)
- A shape that only invalid C++ can write, or that the libc++ fixtures already measure, gets no fixture of its own.
  (0.64, 0.69)

### Reading a result

- A gate's time is wall clock (`date +%s`). Compare it only with a run whose window was awake (`pmset -g log` on a
  Mac). A number that must mean something is CPU time, or one fixture alone against a recorded number. (0.88)
- `TIMEOUT after N s` is a bound, not a value. (0.92)
- A version bump makes the caches cold: a reader bump every C++ summary, either bump the C store. The first run after
  one peaks far above the steady state, and a run killed at its cap writes no summary, so the next run is cold too.
  Re-run before believing a RED that comes with a bump. (0.61, 0.67, 0.105)

### Where a build gave up: test/why.sh

- `sh test/why.sh [cicilang's arguments] FILE` (0.144) builds FILE under cocolog's `library(flow/debug)` and says
  where the compiler gave up. A refusal names a function (`not lowered yet: item(function(pick, block/1))`) or a phase
  (`phase(desugaring)`), and `the check or the lowering failed without saying why` names nothing; the tool names the
  call that failed, its arguments, the clause it failed in and that clause's last call, in two builds at full speed,
  where finding it by hand took probes and traces. A C file goes through `bin/cicilang`, a C++ one through
  `bin/cicilang++`, built with `-c` and no store. It is no gate. (0.144)
- The goal is the command's own: `bin/cicilang` under `CICILANG_GOAL=FILE` writes the `ccl_drive(Inputs, Options)` its
  arguments make into FILE and runs nothing. The tool then builds once as the command would and prints what it says (a
  build that succeeds has nothing to explain: exit 0). The build also writes the C++ summaries it reads BEFORE the
  debugger's two runs: else the probe flattened a header and wrote its summary, the replay read the summary, and the
  two took different roads (`abstract.cpp`'s probe spent 4.4 million steps, its replay 181 thousand). (0.144)
- The program under the debugger is a top file: `:- use_module(library(cicilang)).`; the compiler's own files, named in
  a block the engine skips (`:- if(fail).`, an `ensure_loaded/1` of every `library/ccl_*.pl` but the two generated
  tables, `:- endif.`); and `cw_goal :- nb_setval('$ccl_why', yes), ccl_drive(...).` The debugger reads the clauses an
  exception ended from the program's files as the source's directives load them (cocolog 1.11.7), and
  `library(cicilang)` is a compiled module whose Prolog half's files it does not reach: without them named it found no
  branch and no catch, and its answered failure was an older one further out (`abstract.cpp`: an array-type test of the
  declaration); named, they are read, and the run loads nothing again (0.148). Under `'$ccl_why'` the run ENDS at its
  first error, so the window that the debugger records -- the last `WHY_WINDOW` steps -- holds the code that gave
  up: an error the compiler RAISES passes the driver's five report sites untaken (`dr_catch/3`, 0.146) and ends the run
  as the compiler raised it, and an error the driver says after a FAILURE is thrown after it is written
  (`dr_why_stop/3`, `ccl_why(File, Line, Parts)`). `dr_catch/3` stays, measured at 0.148: cocolog 1.11.7's `caught(K)`
  explains a catch's recovery only where the window recorded the catch's call, and a report site's catch is entered when
  the build starts -- over plain `catch/3` at the five sites no case found the compiler's error, the run ended in the
  report's own throw, and each case took 30 to 31 s and 736 to 751 MB where it takes 12 s and 300 MB. (0.144, 0.146,
  0.148)
- `test/why.pl`'s `cw_main/4` runs `flow_debug/4` (a probe at full speed learns at which step the run ends, a
  replay records the window, each in a child cocolog) with `own(all)`, the chart being of the top file, whose every
  call into the compiler is a library's (cocolog 1.11.4), and with `svg(false)` and `xml(false)` unless `WHY_KEEP`
  (1.11.10: no document drawn or written; the same explanation, line for line, in 12 s and 300 MB a case where the
  documents cost 16 s and 450 MB). It reads the record back with `flow_why_raised/3` and its answers `chose(C)` and
  `caught(K)` (1.11.7) and prints how the run ended; THE ERROR'S PATH, the calls the exception ended from the window's
  top down to the raise, where a raise in a catch/3's recovery is followed by the error that catch took, raised
  further down -- the compiler's own catches that restore a state and throw again (`cpp_stmt/3`,
  `cpp_method_body_/5`) are levels of one path (`abstract.cpp`: 19 calls, from `cpp_items` through the declaration at
  line 5 to `cpp_ctor('Shape', [])`, `cpp_not_abstract('Shape')` and `cpp_refuse/2`); THE BRANCH IT WAS RAISED IN, the
  call whose if-then-else or disjunction took it and every condition it ran, builtins included (`abstract.cpp`:
  then(2) of `cpp_not_abstract('Shape')`, after `nb_current('$cpp_base_ctor', yes)` failed and
  `cpp_abstract_class('Shape')` held); and THE FAILURE IT ANSWERED, a condition that failed having tried a clause, down
  the path where it got furthest (`flow_why_furthest/2`: at each failed call the clause whose body got the most calls
  done, then the most inferences spent, then the earlier, past an explicit `fail`). The rule of 0.146 -- a failed
  call that tried no clause just before the raise, since 1.11.4's answered failure passed a refusal's deciding builtin
  over -- is gone: `chose(C)` names it among the conditions. (0.144, 0.146, 0.148, 0.149)
- `WHY_WINDOW` (20000 steps: a desugaring failure 10,000 steps before the end, behind backtracking, was
  outside a window of 4000), `WHY_KEEP=DIR` (the debugger's files, made only then: `why.txt`, the run a call a line;
  `why.svg` and `why.xml`, the run over its chart), `WHY_SECS` (2400 s) and `WHY_MB` (2800 MB), both caps on the run's
  whole process TREE, killed whole past either: cocolog's process module starts every child in a process group or a
  session of its own, so the debugger's probe and replay were out of the group that 0.144 to 0.147 summed and killed,
  the debugger alone (0.148; `ccl_cocolog_rss` counts a `cocolog … run` too, the Pool topic). Measured at 0.148 on
  1.11.10: the defect seeded in the lowering of a conditional, where the build said only `not lowered yet:
  item(function(pick, ...))`, is the else of `ir_items/1` after `ir_item/1` failed, down to `\==(i32, i32)` failed in
  clause 97 of `ir_expr/4`; the one seeded in the desugaring's `return` the else of `ccl_ir_units/2` after
  `ccl_cpp_units/2` failed, down to the `\=/2` of `cpp_stmt_/3`; and `abstract.cpp`'s refusal as above: 12 to 13 s and
  300 to 308 MB each, the tree summed. (0.144, 0.146, 0.148)

### Where a build's steps and time go: test/prof.sh

- `sh test/prof.sh [cicilang's arguments] FILE` (0.148) profiles the build of FILE with cocolog's `library(flow/debug)`
  (1.11.10; the time since 1.13.3). The build runs once as it is (the C++ summaries it reads written), then once at full
  speed under the debugger to learn its length; then `PROF_WINDOWS` windows (6) of `PROF_WINDOW` steps (20000)
  spread along the run, the last ending where it ends, are each recorded by a cocolog of its own that runs the build
  twice to its window's end, `PROF_JOBS` at a time (2) (`flow_debug_windows/4`, with `svg(false)`, `xml(false)` and
  `time(T)`), and their rows are added up (`flow_profile_merge/5`). It prints the first `PROF_TOP` rows (20) of six
  views: INCLUSIVE, each predicate's calls and the steps spent inside them, a call charged from its Call to its
  first Exit or Fail; STEPS, the windows' steps by what took them, a call one each and the control constructs the
  rest; CALLERS, who made each predicate's calls; REPEATS, the goals asked more than once, where a memo would serve;
  TIME (0.152), each predicate's calls, its inclusive and self time in microseconds and its largest call's -- since
  cocolog 1.15.0 with ` @W:S`, the window and the step of that call, so that a small window recorded around S
  (`from(S)`, `to(S + K)`) reads the call with its arguments --, the most inclusive first, and the control constructs'
  time last (`flow_time_text/2`); RUN (0.156), the WHOLE run's self time by predicate, the most first, its retries'
  time apart, and its steps (`flow_run_time/3`, `flow_run_time_text/2`, cocolog 1.15.0): the build run once more,
  untraced to its end, under a clock read at every step, each step's time charged to the predicate its goal names and
  a retry's to the predicate retried, the clock's own cost taken off each row. It has no window and no replay: it is
  the run's own time, where the windows are a sample, and it costs about twice the build (under `PROF_SECS`).
  `PROF_KEEP=DIR` keeps them whole (`DIR/prof.prof`). A C file goes through `bin/cicilang`, a C++ one through
  `bin/cicilang++`, built with `-c` and no store, as `test/why.sh` builds. Over a `library(flow/debug)` older than
  1.13.3 it gives the four other views, and older than 1.15.0 no RUN view, and says why. It is no gate. (0.148, 0.152,
  0.156)
- A count of steps is no count of time: a copy of a global (`nb_getval/2`), a clause retrieval of a big term, an assert
  or a call of a native module is one step whatever it costs. The TIME view says what each cost (cocolog 1.13.3's
  `time(T)`): each window's PROBE runs the build untraced under a clock read at the top of every step of the window, and
  the replay, numbered as the probe is, says whose each step was; a call's self time is its own step -- a predicate's
  head and the guards its clause runs as it is entered, a builtin's whole run -- and what no call's own step took is the
  control constructs'. A reading of the clock costs some 30 to 35 ns, measured as each probe starts and taken off, so a
  cheap predicate is read by its count and a costly step by its time. The time is a SAMPLE, six windows of 20000 steps
  of a run of millions: a cost it names is measured over the whole run, by the timers of Finding a cost, before it is
  called the cost (0.152: `cpp_shipped_member/5`, taken out at 0.153, the Tables topic of Time and memory). Since 0.156
  the RUN view is that measure, by predicate: the clock is read at every step of the whole run, some 38 ns a reading,
  and taken off. `PROF_SECS` (2400 s) and `PROF_MB` (2800 MB) cap the whole process tree: the windows' cocologs run in
  sessions of their own, each window's probe and replay in process groups of their own. Measured on cocolog 1.11.10:
  `stdvector.cpp` (18.2 million steps) in 82 s at 847 MB, `counter.cpp` in 44 s at 567 MB (0.148); on 1.13.0,
  `stdvector.cpp` (17.9 million) in 79 s at 829 MB (0.151); on 1.13.3, with the TIME view, in 80 s at 792 MB (0.152),
  and over the library of 0.153 (17.1 million) in 71 s at 679 MB; on 1.15.0, with the RUN view, in 155 s at 760 MB, its
  first build cold (88 s; a copied HOME, the Findings) and the whole run 2.816 s untraced, the clock read at 14.2
  million of its 17.1 million steps (0.156). THE WINDOWS ARE ON THE DEBUGGER'S CLOCK, which counts every goal: since
  cocolog 1.12.2 `statistics/2`'s inferences leave out each `true` and `=/2`, as SWI counts none, so the two counts of
  one run differ -- `stdvector.cpp`'s build is 17.9 million on the debugger's clock and 17.2 million by `statistics/2`
  (0.151). cocolog 1.13.6 calls that clock's unit a STEP, each view says how many of its steps were inferences, and the
  two tools print steps since 0.155. (0.148, 0.151, 0.152, 0.153, 0.155, 0.156)

## The driver and the commands

### The commands

- `bin/cicilang` takes clang's arguments (owner's rule: no new flags to learn). It makes one options list and runs
  `ccl_drive/2` in ONE cocolog process: over `--embed $CICILANG_KB` (default `~/.cicilang/KB`) after `kb_prepare`, or
  `--local` under `--no-kb`. (M4, 0.108)
- `bin/cicilang++` is `bin/cicilang` with `CICILANG_LANG=cpp` (`lang(cpp)`), `CICILANG_ME=cicilang++` and `--no-kb`.
  (M5)
- Under `CICILANG_GOAL=FILE` the command writes the goal its arguments make, `ccl_drive(Inputs, Options)`, into FILE
  and runs nothing (0.144): `test/why.sh` runs that goal under the debugger. No flag is added (owner's rule).

### Arguments

- `-c -S -emit-llvm -fsyntax-only -E -ast-dump -v -o -O0..-Oz -I` become `compile_only`, `assembly`, `emit_llvm`,
  `syntax_only`, `preprocess`, `ast`, `verbose`, `out(F)`, `opt(F)` (default `-O0`) and `include(D)`. Link flags pass as
  `link(F)`: `-l -L -shared -Wl, -framework -static -rdynamic -fPIC -pthread -m*`. (M4, 0.44)
- `--target=TRIPLE` and `-target TRIPLE`, clang's spellings, are `target(T)` (0.131): another machine (`dr_set_target/1`,
  the Driver topic below). A run with one keeps no C store (`--local`): another machine reads this compiler's own
  headers (`float.h`, `limits.h`) under its own macros, and the store keys a header by its path.
- `-W -f* -pedantic`, an unknown `-std=` and an unknown `-g` form are accepted and ignored. Any other dash argument is
  `unknown argument`. `-fexperimental-library` acts (0.138), as clang++'s does: libc++ asks
  `__has_feature(experimental_library)`, which answers 0 here, so the command defines what that answer defines,
  `define('_LIBCPP_ENABLE_EXPERIMENTAL')`, and links `-lc++experimental` and `-lc++abi` (the archive names libc++abi's
  symbols directly); a run with it keeps no C store, as with `-D`. libc++'s time zones (`tzone.cpp`, libc++ 21; libc++
  18 has none, `tzone.needs`), syncstream and the rest of its experimental part. `--version` prints the versions of cicilang, cocolog and LLVM; `-h` prints the help. (M4, 0.108)
- `-fno-rtti` acts (0.191), as clang++'s does: the option `no_rtti`, libc++'s no-RTTI configuration and `typeid`
  refused (the Configuration chosen through the macros topic); `-frtti`, the default, takes it back, and the last of
  the two on the line wins (`bin/cicilang`'s `rtti`).
- `-fno-exceptions` and `-fno-cxx-exceptions` act (0.193), as clang++'s do: the option `no_exceptions`, libc++'s
  no-exceptions configuration, and the program's `throw` and `try` refused (the Configuration chosen through the
  macros topic); `-fexceptions` and `-fcxx-exceptions`, the default, take it back, and the last of the four on the
  line wins (`bin/cicilang`'s `eh`).
- `-g` is the option `debug` (0.128, 0.130): `-g`, `-g2`, `-g3`, `-ggdb`, `-ggdb2`, `-ggdb3`, `-gdwarf*`, `-gfull`, `-glldb`
  and `-gsce` give the FULL debug information (the line tables, the variables, their types, the lexical blocks, C++'s
  names and scopes); `-g1`, `-ggdb1`, `-gline-tables-only` and `-gline-directives-only` give `debug(lines)`, the line
  tables alone; `-g0` and `-ggdb0` give none, and the last form on the line wins, as clang (`bin/cicilang`'s `gdbg`).
  `dr_c` sets `'$ccl_debug'` to `file(AbsolutePath)` for the file (`dr_abs_path/2`, `absolute_file_name/2`), else
  `none`, and `'$ccl_debug_kind'` to `full`, `lines` or `none`; the IR cache's signature folds both (`dr_ir_sig/3`): an
  IR with debug information is another IR. The lowering's side is in The lowering topic. gdb reads it: `break
  Counter::bump`, `info args`, `info locals`, `print p`, `ptype p`, `print ns::Outer::made`, `finish`'s value. The
  driver gate's two `-g` checks read it back with LLVM's own `llvm-dwarfdump`. (0.128, 0.130)
- `-fdebug-macro` with a FULL `-g` is the option `debug_macro` (0.134; `-fno-debug-macro` takes it back; alone, or with
  `-gline-tables-only`, it does nothing, as clang): the macros go into the debug information. `dr_c` records them first
  (`dr_macro_trace/2` -> `ccl_pp_macro_trace/2`, a standalone run of the preprocessor over the file BEFORE the read, whose
  own run starts the preprocessor afresh) into `'$ccl_debug_macros'` (`events(Es)`, else `none`), and the IR cache's
  signature folds it (`dr_ir_sig/3`). The lowering's side is in the Debug information topic. (0.134)
- `-D N`, `-DN=v`, `-D'F(x)=...'` and `-U N` are `define(Text)` and `undef(N)` options (0.112): the driver makes the
  list `'$pp_cmdline'` (`ccl_pp_cmdline/1`, the later of a -D and a -U of one name winning), and `pp_outer_macro/3`
  asks it before the predefined macros, so every file and every header's macro table made in the process reads them
  (`<assert.h>` under `-DNDEBUG`); a `-U` takes away a predefined macro and leaves a header free to define it. A run
  with either keeps no C store (`--local`: the store keys a header by its path), and a C++ summary's fold takes the
  list (`ccl_cmdline_key/1` in `ccl_sum_file/2`). The driver gate's `-D and -U` check. (0.112)
- `-std=` names the level of both languages:

  | Flag | Option |
  |---|---|
  | `c++17` `c++20` `c++23` `c++26` (and `1z` `2a` `2b` `2c`) | `std(17)` ... `std(26)`, `iso` |
  | `gnu++17` `gnu++20` `gnu++23` `gnu++26` (and `gnu++1z` ... `gnu++2c`) | `std(17)` ... `std(26)` |
  | `c23`, `c2x` | `cstd(23)`, `iso` |
  | `gnu23`, `gnu2x` | `cstd(23)` |
  | `c17`, `c18`, `iso9899:2017`, `iso9899:2018` | `cstd(17)`, `trigraphs`, `iso` |
  | `c11`, `iso9899:2011`; `c99`, `iso9899:1999` | `cstd(11)`; `cstd(99)`; `trigraphs`, `iso` |
  | `gnu17`, `gnu18`; `gnu11`; `gnu99` | `cstd(17)`; `cstd(11)`; `cstd(99)` |

  The ISO C modes read trigraphs before C23 and the GNU modes do not, as clang. `-trigraphs` alone turns them on. An ISO
  mode is the option `iso` (0.214), `'$ccl_iso'`: it predefines `__STRICT_ANSI__` and not GNU's `linux` and `unix` (the
  Predefined macros topic), `typeof` is a name of the program's where its level has no such keyword, and in C `asm` (the
  Declarators topic), and a C read's keys carry it (the Includes topic); no `-std`, and every `gnu` form, is a GNU mode,
  as clang's default is. THE LAST `-std=` WINS, its level and its mode, as clang's (0.214, `bin/cicilang`'s `lvl`): the
  first level stood, and an earlier ISO form's `trigraphs`; the driver gate's check builds `-std=c17 -std=gnu17` and the
  reverse. A C++ level before 17 is refused, and so are C89 and C90. (0.42, 0.57, 0.108, 0.214)

### `ccl_drive/2`

- `ccl_drive/2` is `once(dr_drive(Inputs, Options))`. Why: cocolog's query loop asks for a second answer, and a stray
  choicepoint prints everything again. It sets `'$ccl_lang_forced'` and `'$ccl_lang'`, `'$ccl_std'` (default 17),
  `'$ccl_c_std'` (default 17), `'$ccl_trigraphs'` and `'$ccl_iso'` (0.214), and asserts a `ccl_include_dir/1` per `-I`:
  `dr_setup/2`, the options as a run of the command sets them (0.188). (M4, 0.108, 0.188, 0.214)
- THE COLD LIBRARY HEADERS OF A C++ BUILD ARE READ BY PROCESSES OF THEIR OWN (0.188, the owner's design): `dr_drive`
  keeps the build's options in `'$ccl_children'`, and before the file's run its prescan (`ccl_pp_prescan/1`) finds the
  library headers it names (`<name>`, `#include_next`, a header unit's `import`) that no valid summary serves
  (`ccl_cold_headers/4`). Where two or more are cold it starts a cocolog for each (`ccl_cold_headers_read/2`,
  `ccl_kids/4` over `proc_spawn/2`), J at a time (`ccl_jobs/1`: `$CICILANG_JOBS`, else the machine's processors,
  `os_cpus/1`; 1 turns it off), each running `ccl_drive_header/3` -- the build's options set by `dr_setup/2`, the
  program's feature-test macros among them (`ftm(L)`, 0.214), then the header read as the prescan reads it and its
  summary written -- and waits for them all; the prescan then serves each header from its summary. Since 0.186 a
  header's read does not depend on what the process read before it, so the summaries are the ones the build writes alone
  (0.188's nets: the same, file for file). One cold header is read in the build's own process; a process past 1800 s is
  killed, its session by signal 9, and one that writes no summary leaves its header to the build. `-v` names each
  process and says how many summaries they wrote. A C build and `-E` start none, and a library header that only the
  program's own header names is read in the build's own process. `aliasptr.cpp`'s eight cold headers over libc++ 18:
  52.8 s where the build alone takes 96.5 s, the same CPU time, peak 562 MB over six processes. (0.188, 0.214)
- ANOTHER MACHINE (0.131): `target(T)` sets it before anything reads it (`dr_set_target/1`): the arch from the triple's
  first word (`aarch64` or `arm64` is `arm64`, `x86_64`), the OS from a word in it (`linux`; `apple`, `darwin`, `macos`
  are `darwin`); `'$ccl_target'` = `target(Arch, OS, Triple)`, and the globals every machine question reads --
  `'$pp_arch'` and `'$pp_os'` (the predefined macros and the target's table), `'$ir_arch'` (`aapcs` or `sysv`),
  `'$ccl_ldbl'` (`quad` on Linux aarch64, `double` on Apple's arm64, `x87`). The compile's flags get `--target=T` for
  the embedded LLVM, the inclusion path the cross sysroot (`ccl_sdk_dirs/1` over `ccl_cross_sysroot/1`:
  `/usr/aarch64-linux-gnu/include`, then `/usr/include`, as clang searches them, never this host's multiarch directory),
  and the link the cross gcc (`ccl_linker/1`: `aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc`, with ` -lm`). An unknown triple is `unknown
  target triple`. In C++ (0.161) the libc++ tree is the one the host would read, under the cross sysroot where it is
  there (`ccl_cxx_dirs`), linked by the cross gcc with ` -lc++ -lm` and an rpath to where that machine keeps it
  (`ccl_link_libs/1`), and a summary is the target's own (`ccl_target_key/1`, the C++ summary cache); without the tree
  `cicilang++ --target` compiles and does not link. (0.131, 0.161)
- `.c` and the C++ extensions (`dr_cpp_ext`) go to `dr_c`; `.ll` compiles as IR; `.o`, `.a`, `.so` and `.dylib` go to
  the link. A missing input is `no such file or directory` (`dr_input`); it once compiled to `cicilang: ok`. (0.46,
  0.108)
- `-E` runs `dr_preprocess`: cocolog's own preprocessor standalone (`ccl_pp_file/3`; owner's rule: no clang), the tokens
  spelled back as text (`ccl_pp_spell/2`), into `-o`'s file or the answer. The text breaks its lines where the source's
  do, escapes a string's codes (`\NNN`), keeps every suffix, and spells a float exactly and an infinite one as `1e999`.
  (0.44, 0.99, 0.143)
- Otherwise `dr_c` reads the file (`cicilang_ast/2`), and `-ast-dump` writes the AST. In C++ mode, `-fsyntax-only` only
  reads: no desugaring, check or lowering, so its success says nothing about them. In C it still checks and lowers
  (`dr_ir/3`). Then `dr_emit` writes the `.ll`, the assembly, the object, or a temporary object to link. (M5, 0.87)
- The link runs unless the run had errors, made no object, or stops before it (`-c -S -emit-llvm -fsyntax-only
  -ast-dump -E`; `dr_no_link`). Its output is `-o`'s file, else `a.out`. The run ends `cicilang: ok` or
  `cicilang: N error(s)`. (M4)
- A phase that merely fails names itself: `ccl_ir_units/2` throws `ir_fail(phase(desugaring | check | lowering))`,
  printed `not lowered yet: phase(...)`. Else the driver says only `the check or the lowering failed without saying
  why`. Under `'$cpp_trace'`, `ir_cpp_trace` prints each phase with the heap. (0.53)

### Diagnostics

- A diagnostic is clang's `file:line: error: what` (`dr_error/3`). `dr_report/2` hands the error term to
  `once(dr_diag/3)`, one clause per term; `once/1` because the callers' recovery fails after the report. An error on a
  macro-expanded line gets `note: expanded from macro ...` (`dr_remember_expansions/1`); an error inside a macro gets a
  note that names the macro's file (`dr_note_macro`). (M1b, M4)
- The user's own `#error` is an error (`dr_diag(F, pp_error(M), ...)`). Its `#warning` lines print after the read as
  `file:line: warning: text` (`dr_pp_warnings`) and count as no error. (0.93)
- One `awk` pass in `bin/cicilang` splits the answer. `: error: `, `: warning: ` and `: note: ` lines go to stderr. The
  `cicilang: ...` lines (but `cicilang: ok`) and `unit(...)` lines go to stdout. All else is DROPPED; under `-E` the
  text passes. (0.44, 0.93)
- The exit status is 0 on `cicilang: ok` and 1 on `cicilang: N error(s)`. Else it is 1, after up to three `ERROR` or
  `error` lines prefixed `cicilang: `. (M4)
- So a library debug `write` must start its line with `cicilang: `. A trace (`nb_setval('$cpp_trace', yes)`, or
  `CCL_IR_TRACE=1` for each emitted IR line) needs cocolog called directly. (0.90)
- Under `'$ccl_why'`, which only `test/why.sh`'s program sets, the run ends at its first error: the driver's five
  report sites -- the read, `-E`, the IR, the compile and the link -- take no error (`dr_catch/3` is `call(G)` there,
  `catch(G, E, Report)` in every other build, 0.146), so an error the compiler raises ends the run as raised; and
  `dr_error/3` throws `ccl_why(File, Line, Parts)` after it writes an error the driver says (`dr_why_stop/3`). A
  build reads the global once per report site and once per error it reports. (0.144, 0.146)

### Compile and link

- `cicilang_compile/3` goes through the embedded LLVM only, `library(ccl_llvm)` (owner's rule: no clang, no LLVM
  binary). Where it is not built, the error names `module/build-llvm.sh`. (M5)
- `cicilang_link/3` (`ccl_link/3`) runs `cc` in C or `c++` in C++ over the objects, the link flags and
  `ccl_link_libs/1`. A failed link is `link: ` with the linker's output. (M2, M5)
- `ccl_link_libs/1`: on Linux, ` -lc++` for C++ and ` -lm` for C; on macOS, nothing. Why: on Linux `c++` is g++, whose
  library is libstdc++, and glibc keeps `sqrt`, `creal` and `cabs` in libm. The C++ link names the library of the tree
  the program was READ from, ` -L<root>/lib -Wl,-rpath,<root>/lib -lc++` (`ccl_cxx_dirs`): two or three libc++ are
  installed side by side on the Ubuntu box (`/usr/lib/llvm-18`, `-21`, `-22`), chosen by `$LLVM`, and the headers of one
  with the library of another do not link. Without `$LLVM` the NEWEST tree is read, 22 here: the gates run with
  `LLVM=/usr/lib/llvm-18` and `LLVM=/usr/lib/llvm-21`. LIBC++ABI IS NAMED after `-lc++` where the tree has one (0.181;
  ` -lc++abi`, `ccl_cxxabi_lib/2`): libc++ 18's `libc++.so` is a linker script, `INPUT(libc++.so.1 -lc++abi -lunwind)`,
  which names it, and libc++ 21's and 22's is the library itself, so the link through g++ found the program's
  `__cxa_throw`, `__cxa_begin_catch`, personality and type information in libstdc++, g++'s own runtime, while libc++'s
  code asked libc++abi -- two runtimes in one process, and `std::current_exception()` captured nothing
  (`exceptionptr.cpp`). Over libc++ 18 the libraries and their bindings are the same as without. For another machine
  (0.161), ` -lm` in C and, in C++, its libc++ under the sysroot: ` -L<sysroot><root>/lib
  -Wl,-rpath-link,<sysroot><root>/lib -Wl,-rpath,<root>/lib -lc++ -lm`, the rpath where that machine keeps the library,
  which `qemu-aarch64 -L <sysroot>` finds under the sysroot. (0.93, 0.100, 0.122, 0.161, 0.181)
- LIBATOMIC IS NAMED AT THE LINK WHERE AN OBJECT CALLS IT (0.208; `ccl_note_libatomic/1` in `ccl_compile/3`,
  `ccl_libatomic_lib/2` in `ccl_link/3`), on Linux, this machine's or another's, as libm is: the compiled IR is asked
  for a call of libatomic's routines (`@__atomic_` -- an atomic object of a size that is no lock-free width, an x86
  `long double`'s) or a sixteen-byte atomic, which LLVM turns into `__atomic_*_16`, and the next link takes ` -latomic`,
  once. clang and gcc name it only when the program's link says so; a program that uses those atomics linked here with
  no flag of its own failed, undefined `__atomic_load`. An IR served from the store holds the same calls, so the text is
  what is asked, split at the string (`ccl_ir_has/2`: cocolog's `sub_atom/5` is quadratic there, the Findings).
  `atomodd.c`, `atomldbl.c`. (0.208)

## The lexers

### Two lexers, one specification

- Two lexers turn a file into the same tokens, `tok(Kind, Value, Line)`. The DCG `ccl_lex//2` (`ccl_syntax.pl`) is the
  specification and the fallback. The native `ccl_lex_native(+Text, +Line0, +Mode, +Lang, -Tokens, -Rest)` in
  `module/cicilang.cicili` is the one that runs: C in Cicili, keyword tables and punctuators in C, `tok/3` built by
  `coco_make` behind `coco_m_machine`. Why: the DCG lexer was the cost floor of every read. (M1)
- THE NATIVE LEXER'S BUFFERS GROW THROUGH A SECOND POINTER (0.190; `ccl_lx_grow_toks`, `ccl_lx_grow_buf`): a refused
  allocation keeps the old block and marks the lexer (`oom`), and `ccl_lex_native/6` frees what it holds and raises
  `resource_error(memory)`, which a `catch/3` takes. The token array and the text buffer were grown by `x = realloc(x,
  n)`, which lost the block, and the next store wrote through a null pointer: signal 11 (cocolog's owner named the
  pattern at 2.11.1). Measured with a shim that refuses the lexer's own large requests (session scratch): a string
  literal of 300,000 characters and 200,000 tokens, each a crash before and the error after. (0.190)
- `ccl_tokens/3` and `ccl_lex_atom/4` (the preprocessor's door) choose the lexer by `'$ccl_lexer'`, which
  `ccl_ensure_globals` sets once from a probe of `ccl_lex_native/6`. `library(ccl_syntax)` loaded alone lexes through
  the DCG. (M1)
- **A lexer rule changes in BOTH lexers.** Reader `k84` compares them token for token and rest for rest on
  `test/c/lexer.c` (every mode, both languages), `rich.c`, `cocolog.c`, `run/btree_del.c`, `test/cpp/classes.cpp`,
  `sys/cdefs.h` and `math.h` -- the preprocessor's marked mode (below) on `lexer.c`, `classes.cpp` and `math.h`, its
  marks among the tokens (0.209); `k85` checks that the native lexer runs. A new token form goes into `test/c/lexer.c`.
  In `punct` mode both lexers read `lexer.c` to its end since 0.210 (below): its last line, the prefixed literals of
  0.93, came after the `@` where both stopped, and no mode had compared it. (M1, 0.209, 0.210)
- THE REST IS IN THE RUN'S TEXT UNITS in both lexers (0.196): the DCG's is what is left of the codes it was given, and the
  native lexer's the codes of the text it did not read as `atom_codes/2` gives them (`coco_m_codes_of`, the SDK's), its
  characters past ASCII, where a token's body is its bytes (the Strings topic). It was the text's bytes, and `k84` met it
  once `test/c/lexer.c` held text past ASCII: in `punct` mode both lexers stop at its first continuation, and the rests
  differed by the bytes past ASCII after it. `ccl_line_of/3` finds the rest in the file's codes. (0.196)
- `'$ccl_hash'` is the mode. In `line` mode (the reader's) a `#` line is one `tok(pp, Text, L)`, continuations joined.
  In `punct` mode (the preprocessor's) `#` and `##` are punctuators and a number is `tok(num, Spelling, L)`, so
  `200112L` pastes whole; a pp-number may start with a dot; a literal, a digraph and an alternative token are spelled as
  written there too (0.211, below). (M5, 0.108, 0.211)
- THE PREPROCESSOR'S MARKED LEX (0.209; `ccl_lex_atom_marked/4` over `ccl_lex_marked//2`, natively the mode `punctsp`):
  a text line and a macro body are lexed in `punct` mode with each token that layout precedes -- blanks, a comment, a
  newline -- and the text's first wrapped `h(T, ['$sp'])`, the preprocessor's stream form, the mark of the white space
  that `#x` keeps (the Macro expansion topic). The DCG looks at the next code before it takes the layout
  (`ccl_layout_ahead//1`); the native lexer compares its place before and after `ccl_lx_layout` and wraps the token it
  pushed last (`ccl_lx_mark`, one `['$sp']` list a call). `#if`'s and the other directives' tails are lexed unmarked
  (`pp_lex_body/2`). (0.209)
- A CHARACTER THAT BEGINS NO TOKEN IS A TOKEN OF ITS OWN IN THE PREPROCESSOR'S MODE (C17 6.4/1's last kind of
  preprocessing token, "each non-white-space character that cannot be one of the above"; 0.210): `@`, `` ` ``, a stray
  `\` or quote is `tok(other, Code, L)` in `punct` mode in both lexers (`ccl_pp_token//3`; natively `ccl_lx_other`, the
  place and the line put back where `ccl_lx_token` read none), so `#x` spells it -- the standard's `str(: @\n)`, whose
  stray `\` begins an escape of the string made (the Macro expansion topic) -- and the user's file refuses it where it
  reaches the reader, `lexical(L)` at its line (`ccl_pp_top/3`; reader `k71`). Both lexers stopped there: the user's
  file was refused at the line even where the character was a macro's argument that `#` takes, and a header's line lost
  its rest. The `line` mode stops there still. `test/c/run/ppexample.c`, `ppexample4.c`. (0.210)
- A TOKEN IS SPELLED AS WRITTEN IN THE PREPROCESSOR'S MODE, as a number is (C17 6.10.3.2/2 and [cpp.stringize]/2: `#x`
  gives "the spelling of the preprocessing token"; 0.211): a string or character literal is `tok(lit, Spelling, L)` --
  its prefix, its escapes, a raw string's delimiters, a multi-character constant's characters --, a digraph `tok(dg,
  Spelling, L)` and C++'s alternative token `tok(alt, Spelling, L)`, the spelling an atom of the codes the token took,
  in both lexers (`ccl_pp_spelled/4` in `ccl_pp_token//3`, `ccl_consumed/3`; natively `ccl_lx_is_lit` and
  `ccl_lx_spell_lit` in the main loop, the kinds `k_lit`, `k_dg` and `k_alt` in `ccl_lx_word`, `ccl_lx_punct` and
  `ccl_lx_token`). The reader's token is made from the spelling where the preprocessor's tokens end (`pp_norm/2` in
  `pp_finish/2`: a literal lexed again in `line` mode, a digraph and an alternative token their punctuator,
  `pp_digraph/2`, `ccl_alt_token/2`), and so are `#if`'s (`pp_normalize/2`) and the operand of `__has_include` and
  `__has_embed` (`pp_norm_all/2`). The lexers made the reader's token, its value, and `#x` spelled `"\x41"` as `"A"`,
  `'ab'` as `24930`, `R"(a\b)"` as `"a\\b"`, `<:` as `[` and `and` as `&&`. A macro body's `%:` and `%:%:` stay its
  operators (the Macro expansion topic). Reader `k84` over `test/c/lexer.c`; `test/c/run/spelling.c`,
  `test/cpp/run/spelling.cpp`. (0.211)
- The DCG lexer writes `"`, `'` and `\` as 34, 39 and 92, never `0'"` or `0''`, which read badly in cocolog. (M1)

### Keywords and punctuators

- The keyword tables are the LANGUAGE's, never the level's: `ccl_keyword/1` is `ccl_c_keyword/1` plus, in C++,
  `ccl_cpp_keyword/1` (natively `ccl_lx_ckw`, `ccl_lx_cppkw`). In C, C23's new keywords arrive as identifiers and the
  grammar reads them at the level. `override` and `final` stay identifiers. Why: k84 compares the shared tables. (0.57)
- `concept requires co_await co_yield co_return consteval constinit char8_t` are C++ keywords in both lexers. (0.42)
- `<=>` is a punctuator in both lexers and both languages (`ccl_punct//1`, `ccl_lx_p3`). `::` lexes in C++ only. `:=`
  is a punctuator. (0.42)
- `tie` is an identifier, and `<*>` is no punctuator in either lexer; the grammar reads `tie` in context. (0.109)
- `$` IS A LETTER of a name in both lexers and in a macro's name (`ccl_alpha/1`, `ccl_lx_alpha`, `pp_word/3`; C17
  6.4.2.1/3's implementation-defined characters, as clang and gcc take it in both languages; 0.210): `int a$b`, `#define
  M$ 3`, `$lead(1)`. It was a lexical error. `test/c/run/dollar.c`; reader `k84` over `test/c/lexer.c`. (0.210)
- AN IDENTIFIER PAST ASCII (C23 6.4.2.1, C++23 [lex.name]; 0.196): a letter, `_`, a digit after the first, a character
  past ASCII -- the bytes of its UTF-8 to the native lexer -- and a universal character name past ASCII, `caf\u00e9` the
  identifier `café`, its UTF-8 in the atom (`ccl_word//2`, `ccl_id_first//2`, `ccl_id_more//1`, `ccl_ucn_codes/3`;
  natively `ccl_lx_alpha`, `ccl_lx_id_ucn`, `ccl_lx_word`); the preprocessor reads a macro's name past ASCII too
  (`pp_word/3`), and one spelled with a universal character name since 0.213 (`pp_word/3` over `ccl_ucn//1`: `#define
  caf\u00e9 3` is the macro `café`, in `#ifdef`, `#ifndef`, `#undef` and a parameter's name alike; it named `caf`,
  `test/c/run/ucnmacro.c`). Which characters past ASCII is the level's since 0.221 (below). They were ASCII alone, and
  `int café = 3;` was a lexical error where clang reads it in C17 and C++17 too. A symbol past ASCII is spelled quoted
  (the Lowering's topic) and the mangler counts bytes (the Itanium mangler's topic). `test/c/run/identutf8.c`,
  `test/cpp/run/identutf8.cpp`. (0.196, 0.213)
- AN IDENTIFIER'S CHARACTER PAST ASCII BY THE LANGUAGE AND ITS LEVEL (0.221; C23 6.4.2.1 and [lex.name]: UAX #31's
  XID_Start first and XID_Continue after, at C23 and at every C++ level; C11 Annex D in C11 and C17, D.2's not first;
  C99 Annex D in C99, its digits not first (6.4.2.1/3); `ccl_id_cp/2`, `ccl_id_level/1` over `library/ccl_xid.pl`,
  natively `ccl_lx_wide_id`, `ccl_lx_id_ucn_ok` over `module/ccl_xid.h`; the native lexer is handed `c23`, `c` or `c99`
  for C, `ccl_lex_lang/1`): every character past ASCII was a letter, one that no level takes included. The tables are
  clang's: clang 18 and 21 were asked of each character of the planes that hold any, initially and after a letter at
  C99, C11 and C23, and each set the generator writes is the one clang takes, character for character (with Unicode
  15.1's U+200C, U+200D, the two katakana middle dots and CJK Extension I, which Perl's 15.0 lacks, and the mathematical
  notation profile clang takes with a warning: U+2202, U+2207, U+221E and their mathematical alphanumeric forms first,
  the superscript and subscript digits and signs after). `int a\u20acb;` is C11's and C17's name and C23's and C++'s
  error, a middle dot first C17's name and C++'s error, `x\u0301` C11's name and C99's error; a macro's name is read so
  too (`pp_wide_id/1` in `pp_word/3`). Read in bytes, the DCG decodes the UTF-8 sequence to ask it (`ccl_id_wide//3`); a
  number's suffix and a pp-number keep every character past ASCII, in both lexers. Reader `k94` (the two lexers token
  for token), the driver gate's level check, `stdc11.c` (`-std=c11`), `idchars.cpp`. (0.221)
- THE WHITE SPACE PAST ASCII IS BLANK (0.221; clang's, in both languages at every level, with its warning `treating
  Unicode character as whitespace'; `ccl_wide_space/2` in `ccl_layout//2` and `ccl_layout_ahead/3`, natively
  `ccl_lx_wide_ws` in `ccl_lx_layout`): U+0085, U+00A0, U+1680, U+180E, U+2000 to U+200A, U+2028, U+2029, U+202F, U+205F
  and U+3000 (`library/ccl_xid.pl`'s `ws`), none a newline. They were letters: `int<U+00A0>n = 7;` declared the name
  `int n`, `undeclared('int n')` at its use. `idchars.cpp`. A CHARACTER PAST ASCII THAT BEGINS NO TOKEN is one token,
  `tok(other, CodePoint, L)` in both lexers (`ccl_other_char//1`; `ccl_lx_other` takes the whole UTF-8 sequence), and
  the user's file names it in the diagnostic as clang does (`lexical_char(L, C)` from `ccl_pp_top/3`, `dr_diag/3`):
  `character <U+20AC> not allowed in an identifier`, and for one that may follow and not begin a name `character
  <U+00B7> not allowed at the start of an identifier`; where no level takes it and it stands first, clang says
  `unexpected character <U+0301>` and this compiler the first form. (0.221)
- THE DIGRAPHS ([lex.digraph], C 6.4.6/3; 0.201): `<:`, `:>`, `<%`, `%>`, `%:` and `%:%:` are `[`, `]`, `{`, `}`, `#`
  and `##` in both lexers and both languages (`ccl_punct//1`'s first clauses, `ccl_token//3` for `%:` and `%:%:`;
  natively `ccl_lx_dg`, `ccl_lx_dgp` and the first branch of `ccl_lx_token`), and a line that begins with `%:` is a
  directive (`pp_hash_intro/2` in `pp_line_mark/3` and `pp_directive_line/2`; the `line` mode reads it as a `#` line).
  In C++ `<::` is `<` and then `::` unless the next character is `:` or `>` ([lex.pptoken]/3.2: `std::vector<::X>`;
  `ccl_dg_lt/2`). They were no tokens, a lexical error. `-E` spells the punctuator, and `#x` the digraph as written
  since 0.211 (the Two lexers topic). `test/c/run/digraphs.c`; reader `k84` over `test/c/lexer.c`. (0.201, 0.211)
- C++'S ALTERNATIVE TOKENS ([lex.digraph]/2, [lex.key]/2; 0.201): `and`, `and_eq`, `bitand`, `bitor`, `compl`, `not`,
  `not_eq`, `or`, `or_eq`, `xor` and `xor_eq` are the punctuators `&&`, `&=`, `&`, `|`, `~`, `!`, `!=`, `||`, `|=`, `^`
  and `^=` in C++ in both lexers, never a name (`ccl_alt_token/2` in `ccl_word//2`; natively `ccl_lx_alt`, `ccl_lx_altp`
  in `ccl_lx_word`); C has them as `<iso646.h>`'s macros. They were identifiers, and `bool t = true and not false;` was
  refused. A stringized one spells as written since 0.211, `#x` of `and` `"and"` as clang spells it, where it spelled
  its punctuator, `"&&"` (the Two lexers topic). `alttokens.cpp`, `hdrrest.cpp`, `spelling.cpp`. (0.201, 0.211)
- A `#cocolog` line takes every line up to the `#end` line, or the file's end, raw into one `tok(cocolog, Text, L)`
  (`ccl_cocolog_body//3`, `ccl_lx_cocolog`). (M1b)

### Integer literals

- Both lexers read `0b1011` (C23, C++14) and the digit separator `1'000'000` in every scan. The native lexer drops the
  separator from the value and the `strtod` text (`ccl_lx_puts_num`). The pp-number takes it (`ccl_pp_number//1`,
  `ccl_lx_pp_number`), else `1'000'` lexes as a char literal. Reader `k88`. (0.57)
- The suffixes `u`, `l`, `ul` (any case, any order) give `tok(uint|long|ulong, N, L)` (`ccl_int_suffix//1`,
  `ccl_int_kind/4`; natively `ccl_lx_int_suffix`, `x->sfx` 0 to 3); `z` is a long. The parser makes `int(N)`,
  `uint(N)`, `long(N)`, `ulong(N)`. Reader `k59`. Why: `1L` was `int(1)`, and `%ld` read garbage. `ll` and `ull` give
  the kinds `llong` and `ullong` (0.179; `x->sfx` 6 and 7, the l's counted), which the parser types as the casts they
  amount to, as it types `1.5f`: `cast(base([], [long, long]), long(N))` and `cast(base([], [unsigned, long, long]),
  ulong(N))` (`ccl_null_constant/1` takes `0ll`). They were `long` and `ulong`, one type with them under LP64 and
  another to `typeid`, `_Generic`, an overload and a template: `f(3ll)` called `f(long)`. `-E` spells them back
  (`ccl_pp_spell_tok/4`). `test/c/run/llong.c`, `test/cpp/run/llong.cpp`. (0.43, 0.179)
- AN INTEGER LITERAL IS THE FIRST TYPE THAT HOLDS ITS VALUE (C 6.4.4.1/5, [lex.icon]/3; 0.201): a HEX, OCTAL OR BINARY
  one with no suffix past INT_MAX that an unsigned int holds is the kind a `u` gives, `tok(uint, N, L)`, in both lexers
  (`ccl_int_end//4` over `ccl_int_based/4`; natively `ccl_lx_emit_int`, a C++ ud-suffix's tail `x->sfx` 8, the int kind
  with no such test), a decimal one stays the `int` token; the inference types `int(N)` past INT_MAX as a long, `uint(N)`
  past UINT_MAX as an unsigned long and `long(big(A))` by `ccl_big_type/2` (`ccl_type_of/2`), as the lowering spells them
  (`ir_expr/4`: `i32 4294967296` was 0), and `0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFll` past LLONG_MAX is an unsigned long long. They were an
  int and an unsigned whatever the value: `~0x80000000` folded to -2147483649, `f(0xFFFFFFFF)` called `f(int)` over
  `f(unsigned)`, and `nanoseconds(2500000000)` deduced an int, the `const int &` bound a temporary of the truncated value
  and <__threading_support>'s `__convert_to_timespec` gave -1 s. In `#if` such a literal is signed (the Preprocessor's
  topic). Reader `k84` over a line of them in `test/c/lexer.c`. `test/c/run/littype.c`, `test/cpp/run/littype.cpp`.
  (0.201)
- C23's `wb` and `uwb` (any case, any base) give the kinds `bitint` and `ubitint` (`x->sfx` 4, 5). The parser makes
  `wb(N)`, a `_BitInt` of the value's width plus the sign, and `uwb(N)`. (0.93)
- An integer literal of 2^60 or more is `big(Atom)` in BOTH lexers (`ccl_lx_emit_int`, `ccl_lx_big`; `ccl_int_value/2`,
  `ccl_big_decimal/1`, `ccl_hex_int/2`, `ccl_bin_int/2`, `ccl_octal_int/2`). The atom is the decimal digits of a
  decimal literal, else `0x` and the lowercase hex digits, no leading zeros. `pp_norm` uses the same door. A reader of
  the atom takes it by its base, the constant evaluator too (`ccl_wide/2`). `test/c/run/bigint.c`, `bighex.c`. Why:
  cocolog's integers were 61-bit (64 since 2.0.0, a result past them an error), and `9223372036854775807LL` was -1.
  (0.94, 0.112, 0.157)
- A `big` literal is the first of `long` and `unsigned long` that holds it (`ccl_big_type/2` over `ccl_big_fits/3`), and
  it keys a template instance by its atom (`cpp_type_key`). A value past 64 bits, which only a fold makes (a 128-bit
  type's constant: `numeric_limits<__int128>::max()`), is the first of `__int128` and `unsigned __int128` that holds it,
  and a negative value is a `long` where it fits one; the lowering spells `int(big(A))` in that type (`ir_expr`). Before
  0.129 such a value was an `unsigned long`, lowered as an `i64` and cut to its low half. (0.94, 0.129)
- AN INTEGER'S TAIL THAT IS NO INTEGER SUFFIX IS ITS UD-SUFFIX in C++ ([lex.ext]/1; 0.179; `ccl_int_end//3`,
  `ccl_udl_int_ahead/2`; natively `ccl_lx_int_suffix`): nothing of the tail is read, and the identifier after the number
  is its suffix (`ccl_udl//2`). `3us` is the literal 3 and the suffix `us`, microseconds: the suffix `u` ran on into it,
  the suffix `s` was left, and `nanoseconds(1us)` was 10^9; `0x10us`, `0b11us`, `017us` and `5ul_x` alike. In C the
  tail is the suffix it was. Reader `k84` over `test/c/lexer.c`. `udlsuffix.cpp` (C++23), `stdchrono.cpp`. (0.179)

### Floating literals

- `1.5f` is `tok(floatf, F, L)` and `1.5L` is `tok(floatl, Text, L)`. The parser makes the casts they amount to,
  `cast(base([], [float]), float(F))` and `cast(base([], [long, double]), ldbl(Text))`. `test/c/run/hexfloat.c`. Why:
  `sizeof`, `_Generic` and a template deduce the literal's own type. (0.108, 0.154)
- A LONG DOUBLE LITERAL'S VALUE IS ITS TEXT (0.154), as a decimal literal's is: `floatl` and `imagl` are text kinds
  (`ccl_text_kind/1` in `ccl_float_value/3`; the native `ccl_lx_emit_float` for `fsfx` 2), the text the lexers spell for
  strtod (`1.18973149535723176502e+4932`, `.5`, `1.0e5`, `0x1.8p1`, `0x.8p-2`, the separators dropped; the hex form by
  `ccl_hex_text/6`), and `ldbl(Text)` or `imagl(Text)` to the parser. The lowering rounds the text once to the long
  double's own format (`ir_ld_value/2`, the Lowering topic). It held the double nearest the text, clamped to the largest
  double (`ccl_finite_float/2`, gone): `LDBL_MAX` and `1e999L` were the largest double, `LDBL_MIN` and `LDBL_TRUE_MIN`
  zeros, and `0.1L` a double's 0.1, where clang reads 1.18973e+4932, a finite 1e999, 3.3621e-4932, 3.6452e-4951 and
  0.100000000000000000001. `-E` spells the text with its suffix. Reader `k84` reads a line of them in both lexers. Reader
  130. `test/c/run/ldconst.c`, `test/cpp/run/ldlimits.cpp`. (0.154)
- Both lexers read hex floats (`0x1.8p1`, the binary exponent required) and a leading dot (`.5f`). (0.108)
- `f16`, `f32`, `f64`, `f128` and `bf16` (any case) are read in both lexers, and the literal stays a double. The
  native lexer reads the character after `b` again. (0.93)
- A DOUBLE OR A FLOAT LITERAL PAST THE LARGEST DOUBLE IS AN INFINITY, as clang reads it (0.143; `1e999`, `1e999f`, `2e400i`).
  Every literal was clamped to the largest double from 0.55 to 0.142, while cocolog wrote an infinity `inf.0`, which its
  own reader refused, and a summary's AST holding one did not consult; 1.10.28 reads `1.0Inf` back, and a stored read
  freezes its floats (0.132). A long double literal keeps its text (above). `test/c/run/fpspecial.c`. (0.55, 0.143, 0.154)
- A DECIMAL FLOATING LITERAL (C23 6.4.4.2; 0.129) ends in `df`, `dd` or `dl` (or `DF`, `DD`, `DL`; `ccl_dec_suffix/3`, the
  native `ccl_lx_float_suffix` with `fsfx` 3 to 5) and is `tok(dec32 | dec64 | dec128, Text, L)`: its TEXT, as the lexers
  spell it for strtod (`0.1`, `1.0e5`, `.5`, the separators dropped; `ccl_float_value/3`), since no double holds 0.1. The
  parser makes `dec32(Text)`, `dec64(Text)`, `dec128(Text)`, and the lowering encodes the text exactly (the Lowering
  topic). `-E` spells it back with its suffix (`pp_dec_suffix/2`). Reader `k84` reads a line of them in both lexers.
  (0.129)

### Imaginary literals

- Both lexers read GNU's imaginary mark `i`, `I`, `j` or `J` after the suffix (`ccl_imag_mark//0`; natively
  `ccl_lx_imag_c`, `x->imag`). A floating one is `tok(imag, F, L)`, a `_Complex double` (`2.0i`); with an `f` it is
  `tok(imagf, F, L)`, a `_Complex float` (`1.5if`, `1.0fi`); with an `l` `tok(imagl, Text, L)`, a `_Complex long double`
  (`1.0li`, `1.0il`; 0.112, as clang has it -- a `_Complex double` before), its text kept (0.154, the Floating literals
  topic). The parser makes `imag(F)`, `imagf(F)`, `imagl(Text)`. (0.101, 0.112, 0.154)
- An integer imaginary literal's suffix names its kind: `imagi`, `imagui`, `imagli`, `imaguli` (`ccl_int_tok//4`,
  `ccl_imag_kind/2`); a `_BitInt` suffix gives the int kinds. The parser makes `imagi(Specs, N)` (`ccl_imag_specs/3`):
  no suffix `int` up to INT_MAX, else `long`; `u` `unsigned` up to UINT_MAX, else `unsigned long`; `l` `long`; `ul`
  `unsigned long`; `ll` `long long` and `ull` `unsigned long long`, the kinds `imaglli` and `imagulli` (0.179); `big(A)`
  by `ccl_big_type/2`. `test/c/run/complex3.c`, `llong.c`. (0.104, 0.179)
- IN C++ A NUMBER'S EXACT `i`, `if` AND `il` ARE A UD-SUFFIX ([lex.ext]/1, [complex.literals]; 0.179;
  `ccl_imag_udl_ahead/2`, `ccl_int_end//3`; natively `ccl_lx_imag_udl`), C++14's `<complex>` literals, and `if` lexes as
  the keyword (`ccl_udl//2` takes it): the desugaring calls `operator""i` where a using-directive or a using-declaration
  makes it visible -- of `std`, `std::literals`, `std::complex_literals` or `std::literals::complex_literals`, at
  namespace scope for the rest of the unit, in a namespace's block to the block's end and in a block to its end
  (`cpp_cplxlit_using/2`, `cpp_cplxlit_visible/1`) -- and else makes GNU's imaginary literal (`cpp_udl_imag/3`: `3if`
  a `_Complex int`, the `f` dropped, `2.0if` a `_Complex float`), as clang's Sema does where the lookup of the operator
  fails. `3i` was GNU's always: `auto e = 3i;` under `using namespace std::complex_literals;` was a `_Complex int`.
  `complexlit.cpp` (C++23), `complexrtti.cpp`, `udlsuffix.cpp`. (0.179)

### Strings, characters and escapes

- Both lexers read the prefixed literals (`ccl_lit_prefix//2`, `ccl_lx_string_k`): `L`, `u`, `U` give `wstr`, `u16str`,
  `u32str` (`wchr`, `u16chr`, `u32chr` for chars), and `u8` the kinds `u8str` and `u8chr` (0.196). The body is a plain
  string's UTF-8 bytes, which the lowering decodes, the DCG's too where it reads characters (`ccl_text_bytes/3`: cocolog
  2's units, a character past ASCII one code). Reader `k91`. (0.93, 0.196)
- A u8 LITERAL HAS ITS LEVEL'S TYPE (C23 6.4.4.5/12, 6.4.5/6, [lex.ccon]/3, [lex.string]/6; 0.196): `u8'c'` is C++20's
  `char8_t`, C23's `unsigned char`, C++17's `char`, the cast a `1.5f` is (`ccl_u8chr_node/2`), and `u8"..."` is C++20's
  `const char8_t[N]` and C23's `char8_t[N]` -- the node `u8str(S)` there alone, a plain `str(S)` before
  (`ccl_string_node/3`): its bytes a plain string's to the lowering (`ir_expr`, `ir_gconst`, an array it initializes),
  its element char8_t's to the inference, deduction and `decltype` (`cpp_string_literal/2`). They were `str` and `chr`:
  `decltype(u8'a')` was `char` at C++20, `std::u8string s = u8"x";` had no constructor, and `sizeof(u8'a')` was 4 at C23.
  `-E` spells the prefix (`pp_str_prefix/2`, `ccl_pp_spell_tok/4`). clang 18 types C23's `u8"..."` as `char[N]`, clang
  21 and 22 as the standard has it, and a fixture's expect is clang 22's. `test/c/run/u8lit23.c`, `test/cpp/run/u8lit.cpp`,
  `u8lit20.cpp` (C++20). (0.196)
- A CHARACTER LITERAL'S ITEMS (C 6.4.4.4, [lex.ccon]; 0.196): a PREFIXED one holds one character, a UTF-8 sequence its code
  point (`L'é'` 233, `U'😀'` 128512; `ccl_wchr_body//1`, `ccl_lx_utf8_at`); a PLAIN one of one byte is a char's value, a
  signed one where plain char is signed (`'\xE9'` -23 on x86-64, 233 on aarch64 Linux; `ccl_plain_chr_value/2`, in an
  expression, a case label, a template argument and `#if` alike, C 6.4.4.4/10 and [lex.ccon]/2) -- it was 233 on both,
  and `c == '\xff'` over `char c = '\xff';` false --, and of two bytes or more -- `'ab'`, `'abcd'`, `'\x41\x42'`, `'é'`'s
  two bytes, a universal character name past ASCII's UTF-8 -- a MULTI-CHARACTER constant, the token `tok(int, V, L)`, an
  `int` in C and in C++, its value the bytes in order, the last four kept, read signed (`ccl_chr_token/3`,
  `ccl_multichar/3`; natively `ccl_lx_char_k`), as gcc and clang give it. The native lexer read one byte and refused
  both; `'é'` and `'\u00e9'`, which clang refuses (`character too large`), are gcc's 50089. A stringized
  multi-character constant spells its value (`#x` of `'ab'` is `"24930"`, clang's `"'ab'"`). `test/c/run/chrsign.c`
  (both machines), `test/cpp/run/chrsign.cpp`. (0.196)
- ADJACENT STRING LITERALS ARE ONE (C 6.4.5/5, [lex.string]/12; 0.196; `ccl_strings_k//4`, `ccl_kind_join/3`): their bodies
  joined, of the prefix one of them has -- `"a" L"b"` and `L"a" "b"` wide, `u"x" "y"` a char16_t string, `u8"x" "y"` a u8
  one; two different prefixes are not joined. Only plain ones were: `L"ab" L"cd"` was refused, and so was a macro's `L""
  x`. `test/c/run/u8lit23.c`, `test/cpp/run/u8lit.cpp`. (0.196)
- A `u"..."` literal is UTF-16 ([lex.string]/10): a code point past U+FFFF is a surrogate pair, two `i16` units
  (`ir_wide_units/3`, `ir_utf16/2`), in the constant, in an array it initializes, in that array's bound
  (`ccl_utf16_count/2`) and in `sizeof` (`ccl_literal_bytes`); it was one unit that kept the low bits.
  `test/c/run/u16pairs.c`. (0.112)
- A raw string literal ([lex.string]/1; C++ only) is read by both lexers: `R"d(...)d"` and its prefixes `u8`, `L`, `u`,
  `U`, the body as it stands, no escape read, up to `)`, the delimiter, `"`; a newline in it is counted
  (`ccl_raw_prefix//1`, `ccl_raw_delim//1`, `ccl_raw_body//4`; `ccl_lx_raw_start`, `ccl_lx_raw`). In C, `R` is a name
  and a plain string follows. Reader `k84` over `test/c/lexer.c`. Why: libc++ 18's escaped-string writer (`<format>` at
  C++23, `std::print`) writes `R"(\')"`. (0.115)
- A RAW STRING THAT SPANS LINES is one line to the preprocessor (0.138; C++ only; `pp_raw_join/5`, `pp_raw_open/2`): a line
  that opens `R"d(` and leaves it open is joined with the next lines, a newline between, up to `)d"`, before the line is
  lexed; the scanner steps over comments, strings, character literals, whole identifiers and numbers, so `uR"`, `u8R"` and
  `LR"` open one and `xR"` does not, and `__LINE__` after it counts the lines it took. libc++ 21's `__chrono/exception.h`
  builds a message so, and the read of `<chrono>` met a `lexical error`. `rawlines.cpp`. (0.138)
- The escapes are C's, GNU's `\e`, `\xHH`, `\x{...}`, `\o{...}`, `\u{...}`, `\uXXXX`, `\UXXXXXXXX`, and `\NNN` with up
  to three octal digits (`ccl_escape//1`, `ccl_ucn//1`; `ccl_lx_escape`, `ccl_lx_ucn`). A code point goes into a string
  as UTF-8 (`ccl_utf8/3`, `ccl_lx_put_utf8`), into a char as itself. Why: `\101` read as `\1` then `01`. (0.43)

### `\N{NAME}`

- Both lexers read `\N{NAME}` ([lex.charset], C23 6.4.3), an EXACT match: UTF-8 in a string, the code point in a char
  or a wide char. The runs `ccl_uname_range(Prefix, Lo, Hi)` (names that end in hex digits, CJK UNIFIED
  IDEOGRAPH-4E00 and kin) are computed first. Aliases of the kinds clang takes (control, correction, alternate,
  figment) are names. `test/c/run/uniname.c`. (0.104)
- An abbreviation (`\N{NUL}`) or an unknown name is a lexical error in both lexers: `ccl_escape//1` and
  `ccl_lx_escape` refuse `N{`, so it never falls back to the letter `N`. (0.103)
- The DCG reads the name by `ccl_uname_value/2` (the runs, then `ccl_uname/2`); `ccl_uninames_ready/0` loads
  `library/ccl_uninames.pl` by `ensure_loaded/1` on the first `\N{`, found on `$COCOLOG_LIBRARY`, and remembers it in
  the global `'$ccl_uninames'`, never a clause (a clause persists under `--embed`). The native `ccl_lx_ucn` calls
  `ccl_uname_code`, raw C that binary-searches `module/ccl_uninames.h`. (0.103)
- The table is written once. `library/ccl_uninames.pl` is GENERATED, never edited: `perl module/gen-uninames.pl >
  library/ccl_uninames.pl` (Perl's `Unicode::UCD`), Unicode 15.0.0, 44,115 names (Hangul syllables computed), 119
  aliases, 16 runs. `module/build.sh` spells `module/ccl_uninames.h` from it (names in `LC_ALL=C` strcmp order, then the
  runs, alias kind comments stripped); the header is never committed. (0.104)

## The preprocessor

### The design

- **The preprocessor is cocolog's own** (owner's rule: no clang, no LLVM binary is run): `library/ccl_pp.pl`. (M5)
- `ccl_pp_file(+Path, -Tokens, -Files)` preprocesses a file standalone (the predefined macros and its own) into reader
  tokens and names every file it pulled (a summary's deps). `ccl_pp_macros/1` answers the run's own macros from
  `'$pp_names'`. `ccl_pp_parse/4` reads the tokens inside `ccl_with_file/2`. (M5)
- A run is a GENERATION: `pp_reset/0` bumps `'$pp_gen'`. A macro is `'$pp:<Name>'` = `mac(Gen, Params, codes(Cs),
  Tokens | none)`, `undef(Gen)` or `nomac(Gen, Inc)`; an older run's macro is not this run's. `Params` is `obj` or a
  list ending in `va(N)`. (M5)
- Each file is preprocessed inside `\+ \+` (`pp_include_file`); its output survives under `'$pp_out:K'`, and
  `pp_finish/2` splices it. Why: cocolog reclaims the heap on backtracking only. (0.46)
- The run lexes in `punct` mode, `line` after. `pp_finish/2` and `pp_normalize` turn `tok(num, ...)` back by `pp_norm`:
  a plain decimal by `ccl_int_value/2` (`big(Atom)` past 2^60), the rest by the lexer. (0.94)

### Lines

- `pp_source/2` makes `line(N, Atom)` once per process and path (`'$pp_src:<Path>'`, or `'$pp_srct:<Path>'` with
  trigraphs): lines by `atomic_list_concat/3`, continuations joined, comments removed, block-comment lines counted.
  Only a line with `/` or a final backslash is walked code by code (`pp_clean/3`). Why: a walk costs ~1 µs a
  character. A DIRECTIVE LINE IS MARKED AS IT IS MADE, `line(N, d(Atom))`, its codes at hand there (`pp_line_mark/3`,
  0.188), and `pp_directive_line/2` takes the mark: a text line fails at its head, where every line was converted to
  codes at every test -- each run over the file, each false group skipped -- 1.40 million tests in a cold read of
  `<thread>` over libc++ 21, the most of them text lines. (M5, 0.188)
- Trigraphs are replaced before anything else (`pp_trigraphs`, `pp_tri`, `pp_trigraph/2`) when `'$ccl_trigraphs'` is
  `yes`: in the ISO modes before C23 and under `-trigraphs`, never in GNU modes or C23 (clang's rule).
  `test/c/run/trigraphs.c`. (0.108)
- Trailing blanks after a final backslash still splice ([lex.phases]/2 as clang reads it; `pp_ends_backslash`); a `//`
  comment ending in a backslash swallows the next line (`pp_join` before `pp_clean`). `test/c/run/splice.c`. (0.99)
- `pp_run/3` sends a `#` line to `pp_directive/6`; it lexes a text line (`pp_lex_line/3`, marked since 0.209: the Lexers
  topic) and expands it (`pp_toks/6`, mode `top`), pulling the next lines for a function-like macro's arguments. (M5,
  0.209)

### Directives and conditional groups

- A false group is skipped by its `#` lines alone (`pp_skip_group/4`, never lexing). `#elifdef` and `#elifndef` are
  read (`pp_cond_word`; `pp_defined_body/3` spells `defined(X)`). (0.43)
- A header that is one `#ifndef X ... #endif` is guarded (`pp_note_guard/2`): included again with X defined, it is
  nothing. `#pragma once` likewise; nesting past 120 is nothing. Why: the SDK includes `sys/cdefs.h` ten times. (M5)
- In a header's run an `#include` (literal, or through the macros) is preprocessed in place; a `.pl` is passed on as
  `tok(pp, ...)`; one found nowhere is nothing. `#include_next` searches past the includer's directory. `#pragma` is
  nothing but `once`; `_Pragma("...")` goes with its operand. (M5)
- A COMPUTED `#include` (C17 6.10.2/4, [cpp.include]/7; 0.211): the directive's tokens are lexed marked, macro-replaced
  and spelled with a space only where white space stood (`pp_computed_codes/2` over `pp_expand_marked/2` and
  `pp_spell_marked/2`), and the header's name is read from that text, as clang and gcc join `<` NAME `>`; `#embed` takes
  its name so too. A space stood between every two tokens: `#define SYS <stdint.h>` named ` stdint . h `, and nothing
  was included, in a header or in the user's file (the User's file topic). `test/c/run/ppinclude.c` (C23: the standard's
  EXAMPLE of `INCFILE`, `#embed INCFILE`), `test/cpp/run/ppinclude.cpp`. (0.211)
- `#line N "file"` (C 6.10.4) and GNU's `# N "file"` set the presumed line and file per file (`pp_presumed`,
  `'$pp_linemap'`) for `__LINE__` and `__FILE__`; a diagnostic names the physical place. (0.108)
- In the user's file `#error` throws `pp_error(L, Text)`, and `#warning` goes to `'$pp_warnings'`, printed by the
  driver after the read (`dr_pp_warnings`). In a header `#error` stops that file (`'$pp_errors'`, unread) and
  `#warning` is nothing. Why: a program's own `#error` compiled to `cicilang: ok`. (0.93)
- `#embed "f"` and `#embed <f>` (with `limit`, `prefix`, `suffix`, `if_empty`, and their `__x__` spellings) put the
  bytes as ints where the directive stood, in C and C++, file or header (`pp_do_embed`). The name resolves as an
  `#include`'s; a code past 255 goes in as UTF-8; a resource nowhere is a `pp_error`. Reader `k89`. (0.93)

### Macro expansion and `#if`

- Expansion follows the standard: an argument is expanded first unless `#` or `##` takes it (`pp_subst/4`); a paste is
  spelled and lexed again (`pp_paste_two/3`); GNU's `, ## __VA_ARGS__` drops the comma (`vamarker`); `__VA_OPT__`
  keeps or drops its group (`pp_va_group`); each token is `h(Token, HideSet)` (`pp_wrap/6`) at the invocation's line,
  so a macro never expands inside itself. A body is lexed on first use (`pp_macro/3`). Reader `k83`. (0.93)
- THE HIDE SETS ARE THOSE OF PROSSER'S ALGORITHM, as clang and gcc expand (C17 6.10.3.4; 0.210). AN ARGUMENT'S TOKENS
  KEEP THEIRS through its expansion and its substitution, the expansion's own joining them (`pp_toks/6`'s mode `marks`
  keeps each element whole; `pp_reline_marks/3` makes it `h(tok(K, V, Mark), HideSet)` in the body's form; `pp_wrap/6`
  over `pp_body_el/6` and `pp_hs_add/3`, a union), so a name that its own expansion left unexpanded stays so where it is
  read again (6.10.3.4/2): `id(obj)` over `#define obj obj+1` was `obj+1+1`, `f(f(z))` of the standard's EXAMPLE 3 `f(2
  * (f(2 * (z[0][0][0]))))`, and `id(LIT(3))(4)` over `LIT(v) v LIT` `3 4 LIT`. A FUNCTION-LIKE MACRO'S EXPANSION IS
  HIDDEN FROM WHAT ITS NAME AND ITS CLOSING `)` BOTH ARE, and its own name (`pp_args/11` gives the `)`,
  `pp_rparen_meet/3`); where a directive or the file's end closes the arguments, from its name's: the name's alone hid
  too much, and `G_0(42)` over `NIL(G_1)(arg)` was `NIL(42)`, `f(2)(9)` over `f(a) a*g` and `g(a) f(a)` `2*f(9)`, where
  both compilers give `42` and `2*9*g` (6.10.3.4/4 leaves the second open). A paste's token is hidden from what both of
  its operands are (`pp_paste_two/3`, `pp_glued/3`). `test/c/run/ppexample.c`, `test/cpp/run/ppexample.cpp`. (0.210)
- `##` IN AN OBJECT-LIKE MACRO PASTES TOO (C17 6.10.3.3/3: "for both object-like and function-like macro invocations";
  0.210), once, where its body is read (`pp_obj_paste/3` in `pp_macro_/6`): `#define AB a ## b` is `ab`, and the
  standard's `#define hash_hash # ## #` the one token `##`; the reader met the three tokens. A `##` THAT AN ARGUMENT
  BRINGS IS NO OPERATOR (6.10.3.3/3, "not from an argument"): an argument's tokens are `h/2` elements in the body's
  form, and `pp_paste/2` takes a bare `##`, a body's own; it pasted every `##`, so `XS(AB2)` over `#define AB2 x ## 1 ##
  y` was `21y` with `x` a macro (`x1y`); the standard's `join(x, y)` over `hash_hash` gave its `"x ## y"` only as the
  two defects met, an argument's `##` pasting the two `#` that the body had left. `ppexample.c`, `ppexample.cpp`.
  (0.210)
- A BODY'S `%:%:` AND `%:` ARE ITS OPERATORS `##` AND `#` (C17 6.4.6/3, [lex.digraph]/2; 0.211; `pp_body_ops/3` in
  `pp_macro_/6`), `%:` in a function-like macro's body, where `#` is the stringizing operator; an object-like macro's
  `%:` and a text line's are digraphs, spelled as written: `#define HH %: %:%: %:` pastes the one token `%:%:`, and the
  standard's `join(x, y)` over it is `"x %:%: y"`, as clang and gcc give. `test/c/run/spelling.c`. (0.211)
- `__VA_OPT__` ASKS THE VARIADIC ARGUMENT AFTER ITS EXPANSION (the examples of C23 6.10.5.1 and [cpp.subst]; 0.210;
  `pp_va_present/1`): `F(EMP)` over `F(...) f(0 __VA_OPT__(,) __VA_ARGS__)` with `EMP` empty is `f(0)`, where the
  argument as written gave `f(0 , )`; one that holds no name is not expanded for the question. `test/c/run/ppvaopt.c`
  (C23), `test/cpp/run/ppexample.cpp`. (0.210)
- `#x` KEEPS A SPACE ONLY WHERE WHITE SPACE STOOD between two of its argument's tokens, none before the first or after
  the last (C17 6.10.3.2/2, [cpp.stringize]/2; 0.209; `pp_stringize/2` over `pp_spell_marked/2`). The mark rides in the
  stream: a text line's token that white space precedes is `h(T, ['$sp'])` (the Lexers topic), a macro body's token
  holds it in its line, 1 or 0 (`pp_lex_mbody/2`: a body's tokens take the invocation's line from `pp_wrap/6`), and an
  expansion's token has `'$sp'` at its hide set's head, which no macro is named. The rules are clang's and gcc's, which
  agree on each but one: an expansion's first token takes the white space before the macro's name, each other its own
  (`pp_wrap/6`); an argument's first token takes the white space before its parameter, each other its own, through the
  argument's expansion too (`pp_reline_marks/3`, `pp_expand_marked/2`, `pp_toks/6`'s mode `marks`); an expansion of
  nothing passes the name's white space to the token after it (`a E+b` with `E` empty is `"a +b"`; `pp_push/4`), an
  empty argument its parameter's (`spmark`), and an empty `__VA_OPT__` its own; a `__VA_OPT__` group's first token takes
  the white space before `__VA_OPT__` or keeps its own, as clang does, where gcc gives it the former alone (the one:
  `V(1, 2)` over `S(a+__VA_OPT__( x))` is clang's `"1+ x"`, gcc's `"1+x"`); a variadic argument's commas are the ones
  the invocation wrote (`pp_args/10` keeps them apart, `pp_join_commas/3`). Every two tokens were a space apart:
  `S(a+b)` was `"a + b"` and `S(f(1,2))` `"f ( 1 , 2 )"`. C++20's and C23's `#__VA_OPT__(...)` is the substituted and
  pasted group stringized, `""` where the variadic arguments have no token; it was a `#` and the group. A LITERAL IN THE
  ARGUMENT IS SPELLED WITH ITS ESCAPES ONCE (`pp_escape/4`, the one escaper of `#x`, `##`, a directive's text and `-E`):
  `S("x y")` printed `\"x y\"`, its text escaped a second time, and a tab, a character constant's quote and a control
  character were spelled raw. A literal is spelled as written (0.211; the Lexers topic): `"\x41"` is `"\x41"`, each
  quote and `\` of it escaped once, where it was spelled from its value, `"A"`. A `\` of no literal (a character that
  begins no token, the Lexers topic) begins an escape of the string made: the argument's text, a literal's quote and `\`
  escaped, is read back as a string's body (`pp_str_decode/3`; 0.210), so the standard's `str(: @\n)` is `": @"` and a
  new-line. What the marks cost is below the box's noise: alternating rounds of a cold `<map>` at C++20 (`cicilang++
  -fsyntax-only`, a fresh HOME each, four rounds) took 31.0 s of CPU at the least and 33.6 s at the median with 0.208's
  library, 31.8 s and 33.4 s with 0.209's and 32.4 s and 33.6 s with 0.210's; 0.210's record of about 4 %, one library's
  reads after the other's, measured the box's drift (0.211). `test/c/run/stringize.c`, `stringize2.c`, `stringizeva.c`
  and `stringizevo.c` (C23), `test/cpp/run/stringize.cpp` (C++20). (0.209, 0.210, 0.211)
- `#x` MAKES A STRING'S BYTES FROM ITS SPELLING'S CHARACTERS (0.211): the string is the UTF-8 of the spelling
  (`pp_utf8_bytes/2` in `pp_stringize/2`), and a narrow literal's bytes are spelled as the characters their UTF-8
  sequences are, a byte of none `\NNN` (`pp_escape_utf8/5`, `pp_utf8_tail/5`, in `pp_escape/4`'s `raw` mode), so
  `S(café)`, `S("café")` and `XS(S(café))` hold the bytes of `café`, where the name's `é` was one byte, 0xE9, and
  clang's two. `__FILE__` is a string's bytes too (`ccl_atom_bytes/2`): a `#line` name past ASCII was one byte a
  character. `test/c/run/spelling.c`. (0.211)
- `#if` (`pp_eval/1`): `defined` and the built-ins (`pp_defined_pass/2`), the expansion, the built-ins again; a name
  left is 0 and `true` 1 (`pp_normalize`); then `ccl_cond_expr//1` and `ccl_const_eval/2`. What does not evaluate is
  false. The evaluation is C's `#if` arithmetic (C 6.10.1/4): `pp_eval_/1` sets `'$ccl_cv_pp'` around it, and every
  unsigned operation is done in `uintmax_t`, 64 bits (`ccl_cv_width/2`), so `#if ~0u == 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF` holds; the
  global is put back on success, failure and throw. `test/c/run/unsignedconst.c`. An int there is an `intmax_t` (C
  6.10.1/4, [cpp.cond]/12; 0.201): a hex, octal or binary literal with no `u` that the lexers make an unsigned int past
  INT_MAX (the Integer literals topic) is signed in `#if` (`pp_normalize/2`), as clang evaluates `#if 0x80000000 > -1`.
  `pp_norm/2` puts the lexer's mode back before its answer meets the caller's: a bound answer that did not unify left
  the mode `line` behind it. `littype.c`. (M5, 0.128, 0.201)
- Built-ins (`pp_builtin_answer/3`): `__has_include(_next)` resolve for real (`ccl_resolve_include/3`), their operand
  and `__has_embed`'s macro-replaced where it begins with no header name (C23 6.10.1/4's second form, [cpp.cond]/4;
  `pp_has_args/2`, 0.211: `__has_include(INC)` was 0); `__has_builtin` and `__is_identifier` 1 (libc++'s other branch is
  an `#error`), but `__has_builtin(__builtin_common_type)` 0 (`pp_no_builtin/1`, a table of the builtins this compiler
  does not model: libc++ 21 then flattens `common_type` on its own specializations, the ones libc++ 18 has, and not on
  clang's builtin class template; reader 118; 0.126), and `__has_builtin(__builtin_clear_padding)` 0 (0.194), GCC's,
  which no clang of 18, 21 and 22 has: libc++ 21's atomic_ref then clears no padding and compares the whole object, the
  branch clang++'s build takes; `__has_embed` 1 found, 2 empty, 0 nowhere; `__has_c_attribute` (C only) the standard
  attributes' dates (`pp_c_attribute/2`), and `__has_cpp_attribute` (C++ only) its standard attributes' values, clang
  21's at every level (`pp_cpp_attribute/2`, 0.198: `nodiscard` 201907, `no_unique_address` 201803 ...), a scoped one 0
  -- it was 0 for every attribute, and libc++ 18 laid out its algorithm results, its views, `shared_ptr`'s array control
  blocks and its format buffers without `[[no_unique_address]]`: `sizeof(std::ranges::in_in_result<E, int>)` 8 where
  clang++'s build has 4 (`nualayout.cpp`; the Object layout topic's empty data member is the rest of it); these
  questions and `__has_builtin`, `__has_feature` and kin are answered in a text line too (`pp_text_builtin/1`, 0.198),
  as clang answers them (`hascppattr.cpp`: the name was undeclared); `__is_target_arch`, `_vendor`, `_os`,
  `_environment` per host; every other `__has_*` 0, the plainest path, the one the reader reads best. (0.93, 0.198,
  0.211)
- A SCOPED ATTRIBUTE IS ANSWERED BY ITS VENDOR'S LIST (0.205; `pp_cpp_attr_value/2`, `pp_attr_vendor/2`,
  `pp_vendor_attribute/2`): `__has_cpp_attribute(gnu::N)` and `__has_cpp_attribute(clang::N)` -- `__gnu__::` and
  `_Clang::` too, the spellings libc++ writes, the name with or without its underscores, and `__has_c_attribute(gnu::N)`
  in C -- answer 1 for an attribute the compiler honours in that spelling (gnu's `packed` and `aligned`, the C reader's
  topic of GCC's attributes) or that changes nothing a program can see (gnu's `always_inline`, `noinline`, `cold`,
  `hot`, `deprecated`, `format`, `nonnull`, `pure`, `const`, `noreturn`, `malloc`, `nothrow`, `fallthrough`, `may_alias`
  ...; clang's `lifetimebound`, `preferred_name`, `no_specializations`, `standalone_debug`, the capability attributes,
  `ptrauth_vtable_pointer`, `fallthrough`, `assume` ...), as clang 21 answers them, and 0 for one that would change a
  layout, a linkage or a call that this compiler does not model from that spelling (gnu's `vector_size`, `weak`,
  `section`, `constructor`, `cleanup`, `used`, `visibility`; clang's `trivial_abi`, `no_destroy`, `musttail`,
  `internal_linkage`), where clang answers 1, since a program asks such an attribute to build otherwise. Each scoped one
  was 0, so a program and a header took the branch no clang build takes: libc++ 21 asks `_Clang::__lifetimebound__`,
  `__preferred_name__`, `__no_specializations__` and the capabilities, and writes them into its declarations, which the
  reader drops; `__no_destroy__` stays its fallback. `protoreq.cpp`, `vendorattr.cpp` (C++20), `gnuattr.cpp`,
  `test/c/run/gnuattrc.c` (C23).

### The predefined macros

- The predefined macros are `pp_predef(Name, Table, Text)` facts, from the reference compiler's `-dM -E` per level,
  answered BY NAME on a miss (`pp_predef_macro/3`), never defined in bulk. Why: defining them cost 25 ms a run. (M5)
- The order: the level's table (C++ `pp_std_table/2`: `cpp26`, `cpp23`, `cpp20`, newest first; C `pp_c_std_table/2`:
  `c23`, then its OS's own, `c23_linux` or `c23_darwin`, `pp_c_os_table/2`, 0.194), the TARGET's own
  (`pp_target_table/1`, `<os>_<arch>`, 0.131), `any`, the OS (`pp_os/1`), the arch (`pp_arch/1`), C++'s `cpp_rtti` and

  and `unsigned int`, the quad's `__LDBL_*`, `__SIZEOF_LONG_DOUBLE__` 16, `__BIGGEST_ALIGNMENT__` 16, the generic
  armv8's features, and `'$undef'`, no macro, for Apple's names (`__arm64__`, `__ARM_NEON__`, the M1's

  `<inttypes.h>`'s binary formats are predefined as clang 22 has them; `__FLT_EVAL_METHOD__` is 0. A header's
  `__STDC_VERSION_*_H__` is the header's own (C23 7.x.1: `<stddef.h>`, `<limits.h>`, `<stdarg.h>`, `<float.h>`,

- The OS and the arch are the HOST's -- the module's compile-time `ccl_host_os/1`, `ccl_host_arch/1` (`uname` only
