### Configuration chosen through the macros

- EXCEPTIONS IN libc++, AS clang++ HAS THEM (0.193, the owner's decision of 0.190): `__cpp_exceptions` and
  `__EXCEPTIONS` are the predefined table `cpp_eh`'s, which `pp_predef_macro/3` asks in C++ unless the build says
  `-fno-exceptions` (`'$ccl_exceptions'` = `no`, set by `dr_setup/2`); libc++ then builds its exceptions configuration:
  what its headers throw is thrown (`__throw_out_of_range` ...), its try blocks are there, and a vector grows through
  `std::move_if_noexcept`, copying an element whose move constructor may throw where it has a copy (the nothrow traits,
  the Traits answered topic). `-fno-exceptions` gives the no-exceptions configuration this compiler built from 0.50 to
  0.192 (when nothing here unwound), where a throw in libc++'s headers' code aborts with a message and a vector moves
  every element (`noexcgrow.cpp`); under it the program's own `throw` and `try` are refused,
  `throw_requires_exceptions` and `try_requires_exceptions` (`cpp_eh_needed/1`), as clang++ `-fno-exceptions` refuses
  them (`cannot use 'throw' with exceptions disabled`), never in a header's code nor the desugaring's own terminate
  guard. A C++ summary read under it is keyed apart (`@no-exceptions`, `ccl_config_key/1`, the C++ summary cache).
  (0.50, 0.108, 0.190, 0.193)
- RTTI IN libc++, AS clang++ HAS IT (0.191, the owner's decision of 0.190): `__cpp_rtti` and `__GXX_RTTI` are the
  predefined table `cpp_rtti`'s, which `pp_predef_macro/3` asks in C++ unless the build says `-fno-rtti`
  (`'$ccl_rtti'` = `no`, set by `dr_setup/2`); libc++ then decides `_LIBCPP_HAS_RTTI` as clang++'s build does.
  `std::any::type()`, `std::function::target_type()` and `target<T>()`, `std::get_deleter` and the `any_cast` that
  compares type information run (`rttilib.cpp`). `-fno-rtti` gives libc++'s no-RTTI configuration, which this compiler
  built from 0.86 to 0.190 (nothing here made a `type_info` then): `any`, `exception_ptr`, `shared_ptr` and `function`
  change, the vtables do not, so the control blocks lay out as the shipped library's either way (`nortti.cpp`). Under it
  `typeid` and a `dynamic_cast` that asks the type information -- a downcast, a cross-cast -- are refused,
  `typeid_requires_rtti` and `dynamic_cast_requires_rtti` (`cpp_rtti_needed/1`), as clang++ `-fno-rtti` refuses them
  (`use of typeid requires -frtti`), in a header's code too: libc++ leaves `std::dynamic_pointer_cast` unguarded, and
  clang++ `-fno-rtti` refuses it where a program calls it; a cast to a base, `dynamic_cast<void *>` and the exceptions
  need none. A C++ summary read under `-fno-rtti` is keyed apart (`ccl_config_key/1`, the C++ summary cache).
  (0.86, 0.108, 0.190, 0.191)
- `__OPTIMIZE_SIZE__` IS NOT PREDEFINED (0.162), as clang predefines it only at `-Os` and `-Oz`: libc++ 21 compiles
  its VECTORIZED algorithms behind `_LIBCPP_HAS_ALGORITHM_VECTOR_UTILS && !defined(__OPTIMIZE_SIZE__)` (`mismatch`, and
  through it `lexicographical_compare` and so a vector's `operator<`): `__simd_vector<_Tp, _Np>`, an `ext_vector_type`
  alias template, `__load_vector`'s braced vector from a pack, `__all_of` and `__find_first_set` over a bool vector and
  `__builtin_bit_cast`. From 0.92 to 0.161 it was predefined in C++ to keep that road off, since nothing here read a
  vector type (the Vector types topic of the lowering). libc++ 18 reads it nowhere. `mismatchvec.cpp` (C++17: libc++ 21
  takes the road from C++14 on). (0.92, 0.162)
- 128-BIT INTEGERS IN BOTH LANGUAGES: `__SIZEOF_INT128__` is predefined in C and in C++ (16; `pp_predef(..., any,
  '16')`, 0.129), so libc++ builds its int128 configuration: `is_integral<__int128>`, `make_unsigned`,
  `numeric_limits<__int128>`, `to_chars` and `from_chars` in 128 bits, `std::hash<__int128>`, `std::format` of one.
  From 0.112 to 0.128 C++ went without the macro, and libc++ in its `_LIBCPP_HAS_NO_INT128` configuration: its
  `__basic_format_arg_value` holds an `__int128_t` member, which nothing typed before `__int128` lowered (0.117). The
  configuration found three defects, mended in 0.129: a conditional over bit builtins had no type, a folded constant past
  64 bits was cut to 64, and every explicit specialization of a function template was ignored (each in its topic).
  Reader 124. `int128lib.cpp`, `int128fmt.cpp` (C++20). (0.112, 0.117, 0.129)
- `__has_extension(c_atomic)` and `__has_extension(datasizeof)` (0.112) answer 1, the two extensions answered
  (`pp_builtin_answer`; the second makes libc++ 18 take `__datasizeof(T)`, folded by the desugaring);
  `__has_feature(cxx_atomic)` and `__has_keyword(_Atomic)` stay 0. libc++ 18 then defines `_LIBCPP_HAS_C_ATOMIC_IMP`,
  declares `memory_order` and builds `<atomic>` on `_Atomic(T)` and `__c11_atomic_*`. `__ATOMIC_RELAXED` 0 to
  `__ATOMIC_SEQ_CST` 5 are clang's numbering. `test/cpp/run/stdatomic.cpp`. Why: with all three at 0 no implementation
  was defined. (0.100)
- The table is clang-shaped (`__clang__` 1) while `__has_feature` answers 0, so glibc's `sys/cdefs.h` takes a branch
  neither compiler takes. (0.87) `__HAS_ATTRIBUTE(x)` ANSWERS 1 FOR A GNU ATTRIBUTE THE READER RECOGNIZES IN THE
  `__attribute__((x))` FORM (0.221; `pp_gnu_attribute/1`): one it honours -- `packed`, `aligned`, `vector_size`,
  `ext_vector_type` -- and one whose meaning is a diagnostic, an optimization's hint or the debug information, which
  reading and dropping implements (the `gnu` list of `__has_cpp_attribute`, 0.205), with or without its underscores; 0
  for any other, `weak`, `section`, `constructor`, `cleanup`, `visibility` and `nodebug` among them, which clang answers
  1 and the reader drops. It was 0 for every attribute: a program's `#if __has_attribute(packed)` laid its struct
  unpacked, 8 bytes for clang's 5 (`hasattr.c`), and libc++ wrote no `_LIBCPP_PACKED`, `_LIBCPP_NOALIAS`,
  `_LIBCPP_NOINLINE` or `__attribute__((__deprecated__))`, which clang++'s build writes; std::string's size words and
  the stream's fill over the new roads lay as clang's (`libattr.cpp`, over libc++ 18 and 21). glibc's `__COLD`,
  `__returns_nonnull` and `__attribute_artificial__` take their attributes too. (0.87, 0.221)
- With `__has_builtin` 1, glibc's `<math.h>` writes `INFINITY`, `NAN`, `HUGE_VAL`, `isnan` and kin on `__builtin_*`,
  which the lowering answers. `test/c/run/complex2.c`. (0.101)
- `_FORTIFY_SOURCE` is 0, so `strcpy` stays a function, not `__builtin___strcpy_chk`. (M5)

### The user's file and the headers' macros

- `ccl_pp_top/3` (from `ccl_read_file_/3`) runs the user's file in TOP mode (`'$pp_top'`). A `#define` or `#undef` is
  done AND passed on as `tok(pp, Text, L)` (`pp_pass/4`). An `#include` is passed on for the parser (a cached unit, a
  `.pl` macro file, or `missing`), and its header joins `'$pp_hdrs'`, the last first. A `#cocolog ... #end` block is one
  `tok(cocolog, Text, L)` of the raw lines, read again from the file (`pp_cocolog_block/5`). The groups are decided, and
  every macro is expanded. A character that begins no token and reaches the reader throws `lexical(L)` at its line
  (0.210: a line that did not lex whole threw it, a character that `#` took among them; the Lexers topic). Reader `k86`,
  `k71`; `test/c/run/macros.c`, `test/c/run/pp.c`. (M5, 0.210)
- A run is not re-entrant, so `ccl_pp_prescan/1` first sends each literal `#include`, and each C++ header-unit `import`,
  to `ccl_header_macros_ready/2` (the header by `ccl_include_read/2`, then `ccl_header_macros/2`). The table's kind is
  memoized per level in `'$ccl_hm:<Path>@<Level>'` (`ccl_hm_key/2` over `ccl_read_level/1`, `t` appended with trigraphs
  and `i` in an ISO mode, 0.214). (0.99, 0.110, 0.214)
- A COMPUTED `#include` IN THE USER'S FILE (C17 6.10.2/4; 0.211) is passed on with the name it resolved to
  (`pp_inc_text/4`), since the reader reads no name from `#include INC`: the header's declarations were lost with its
  macros. The prescan knows no computed name, so the macros of a header that one names and that the prescan did not make
  ready are made ready after the run, and the file is run again, once for each such header new to the file
  (`ccl_pp_top_run/4` over `'$pp_late'`, which `pp_do_include/6` fills and `pp_reset/0` empties; `pp_new_specs/3`).
  `test/c/run/ppinclude.c`, `test/cpp/run/ppinclude.cpp`: a local header and a library header named by a macro. (0.211)
- THE PROGRAM'S FEATURE-TEST MACROS CONFIGURE EVERY HEADER'S READ (0.214, 0.215; POSIX 2.2.1, glibc's `features.h`): a
  name of `pp_ftm_name/1`'s that the user's file, or a local header it includes, defines or undefines is read by every
  header as a `-D` or a `-U` is: `'$pp_ftm'`, a list of `N-def(Params, Codes)` and `N-undef` where they differ from the
  predefined macros and the command line's (`pp_ftm_state/1`), which a header's run asks before the command line's
  (`pp_outer_macro/3`; the user's file's own run defines them itself), which every key of a read folds (`ccl_ftm_tag/1`
  in `ccl_read_level/1` and `ccl_sum_file/2`: the unit cache, the header macros' memo, the store, the C++ summaries'
  names), and which the processes for cold headers are given (`ftm(L)`, `dr_setup/2`). A NAME COUNTS WHERE CLANG'S
  HEADERS READ IT (0.215): glibc's and POSIX's feature-test macros and Apple's (`pp_ftm_fixed/1`: `_GNU_SOURCE`,
  `_DEFAULT_SOURCE`, `_POSIX_C_SOURCE`, `_XOPEN_SOURCE`, `_FILE_OFFSET_BITS` and kin) as they stand at the file's first
  `#include` of a header that reads the C library, since glibc reads `features.h` once (`pp_spec_clib/1`: in C every
  system header but those of clang's that read none of it, `<stddef.h>`, `<stdarg.h>`, `<stdbool.h>`, `<float.h>`,
  `<iso646.h>`, `<stdalign.h>`, `<stdnoreturn.h>` and `<stdckdint.h>`, `pp_ftm_free_header/1` -- clang's `<stdatomic.h>`
  reads `<stdint.h>` and `<stdbit.h>` is glibc's --; in C++ every one, libc++'s `__config` reading `features.h`); every
  `__STDC_WANT_*` and `_LIBCPP_*` name (`pp_ftm_each/1`) as it stands at the file's last system `#include`, since
  glibc's headers ask `__STDC_WANT_*` at each inclusion (`bits/libc-header-start.h`) and libc++'s their own
  `_LIBCPP_ENABLE_*` names. The first are found before the read (`pp_ftm_find/1`, from `ccl_read_file/3`, so the store's
  key of the file is the right one) by one run of the file that stops at that `#include` (`pp_do_include/6` through
  `pp_ftm_at_include/1` throws `pp_prologue(State)`), or at its end where it has none; a file whose lines before it
  define none of the names and include no local header is not run (`pp_prologue_scan/3`, which reads past `#include
  <stdarg.h>` and kin). The others are what the top run found at its last system `#include` (`pp_ftm_at_include/1`,
  `pp_ftm_result/1`): the file's own `#define` and `#undef` of them (`'$pp_ftm_defs'`, `pp_ftm_note/1`), and the nine
  `__STDC_WANT_*` names that glibc asks wherever they are defined, a local header among them (`pp_ftm_want/1`:
  autoconf's `config.h` defines them, and no system header does, where libc++'s define `_LIBCPP_*` names); where they
  differ from what the headers were read under, the file is run again under them, its headers made ready again
  (`ccl_pp_top_run/4`, twice at most). It is one configuration for the file: a header included before such a definition
  is read under it too, where clang's is not. A header was read standalone under the predefined macros alone until
  0.214: under `-std=c17` `#define _POSIX_C_SOURCE 200809L` gave no `strdup`, and `hdrdefs.c`'s `#define
  _DEFAULT_SOURCE` no `htobe32`; and until 0.215 a name defined after the file's first system `#include` configured no
  header's read, a `__STDC_WANT_*` name and a name after `<stdarg.h>` among them. `ftmacro.c` (`-std=c17`, over
  `ftmacro.h`), `ftlate.c` (`-std=c17`). (0.214, 0.215)
- `<assert.h>` DEFINES `assert` BY `NDEBUG` AS IT STANDS AT EACH INCLUSION (C17 7.2/1, [cassert.syn]; 0.214;
  `pp_assert_include/1`): in the user's file an `#include <assert.h>` or `<cassert>` defines `assert` as `((void)0)`
  where `NDEBUG` is defined, glibc's `assert_perror` with it, and else as the header's table has it, which is read with
  no `NDEBUG` (no name of `pp_ftm_name/1`'s). The table alone answered: `#define NDEBUG` before the include still
  asserted, in 0.213 and before it. An inclusion through another header asks no `NDEBUG`. UNDER `-DNDEBUG` THE HEADER'S
  OWN READ SEES NO `NDEBUG` (0.221; `pp_ndebug_hidden/1` in `pp_outer_macro`: in the run whose first file is
  `<assert.h>` or `<cassert>` the command line's `NDEBUG` is no macro), so its table holds the asserting `assert`, and
  an `#undef NDEBUG` before the include asserts again, as clang's build does: it left the program's assertions out.
  `ndebug.c`, `ndebug.cpp`, the driver gate's `-DNDEBUG` check. (0.214, 0.221)
- A header's macro reaches the run BY NAME on first use (`pp_macro/3`, `pp_defined/1`). The run's own `'$pp:<Name>'`
  comes first; a miss is kept until the next include (`'$pp_ninc'`). Then `pp_outer_macro/3` asks the predefined
  macros (no header redefines one), then the headers, the last included first (`pp_header_macro/3`). Why:
  `<stdio.h>` brings 1200 macros, and a file uses a dozen. (M5)
- No table is parsed whole. `indexed` (C++): the `.mac` file beside the summary, `mnames([...])` lines of up to a
  hundred names, then `macro(N, Ps, text(A))` lines as written; `ccl_mac_lines/3` splits it, `ccl_hml_assert/3`
  asserts `'$ccl_hml'(Name, Path, raw(Line))`, and `pp_raw_macro/4` parses a line into a fresh term when asked.
  `store(Key)` (C): rows `'$ccl_hmacros:<Path>'(Name, Key, macro(...))` (`ccl_kb_macro/5`), a row per closure file
  under `'$dep'`, the index `'$ccl_hmeta'(Path, Key, meta(N, ND))` (`ccl_kb_macros_cached/2`). `list`: a table the
  store refused, in `'$ccl_hmlist:<Path>'`. (M5)
- `ccl_kb_remember_macros/3` replaces only this level's rows. Why: a C23 read retracted the C17 rows, and `macros.c`
  met `undeclared(EOF)` in the gate's order. (0.99)
- A table that no cache holds comes from one standalone run (`ccl_pp_file/3`, `ccl_pp_macros/1`), once per store; a
  header read preprocessed by `ccl_read_unit/3` stores its macros then. (M5)
- A C++ header unit's macros are the importer's ([module.import]/5): `pp_import_line/2` catches `import "h";`, `import
  <h>;` and `export import ...`; the macros are visible after the line, and the line goes on to the reader.
  `test/cpp/run/headerunit.cpp`. (0.110)

### The flattened text (`-E`)

- `cicilang++ -E f.cpp -o flat.cpp` (`dr_preprocess`) runs `ccl_pp_file/3` and spells the tokens back by
  `ccl_pp_spell/2`. A space separates two tokens, a newline comes where the line changes, and at most three blank lines
  stand for skipped lines. A literal is spelled by `pp_escape/4`, the escaper of `#x` (the Macro expansion topic): `\"`
  in a string, `\'` in a character constant, `\\`, `\n`, `\t`, `\r`, `\a`, `\b`, `\f`, `\v`, `\0` where no octal digit
  follows, `\NNN` for another control character and past ASCII below 256, `\u{...}` above (0.209: `\'` was escaped in a
  string too, and the other control characters were `\NNN`). Why: the census reads the flattened text. (0.44, 0.209)
- Every token spells back as the reader takes it (`ccl_pp_spell_tok/4`, `pp_spell/2`), a character that begins no token
  as itself (0.210); a literal, a digraph and an alternative token spelled as written are the reader's tokens by then
  (`pp_finish/2`; 0.211). The suffixes stay: `u`, `l`, `ul`, `wb`, `uwb`, `f`, `L`, and the imaginary `i`, `if`, `ui`,
  `li`, `uli` (`pp_imag_suffix/2`). A literal keeps its prefix (`pp_str_prefix/2`). A literal past 2^60 spells as its
  digits (`pp_int_codes/2`). A float spells as the fewest digits that read back as the same double, cocolog 1.10.28's
  writer, and an infinite one as `1e999` (`pp_float_codes/2`; 0.143): every float past 1.0e308 was `1e999`, so
  `__DBL_MAX__` and `1.5e308` became infinities, and a float of 16 or 17 digits came back another double. A long double
  literal spells as its text and its suffix (0.154: `L`, an imaginary one `il`), where it spelled the double it held
  (`__LDBL_MAX__` was `1.7976931348623157e308L`). A `#cocolog` block spells whole. The driver gate compiles the text
  with clang, a line of long double literals among it (0.154). (0.108, 0.143, 0.154)

### The compiler's own headers

- **Nothing of the standard library is the compiler's own** (owner's rule): the C freestanding headers in
  `library/include` are the one exception; C++ compiles against libc++ as it is. (0.41)
- They sit in each `$COCOLOG_LIBRARY` directory plus `/include` (`ccl_own_include_dirs/1`): after libc++'s tree in C++,
  before `/usr/local/include` and the system's headers. The guard is `_CICILANG_<NAME>_H` (`__CCL_STDATOMIC_H`). (M2)
- `stddef.h`: LP64's `size_t`, `ptrdiff_t`, `wchar_t` (C only), `max_align_t`, `NULL` as `((void *)0)` in both
  languages (C++'s `NULL` reads as C's cast), `offsetof` over `__builtin_offsetof`; at C23 `nullptr_t` and
  `unreachable()`. It CLEARS A REQUEST of one piece, glibc's `#define __need_size_t` before `#include <stddef.h>` and
  the others clang's header names, on every inclusion, as clang's header clears it (0.179): left defined, it made every
  later inclusion one more request, which libc++ 18's `<stddef.h>` answers by `#include_next` alone -- so at C++23,
  whose headers include `<cstddef>` after a C header, `::nullptr_t` was never declared, `<cstddef>` stopped at its
  `#error` and a read stopped at its first `nullptr_t`: `<complex>` at `unique_ptr<T[]>::reset`, its literal operators
  lost (a partial read is silent). libc++ 21's `<stddef.h>` reads no request. `complexlit.cpp`. (0.93, 0.179)
- `stdarg.h`: `va_list` is `__builtin_va_list`, `va_start`, `va_arg`, `va_end`, `va_copy` the builtins; glibc's
  `__need___va_list` gets `__gnuc_va_list` alone, as from clang's header. `test/c/run/varargs.c`. (0.108)
- `limits.h` defines `_GCC_LIMITS_H_` and the limits from the predefined macros (`__INT_MAX__` and kin, the widths at
  C23, `__INT_WIDTH__` and kin since 0.194, and C23's `__STDC_VERSION_LIMITS_H__`), then takes the C library's own
  `limits.h` by `#include_next` where there is one. Why: glibc asks the compiler's header for them, so `INT_MAX` was
  undefined on Linux. (0.93, 0.194)
- `float.h` (from the predefined macros), `stdbool.h` and `iso646.h` (C only), `stdalign.h`, `stdnoreturn.h`. (M2)
  `stdbool.h` defines `bool`, `true` and `false` before C23 alone (0.214; C23 7.18: they are keywords there, as in
  clang's and gcc's headers; `true` was the int 1, `c23bool.c`). `float.h` holds C11's limits too, under clang's guard
  (0.154): `FLT_TRUE_MIN`, `DBL_TRUE_MIN`, `LDBL_TRUE_MIN`, the three `_DECIMAL_DIG` and the three `_HAS_SUBNORM`, and
  C99's `DECIMAL_DIG`; `LDBL_TRUE_MIN` was undefined. Since 0.194 `FLT_ROUNDS` is the CURRENT rounding direction,
  `__builtin_flt_rounds()` (LLVM's `llvm.get.rounding`, which `fesetround` moves; it was 1), `FLT_EVAL_METHOD` is
  `__FLT_EVAL_METHOD__`, and C23's own come under clang's guards: `FLT_SNAN`, `DBL_SNAN` and `LDBL_SNAN` over
  `__builtin_nans*` (a signaling NaN, the Lowering's floating constants), `FLT_NORM_MAX` and kin, `*_IS_IEC_60559`,
  `__STDC_VERSION_FLOAT_H__`, and `INFINITY` and `NAN`, which `<math.h>` defines too (taken away first, as clang's and
  gcc's headers do). IN C++ THEY COME BY THE LEVEL ALONE, never by the mode (0.214): C++26's `<cfloat>` is C23's
  `<float.h>` without the normalized maxima and the conformance -- `__STDC_VERSION_FLOAT_H__`, `INFINITY`, `NAN` and the
  signaling NaNs (P3348R4, [cfloat.syn]) -- and C++17's to C++23's is C17's, in both modes, as clang 18 and gcc have it;
  clang 21's `gnu++` modes add the normalized maxima. Why: a C++ read is one for both modes (the C++ summary cache
  topic), and clang's guard asks `__STRICT_ANSI__`, which gave C23's names to every C++ level. `cfloat26.cpp`
  (`-std=c++26`, its reference clang++ over the four names defined on its command line). `stdarg.h` and `stdatomic.h`
  define their own `__STDC_VERSION_*_H__` at C23, and `stdatomic.h` `atomic_char8_t` and `ATOMIC_CHAR8_T_LOCK_FREE`, and
  no `ATOMIC_VAR_INIT` in C23, which removed it. `c23float.c` (`-std=c23`).
- `stdckdint.h` (C23 7.20): `ckd_add`, `ckd_sub`, `ckd_mul` over `__builtin_*_overflow`. `stdbit.h` (C23 7.18): the
  suffixed functions over the bit builtins, the generic forms through `_Generic`. (0.93)
- `stdatomic.h` (C11 7.17) over the `__c11_atomic_*` builtins, as clang's: the `atomic_*` typedefs through `_Atomic(T)`,
  `memory_order` over `__ATOMIC_*`, `atomic_flag`, every function and its `_explicit` form. `test/c/run/atomic.c`.
  Why: glibc has none, and clang's lives in a resource directory off the path. (0.99)
- `complex.h`: the C library's declarations by `#include_next`, then `_Complex_I`, `I`, `CMPLX`, `CMPLXF`, `CMPLXL`
  over `__builtin_complex`; `CMPLXL` casts to `long double` (0.112: it cast to `double`, and `long double` is x86_fp80).
  Why: glibc defines `CMPLX` for GCC only. `test/c/run/complex.c`, `complex4.c`. (0.100, 0.112)
- `tgmath.h` (C17 7.25; 0.194): the type-generic macros over the C library's `<math.h>` and `<complex.h>`, the set
  clang's own header defines, chosen by `_Generic` (`__TG_P`, `__TG_R`, `__TG_C`, `__TG_X`): an integer argument counts
  as a double, several generic arguments by the type their sum has, a complex one by the complex function, `carg`,
  `cimag`, `conj`, `cproj` and `creal` for a real argument too; `frexp`, `ldexp`, `scalbn`, `scalbln` and `nexttoward`
  generic in their first argument. Why it is the compiler's own, as `stdatomic.h` is: glibc's `<tgmath.h>` refuses a
  compiler with clang's macros at its `#error "Unsupported combination of types for <tgmath.h>."` (`__HAVE_FLOAT64X`
  without `__HAVE_FLOAT128`), which stopped the header silently -- `sqrt(z)` of a complex called the real `sqrt` over
  its real part -- and clang's lives in a resource directory off the path. In C++ libc++'s `<tgmath.h>` comes first.
  `tgmath.c`.

## The C reader and the language's own forms

### The reader's door and the item loop

- `cicilang_ast(+File, -AST)` mirrors `phrase/2`: the whole file, else `error(syntax_error(cicilang_ast(File, line(L),
  near(Far))), _)`, L where the unread tokens start, Far the farthest line reached. `cicilang_ast/3` mirrors `phrase/3`.
  A lexical error is `syntax_error(cicilang_ast(File, lexical, line(L)))`. Reader `k69` to `k71`. (M1)
- `ccl_read_file/3` sets the language (`ccl_set_lang/1`), serves the store's read (`ccl_kb_cached/3`), else runs
  `ccl_pp_top/3` and `ccl_unit/3` inside `ccl_with_file/2` and stores a whole read. (M5)
- `ccl_unit/3` seeds the typedef names, resets `'$ccl_far'`, `'$ccl_macros'` and `'$ccl_expansions'`, registers the
  standard macros, empties the tables (`ccl_scope_init`) and reads the items with `ccl_externals//2`. (M1b)
- The item loop parses EACH ITEM inside `\+ \+` (`ccl_externals/4`). The item and the count of the tokens it TOOK
  pass through `'$ccl_item'`, and `ccl_skip/3` recovers the position. Later items get the marker `genv`. A `clang -E`
  line marker `# N "file"` is dropped (`ccl_line_marker/1`). Why: cocolog reclaims the heap on backtracking only.
  (0.46)
- THE COUNT IS THE ITEM'S OWN (0.184; `ccl_item_length/3`): its input walked to the tail its parse left, which `==`
  finds at once (the same cell); a tail the parse made itself, which no walk meets, is counted by the two lengths.
  Until 0.183 the loop took the length of what was LEFT after each item, and of the whole input at each body's start,
  a walk of the rest of the file each: a read was quadratic in its length, and `<thread>`'s flattened text (libc++
  21, 50,720 lines) read 7,523 items at every depth in 1,223 bodies (the file's, the namespaces', the linkage blocks')
  and spent 41 of its 71 s in those 8,746 walks, calls of `length/2`. A cold read of a header's text is 2.8 to 3.4
  times faster, its tree the same, byte for byte: `<vector>` 48.5 s to 17.5 s and C++20's `<iostream>` 82.9 s to
  29.4 s with this alone, `<thread>` 66.7 s to 19.5 s and `<iomanip>` 67.8 s to 20.2 s with the two bounds of
  `sub_atom/5` too (Time and memory). (0.184)
- Every statement carries its line first: `expr(L, E)`, `if(L, C, T, E)`, `return(L, E)`. Reader `k77`. (M1)
- `ccl_p//1`, `ccl_kw//1`, `ccl_id//1` note the farthest line (`ccl_far/1`, `'$ccl_far'`, `ccl_farthest/1`) for the
  error's `near(F)`. (M1)
- A `#define`, `#undef` or `#include` comes from the preprocessor as `tok(pp, Text, L)`, read as the `directive/2` or
  `include/3` item. A `tok(pp, ...)` is skipped in a struct body, between declarators, among enumerators and in a
  block. (M5)

### The expression grammar

- **One rule reads the ten binary levels** (owner's rule, 2026-09-06: a pattern is written once).
  `ccl_binary(Min, E)` climbs precedence over `ccl_binop(Op, Level)`: `||` 1 to `* / %` 10, `<=>` 7.5 (below the
  relational, above the shifts). `ccl_lor` starts at 1, `ccl_shift` at 8 (a template argument's, so `>` closes it).
  Reader `k65`. Why: a cascade of one level per class cost thirty token matches a token; this costs eight. (2026-09-06)
- ONE look chooses the clause: `ccl_unary_(V, K, E)`, `ccl_primary_(K, V, E)`, `ccl_postfix_p(V, A, E)`, value or kind
  first for indexing. The assignment's left is read once, as a conditional expression. A cast's type name is tried once
  (`ccl_cast_expr`); `(T){...}` is `compound_lit/2` (`ccl_cast_rest`). (2026-09-06)
- `({ ... })` is `stmt_expr/1`. `__real__ z` and `__imag__ z` are `real_part/1` and `imag_part/1`; both words stay out
  of the typedef heuristic, so `__real__ z = 5.0;` is a statement. (0.101)
- `_Generic` is chosen AT THE READ (`ccl_generic_pick`). `ccl_type_of/2` types the controlling expression over the
  parser's table; it is decayed and its top-level qualifiers go (DR 481). `ccl_type_canon/2` matches it (typedefs
  resolved, `unsigned` = `unsigned int`, inner qualifiers kept, but the layout's: GCC's `packed` and `aligned`, a
  typedef's `aligned` and a place's alignment say where an object lies, not what it is, `ccl_layout_free/2`, 0.203),
  else `default` is taken. An expression that cannot be typed stays `generic/2`, which the lowering refuses. It is a
  primary, so `_Generic(...)(x)` calls the pick (<stdbit.h>). Reader `k90`. (0.93)
- `_Alignof(T)` and C23's `alignof(T)` are `alignof_type(T)`. GNU'S ALIGNMENT OF AN EXPRESSION, which gcc and clang read
  in C and C++ (`__alignof__ x`, `__alignof(x)`, and `_Alignof(x)` and C++'s `alignof(x)` with a warning), is
  `alignof_expr(E)` (0.205, reader 155; `ccl_alignof_operand//1`): the alignment of the object it names, its `_Alignas`
  among it, else of its type, a `size_t` (`ccl_const_eval/2`); `__alignof__` and `__alignof` are read in C too. It was a
  call of `__alignof__`, undeclared, and a syntax error after `_Alignof`. `alignexpr.c`. (0.93, 0.205)

### Declarators and types

- Declarators are parsed inside out and folded onto the base by `ccl_mk_type/4`, which drops the `constexpr` marker
  (`ccl_constexpr_fold`; a function's result loses its `const` too). (0.95)
- IN C AN ARRAY'S SIZE IS FIXED WHERE IT IS DECLARED (6.7.6.2/5; 0.195): a bound that names a constant -- a named
  constant, an enumerator, a block's `constexpr` -- is folded where the declaration is read, at file scope and in a block
  (`ccl_fix_bounds/2`), and a member's bound and bit-field width too (`ccl_fix_member/4`); a bound that names one of the
  statement's own declarators, or no constant (a VLA's), stays as written. Else a later local of the name named it: `int
  a[N];` under a block's `constexpr int N = 7;` read the inner block's `int N = 2;` at a `sizeof a` there, as the layout of
  `struct S { int a[K]; }` read a shadowing local where it was first asked. C++'s bounds are the desugaring's
  (`cpp_array_bound/2`). `fileconst23.c`.
- `auto a = x, b = y;` (C23 and C++) is one declaration per declarator, each initialized by an ASSIGNMENT-expression and
  deduced alone (`ccl_auto_more//3`, `ccl_auto_next//3`; a `'$splice'/1` in a block and at file scope). The clause
  commits after its `;`, so a form it cannot take (`auto a = 1, *p = &a;`) falls to the general declarators. Else the
  first initializer was read as an EXPRESSION, its comma took the second declarator for a comma expression, and the
  declaration named one variable (`not lowered yet: auto(q)`). `autodecl.cpp`. Why: `auto q = a / b, s = a - b;` over
  `std::complex`, and the idiom `auto it = v.begin(), e = v.end();`. (0.117)
- An init-declarator names what it declares ([dcl.decl]/1): `ccl_init_declarator` refuses an unnamed declarator, so
  `Loop()(1, 2);` is a call. Why: it read as a declaration of nothing initialized by `(1, 2)`, the call was dropped, and
  libc++'s `ranges::copy` copied nothing. `test/cpp/run/tempcallstmt.cpp`. (0.115)
- `ccl_sto_pick/2` picks the deciding storage word. Why: `static inline constexpr` lost `static`. (0.44)
- AN ASM LABEL IS THE SYMBOL A DECLARATION STANDS FOR (0.194; GCC's `asm` labels, which clang reads; 0.214): `int
  f(void) __asm__("g");` and `extern long strtol(...) __asm__ ("" "__isoc23_strtol");` -- string literals alone, joined
  (`ccl_asm_string//1`) -- are noted as the attribute goes past (`'$ccl_asm'`) and taken by the init-declarator
  (`ccl_asm_take/3`) as the qualifier `asm(Name, Sym)` where a tie stands (`ccl_add_asm/4`: through an array to its
  element, through a function to its result). The label names its OWNER: a type taken from the declaration (`auto g =
  strtol(s, 0, 10);`, `__typeof__ (strtol) h;`) carries the qualifier and is no label of the new name (`ccl_asm_of/3`
  matches the name). A name's label comes from ANY of its declarations at file scope, a prototype's being its
  definition's (`ccl_asm_label/2` over the file scope, kept per name in `'$ccl_asm:'`, a named cache with misses), and
  the lowering spells it wherever it spells the name (`ir_gname/3`, `ir_fn_sym/2`: a definition, a declare line, a call,
  an address in a constant). It was dropped: glibc's C23 and GNU redirects were not taken -- `strtol` is
  `__isoc23_strtol` at C23 and in C++ (`_GNU_SOURCE`), which reads a `0b` prefix -- and a program's own label did not
  link. `asm` itself is the label's keyword `__asm__` in a GNU C mode and in every C++ mode, a name of the program's
  under `-std=c17` and `-std=c23`, as clang reads it (0.214, `ccl_asm_keyword/0` in `ccl_attr_word/1`,
  `ccl_gnu_attr_//0` and `ccl_gnu_word/1`): it was a name everywhere, and `int f(void) asm("g");` a syntax error.
  `asmlabel.c`, `asmlabel23.c` (`-std=c23`), `gnusource.cpp`, `gnumode.c`, `gnumode.cpp`.
- GNU'S INLINE ASSEMBLY IS READ (0.215; GCC's manual, How to Use Inline Assembly Language in C Code, which clang reads;
  C17 J.5.10, C++'s asm-declaration [dcl.asm]): at file scope, in a namespace and in a linkage block `asm ( string ) ;`
  is the module's, `gnu_asm_file(L, Text)` (the first clause of `ccl_external//3`, before C++'s leading attributes); in
  a block `asm [volatile] [inline] [goto] ( template [: outputs [: inputs [: clobbers [: labels]]]] ) ;` is a statement
  (`ccl_gnu_asm_stmt//1`, in `ccl_block_item//3` and `ccl_statement//2`): `gnu_asm(L, basic(Text))` where no colon
  follows the template, else `gnu_asm(L, ext(Quals, Text, Outputs, Inputs, Clobbers, Labels))`, an operand `op(Name,
  Constraint, Expr)` with its symbolic name or `none`, and `::` two colons (`ccl_asm_sections//3`). The word is
  `__asm__`, `__asm`, or `asm` where `ccl_asm_keyword/0` makes it one (`ccl_asm_word//0`, which the label's reader
  shares), the text the joined literals (`ccl_asm_text//1`, under `ccl_asm_string//1` too). Both were syntax errors, and
  in C++ a file-scope one was taken for a leading attribute and dropped. Its lowering is the Lowering's topic of inline
  assembly, its check the safe part's What is refused. `gnuasm.c`, `gnuasm.cpp`. (0.215)
- GCC'S `packed` AND `aligned` ATTRIBUTES ARE KEPT (0.203; GCC's manual, Common Type and Variable Attributes, which
  clang reads), noted as the attribute goes past, as `vector_size` is (`ccl_layout_note//0`; `ccl_layout_clear/0` at a
  block's start, at a member list's end and after a parameter), and taken where they stand: on a struct or a union,
  before its name or after its closing brace, the layout markers `packed(1)` -- its members aligned at one, a bitfield
  at the next bit -- and `align_as(E)`, the one `alignas` makes, at the end of its members (`ccl_layout_grab/2`,
  `ccl_align_members/3`); on a member's declarator the qualifiers `packed` and `aligned(E)` on its type, where its
  alignment is read, through an array to its element (`ccl_layout_take/2`); on a variable's declarator `aligned(E)`
  (`ccl_galign_take/2`); on a typedef `taligned(E)`, the alignment of the type it names, lower or higher, as GCC's
  manual has it (`ccl_talign_take/2`, `ccl_typedef_aligns/2`); on an enum the smallest integer type that holds its
  values -- unsigned char for 0 to 255, signed char for -128 to 127, then the shorts and the ints, unsigned where no
  value is negative -- as its underlying type marked `packed_enum`, which no C23 rule takes for a fixed one, its
  enumerators ints (`ccl_packed_enum/5`, `ccl_packed_enum_type/3`, `ccl_enum_typed/2`), and `aligned` on an enum the
  qualifier `aligned(E)` on its base, the type's alignment raised and its size kept, as clang lays it (0.205;
  `ccl_aligned_enum/4`: a base `[int]` marked `packed_enum` where none was written, its enumerators ints and C++'s
  underlying type its values', `cpp_underlying_of/2`; an alloca and a global aligned so, `ir_laid_tag/1`; a promoted
  value no aligned type, `ccl_enum_base_plain/2`): `struct { char c; enum E e; }` over `enum __attribute__((aligned(8)))
  E` was 8 bytes, e at 4, where clang lays 16, e at 8 (gcc ignores the attribute there; `alignexpr.c`). `aligned` alone
  is the target's largest alignment, 16; a parameter's is dropped. Each was dropped: a packed struct kept its natural
  layout -- glibc's `struct epoll_event`, packed on x86-64, was sixteen bytes where gcc and clang lay twelve -- and
  `aligned(64)` on a cache line's struct left it at its members' alignment. AN ALIGNMENT SPECIFIER IS THE OBJECT'S (C
  6.7.5, [dcl.align]): `_Alignas(16) char *p` aligns the pointer, the qualifier moved from the pointee to the pointer it
  declares, through an array to its element (`ccl_align_fold/3`); it stayed on the pointee, and a struct member of that
  form lay at a pointer's alignment, eight where clang lays it at sixteen. AN ATTRIBUTE BEFORE A STRUCT'S, A UNION'S OR
  AN ENUM'S KEY IS THE DECLARATION'S, as clang reads it (`attribute ignored, place it after "struct"`): the note is set
  aside at the key and put back after the specifier (`ccl_layout_saved/1`, `ccl_layout_put/1`), so that
  `__attribute__((packed)) struct I { ... } m;` is a packed member of a struct I of its natural layout; AN ATTRIBUTE
  AMONG THE DECLARATION SPECIFIERS IS EVERY DECLARATOR'S (GCC's manual, Attribute Syntax): its `aligned` joins the
  qualifiers as `_Alignas` does, a member's `packed` too, a variable's `packed` meaning nothing (`ccl_lead_layout/3`, at
  the end of `ccl_decl_specs//4` at file scope, in a block and in a member); the step's probes against clang met both,
  the struct packed and `__attribute__((aligned(16))) int a, b;` aligning a alone. THE STANDARD SPELLING IS GCC'S TOO
  (0.205, reader 155; `ccl_skip_attr//0` over `ccl_gnu_scope//0`): `[[gnu::packed]]` and `[[gnu::aligned(N)]]` --
  `__gnu__::`, `__packed__` and `__aligned__` alike, and C23's `[[gnu::...]]` in C, whose lexer reads `::` as two colons
  -- set the notes GCC's spelling sets, on a struct, a member, a variable and an alias; they were dropped, so `struct
  [[gnu::packed]] S { char c; int i; }` was 8 bytes where clang lays 5, and libc++ 21's atomic_ref, whose `using
  _Aligned_Tp [[__gnu__::__aligned__(required_alignment)]] = _Tp;` raises a 4-byte struct of alignment 2 to 4, called
  libatomic's generic routines, which the link did not find (the Atomics topic of the lowering). A MEMBER'S LEADING
  ATTRIBUTE IS ITS OWN in C++ too (`ccl_lead_layout/3`, `ccl_members//2`: the note is kept while a member's rules are
  tried and cleared before the next member, and `ccl_add_layout_q/3` adds a qualifier once):
  `__attribute__((aligned(16))) int i;` and `[[gnu::aligned(16)]] int i;` in a class lost it to the first rule tried,
  which failed, a defect of 0.203. The layout is the Object layout topic's. Reader 154, 155. `test/c/run/packed.c`,
  `packattr.c`, `packunion.c`, `aligntd.c`, `packenum.c`, `packlead.c`, `gnuattrc.c` (C23),
  `test/cpp/run/packedcpp.cpp`, `packnonpod.cpp`, `gnuattr.cpp`, `leadattr.cpp`. (0.203, 0.205)
- `__attribute__((...))` and every other `__asm("...")` are read and dropped (`ccl_gnu_attr`). `__typeof__` and
  `__typeof` are type specifiers at every level, `typeof` in C23 and in a GNU mode, and `typeof_unqual` in C23 alone, as
  clang has them (`ccl_typeof//1` over `ccl_typeof_word/1`, 0.214: under `-std=c17` and `-std=c++20` `typeof` is a name
  of the program's, and in C17 and C++ `typeof_unqual` is; both were keywords everywhere, and `int typeof = 1;` was
  refused; `strictansi.c`, `strictansi.cpp`); `typeof_unqual(X)` is `typeof(unqual(X))`. `(^b)` is `block(Q, T)`. (0.93)
  `__extension__` before an expression is the expression (`ccl_unary_`), and before a block's alias declaration it is
  dropped (C++ only; reader 127, 0.136): libc++ 21's linear_congruential_engine writes `__extension__ using __calc_type
  = unsigned __int128;` in a function body, the read of `<random>` stopped there -- silently, a partial read -- and
  `mt19937` was no type (`stdrandom.cpp` over libc++ 21).
- A nullability word (`_Nonnull`, `_Nullable`, `_Null_unspecified`, `__nonnull` ...) is read and dropped, bare or with
  an argument list (`ccl_gnu_attr`). Why: glibc's `__nonnull(params)` arrives as `_Nonnull ( ( 1 ) )`; read bare, it
  stopped `<stdio.h>` at `fclose`, and `printf` was undeclared. (0.87)
- `__signed`, `__const`, `__volatile`, `__restrict`, `__inline` and their `__x__` forms ARE the words. A fact per
  spelling (`ccl_gnu_word/2`) and one rule (`ccl_gnu_spec`) route each as a type, a qualifier or a storage word. The
  grammar reads them, not the lexers. (0.71)
- `_BitInt(N)` is the specifier `bitint(N)` in C and C++, half a rank below the standard type of its width
  (`ccl_bitint_rank`), never promoted (`ccl_promote`; C23 6.3.1.1/2). (0.93)
- The usual arithmetic conversions answer an unqualified value (`ccl_usual/3` over `ccl_usual_/3`): an operand's
  `const` is not the result's. C++'s `char32_t` promotes to `unsigned int` and `wchar_t` to `int`, their underlying

- An ENUM ranks and promotes as its underlying type, the written base or `int` ([conv.prom]/3-4, C23 6.3.1.1; `ccl_int_rank`,
  `ccl_promote` over `ccl_enum_underlying/2`): `e + 1` and `~e` are that type's arithmetic. Fixture: `promotion.cpp`. Why: an

- `_Decimal32`, `_Decimal64` and `_Decimal128` are type words of the grammar's table, as `__int128` is
  (`ccl_gnu_word/2`; the lexers' keyword tables are the language's, and C23's new keywords arrive as identifiers), at
  every level as gcc reads them; they were read as typedef names (0.129).
- `__int128` is a type word (`ccl_gnu_word('__int128', '__int128')`, `ccl_basic_type`; `signed`/`unsigned` with it,
  `long` never): `ccl_builtin_typedef/2` gives `__int128_t` and `__uint128_t` their types, integer rank 6 above `long
  long`, size and alignment 16, LLVM `i128` (`ir_base`), Itanium `n` and `o`. Reader `k92` over `test/c/run/int128.c`.
  The decimal floating types are the Lowering's topic (0.129). (0.71, 0.93, 0.117)
- `_Thread_local` and `thread_local` (C++, C23) are the QUALIFIER `thread_local`, not storage; their clauses precede

  it as it goes past, `'$ccl_vec'` cleared at each item's start; `ccl_vec_take/2` folds it onto the declared type's
  base): `base(Q, [vector(size | ext, X, Elem)])`, X as written, the bytes or the lanes, an expression that a template's
  parameter may be. The inference resolves it (`ccl_resolve_base/3` over `ccl_vec_count/4`) to `vec(Kind, Lanes, Elem)`:
  its size the lanes' bytes, a bool ext vector's a bit a lane, rounded up to a power of two, and its alignment its size
  (`ccl_size_align`); `v[i]` a lane, a comparison of two vectors a MASK, the signed integer vector of the element's size
  whose lanes are -1 or 0 (`ccl_vector_mask/2`), an arithmetic, bitwise or shift operator the vector's own type, a
  scalar operand converted to the element. `__builtin_convertvector(e, T)` is read in C and C++ with its operand an
  expression and its second a type (`ccl_postfix_p`; it was a trait of types). The attribute was dropped and the vector
  was its element: `v4si c = a + b` added two ints. Reader 133. `test/c/run/vector.c`, `test/cpp/run/vector.cpp`.
  (0.162)
- `_Alignas(E)`, and C23's and C++'s `alignas(E)`, on an object are the qualifier `aligned(E)`; in an attribute
  position they are dropped. `test/c/run/wstr_alignas.c`. (0.99)
- An alignment specifier changes the alignment, never the size (`ccl_size_align`): `sizeof x' of `_Alignas(16) int x'
  is 4, a member after an aligned member lies right after it, and an aligned array counts its elements at their own
  size. Why: rounded, `alignas(S) unsigned char buf[sizeof(S)]' had `sizeof buf' 192 for 24 bytes, and a loop over it
  wrote past the stack slot. `test/c/run/alignsize.c`. (0.112)
- `_Atomic(T)` (C11 6.7.2.4) is T's specifiers plus the qualifier `_Atomic`; a pointer or qualified T is `typeof(T)`
  (`ccl_atomic_spec`). (0.99)
- `typeof` is resolved (`ccl_resolve_base([typeof(X)], ...)`): a type as it is, an expression by `ccl_type_of/2`,
  `unqual` stripping top-level qualifiers; where the expression's object lies is no part of the type it names (GCC's
  manual, Typeof): a packed member's `packed`, an object's `aligned(E)` and a place's `ualign(K)` are off, a typedef's
  own alignment kept, as clang has it (`ccl_place_free/2`, 0.203: `__typeof__(q.i)` of `int i __attribute__((packed))`
  was aligned at one; `packlead.c`). `typeof(K)` of an object is its expression (`ccl_typeof_type/1`). (0.93)
- A K&R definition (C 6.9.1/13) is read as its prototype (`ccl_knr_ids`, `ccl_knr_decls`, `ccl_knr_params`,
  `ccl_knr_adjust`): an undeclared parameter is `int`, an array a pointer, a `float` a `double`.
  `test/c/run/cforms.c`. (0.108)
- `a[static 3]`, `a[const static 3]` and `a[*]` parameters are the pointer they decay to. `_Bool` is a byte with C's
  conversion rules. (0.108)
- A C11 anonymous struct or union member is a hidden member `$anonK` (`ccl_anon_name`, C only), its members the
  holder's, reached through `ccl_anon_route`. (0.108)
- A label's body may be a declaration ([stmt.label], C23): `ccl_label_body` falls to `ccl_block_item`. (0.91)
- `__func__`, `__FUNCTION__`, `__PRETTY_FUNCTION__` name the enclosing function unless the program declares them
  (`ccl_func_name/1`); their text is clang's since 0.166 (the topic Function names and source locations). (0.108,
  0.166)

### Initializers and objects

- An unbounded array takes its bound from its initializer at the read (`ccl_sized_by_init`, C 6.7.9/22). A
  designator moves the position (`ccl_init_bound`). A string gives its length plus one, and a wide string its code
  points plus one (`ccl_utf8_count`). A pack expansion sizes nothing. `(T[]){...}` is sized by its items. Why: a
  global's `sizeof` was 0. (0.104, 0.108)
- Designated initializers work in arrays and nested (`[3] = x`, `.a.b = y`); a global's list is made positional
  (`ccl_init_norm`, C 6.7.9). `offsetof` folds through members, elements and anonymous members (`ccl_offsetof`).
  `test/c/run/designated.c`. (0.108)
- Tentative definitions are one object (C 6.9.2; `ir_flush_tentatives`). An array argument to a function without a
  prototype decays. (0.108)

### Typedef names and the symbol table

- A typedef name from a header the reader has not seen is known from its context: `name x`, `name *p` where no
  expression can stand, `(name *)`, `(name){`, `name *p = ...` in a block. A seed of standard names starts every unit
  (`ccl_seed_typedefs/1`). (M1)
- The file's typedef names are threaded as an Env and held in the bucket set `'$ccl_envs'` (`ccl_set_has/2`) for the
  casts deep in an expression, the set the whole record since 0.187 (the Tables topic of Time and memory).
  `ccl_env_sync/2` MERGES an item's new names and never replaces the global env; a deep rule passes `genv`
  (`ccl_env_member/2`), a lambda's head too since 0.187, which handed on the list of every name and walked it to its
  end at each name it asked. Why: a replace dropped C++'s class names. (0.44, 0.46, 0.187)
- The table kept while parsing: `'$ccl_scope'` the OPEN frames of Name-Type, innermost first, `[]` at file scope
  (pushed by `ccl_compound`, and at a function's parameters only when `{` is next); `'$ccl_gscope'` the file scope;
  `'$ccl_typedefs'`; `'$ccl_tags'` (a C++ class without its bodies, `ccl_slim_members`) -- these three in 128 buckets
  each since 0.120 (the Tables topic of Time and memory); `'$ccl_enums'`. `library(ccl_infer)` answers over it
  (`ccl_type_of/2`, `ccl_resolve_type/2`, `ccl_size_of/2`, LP64). Reader `k25`. (M1b, 0.120)
- `ccl_declare/2` puts a name in the innermost open frame, else `ccl_gdeclare/1`; `ccl_declared/2` asks the open frames,
  then `ccl_gdeclared/2`; `ccl_scope/1` answers all frames, file scope last; `ccl_locals/1` the open ones;
  `ccl_scope_add/1` adds a list. Why: `nb_getval/2` copies, and a local must not copy the file scope. AT FILE SCOPE
  ONLY AN ATOM IS DECLARED (0.188): a member defined out of its class (`scoped(Path, N)`), an operator
  (`operator(Op)`) and a template-id are no name the file scope is asked for, as the bulk noter has never kept them,
  and each went to the bucket of the keys that are no atom, whose every write copied it whole: 861 of the file scope's
  3,649 writes in a read of `<thread>`'s flattened text, 0.80 s of its 13.4 s. (M1b, 0.188)
- `ccl_note_item/1` notes one item; a unit tree goes through the BULK noter `ccl_items_note/1`: difference lists, each
  table set once, the unit's own items before its includes' (`ccl_own_first`). Why: per item it was quadratic, and a
  unit's own definition shadows a header's declaration. (0.78)
- Answers are cached: `ccl_cached/4` for small values, `ccl_cached_named/4` with a global per name for large ones.
  `ccl_tables_changed/0` empties them wherever a table is written. A cached predicate is not re-entrant. (2026-09-06)
- An enumerator is of its ENUM's type in C++ ([dcl.enum]/5) and an `int` in C and for an unnamed enum
  (`ccl_type_of(id(N))` through `ccl_enumerator_type/3`): the table of values keeps each enumerator's enum beside its
  value, `'$t'(Name)-Tag`, and a scoped enum's tag as `'$s'(Tag)-1` (the parser's `ccl_declare_enumerators/2`, which
  declares the enumerator with that type, and the bulk noter's `ccl_collect_enum_tags/4`). A compound key never answers
  a lookup of a value by name, so every writer, save and restore of the table carries the two kinds of entry without a
  word, a summary's `enum/2` lines too (reader 121). A scoped enum converts to no arithmetic type (`ccl_scoped_enum/1`).
  An enumerator of an unscoped enum NESTED in a class, named through the class (`Shape::Circle`), is of the nested
  enum's type too (`cpp_enum_class_tag/3`, a `cpp_expr` clause before the class road, which folded it as an `int`
  static). Fixture: `enumtype.cpp`. Why: `h(Red)` called `h(int)` over `h(Color)`, `k(Fruit::Pear)` called `k(long)`, a
  template deduced an `int`, and `v.push_back(Green)` was refused (`undeclared(Green)`). AN ENUMERATOR IS A CONSTANT OR
  NOTHING (0.160; C 6.7.2.2/2, [dcl.enum]/5): in C an initializer that does not fold fails the item
  (`ccl_declare_enumerators/4`), so a header read raw stops there and is read preprocessed and the program's file says
  where it gave up; in C++ the reader keeps the value after the one before as a placeholder, and the desugaring folds
  the initializer through the constexpr evaluator, the enumerators before it put in as their values
  (`cpp_fold_enumerators/5`, `cpp_enum_unfolded/3`: `enum { A = f(), B }` over `constexpr int f()` was 0 and 1 where
  clang++ has 7 and 8), else refuses the program's own by name, `enumerator_not_constant(N)`
  (`test/cpp/enumnotconst.cpp`), as clang++ refuses it; it took the value after the one before it, silently. The next
  value is wide (`ccl_w_add/3`), past 2^60 a `big(_)`, and an enumerator of a value no int holds is typed as a literal
  of it, an int else (`ccl_enumerator_type/3`, `ir_expr(id(N))` over `ir_expr(int(V))`): `i32 18446744073709551600`
  reached LLVM. `enumconstexpr.cpp`, `test/c/run/enumfloat.c`. (0.100, 0.127, 0.160)
- AN ENUMERATOR'S VALUE THAT NAMES ANOTHER ENUM'S, A HEADER'S OR A CONSTANT (0.195): the bulk noter sets the unit's table
  once, at the end, and folded each enum with its own enumerators alone, so `enum B { Y = X + 1 };` after `enum A { X = 5
  };`, an enumerator over a header's (the unit's own items come first) or over a named constant took the value after the
  one before it -- Y was 0 and `int arr[Y];` had no element, in C and in C++, since the first enums. Such an enum is kept
  (`'$ccl_eretry'`, `ccl_collect_enum_values/3`) and folded again once the table is written and once the program's named
  constants are noted (`ccl_enum_retries/0`), the values it KNOWS then put before the ones it had -- an initializer that
  folds, or none after a known value (`ccl_retry_enumerators/5`): a placeholder of the first pass put first answers a bare
  name before an earlier enum's, and libc++ 21's `_PartialOrdResult::__less = static_cast<signed char>(_OrdResult::__less)`,
  which folds nowhere here, made the bare `__less` 0 and every `partial_ordering` compare false (the first net of 0.195,
  `stdcompare.cpp`). In C an enumerator's value is also
  FIXED WHERE IT IS READ (`ccl_fix_enumerators/2`, in the enum's rule): its initializer folded there, the enumerators
  before it put in as their values, and kept as the literal -- a block's `constexpr` is no name the passes know. C++'s
  unfolded ones are the desugaring's (`cpp_fold_enumerators/5`). `enumcross.c`, `enumcross.cpp`. (0.195)
- `ccl_type_of/2` of a statement expression puts its declarations in scope for its last expression. (M1b)
- A typedef, tag or enum declared in a block joins the unit's one table in C (`ccl_collect_item(function)` through
  `ccl_stmt_typedefs`, by statement shape; two blocks that typedef one name must agree; `test/c/run/typedef_block.c`).
  In C++ a block's TYPEDEF does not (0.127): the bulk noter takes only the tags and enumerators of its type
  (`ccl_collect_typedef_types/5`), and the desugaring notes it for the statements of its own block and takes it out at
  the block's end, on success, failure and throw (`cpp_scoped_typedefs/2` over `ccl_tab_del/2`, which removes the NEWEST
  entry of the name, so the one it shadowed answers again). Fixture: `blocktypedef.cpp`. Why: one table holding every
  block's `using _Tp = ...;` made `_Tp` a KNOWN name to every rule that tells a template's own parameter by the tables
  not knowing it; 0.126 had worked round it twice (`cpp_callee_param_type/2`, `cpp_lambda_params/3`). (0.108, 0.127)
- A BLOCK'S STRUCT OR UNION IS ITS BLOCK'S OWN TYPE (C17 6.2.1/4, 6.7.2.3/5, [basic.scope.block]; 0.201): in C, one that
  a block defines under a tag the unit defines otherwise too -- another block's, the file's -- is renamed `N.local_K` for
  the rest of its block (`ir_block_tags/2`, before the check, the table noted again from the renamed units): its own
  members' `struct N *`, its declarators' types and every use whose innermost definition in force it is, the elaborated
  name alone or the definition's own members; a nested block's definition ends with the block. A tag defined once keeps
  its name. In C++ every plain local struct is renamed (the Classes topic), one defined with its declarators too: the
  reader reads `struct S { long a; } s;` in a block as its definition and a declaration over the elaborated name
  (`ccl_block_tag_split/2`), since a declaration whose type is a struct with its members is no definition to the
  desugaring -- a template argument's substitution makes that shape too, and the first chain of 0.201 met `T y = x;`
  over a deduced struct of the program renamed a local one of its own (`std::sort` of a vector of the program's
  struct, `argument_mismatch`; `std::sort` of strings, `no_constructor`). The rename of a local class's or
  struct's name stops where a nested block defines the name again (`cpp_tag_scoped_list/4`). The tables hold one tag a
  name and the lowering one layout a tag (`%struct.S`, the first met): `struct S { long a; } s; s.a = 5000000000L;` in a
  function after another's `struct S { int a; }` stored and read through the first's `i32`, a silent wrong answer, and a
  member the first lacked was `no_member`. `test/c/run/blocktag.c`, `test/cpp/run/blocktag.cpp`. (0.201)
- The bulk noter skips a name that is no atom, a member defined out of its class (`ccl_collect_vars`:
  `Counter::made`; `ccl_collect_item`: `Shape::scale`). Why: it crashed `atom_concat`. (0.32)
- A DELETED FUNCTION TYPES NO CALL OF ITS NAME (0.201; `ccl_collect_vars/7`, `ccl_declare_vars/1`): the table keeps one type
  a name, and libc++'s poison pill `void make_error_code() = delete;` (`std::__adl_only`), noted first, answered
  `std::make_error_code(e)` with `void`, so `std::error_code ec = std::make_error_code(errc::invalid_argument)` chose no
  constructor. The desugaring's own test for the same is `cpp_arity_clash/1` (Overload resolution). `stdmisc.cpp`. (0.201)
- In C++ a tag's name is a type. `ccl_resolve_base([typedef(N)], ...)` asks `ccl_tag_type/4`, which tells the kind by
  the members' shape. A class resolves to its desugared struct (`ccl_tag_struct/2`, cached `'$ccl_ts:'`), so a tag
  noted twice resolves to the struct. `::N` is the global N, which keeps the bare name (0.201; `ccl_resolve_base/3` on
  `scoped([global], N)`): libc++ 18's `typedef ::timespec __libcpp_timespec_t;` at file scope resolved to nothing, and
  `std::barrier`'s wait met `decltype(__ts.tv_sec)` of no type. `stdsync.cpp`. (0.41, 0.201)
- `ccl_resolve_base/3` leaves a template-id typedef raw (an `atom(N)` guard before the named cache). (0.35)
- In C++ an included unit's class, struct and enum class names join the includer's Env (`ccl_items_typedefs`), so
  `Name &s` parses. (0.41)

### C's language levels

- C's level is its own global, `'$ccl_c_std'` (`ccl_c_std/1`, default 17), since 17 and 23 are both languages'. The
  driver gives `cstd(N)`: `-std=c23|gnu23|c2x|gnu2x` 23; c17, c11, c99 and their GNU forms accepted; c89, c90 refused.
  A fixture names its level in `NAME.std` (`test/c/run/c23.c`, `c23b.c`, `c23pp.c`). (0.57)
- THE C LEVEL IS COMPARED BY THE YEAR IT NAMES (0.221; `ccl_c_at_least/1`, `ccl_c_year/2`): `-std=c99` is 99, and every
  test of the level was `S >= 23`, which 99 passes -- -std=c99 read C23's forms (`typeof` a keyword in the ISO mode,
  `int bool = 2;` a syntax error, an enumeration's fixed type, a `u8` character constant unsigned char, `(void)` in
  `__PRETTY_FUNCTION__`) and defined `__STDC_VERSION__` as 202311L. The compile gate's trigraphs for a fixture's ISO
  level before C23 ask the year too. `stdc99.c` (`-std=c99`; refused by 0.220), `stdc11.c` (`-std=c11`; 0.220 printed
  C17's version). (0.221)
- The grammar asks `ccl_c23//0`, and `ccl_c_or_cpp//0` for a form C23 took from C++ (C++ always, C from 23). Forms are
  READ at the level, never lexed at it. (0.57)
- At `-std=c23`: `bool` a specifier; `true`, `false`, `nullptr` primaries; `constexpr` is `const` plus the marker
  `constexpr`; `thread_local` the qualifier; `alignas(E)` on an object `aligned(E)`. Reader `k88`, `k90`. (0.99)
  `nullptr` is a `nullptr_t`, a type of its own (C23 6.4.4.6, 6.3.2.4; the Overload resolution topic): `_Generic` tells
  it from `void *`, and a `nullptr_t` value converts to a null pointer and to `false`. `nullptrtype.c`. (0.206)
- A FILE-SCOPE `const` integer whose initializer folds is a NAMED CONSTANT at every level, a C23 `constexpr` one among
  them, as clang folds a C17 one (GNU's folding; gcc refuses it): an array's bound, an enumerator, a bit-field's width,
  `_Static_assert`, a case label. A C23 `constexpr` object in a BLOCK is a constant of its block alone. The Constant
  evaluation topic has the tables. Reader `k87`. `fileconst.c`, `fileconst23.c`. (0.57, 0.195)
- From C23, C reads C++'s forms: `[[attributes]]` dropped; `enum E : unsigned char` (`ccl_enum_base//1`, `enum_base(T)`
  the first member); `auto x = e` deduced (`ccl_auto_decl/5`); `static_assert(e[, "msg"])` at file scope and in a
  block. `_Static_assert` is read in every C. (0.57)
- AN ENUM WITH A FIXED UNDERLYING TYPE IS ITS BASE'S SIZE AND ITS ENUMERATORS ARE OF ITS TYPE (C23 6.7.2.2/5, /15;
  [dcl.enum]; 0.194): in C23 a named enum with a written base is noted as C++'s are (`ccl_enum_typed/2` in the bulk
  noter's `ccl_collect_enum_tags/4` and the parser's `ccl_declare_enumerators/2`), its enumerators typed `enum(Tag, Ms)`
  (`ccl_enumerator_type/3`), and `enum E` named alone resolves to the tag's members, its base among them, in C and C++
  (`ccl_resolve_base/3` on `enum(Tag, none)`): `sizeof(Y)` of `enum Big : unsigned long long` and `enum E e;` were an
  int's 4. `c23enum.c` (`-std=c23`), `enumelab.cpp`.
- A static assertion is CHECKED where it folds: in C at the read (`ccl_assert_holds/3` throws
  `static_assert_failed(Text)`), one among a struct's members too (C11 6.7.2.1/1: a static_assert-declaration is a
  struct-declaration; 0.205: it was a syntax error, `memassert.c`; the driver gate refuses a false one), in C++ by the
  desugaring (0.198, the Constants of the desugaring topic), since C++ allows `static_assert(false)` in a branch no
  instantiation takes. (0.57, 0.198) The fold is asked ONCE (`once(ccl_const_eval(E, V))`, 0.117): `sizeof` of a struct
  had alternatives (16, 0, 0, 0), the test `V =:= 0` failed on the first and backtracked into a 0, and
  `_Static_assert(sizeof(T) == 16, ...)` over `struct { char c; long v; }` failed since 0.57. `sizeof`, `sizeof_type`
  and `alignof_type` answer one value in `ccl_const_eval/2` now. `test/c/run/sizeofassert.c`. (0.117)

### The language's own forms

- **`name := expr;` is a declaration by inference** (owner's rule): `ccl_infer_decl/4,5` takes `ccl_type_of/2` of the
  right side, decays arrays and functions, strips top-level qualifiers, and builds `declaration(L, none, Base,
  [var(N, T, E)])`; `unknown` throws `cannot_infer(N, E)` with `here(File, L)`. A clause of `ccl_external`,
  `ccl_block_item`, `ccl_for_init`, before the others. Reader `k30` to `k36`. (M1b)
- **The left of `:=` may be a pattern** (owner's rule), `{ a, _, f: b, g: { c } } := e`. `ccl_pattern//1` reads it
  into `bind`, `skip`, `field` and `sub` terms. `ccl_destructure/4` makes one inferred declaration per binding: by
  position through `ccl_nth_member/4` (an array's element by index), by name through `ccl_member_access/6`. A
  `ccl_gensym` temporary comes first unless the right side is an `id/1`. The result is a `'$splice'/1`. The errors
  are `no_member(Field | position(I), Type)` and `cannot_infer(pattern, E)`. Reader `k37` to `k41`. (M1b)
- **`name { members }` at file scope is `typedef struct name { members } name;`** (owner's rule). A `ccl_external`
  clause on `ccl_id(N), ccl_peek(p, '{')` reads it, the members by `ccl_members//2`. The name joins the Env, and the
  item is a plain `typedef/2`. Reader `k47` to `k49`. (M1b)
- **`defer(a, b) { body }` is a statement** (owner's rule: scope-bound like Cicili's cleanup, a static cleanup chain,
  no runtime): `ccl_statement` takes `defer ( ids ) {` only, so a call named defer stays a call. `defer(Line,
  [id(V)...], block(...))` runs at every exit of its scope, LIFO, over the variables' values then. Reader `k72`,
  `k73`. (M2)
- `own` is a qualifier read in the specifiers, on the pointee as C has it: `own char *p` is `ptr([], base([own],
  [char]))`. `move(E)` is a node, read at the macro door (`ccl_call_or_macro/3`). Reader `k75`, `k76`. (M3)
- `own` is a keyword in both languages, so a C++ member or variable named `own` does not read: the qualifier takes it
  (found when a fixture of 0.121 used it, and renamed). (0.121)
- **`x tie y` is the tie** (owner's rule, and the spelling): x lives within y. `tie` is CONTEXTUAL, read only where a
  tie can stand and only before a name (`ccl_id(tie), ccl_id(Y)`), so `std::tie` and a C variable `tie` are untouched.
  `ccl_tie//2` reads it after a declarator (init-declarator, member, parameter, function definition before `{`),
  `ccl_tie_name//1` after the `:=` forms. (0.109)
- `ccl_add_tie/3` puts `tie(Y)` in the OUTERMOST qualifier list, through an array to its element and a function to its
  result; `ccl_tie_of/2` reads it. Only the check reads a tie. Reader `k81`. (0.109)

### Macros: `.pl` files, `#cocolog` blocks and the global macros

- **A `.pl` included is a macro file** (owner's rule): every predicate it defines is a macro. `name(a, b)` with
  `name/3` runs NOW as `name(ASTa, ASTb, R)`, and R replaces the call (`ccl_call_or_macro/3` in `ccl_postfix_p`). A
  statement R is unwrapped (`ccl_stmt_of/3`), and `ccl_add_lines/3` gives a short form the call's line. A list R is a
  `'$splice'/1`, spliced in blocks and at file scope (`ccl_splice/3`). A file-scope `name(args);` is its own
  `ccl_external` clause. `name(R) --> ...` is `dcg(name)`, called as `phrase(name(R), Args)`. Reader `k19` to `k24`.
  (M1b)
- The registry `'$ccl_macros'` holds `macro(CName, Pred, Arity | dcg)`; `ccl_macro_X` defines `X`
  (`ccl_macro_cname/2`). `ccl_load_macros/2` loads by `ensure_loaded/1` and records `'$ccl_macro_files'`;
  `ccl_pl_clauses/2` finds the heads by splitting the text and `term_to_atom/2` per clause, since `current_predicate/1`
  does not list consulted clauses. `ccl_with_file/2` saves and restores the registry. (M1b)
- A macro's error carries both places, `here(File, Line, in_macro(Pred, MacroFile))` on `macro_failed/2` and
  `macro_error/3` (`ccl_macro_file/2`). Each expansion is `expansion(Line, Name, Args)` in `'$ccl_expansions'`; the
  unit ends with `'$expansions'(List)`, and the driver adds `note: expanded from macro` (`dr_remember_expansions/1`).
  Reader `k28`, `k29`, `k79`, `k80`. (M1b)
- **`#cocolog ... #end` is a macro file in place** (owner's rule). The item `cocolog(L, Text)` calls
  `ccl_cocolog_block/2`. It writes `tmp_file(cocolog)-L.pl` and runs `ccl_load_macros/2`, the `#include "m.pl"` door,
  so a macro's error names that file. The text rides into the store; over the clause budget the file stays uncached.
  A cache hit loads nothing again, since the expansion happened at the read. Reader `k82`. (M1b)
- **`format`, `print`, `println` are global macros** (owner's rule), in `library/ccl_format.pl`.
  `ccl_standard_macros/0` registers that file at the start of every unit, found on `$COCOLOG_LIBRARY`. It never does
  inside a library header's read (`ccl_lib_unit/1`, `'$ccl_lib_unit'`). Why: libc++ calls a `format` of its own.
  (0.99)
- They are DCG macros. Rust's holes `{}`, `{0}`, `{name}`, `{{`, `}}` become printf conversions by `ccl_type_of/2`; a
  struct prints by its members. `print` is `printf`, `println` adds `\n`, `format` is `({ char *b; asprintf(&b, ...);
  b; })`, a malloc'd `char *`. An argument that cannot be formatted stops the read (`cannot_format(Expr)`). Reader
  `k42` to `k46`. (M1b)
- **`clone(p)` is a global macro** (owner's rule), `ccl_macro_clone/2`: `({ own T *c = malloc(sizeof(T)); *c = *p; c;
  })`, a fresh owner, so an own parameter takes the copy and `p` stays the caller's. It refuses a non-pointer
  (`cannot_clone`), a pointee with an own member (`cannot_clone_own_members`, `ccl_has_own_member/1`) and a file with
  no `malloc` (`clone_needs_malloc`). `test/c/run/clone.c`. (M3)

## The C++ reader

### The mode and the level

- The global `'$ccl_lang'` is `c` or `cpp`. `ccl_set_lang/1` takes it from the extension (`ccl_lang_of_file/2`: `.cpp
  .cc .cxx .C .hpp .hh .hxx .cppm .ccm .cxxm .ixx .mpp`). The driver's `lang(cpp)` forces it (`'$ccl_lang_forced'`), and
  `cicilang++` sets that through `CICILANG_LANG=cpp`. (M5, 0.108)
- Every C++ rule is guarded by `ccl_cpp//0` and stands BEFORE the C clause it extends, so a `.c` file reads as before.
  (M5)
- Every C++ form is read at every C++ level, except `a[i, j]`: a multi-index from C++23 only (`ccl_std_at_least/1` over
  `'$ccl_std'`, default 17). (0.42, 0.43)
- In a DCG body, `( A, ! ; B )` cuts the WHOLE clause. Use it only for a choice that decides the clause. An optional
  word is `( ccl_kw(inline) ; [] )`, with no cut. Why: a cut before `namespace` killed every inline function. (M5)
- `ccl_make_class` makes `class(K, N, Bases, Members)` of a C++ `class`, a class with bases, or a body with a member
  that is not data. A `union` stays `union(N, Ms)`, and a C++ `struct` of data only stays C's `struct(N, Ms)`. (M5)
- The bulk noter (`ccl_collect_item`) takes the items of `extern_c` and `namespace` under bare names, a `template`'s
  item, and a `class` as a tag. It skips a method defined out of its class. An alias or variable template is never a C
  typedef. (0.44)

### Names and template-ids

- `ccl_qname//3` reads `::a::b<args>::c` into an atom, `tmpl(N, Args)` or `scoped(Path, Last)`; a leading `::` puts
  `global` first. A segment may be `decltype(E)`, `operator(Op)` or `::template f<U>` (`ccl_qseg`, `ccl_qrest`).
  (M5, 0.44)
- `N <` starts a template-id when N is a known template (`ccl_known_template/1`: the set `'$ccl_tmpls'`, the whole
  record since 0.187). In a type context it also starts one when `ccl_targs_ahead//0` finds the matching `>` and a
  declarator-like token follows. The scan skips parentheses and stops at `;`, `{` or `}`; a `>>` that closes both lists
  ends it (0.201, `ccl_skip_targs/3`: `ns::Unknown<ns::B<int>> x;` with the outer template unknown failed where `> >` read).
  (M5, 0.44, 0.187, 0.201)
- `ccl_ensure_globals` seeds the templates with common standard library names and the compiler's template-shaped
  builtins (`__type_pack_element`, `__make_integer_seq` ...). Every template item adds its name (`ccl_note_template/1`).
  (M5)
- In template arguments, `ccl_op_open/1` makes `>` and `>>` closers; `>>` closes two, and `ccl_tclose//0` leaves one.
  `'$ccl_targ'` counts the depth, and parentheses reset it (`ccl_targ_save`, `ccl_targ_restore`). (0.44)
- A template argument is a type only where it names no declarator (`ccl_targ_type`: the name is `anon`). Else it is a
  full expression (`ccl_targ_expr`). `Ts...` is `pack(T)`. Why: libc++'s `pair` writes `__conditional_t<A::value &&
  B::value, ...>`, and `A::value &&` read as a reference. (0.44, 0.71)
- `typename T::x` is `typedef(Q)`. `ccl_qrest` reads `X<T>::template f<U>`, and `X<T>::template f` alone as a template
  template argument. `decltype(auto)` is `auto`. (0.44, 0.84)
- A member name takes template arguments by look-ahead (`x.f<T>()`) or after `template` (`x.template f<T>()`,
  `f.template operator()<I>()`; `ccl_member_name`). (0.84)

### Type or expression: the vexing parse

- A compound qualified name is a type (`ccl_cpp_type//3` in `ccl_specs`) only where `ccl_qname_typish/2` holds or a
  declarator follows (`ccl_declarator_follows`). Before `(` it is an expression: `S b(std::move(a));` declares no
  function -- but before a PARENTHESIZED declarator of a pointer or a reference, `(*`, `(&` or `(&&`, it is a type in a
  block too ([stmt.ambig]: what can be a declaration is one; `ccl_paren_declarator_ahead//0`, 0.161): `ns::T (*m)(int) =
  &ns::make;` was read as the call of a functional cast, and `std::chrono::seconds (*a)(std::chrono::seconds) = ...`
  named an `a` nothing declared (`no_constructor(duration, 1)`). A plain name is left to the C heuristics, so `std::cout
  << x` is an expression. Reader 132; `parendecl.cpp`. (0.44, 0.161)
- `ccl_qname_typish/2` holds for a template-id whose template is no function's, for a last name known as a typedef or as
  such a template, and for a fixed list of type-like names (`string`, `size_t`, `value_type`, `iterator` ...;
  `ccl_type_like_name/1`). A QUALIFIED NAME THAT NAMES NO TYPE DECLARES NO PARAMETER (0.186; `ccl_param_no_type/3`, in
  a parameter list): before what ends an unnamed parameter it is an expression, and the declarator before the list an
  object's with an initializer ([dcl.ambig.res]) -- where its qualifier is an enumeration, whose members are its
  enumerators ([dcl.enum]), or a class with a data member or a member function of its name, which hides a type
  ([basic.scope.hiding]), and where its last name is a type only as a class TEMPLATE's, with no arguments, a
  placeholder for a deduced class type, which never stands in a parameter list ([dcl.type.class.deduct]/2). libc++'s
  `inline constexpr partial_ordering partial_ordering::less(_OrdResult::__less);` was a member function's declaration
  wherever `std::__less` (`<__algorithm/comp.h>`) had been read before: no item kept it, and the orderings' `less` were
  undefined symbols over 13 of the 38 summaries of libc++ 18 that hold them (`<map>`, `<string>`, `<algorithm>` ... at
  C++20, 0.184's chain); `O b(R::tag);` and `int y(Q::less);` in a block declared functions. Reader 140.
  `qualparam.cpp`, `ordless.cpp`. (0.44, 0.186)
- A function template's name is a template, never a type. `ccl_note_if_fn_template` records it (the set
  `'$ccl_ftmpls'`; a summary's `ftemplate(N)`), and `ccl_qname_typish` refuses it, its explicit template-id too. So
  `_Tp __t(std::move(__x))` and `T &r(std::forward<U>(v))` declare variables. (0.45, 0.84, 0.187)
- `X<T>::f`, `v<T>` and `operator+<...>` are the declarator-id `name(Q)` only where a declarator may end
  (`ccl_declarator_id_end`) and outside a block (`\+ ccl_in_block`). So `(is_x<T>::value && y)` is no cast, and
  `traits::take(x);` in a body is a call. `test/cpp/run/qualstmt.cpp`. (0.44, 0.55)
- In a C++ parameter list, a lone undeclared name before `,` or `)` is an unnamed parameter of that type
  (`ccl_typedef_name(_, param, N)`). A declared object keeps the vexing parse. Why: libc++ 18's undeclared
  `memory_order` stopped the read of `<iostream>` silently. (0.93)
- That rule is for a PROTOTYPE, not for a body: the declarators of a block-level declaration are read with
  `'$ccl_blockdecl'` set (`ccl_block_declarators//3`, `ccl_blockdecl/0`; restored on success and on failure), and there
  an undeclared lone name is the argument of an object (0.117, reader 114). A class body is a complete-class context
  ([class.mem]/6), so `std::lock_guard <std::mutex> g(mu);` in a member function, with `mu` declared LATER in the class,
  was the declaration of a function `g` taking an unnamed parameter of the type `mu`, and the build stopped at `not
  lowered yet: typedef(mu)`. `mutexmember.cpp`.
- A name declared as a variable in an OPEN frame is no type name there ([basic.scope.hiding]; `ccl_local_variable/1`
  in the first `ccl_typedef_name` clause): a program's `const char *path` hides the filesystem's `path` that `<fstream>`
  brings, and `std::ofstream out(path);` is the variable's initializer, not a function declaration of a parameter of
  type `path`. Reader 112. (0.117)
- `(T())` and `(T(n))` are PARENTHESIZED FUNCTIONAL CASTS, never a cast to the function type `T ()` (`ccl_cast_expr`
  refuses a type of the shape `fn(_, _, _)`) and never a type-id with a named declarator: a type-id's declarator is
  ABSTRACT (`ccl_type_name//2` demands `N == anon`), so `(std::vector<int>(n))` is the temporary and
  `(std::vector<int>)(n)` the cast. Else the cast took the call for a type, found no operand after `)` and stopped the
  read: libc++ 18's `<thread>` writes `thread() : __t_((__libcpp_thread_t())) {}`, and the idiom `std::vector<int>
  r((std::istream_iterator<int>(in)), std::istream_iterator<int>())` is the vexing parse's own cure. Reader 114.
  `parencast.cpp`. (0.117)
- The compiler's traits are two FIXED lists: `ccl_builtin_type_name/1` gives `builtin_type(N, Args)`, and
  `ccl_builtin_trait/1` gives `call(id(N), [type(T) ...])`. Why fixed: libc++ has functions of the same spelling
  (`__is_overaligned_for_new(__align)`). (0.44, 0.45)
- `operator T()` is `method(L, Qs, T, operator(conv(T)), [], false, Body)`. `ccl_conv_type` reads specifiers and
  pointers only, since `int ()` would read as a function type. (0.44)

### Templates, packs and constraints

- In `template(L, TParams, Item)`, the type, pack and template parameters are type names for the whole item:
  `ccl_tparam` adds each to the global env, `ccl_tparams_enter/3` and `ccl_tparams_leave/1` wrap the item, and the leave
  removes those the head added: the names the env logged after the mark taken before the head (`ccl_env_mark/1`,
  `ccl_env_since/2`; 0.187, where a copy of the env taken before the head was compared with the env after it).
  `'$ccl_tmpl_depth'` and `ccl_note_if_template` make the item's own name a template in its body. (0.44, 0.187)
- Parameters are `tparam(type | pack | template, N, Default)`, `tparam(vpack(T), N, none)` and, for a value,
  `tparam(T, N, Default)`. An unnamed one is `anon`. `typename T::x = 0` is a value (`ccl_tparam_end`). `template <int
  &...>` and `template <class...> class F = X` are read. (0.44)
- A VALUE template parameter's name hides a typedef or a template of that name for its item (`'$ccl_vparams'` frames
  pushed by `ccl_tparams_enter/3`, popped by `ccl_tparams_leave/1`; `'$ccl_vhead'` for the names of the head being read;
  `ccl_value_param/1` asked by `ccl_local_variable/1` and `ccl_known_template/1`). Why: the class-scope typedefs of
  every class read before stay in the env, an out-of-class member's body needs them; a `typedef int _Size;` in one of
  libc++'s classes made `bitset<_Size>` of `template <size_t _Size>` a TYPE argument, so no out-of-class member of
  `std::bitset` matched `bitset<16>` and its `set`, `flip`, `count` and `test` stayed declarations; `template <size_t
  __count, __enable_if_t< __count < _Dt, int> = 0>` of `<random>` read `__count <` as the algorithm's template-id.
  `valueparam.cpp`. (0.117)
- A template template parameter's name is a template inside its item only (`ccl_note_tt_param`, un-noted per item frame
  by `ccl_tparams_leave`). ITS OWN LIST IS READ by the head's rule (0.185; `ccl_tt_inner/4`): its names are types
  while the list is read and leave the env after it, a template template parameter in it is un-noted, and the head's
  value names stay as they were ([basic.scope.temparam]: the names are the list's). Where a parameter of the list has a
  default, the head gets a second entry, `ttp(N, List)`, last with the requires-clause (`ccl_gather_requires/2`; the
  Template template parameters topic). A list that the head's rule does not take, or whose read raises, is skipped as
  before: `ccl_skip_to_close` counts nested `<>`, skips a parenthesized group whole and ends at a `;` (0.184). A list
  with no default gives the head it gave, so libc++'s read is the same. Why: `<variant>`'s `template <_Trait X, ...>`
  read as a constrained parameter; `template <template <class T, bool = (sizeof(T) < 4)> class TT>` counted the
  comparison's `<` and was a syntax error, as the scan ahead of a class body did until 0.183. Reader 139.
  `ttpdefault.cpp`, `ttpown.cpp`. (0.45, 0.93, 0.184, 0.185)
- Packs and folds: `param(pack(T), N)`; `pack(X)` for an expansion in a template argument, a call argument, a base, an
  initializer item or a constructor initializer; `sizeof_pack(N)`; `fold(Op, dots, E)`, `fold(Op, E, dots)`,
  `fold(Op, A, dots, B)`. C++26's pack index is `pack_index(N, I)` as a type and `pack_index(A, I)` as an
  expression. (0.44, 0.93)
- A specialization `struct X<Args>` is `class(K, tmpl(X, Args), Bases, Members)` (`ccl_class_targs`). The noters skip a
  tag whose name is compound. (0.44)
- C++20: a concept is `concept(L, N, E)`, its name a template. A requires-clause on a head is `requires(E)` among the
  parameters (`ccl_add_requires`). A requires-expression is `requires_expr(Ps, Reqs)` of `type(T)`, `compound(E, C)`,
  `nested(E)` and `expr(E)`. (0.42)
- A constraint is primaries joined by `&&` and `||` (`ccl_constraint`; [temp.pre]), never a full expression. Why: a full
  expression took the `[[nodiscard]]` after a concept-id for a subscript. (0.84)
- A constrained type parameter (`template <C T>`, `C<A> T`, `ns::C T`; `ccl_tparam_c`) is a type parameter plus its
  concept-id as a `requires` entry. `ccl_gather_requires` conjoins the entries into ONE, last. A tag or a typedef is no
  concept (`ccl_concept_name`). (0.84, 0.93)
- A constrained `auto` keeps its concept as the qualifier `constrained(C, As)` (`ccl_specs`). The desugaring checks it
  where it deduces (`cpp_constrained_ok`). (0.93)
- A requires-clause on a member template's head and a trailing one (`requires(R)` in `ccl_method_quals`) are kept. A
  FREE FUNCTION TEMPLATE'S TRAILING ONE joins its head's, conjoined ([temp.pre]/9; 0.199, reader 151): the definition
  rule keeps it in the storage slot, `treq(R, Sto)`, and the template's item takes it off (`ccl_take_treq/4`). It was
  read with the qualifiers and dropped, so of `template <class T> int f(T) requires (sizeof(T) > 4)` and its twin
  `requires (sizeof(T) <= 4)` both held and the first declared won (`treqfree.cpp`). A PROTOTYPE'S joins its head's too
  (0.205, reader 155): `ccl_fn_quals//2` notes the clause of the last function declarator it read (`'$ccl_ptreq'`) and
  `ccl_take_treq/4` takes it -- `template <class T> int f(T) requires (sizeof(T) > 4);` declares the candidate its
  definition is, and where the definition is no item before the call, a later one or another unit's, both of two such
  prototypes held and the first declared won; and A MEMBER'S DEFINED OUT OF ITS CLASS keeps its clause in its storage
  slot, `mreq(R, Sto)` (`ccl_req_sto/4`), which the desugaring compares with the declaration's (the Templates topic's
  members defined out of class). `protoreq.cpp` (C++20). On a lambda it is read and dropped. (0.84, 0.199, 0.205)

### Classes

- A class's name joins the global env at its declaration (`ccl_add_env/1`). Its body parses with the name on
  `'$ccl_class'` (`ccl_class_push`), so a constructor is known by it (`ccl_current_class`, through `ccl_class_bare`).
  (M5, 0.71)
- A class body is a complete-class context ([class.mem]/6). Before the members, `ccl_member_templates_ahead`
  (`ccl_scan_mts`, `ccl_scan_did`, `ccl_note_mt`) notes at the body's depth:
  - a member FUNCTION template (the declarator-id before `(`) as a template and a function template; a constructor or
    destructor template (the class's own name) as a template only, else `pair<...>` was no type;
  - a member CLASS template (a name after `struct`, `class` or `union`, with no `::` after it);
  - a member ALIAS template, and a class-scope alias, `using N =` or `typedef ... N;` (the name before `;`);
  - a NESTED CLASS OR ENUM (0.201): `struct N {`, `class N :`, `union N;`, `enum class N : int {` -- N as a type, a member
    class template's name aside: libc++ 18's stop_callback delegates `: stop_callback(__private_tag{}, ...)` in its public
    constructors and declares `struct __private_tag {};` under `private:` after them, and the read of `<stop_token>`
    stopped at its first constructor, `std::stop_source` no type (`nestedahead.cpp`).
