  before. `constexpr bool ce = std::is_constant_evaluated();` was false. `constexpr20.cpp` (C++20's virtual calls, `dynamic_cast`, try blocks, a
  union's member changed and a transient `std::vector` and `std::string` in a constant expression).
- A file-scope `const` initialized by a CALL is folded TWICE at its declaration (`cpp_fold_const_inits_`): the first
  attempt EMITS the library instances the call runs through (`numeric_limits<size_t>::max()`), and only the second sees
  them. A value past 2^60 is the initializer `int(big(A))`. Else `inline constexpr size_t dynamic_extent` stayed a call
  and became a run-time initialization (0.117).
- A `const` local aggregate with a constant initializer is an evaluator value, `'$cpp_gagg:N'` = `agg(T, Init, local)`,
  read by `cpp_global_agg/2` only while the name is a local. Traces: `const_agg_not_folded`, `agg_item`. (0.104)
- A file-scope `const` integral object with a constant initializer is a constant ([expr.const]): a HEADER's through
  `cpp_global_const/2` -> `cpp_fold_global/2` under `'$cpp_gfolding:N'`, keeping only a SUCCESS (`'$cpp_gconst:N'`), the
  program's own a named constant (above, 0.195). Why: a failure in an abandoned candidate would stand for ever;
  `__aligned_storage_max_align`. (0.88, 0.195)
- A file-scope `const` object initialized by a constexpr call takes its value (`cpp_fold_const_inits/3`): a scalar, a
  `bool`, or an aggregate spelled as braced items (`cpp_eval_init_term/2`). A file-scope `const` aggregate is a value,
  `agg(T, Init, global)` in `'$cpp_gagg:N'`, so `table[2]`, `origin.x` fold anywhere. Why: `constexpr int N =
  twice(21);` reached the lowering as a call. (0.95, 0.97, 0.98)
- `cpp_const_fold/2` also folds an index into a static member array with an in-class initializer (`get<T>`'s
  `__find_idx`), and a member or index of a call's aggregate answer (`make(5).y`). (0.90, 0.98)
- A static member's braced initializer is walked ONCE per item (`cpp_init_expr`, `once/1` in its `findall`: a
  template-id's call has two answers) and each item is folded, a constexpr call through the evaluator
  (`cpp_static_aggregate`, `cpp_fold_items/2`). Why: libc++ 18's `basic_format_string` holds `static constexpr
  array<__arg_t, sizeof...(_Args)> __types_{__determine_arg_t<_Context, ...>()...}`, which came out doubled and

  not defined (`cpp_has_call/1`), which costs nothing where it is unused -- libc++ 18's `__handles_`, for the consteval
  check this compiler drops. `staticpack.cpp`, `staticunused.cpp`. (0.90, 0.112)
- A `case` label is a constant expression ([stmt.switch]/2): desugared, then folded through the evaluator where it is a
  call (`cpp_stmt_` on `case/3`). Why: libc++ 18's `case __format_spec::__type::__default:` reached the lowering raw.
  `caselabel.cpp`. (0.112)
- A reduction that changed nothing is no value (`cpp_const_fold`'s member and index clauses; 0.121): the evaluator
  leaves an expression it cannot take as it was, `cpp_eval_value` handed that back to `cpp_const_value`, and it came
  here again with the same term -- no depth limit covers a member. `const bool v = as(b).vl();` over a derived class's
  object and a template that returns its argument's reference compiled for 20 minutes (the prologue of `std::visit`).
  `varvisit.cpp`.
- An array bound is desugared in its class and folded, the evaluator included (`cpp_array_bound/2`); else it is a VLA.
  `padding.cpp`. Why: `char __padding_[sizeof(_ToPad) - __datasizeof_v<_ToPad>]` was empty. (0.45, 0.99)
- `__builtin_offsetof` folds from the layout (`cpp_offsetof/4`): libc++'s data size. `offsetof.cpp`. In C++,
  `decltype(sizeof ...)` is `unsigned long`, any other `decltype` its expression's type (`ccl_resolve_base`,
  `ccl_sizeof_expr/1`). Why: through `ccl_type_of`, libc++'s `size_t` went round in a circle. (0.45)

### The constexpr function evaluator

- A call folds through the evaluator first ([dcl.constexpr]; `cpp_eval_fn/3`, `cpp_eval_args/4`, `cpp_eval_call/5`),
  over an emitted instance (`'$cpp_out'(Name, Item)`) or the program's own desugared function or method
  (`'$cpp_ownfn'(Name, Function)`), each found by its NAME, the first argument (0.165: an emitted item that is no
  function is keyed `''`, `cpp_item_key/2`); the door wants a scalar (`cpp_eval_scalar/1`). `constexprfn3.cpp`. (0.96,
  0.98, 0.165)
- Else 0.72's road folds a one-`return` body, the parameters bound as written (`cpp_param_binds/3`, `cpp_replace_ids/3`;
  `this` null). `cpp_targ_value/2` turns `X::template f<U>()` into that call. `constexprfn.cpp`, `stdtraits.cpp`. Why:
  pair's `__is_pair_constructible<_U1, _U2>()`. (0.72, 0.95)
- Both roads stay under depth 32 (`'$cpp_fold_depth'`): a constexpr function may call itself. (0.72, 0.96)
- The evaluator runs statements (`cpp_eval_stmts/4`): declarations, a block's own dropped at its end; effects, also
  inside operands (`cpp_eval_effect/4`); `if`, `if constexpr`, `while`, `do`, `for`, `switch`, a range-for over an
  array, `break`, `continue`, several `return`s. A void function falling off its end answers 0. A type a body declares
  (a local struct's `declare/2`) and a constructor's cleanup of what it built (`eh_cleanup/2`, which only an unwinding
  runs) are nothing to it (0.201). A CALL OF A FUNCTION THAT RETURNS A REFERENCE IS A PLACE to store through (0.201;
  `cpp_eval_placeish/1` over `cpp_eval_ref_fn/1`): `__partial_sums[__i] = __running_sum;` over a std::array in
  `<mdspan>`'s `__static_partial_sums`, and `constexpr std::array<int, 3> r = f();` over such a store was a run-time
  initialization. `constexprstore.cpp`, `stdmdspan.cpp`. (0.96, 0.97, 0.201)
- ONE step budget per fold: `cpp_eval_step/0` counts `'$cpp_eval_steps'` to 200000, so an endless loop fails and never
  hangs; only depth 0 resets it, nested calls share it, and an unset count reads 0. (0.96, 0.98)
- Each local and parameter is a CELL, the global `'$cpp_ec:K'` (`cpp_ec_new/2`; `'$cpp_ec_n'` never restarts). The
  environment holds `N-'$cell'(K)`, `'$t'(N)-T`, and a reference as `N-'$alias'(Ptr)`. (0.99)
- A value is an integer, `big(A)`, `arr(Elems)`, `obj([Name-Value ...])` or `ptr(cell(K), Path)`; the path is `[]` the
  whole, `[2]` an element, `[x]` a member, `[1, y]` nested. (0.97, 0.99)
- An expression is REDUCED bottom up (`cpp_eval_reduce/3`): names to values, arrays to pointers to their first element
  (`cpp_eval_decay/3`), places to contents, a string literal (or the address of a value that is no place) to a pointer
  into a new cell, a constexpr call to its answer (an aggregate as `'$val'(Agg)`), pointer arithmetic, a statement
  expression to its last value, a compound literal. The scalar rest is `ccl_const_eval`'s (`cpp_eval_value/2`).
  (0.98, 0.99)
- AN OPERAND IS REDUCED ONCE (0.165): the reduction tries a clause that reduces an operand, fails and hands the term to
  the next, which reduces it again, so each road a form gains multiplies a chain of n of them -- 0.164's clauses for a
  function's value made `*e` and `&e` reduce their operand three times, 3^n down a chain, and a `?:`, `&&` or `||`
  whose condition did not fold reduced it twice, 2^n. Now `*e` and `&e` of an operand with no effect reduce it once and
  its value decides (a pointer's place, a temporary's cell, a function's value, else the term rebuilt), and the
  condition is reduced once (`cpp_eval_bin_rest/4` the rest of a binary operation); the side-effect test walks no
  literal and no value (`cpp_eval_inert/1`); a static's name and a callee's are split once (`cpp_static_split/3`,
  `cpp_eval_short_name/2`, one `atomic_list_concat/3` where a search took a step a character). `std::visit`'s builds:
  `stdvariantsel.cpp` 13.9 s of CPU where 0.164 took 153.0 s and 0.163 17.1 s, the IR 0.164's (HISTORY.md, 0.165).
- A store through a pointer writes the named cell in any function (`cpp_eval_addr/3`, `cpp_eval_load/2`,
  `cpp_eval_store_ptr/2`, `cpp_eval_padd/3`): `*p`, `p[i]`, `q->x`, a callee's `a[i]`, `this->x` in a non-const member,
  `&x` of a scalar, a reference. `constexprfn6.cpp`. (0.99)
- Pointers into one array compare and subtract by their last path step; a pointer compared with null is not null. A
  method on an object is a call over `&q` (`corner.scaled(3)`). `constexprfn5.cpp`. (0.98)
- An aggregate is built from its braced initializer (`cpp_eval_agg_kind/2`, `cpp_eval_agg_init/5`): by position, by
  `.f = e`, nested braces, the rest zero ([dcl.init.aggr]); an unbounded array takes its items' count.
  `constexprfn4.cpp`. (0.97)
- `switch` runs from the matching label or `default` through to a `break` (`cpp_eval_switch_flat/2`,
  `cpp_eval_switch_run/4`); a range-for over an array binds each element (`cpp_eval_foreach/6`). (0.97)
- `sizeof` over a local comes from its declared type, an unbounded array's from its value (`cpp_eval_sizeof/3`). (0.99)
- The C library's `strlen` over a string the evaluator holds counts its codes (`cpp_eval_strlen/3`), and `nullptr` is
  0 (`cpp_eval_value/2`), the null `this` of a static member function. Why: `basic_string_view(const char *)` counts
  its literal through `__builtin_strlen`, and `n(len(s))` in a constexpr constructor called a static `len`.
  `constsv.cpp`. (0.112)
- THE BIT COUNTS FOLD IN THE EVALUATOR (`cpp_bitcount/3`, `cpp_eval_bitcount/6`): `__builtin_clz`, `ctz`, `popcount` and their
  `l`, `ll` and `g` forms over the argument reduced to a value and WRAPPED TO ITS WIDTH, unsigned (the builtin's own: 32 bits, `l`
  and `ll` 64; for a `g` form the argument's type, read from the callee's declared parameter or a cast, `cpp_eval_width/3`), counted
  on the base-2^30 limbs. Zero has no leading or trailing bit: a `g` form answers its second argument, the others are undefined
  and do not fold. The desugaring folded a count of a CONSTANT argument alone (`cpp_builtin_call`), and the argument of
  libc++ 21's `__countl_zero` -> `__builtin_clzg(__t, numeric_limits<_Tp>::digits)` is the callee's parameter: its radix sort's
  `static constexpr auto __radix_size = std::__bit_log2<uint64_t>(...)` stayed an unfolded static, an undefined symbol at the
  link (`stable_sort` of ints). `bitcount.cpp`, `stdalgorithm6.cpp`. (0.126)
- A CAST TO A POINTER TYPE keeps the pointer the evaluator holds (`cpp_eval_ptr_cast/4`), `cast(T, E)` and the C++ named
  forms the desugaring keeps, `ccast(reinterpret, T, E)`: libc++ 21's `__constexpr_strlen` counts through
  `__builtin_strlen(reinterpret_cast<const char *>(__str))` (the evaluator's `__libcpp_is_constant_evaluated()` is
  false, so the loop above it is not taken but in a library consteval constructor's check, 0.164), and a pointer wrapped
  in a cast was none to `strlen`: `std::string_view s{"true"}` of a constant did not fold, and the static member stayed
  an undefined symbol (`constsv.cpp`, `staticsv.cpp`, `strlencast.cpp`). (0.126)
- A wide literal (`L"..."`, `u"..."`, `U"..."`) is its code units to the evaluator (`ir_utf8_decode`,
  `ir_wide_units`), `wcslen` counts them, and a pointer into such a cell spells back as the literal (`cpp_ec_lit`). Why:
  `__bool_strings<wchar_t>::__true{L"true"}` did not fold and was an undefined symbol. `widesv.cpp`. (0.115)
- `if consteval` keeps both branches, `ifce(L, CT, RT)`: the evaluator takes CT (`cpp_eval_stmt(ifce)`), the check and
  the lowering RT (`ck_stmt(ifce)`, `ir_stmt(ifce)`). `ifconsteval.cpp`. (0.108)
- WHAT A LIBRARY CONSTEVAL CONSTRUCTOR'S CHECK RUNS INTO (0.164; the next topic), the evaluator takes: a FUNCTION'S
  ADDRESS is the value `fn(F)` (`cpp_eval_function/1`: a name declared of function type, or one the evaluator finds, a
  lambda's invoker made in a frame since closed), stored, loaded and CALLED THROUGH (a format handle's `__parse_`);
  `std::move` and a cast to a reference name their operand, as a value and as a place (`std::forward` is
  `static_cast<_Tp &&>(__t)`); an assignment or an increment INSIDE AN OPERAND is done once, where it is reduced
  (`cpp_eval_effect_place/2`: `*__out_it++ = *__begin++`), and the general road never reduces such a term again
  (`cpp_eval_tried/1`); `?:`, `&&` and `||` evaluate the operands C++ evaluates and no more -- an arm not taken may call
  what is no constant expression; the desugaring's `memset` and `memcpy` of a whole object (`sizeof_type`) zero and copy
  its value (`cpp_eval_zeroed/2`), value-initialization's zeroing; an aggregate's item may be a pointer or a function
  pointer (`cpp_eval_simple/1`: `__parse_number_result{__begin, __value}`); an array member given an item that is no
  braced list takes the items that follow, brace elision (`cpp_eval_fields`, `cpp_eval_take/4`: `array<T, N>{a, b}`); a
  class's STATIC CONSTANT is a place, its initializer desugared in its class (the statement's register of temporaries
  set aside) and its value built into a cell once per unit (`cpp_eval_static_cell/2`, `'$cpp_scell'(Name, Id)`:
  `basic_format_string`'s `__types_` and `__handles_`, whose `.data()` the check hands its context); and a header's
  constant inline aggregate is a value (`'$cpp_gagg:N'`, recorded by `cpp_lazy_inline_var`, as the program's own since
  0.97: `__fields_integral`, which every integer's format spec is parsed against). `std::is_constant_evaluated()` and
  `__libcpp_is_constant_evaluated()` are true in such a check alone (`'$cpp_eval_ce'`). `fmtcheck.cpp`. (0.164)
- WHAT THE CHECKS OF A PAIR'S, A TUPLE'S AND A MAP'S FORMAT STRING RUN INTO (0.168), the evaluator takes too. A CAST TO
  A BASE'S REFERENCE NAMES THE BASE SUB-OBJECT (`cpp_eval_addr/3` on `ccast/3` over `cpp_eval_base_path/4`, the
  desugaring's own hops `$base`, `$base$K`): libc++'s `std::get<I>(t)` is `static_cast<__tuple_leaf<I, T>
  &>(t.__base_).get()`, the I-th leaf a later base of `__tuple_impl`, and the cast named the whole object, which has no
  `__value_` of its own. A REFERENCE MEMBER NAMES ITS REFERENT (`cpp_eval_ref_through/4`): its slot holds the address
  it was bound to, so the place `x.r` is that address -- a closure's `$this` and its captures by reference; the tuple
  formatter's `[&]<size_t _Index> { auto &__formatter = std::get<_Index>(__underlying_); ... }` reads
  `this->$this.__underlying_` -- and a member of a reference is its referent's (`cpp_eval_type_of/3`). AN AGGREGATE'S
  REFERENCE MEMBER BINDS ITS ITEM (`cpp_eval_init/5`'s reference clause): the slot holds the item's address, a
  prvalue's in a cell of its own, as the lowering binds it (`ir_init_sub`), and an ADDRESS ITEM -- the item a closure
  gives a capture by reference, `&x` or `this`, a pointer to the referent's type -- is that address already
  (`cpp_eval_address_item/3`, as the lowering's `ir_address_item/2` tells it). A FUNCTION THAT RETURNS A REFERENCE
  ANSWERS ITS REFERENT'S ADDRESS (`cpp_eval_ref_fn/1`): its returns are evaluated as places (`'$retref'` in the
  environment), its call is that place (`cpp_eval_addr/3`) and, as a value, what the place holds; it answered the
  referent's value, a copy, and `std::get<0>(t).parse()` over a constexpr tuple changed a temporary and the tuple kept
  its 0, a silent wrong answer once the base cast let `std::get` through. `constevaltuple.cpp` (C++20: each step of the
  tuple formatter's parse, a consteval function each). (0.168)

### Constexpr constructors, globals and consteval

- A global of a class with constructors -- any initializer, or none where its default construction is no trivial one
  (`cpp_global_object/5`) -- is constructed at compile time over a cell of the class's zero where the evaluator can
  ([basic.start.static]; `cpp_fold_ctor_value/4`, `cpp_eval_construct/4`). A PRVALUE OF THE CLASS WRITTEN AS ITS
  CONSTRUCTOR'S CALL, `Tag(3)` or `Tag{3}`, IS THE OBJECT (C++17's elision; `cpp_prvalue_init/3`, 0.186): the global
  is folded, and else constructed, from its own arguments. The fold took the walked initializer and walked it again,
  and the temporary that the first walk had declared was default-constructed: `const O g = O(3);` and `P g = P{3};`
  were `no_constructor('O', 0)` where the class has no default constructor (since 0.99), and the copy of a
  default-constructed temporary where it has one. `constexprfn6.cpp`, `globalprvalue.cpp`. (0.99, 0.112, 0.186)
- Else it is INITIALIZED DYNAMICALLY ([basic.start.dynamic]; `cpp_global_ctor_init/8`, `cpp_dynamic_init/5`): the
  global stays zero bytes, and the unit's one function `$cpp_ginit` -- run before main through `@llvm.global_ctors`,
  which the lowering spells where it lowers that function -- constructs it where it stands, a placement new over its
  address from the RAW initializer (a prvalue `Tag(3)` its own arguments, `cpp_prvalue_init/3`; a braced list for an
  `initializer_list` constructor one argument), and registers its destructor with `atexit` through a wrapper
  `$cpp_gdtor.N`, in declaration order, so the globals die in the reverse order ([basic.start.term]). `extern` stays a
  declaration; `dynamic_initialization_of_global(N, C)` remains for a static member the evaluator cannot build.
  `globalinit.cpp`. A STATIC DATA MEMBER OF SUCH A CLASS DEFINED OUT OF ITS CLASS takes the same two roads, in its
  class's words and access ([class.static.data]/4; `cpp_static_object_init/7`, `'$in_class'`; 0.186): it took a
  scalar's, `const O O::low(3);` and `const O O::low = O(3);` reached the lowering raw (`global_init(ctor(...))`), and
  `const O O::low{3};` over `O(int x) : v(x * 2)` was the aggregate {3}, where clang++ gives 6. (0.112, 0.186)
- A file-scope SCALAR whose initializer needs the run time is initialized dynamically too (C++ only, 0.117): `int g =
  f() * 2;`, `static int h = g + 4;`, `const int k = f();`, `double d = f() / 2.0;`, `Color c = pick();`, `int
  br{f(3)};`, `int *p = &arr[2];`, `int A::v = A::compute() * 2;` were refused by the lowering as `global_init(...)`,
  for the constant initialization of a global is all it spells. `cpp_dynamic_scalars/7` (after `cpp_fold_const_inits` in
  `cpp_item(declaration)`, and in the scoped-static clause) leaves the declaration's initializer `none` -- the global is
  its zero -- and appends `expr(L, assign('=', id(N), Raw))` to `'$cpp_ginit'`, the RAW initializer, walked as any
  statement of the function is (temporaries, copies), in declaration order beside the class-typed globals; a static
  member defined out of its class is assigned inside `'$in_class'(C, ...)`, in the class's words and access. The test
  (`cpp_runtime_init/1`) is on the desugared initializer: a call that did not fold, a read of a variable (a name that is
  no function, no enumerator and does not fold), a dereference, a member, an index, an assignment, an increment, a `new`
  or the address of anything but a name. Everything else stays what it was, a constant the lowering spells or refuses.
  Never for a `thread_local`, an `extern` declaration, a class, an array or a reference. A global `int *p = new int(7);`
  is still `untied` (the safe part's rule: a global slot with no owner behind). `globalscalar.cpp`. (0.117)
- The constructed value becomes the initializer whole or not at all (`cpp_eval_init_term/2`, `cpp_eval_init_items/2`):
  a pointer into a string literal's cell (marked `'$cpp_ecs:K'` where the literal is reduced) is the literal at its
  offset, `str(Cs)` or `bin('+', str(Cs), int(K))` (`ir_gconst` spells a `getelementptr` into it); a value it cannot
  spell fails the conversion. Why: a member it could not spell was DROPPED and the items after it moved up, `{ ptr 4,
  i64 0 }` for a `string_view` of size 4. `constsv.cpp`. (0.112)
- A file-scope object is declared again under its RESOLVED type (`cpp_redeclare_globals/2`): the table held the
  reader's `std::string_view`, a scoped name the inference cannot resolve, and `g.size()` stayed a raw member call.
  (0.112)
- A static data member of class type initialized in its class is built so and emitted `linkonce`
  (`cpp_static_constructed/4`): `strong_ordering::less`. (0.101)
- In a body, a class local and a temporary use cells too: the declaration, then the constructor over its address. (0.99)
- A call of the program's `consteval` free function folds to a scalar or refuses `consteval_call_not_constant(F)`
  ([dcl.constexpr]/13; `'$cpp_consteval'`, `cpp_free_call/5`). `consteval.cpp`. (0.99)
- So does the program's consteval member function, static or not (`cpp_note_consteval/3` where the method is emitted,
  `cpp_consteval_fold/2` after every call), and its consteval constructor builds a local at compile time
  (`cpp_eval_construct` in `cpp_decl_pieces`: the object's value is the local's initializer). `constevalm.cpp`. (0.112)
- AN IMMEDIATE FUNCTION CONTEXT (C++20 [expr.const]/16, C++23's P2564; 0.198; `cpp_immediate_context/0`): a call of a
  consteval function that does not fold stays a call in a consteval function's body, and in an instance of a function
  template that is being made it makes that instance immediate (`'$cpp_consteval'`, trace `immediate_escalated`), whose
  own calls its callers fold: `template <class T> constexpr int prop(T x) { return cev(x); }` and `prop(4)` are 5. A
  template's instance is escalated whether or not it is declared constexpr (the reader keeps no such mark on a function),
  where clang++ refuses the program. `cevescalate.cpp`.
- A LIBRARY CLASS'S CONSTEVAL CONSTRUCTOR IS RUN AT COMPILE TIME where its object is made ([dcl.constexpr]/13,
  [expr.const]; 0.164; dropped from 0.110 to 0.163): `basic_format_string`'s parses the format string against the
  arguments' kinds, through `__format::__vformat_to` over a `__compile_time_basic_format_context`, and libc++ 21's
  `_CmpUnspecifiedParam`'s is the `0` of `o < 0`. The run-time constructor initializes the members and runs no body; the
  whole constructor -- its member initializers and its body -- is desugared once more as its CHECK TWIN `<Name>.ce`, a
  function the evaluator finds (`'$cpp_ownfn'`) and the lowering never sees (`cpp_ce_twin/7`,
  `'$cpp_cecheck'(Name, Twin, C)`). Where a temporary of the class is constructed (`cpp_temporary`'s two last clauses,
  after the copy pass: the literal converted to `format_string<int>`), `cpp_ce_check/3` runs the twin over a cell of the
  class's zero and the call's own arguments (`cpp_eval_construct/4`), `std::is_constant_evaluated()` true. A call of a
  library throw helper met on the way -- `__throw_format_error(Msg)`, any other `__throw_*` (its name and its string
  arguments: the type error builds its message at run time), the verbose abort they end in (`cpp_eval_abort_fn/2`, the
  first one met kept in `'$cpp_eval_abort'`) -- is the call that makes the expression no constant one, and the program
  is refused by name at the statement's line, the library's message in the refusal, as clang++ refuses it:
  `std::format("{} {}", 1)` is
  `consteval_call_not_constant('basic_format_string.char.int', 'Argument index outside the valid range')`
  (`test/cpp/fmtindex.cpp`), `std::format("{:x}", 1.5)` names `__throw_invalid_type_format_error: a floating-point`
  (`fmttype.cpp`). A check the evaluator cannot take leaves the format string to the library's own parser at run time,
  as before (trace `consteval_ctor_unevaluated`); one that passes traces `consteval_ctor_checked`. `fmtcheck.cpp`
  (C++23: the format strings of 17 calls -- positional and automatic arguments, fill, alignment, signs, bases, widths
  and precisions from arguments, the char, bool, string, pointer and floating formatters, escapes, a wide string, a user
  formatter's own `parse` -- each checked, over libc++ 18 and 21): its 29 checks over libc++ 18 and its 35 over 21 pass,
  none left unevaluated. EVERY CHECK OF THE FORMAT FIXTURES IS EVALUATED SINCE 0.168, none left to the run-time parser,
  where 0.165 counted three left over each libc++ (`std::format` of a map in `fmtrange.cpp`, of a pair and a tuple in
  `fmttuple.cpp`; the evaluator's roads of 0.168, the previous topic): over libc++ 18, 71 -- `fmtchrono` 15,
  `fmtchrono2` 22, `fmtrange` 4, `fmttuple` 2, `formatton` 3, `int128fmt` 3, `stdformat` 9, `stdformatter` 7,
  `stdprint` 3, `stdvformat` 2, `stdwformat` 1 -- and over libc++ 21, 94 -- `fmtchrono` 17, `fmtchrono2` 27, `fmtrange`
  11, `fmttuple` 8, `formatton` 3, `int128fmt` 3, `stdformat` 9, `stdformatter` 4, `stdprint` 9, `stdvformat` 2,
  `stdwformat` 1 -- 72 format strings and 22 checks of `_CmpUnspecifiedParam`; each fixture built at its level, its
  `consteval_ctor_checked` and `consteval_ctor_unevaluated` trace lines counted. (0.164, 0.168)

## Object layout and the ABI

### Structs, unions and bitfields

- A struct has its C layout with SysV packing (`ccl_members_layout/4`, cached in `'$ccl_laycache'`). Each member is
  `lay(Name, T, ByteOff, none | bits(BitOff, Width, UnitBytes) | empty)`. A bitfield that would cross an alignment
  boundary of its type starts at the boundary; a zero width closes the unit. (M2b)
- A PACKED STRUCT OR UNION (GCC's `packed`, 0.203; clang's FieldPacked) lays each member at alignment one, or at what
  the member's own `aligned` says, and a packed bitfield at the next bit, whatever unit of its type it crosses, a
  zero-width one moving nothing there (`ccl_members_layout/5` in the mode `packed`, `ccl_member_align/4`,
  `ccl_union_layout_/6`: `union __attribute__((packed)) { int a : 3; char c; }` is one byte); a member's own `packed` is
  its alignment one (`ccl_size_align/3` over the qualifier, `ccl_q_align/3`); an object's and a member's `aligned(E)`
  raises its alignment and never lowers it, and a typedef's `taligned(E)` replaces the type's natural alignment, lower
  or higher, its size unchanged, which a packed struct's member does not keep (`typedef int I2
  __attribute__((aligned(2)))` is aligned at two, `struct { char c; I2 i; }` six bytes); a struct's or a union's
  `align_as(E)` raises its alignment and rounds its size. A C++ class's `packed` is its data's, a derived class's among
  them (`packedcpp.cpp`), and A MEMBER OF A CLASS THAT IS NO POD IS NOT PACKED in C++ (clang's FieldPacked since its ABI
  16, but on Apple's platforms; `ccl_nonpod_field/1`): it keeps its alignment unless the class or the member says
  `packed`, an array of such a class being packed (`packnonpod.cpp`). Each was dropped (the C reader's Declarators
  topic). (0.203)
- The LLVM shape follows the layout (`ir_struct_shape/3`): one element per plain member, one `[K x i8]` per bitfield
  run (split where no byte is shared), and padding where C's offset passes LLVM's and up to `ccl_tag_size`. The map
  `m(Name, Index, T, none | bf(RunLL, BitOff, Width, Signed))` goes to `'$ir_maps'`. A struct is named once
  (`%struct.Tag`, `'$ir_structs'`); an anonymous one is keyed by its members (`'$ir_anons'`). (M2b, 0.89)
- A STRUCT THAT LLVM CANNOT LAY AS C DOES IS LLVM'S PACKED ONE (0.203; `ir_lays_unaligned/1`): where C lays a member at
  an offset that is no multiple of its LLVM alignment -- a packed struct's, a packed member -- the shape is `<{ ... }>`,
  every padding explicit, and a member is loaded and stored at the alignment its place has, the largest power of two
  that divides the struct's alignment and the member's offset, where it is below the member's own: the qualifier
  `ualign(K)` on the member's type in the shape's map (`ir_map_ualign/4`), which `ir_load_slot/4` and `ir_store_slot/4`
  read (`ir_ualign_q/2`); a union's member's place has the union's alignment, a packed union's one
  (`ir_union_member_type/4`). A natural struct's element lies at its LLVM alignment, padded to C's offset where an
  `_Alignas` member's passes it, and a struct that holds a packed base keeps its alignment by a forcer
  (`ir_align_forcer/2`). A type that a typedef aligns below its natural alignment is loaded and stored at it
  (`ir_talign_low/2`: `*(const u32u *) p` over `typedef uint32_t u32u __attribute__((aligned(1)))`, the idiom of an
  unaligned read). A union's LLVM type has the size `ccl_size_align/3` gives it, an `alignas` or `aligned` union's too
  (it was the members' alone); an object's `aligned(E)`, a pointer object's own and an array's element's are the `align`
  of its alloca and its global (`ir_aligned_q/2`: `_Alignas(16) char g[24]` had none). On SysV an unaligned field's
  eightbytes are MEMORY, as clang classifies them (`ir_leaves/3`): a struct with one crosses a call in memory. A
  member's initializer is stored through its slot's type (`ir_init_slot/5`). Lowering 116. `packed.c`, `packattr.c`,
  `packunion.c`, `aligntd.c`. (0.203)
- A member is a slot (`ir_member_slot/5`): an address, `bf(Addr, RunLL, Off, W, Signed)` or `empty(P)`. All lvalue
  loads and stores go through `ir_load_slot` and `ir_store_slot`; a bitfield run loads `align 1`, shifted and masked.
  `&` of a bitfield refuses `address_of_bitfield`. `ir_ref_of` takes a slot's address only through `ir_slot_addr`.
  (M2b, 0.89)
- A BITFIELD IS STORED EXACTLY AT ANY WIDTH (0.155): the store (`ir_store_slot/4`) makes the field's mask, `2^W - 1`
  (`ir_low_ones/2`), and the run's mask of the other bits in the wide arithmetic (`ccl_w_shl/3`, `ccl_w_sub/3`), and a
  constant past 59 bits is spelled whole (`ir_iconst/3` over `ir_big_text/2`); a global's packer wraps each field's
  value to its width and lays it at its bit offset (`ir_gpack/4` over `ccl_w_wrap/4`, `ccl_w_shl/3`, `ccl_w_bit/4`;
  `ir_le_bytes/3` takes the bytes off). They were cocolog's integers, which had 61 bits through 1.15.0 and whose `<<`
  took its count modulo 64 through 1.13.7 (the Findings): a store into `unsigned long long a : 64` wrote nothing (its
  mask was 0), and so did one into `long long a : 64`; a store into a field of 61 to 63 bits at offset 0 cleared the
  field above it; a 100-bit `unsigned __int128` field kept 36 bits; a global's field at bit 61 or above lost its value,
  and a global's value past 60 bits in a bitfield was refused (`type_error(evaluable, '0xfedcba9876543210'/0)`). A load
  is shifts alone and was right. libc++'s string, whose 63-bit `__cap_` lies above its 1-bit `__is_long_`, was stored
  right (the shift by one dropped the extra bit of the old mask, all ones) and spells its mask whole now.
  `test/c/run/bitfield64.c`, on aarch64 too. (0.155)
- A union is `{ iA, [N-A x i8] }` for its alignment A, `[N x i8]` when A is 1 (`ir_union_type`). A union with
  constructors keeps a union's layout; its tag starts with `union_tag` (`ccl_is_union_tag/1`). Every member lies at the
  union's address. A member of an anonymous struct or union is reached through the hidden member (`ccl_anon_route`).
  Struct and union allocas and globals carry `align`. (M2b, 0.63, 0.108)
- A bitfield in a union is the low bits of the union's first bytes (SysV, little-endian): its slot is
  `bf(Base, RunLL, 0, W, Signed)` over the bytes its bits span (`ir_union_slot/4`), so a read masks and a write keeps
  the other bits. `test/c/run/unionbits.c`. Why: every union member was read at the union's address whole, so a 3-bit
  `al` read the byte a struct member had written; libc++'s `__parsed_specifications` reads `__alignment_` so.
  (0.112)
- A layout uses the data members only: `ccl_members_layout_` and `ccl_union_layout` skip each term that is not
  `member/3` (a C++ tag also holds methods, as libc++'s `union __rep` does). A MEMBER THAT HAS A SIZE IS LAID ONCE (0.201;
  a cut after its size in both, `once/1` over the data size in `ccl_overlap_size/3`): the clause that skips a member
  without a size also skipped one it had laid, on backtracking, and a union of four bytes had the data sizes 1 and 0.
  (0.63, 0.201)
- Layout markers (`align_as(E)`, `virtual_base`, `virtual_base_of(T)`) leave the member list at one door,
  `ccl_members_of` (`ccl_data_members`, `ccl_layout_marker`). A tag with markers is still a plain struct
  (`ccl_class_shape`). Else a marker failed a field walk with no message (`phase(check)`). (0.89, 0.110)
- An enum with an underlying type has that type's size and LLVM type (`ccl_size_align`, `ir_base` on `enum_base(T)`);
  an underlying type named by a typedef is resolved first: `enum class __alignment : uint8_t`. Other enums are 4 bytes.
  An enum with no enumerators is no empty struct (`ccl_is_enum_tag/1` in `ccl_tag_type/4`), so `__element_count(n)` is
  a cast. An enum is no scope (`cpp_path_class`): `Color::Green` is its enumerator. `enumbits.cpp`. (0.55, 0.112) An
  underlying type named by a QUALIFIED name, `enum class Color : std::uint8_t`, is resolved by the desugaring at the
  enum's item and the tag noted again with it (0.194; `cpp_item` on `declare(L, base(Q, [enum(...)]))`), so the table
  the passes build again from the output holds the type the lowering sizes the enum by: it met
  `typedef(scoped([std], uint8_t))`. `enumbase.cpp`.
- An underlying type named through a typedef of a DEPENDENT name is SETTLED where the enum is first named (0.117;
  `cpp_type` on the enum's name through `cpp_enum_unsettled/4`): libc++ 18's `enum class memory_order :
  __memory_order_underlying_t` over `typedef underlying_type<__legacy_memory_order>::type __memory_order_underlying_t`
  keeps a template-id in the tag, and the lowering cannot instantiate a class. The base is resolved by `cpp_type`, the
  tag noted again and the typedef OUTPUT as an item (`cpp_settle_typedef/2`): the passes build the symbol table again
  from the output's items, and a note made during the desugaring is gone by then. The clause asks `ccl_tag/2` with its
  members unbound and a refusal while resolving leaves the tag as it was. Every `-std=c++20` program that stored into a
  `std::atomic` met `typedef(scoped([tmpl(underlying_type, ...)], type))` in `main`. The typedef may be a TEMPLATE-ID of an
  alias template too (`cpp_dependent_typedef/1`): libc++ 21 writes `using __memory_order_underlying_t =
  __underlying_type_t<__legacy_memory_order>;` over `template <class _Tp> using __underlying_type_t =
  __underlying_type(_Tp);`, and the base stayed `typedef(tmpl('__underlying_type_t', ...))` for the lowering (a typedef of the
  program's own is walked as an item and needs none of this: only a LIBRARY header's alias reaches the lowering raw, so
  `stdatomic20.cpp` at libc++ 21 is the measure). `enumsettle.cpp`, `stdatomic20.cpp`. (0.117, 0.126)
- A bitfield is read with its type's sign (`ir_signed/1`, written once in `ir_signed_/1`): `bool`, `_Bool`, `char8_t`,
  `char16_t` and `char32_t` are unsigned ([basic.fundamental]), an enum with an underlying type takes that type's sign
  ([dcl.enum]/5). The same test decides every extension, comparison and division. Why: a `bool f : 1` holding true read
  as -1, and a `char16_t` past 0x7FFF was sign-extended. `enumbits.cpp`. (0.112)

### How values and classes cross a call

- A struct by value crosses a call as the platform ABI says (`ir_abi/2`, cached in `'$ir_abicache'`): `scalar`,
  `direct([piece(LL, Off)...])`, `memory(LL, Align)` (SysV byval and sret) or `indirect(LL, Align)` (AAPCS64's copy).
  SysV: over 16 bytes in memory, else each eightbyte `iN` when an integer or pointer lies in it, else `double`, `float`
  or `<2 x float>`. AAPCS64: an HFA `[k x float|double|fp128]` (k up to 4) FIRST, whatever its size (three doubles go
  in v0-v2, never by reference: the order was the other way round and `d24` crashed), else over 16 bytes indirect,
  else `i64`, `i128` for a 16-aligned value (an even register pair), or `[2 x i64]` (`ir_abi_/6`). Proven against
  aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc under qemu both ways by the cross gate (0.131). (M3, 0.131)
- `ir_leaves/3` gives the leaves from the same layout. A pointer to member function is two INTEGER eightbytes, and a
  complex its two components. On SysV an aggregate with a long double (`x87`) leaf goes in memory; a result of one long
  double or one complex long double comes back on the x87 stack, `%st0` or `%st0` and `%st1` (`ir_ret_abi/2`,
  `ir_x87_ret/2`). (0.100, 0.108)
- A class that is not trivially copyable or destructible crosses a call by invisible reference and returns through a
  hidden pointer, whatever its size (the Itanium C++ ABI). `cpp_note_nontrivial` marks it in `'$cpp_nontrivial'`: a
  destructor, a written copy or move constructor, a virtual function, a virtual base (0.160: its copy constructor is
  never trivial, [class.copy.ctor]/11), or such a base or member. `ir_nontrivial_class` makes it `indirect` (`ir_abi_`),
  the program's classes too. Else `ios_base::getloc()`'s `locale` came back in a register. (0.73)
- `ir_leaves` resolves an array member's ELEMENT type first (`once(ccl_resolve_type(E0, E))`): `unsigned long
  __first_[2]` of a bitset's base held `typedef(size_t)`, which has no size, so the ABI of `bitset<70>` failed -- and a
  failure in the lowering backtracks into the resolver and every statement before it, which are emitted AGAIN (nothing
  undoes an emitted line): the body of `main` came out twice, a duplicate alloca LLVM refused. (0.117)
- An empty class crosses a call as one byte, one `i8` piece on SysV. A zero-size aggregate takes `ir_abi_`'s size-0
  clause, also `i8` (`ir_pieces_type([], i8)`). (0.54, 0.89)
- `ir_fn_sig/6` spells a define, a call and a declare alike. A define stores the pieces in an alloca aligned 16 and uses
  byval and indirect parameters in place (`ir_params/4`). A call goes through a temporary, sret first, and reloads a
  direct return (`ir_call_/6`, `ir_arg_parts/5`). Variadic arguments take the default promotions
  (`ir_promote_arg/4`). `ir_arch_init` sets `'$ir_arch'`: `aapcs` on arm64 (`ccl_host_arch/1`, or `--target`'s), else
  `sysv`. `test/driver.sh` checks both directions against clang (`test/c/link/abi_main.c`, `abi_helper.c`, and the
  variadic `va_main.c`, `va_func.c`), `test/cross.sh` the same files on aarch64 against gcc, and `test/c/run/abi_libc.c`
  goes through `div` and `ldiv`. (M3, 0.131)
- A reference handed to a by-value aggregate parameter is read through before the argument is split into its parts
  (`ir_args_`, `ir_ref_value_type/2`): the value of a cast to a reference and of a forwarding reference is the
  referent's address. `test/cpp/run/refbyvalue.cpp`. Else `std::invoke` of a generic lambda `[](auto a)` stored
  the address as the struct, and LLVM refused it (`std::format`'s visit over `monostate`). (0.112)
- THE SysV REGISTER BUDGET (psABI 3.2.3, 0.117): six INTEGER and eight SSE registers serve a call, and an argument whose
  eightbytes do not ALL fit the free ones goes wholly on the stack. `ir_regs_start/2` opens the budget (a result in
  memory takes one INTEGER register for its sret pointer), `ir_regs_take/5` charges each parameter: a scalar one
  register of its class, an `__int128` two INTEGER, a `direct` struct one register per eightbyte by that eightbyte's
  class, and the struct that does not fit becomes `memory` (byval) -- a long-lived defect: after five `long`, a 16-byte
  struct of two `long` went to the sixth register and the stack, where clang passes it on the stack whole. The budget is
  threaded through the declare (`ir_params_lls`), the define (`ir_params`) and the call (`ir_args_`, the variadic tail
  included). Checked both ways against clang in `test/c/link/abi_main.c` (`budget_*` built by clang, `bud_*` by
  cicilang) and `test/driver.sh`; the 0.116 library fails the new lines. AAPCS64 has no such rule here. (0.117)
- `__int128` and `unsigned __int128` are `i128`: two INTEGER eightbytes, aligned 16, in two registers or none (the
  budget above), 16 bytes in a struct at a 16-byte boundary, `big(A)` constants spelled whole (`ir_gconst`,
  `ir_big_text`). `test/c/run/int128.c`, `test/cpp/run/int128.cpp`. (0.117)

### The empty class and the empty base

- A C++ class with no data members has size 1 ([class]/4; `ccl_class_size`, C++ only); a C empty struct stays 0 bytes.
  The test is the member list, written once (`ccl_no_data_members`, for `ccl_class_size` and `ccl_empty_layout`), never
  "lays out to zero": `ccl_members_layout_` skips a member that it cannot size yet. `char p[0]` alone stays 0 bytes.
  `emptyclass.cpp`. Else basic_string's `__rep_` became a member of no bytes. AN EMPTY DATA MEMBER IS NO DATA (0.198; the
  Itanium ABI's term, a `[[no_unique_address]]` member of empty class type; [meta.unary.prop]'s is_empty, "subobjects of
  zero size"; `ccl_empty_data_member/2`, its type resolved for real): a class whose members are all such is empty itself, to
  the layout, to the desugaring (`cpp_empty_class/1` over `cpp_empty_data/1`; a plain struct, no registered class, by the
  layout's test) and to `__is_empty` -- as a member, as a base, and where its zero-fill would write a byte over the member
  that shares its address. libc++'s `__movable_box<F>` of a captureless lambda holds only such a member,
  `__movable_box_holder<F>`, which holds only one of F, and each took a byte: a `transform_view` over a lambda was 16 bytes
  where clang++ lays 8, over libc++ 21 and, since 0.198 answers `__has_cpp_attribute`, over libc++ 18;
  `struct P { [[no_unique_address]] H h; int *p; }` over `struct H { [[no_unique_address]] E e; }` was 16 for 8, `struct S :
  H { int x; }` 8 for 4, and `std::is_empty_v<H>` and `std::is_empty_v<E>` of a plain `struct E {}` were 0.
  `nuaempty.cpp`, `nualayout.cpp`. (0.89, 0.198)
- An empty base (`cpp_empty_class`: no data, no slots) has no sub-object, as the first base (`cpp_base_layout_`) or a
  later one (`cpp_extra_bases_`). Its address is the object's (`cpp_base_place`, `cpp_base_src`, `cpp_base_hop`); a
  memberwise copy names it by a reference cast. It keeps its alignment as `align_as(int(A))` (`cpp_empty_base_align`):
  libc++'s `__max_align_impl` derives from six empty `alignas` bases. (0.71, 0.89)
- A base's names are found through `cpp_base_scope/2`, the first base, then each later one (`'$cpp_extra'`): typedefs,
  static constants, statics, `cpp_has_member` and methods. `cpp_extra_method` takes the object's address for an empty
  base, `'$cpp_base_slot'` for one with storage. `ctype<char> : locale::facet, ctype_base`. (0.71, 0.88)
- POD FOR THE PURPOSE OF LAYOUT (the Itanium ABI 2.2's term, C++03's POD; 0.135), as clang 18 and 21 decide it, measured
  shape by shape: no base, no virtual function, no non-static data member that is not public, no reference member, no
  member (or array element) of a class that is no POD, no user-provided constructor (a constructor template counts; `=
  default` and `= delete` in the class do not, one defaulted out of it does), no default member initializer, no
  user-provided COPY assignment (a move assignment and an `operator=` from another type do not count), no user-provided
  destructor, and no lambda's closure (`cpp_layout_pod/7`, at registration, with the class's kind for the default access).
  A class that is not one is noted `'$cpp_nonpod'(C)` and its tag carries the layout marker `'$nonpod'`
  (`cpp_pod_mark/3`, at registration and at the struct's emission, since the passes note the tags again from the items).
- A BASE OR A `[[no_unique_address]]` MEMBER OF A CLASS THAT IS NO POD TAKES ITS DATA SIZE, and what follows lies in its
  TAIL PADDING ([intro.object]/7, the Itanium ABI 2.4 II.2; 0.135): `ccl_members_layout/5` advances past such a member
  (`ccl_overlapping/2`: `$base`, `$base$K`, the `[[no_unique_address]]` mark) by `ccl_data_size/2` -- a non-POD class's
  bytes up to the end of its last data member (the walk's own data size, `DSize`), any other type's whole size -- and the
  class's size still covers the sub-object's. `struct D : B { int y; }` over `struct B { virtual int f(); int x; }` lays y
  at 12 in sixteen bytes, as clang does, where it lay at 16 in twenty-four; `struct B { B() {} int a; char c; }; struct D :
  B { char d; }` lays d at 5. `itaniumlayout.cpp`, and the C++ gate's ABI check against clang++.
- Its LLVM element is a PACKED struct of the base's own elements up to its data size (`ir_packed_base/3`,
  `ir_packed_shape/4` over `ir_shape/8` in the mode `packed`), `<{ ptr, i32 }>`; its members are reached through the base's
  own type from its address, as any base's are. A struct holding one ends with `[0 x i64]` (`ir_align_forcer/2`, the
  class's alignment), which keeps the alignment LLVM would otherwise take from it. A global's constant spells the base in
  its packed shape (`ir_gpacked/3`).
- A WHOLE STORE OF A CLASS THAT LENDS ITS TAIL PADDING WRITES ITS DATA SIZE ALONE (`ir_overlap_store/2`, `ir_store_data/5`;
  0.135), as clang copies an object that may be a base sub-object: through a temporary and `llvm.memcpy`, a zero through
  `llvm.memset` (an aggregate's zero first, `ir_init/3`). `NP &r = nd; r = NP(5, 'z');` keeps nd's own member in NP's tail.
- An empty class value moves no bytes. A store to an `empty(_)` slot or of an empty class value writes nothing, and a
  load gives zero (`ir_store_slot`, `ir_load_slot`, `ir_empty_class`). `emptyassign.cpp`. Else libc++ 18's compressed
  pair wrote over a pointer's low byte when it swapped its empty deleter. (0.89, 0.94)

### `alignas` and `[[no_unique_address]]`

- `alignas` on a class, struct or union stays in the tag as `align_as(E)` after the members, folded in the class's
  words (`cpp_align_tag` via `cpp_array_bound`). The layout reads it (`ccl_tag_size` -> `ccl_align_as`): never below
  the natural alignment, the size rounded up ([dcl.align]). `alignas.cpp`. (0.89)
- `_Alignas(E)` or `alignas(E)` among an object's or a member's specifiers is the qualifier `aligned(E)`, which
  `ccl_size_align`, the alloca and the global read (`ir_aligned_q`, `ir_galign`). It raises the alignment and leaves the
  size alone (0.112). As an attribute elsewhere, `ccl_gnu_attr` drops it. (0.99) A member's alignment FOLDS IN THE
  CLASS'S WORDS where the members are resolved (0.194; `cpp_fold_aligned/2` in `cpp_member_types/2`,
  `cpp_split_members/4` and `cpp_plain_members/2`, over `cpp_array_bound/2`), as a bitfield's width and the class's own
  `alignas` do: `alignas(_Alignment) char __data;` of an instance of libc++ 21's `__alignment_checker_type`,
  `_ALIGNAS_TYPE(_Tp) char __buffer_[sizeof(_Tp)]`; the layout reads the qualifier by the inference's fold, which knows
  no template's value nor the evaluator; and through a pointer, the pointee's own, a typedef's `taligned(E)` among it
  (0.205; `cpp_fold_align_qs/2`): libc++ 21's atomic_ref holds `_Aligned_Tp *__ptr_` over an alias aligned by its
  class's static `required_alignment`. A CLASS'S TYPEDEF folds its alignment in the class that defines it where it is
  resolved (0.205; `cpp_ctype_resolve/3`, through the class as `R<P>::AT` and bare in it): `alignof(R<P>::AT)` was the
  aligned type's own. `alignmember.cpp`, `atomicrefalign.cpp` (C++20, libc++ 21), `atomicalign.cpp`.
- `[[no_unique_address]]` is the one attribute the reader keeps, in the member's bit-width slot (`ccl_take_nua`,
  `ccl_plain_width`). A marked member whose type has bytes lies where an unmarked one lies; the ABI agrees.
  `nounique.cpp`. (0.89, 0.96)
- An empty marked member lies where Itanium 2.4 II.3 puts it (`ccl_empty_offset`, `ccl_empty_step`): at 0, unless an
  empty subobject of its type is there; then at the data size rounded to its alignment, stepping by it. It takes no data
  bytes and keeps its alignment. The size is the larger of the data and the end of the empty subobjects
  (`acc(Seen, EmptyEnd)`). A plain member of an empty class counts as one in the way. `nounique2.cpp` (C++20). An empty
  subobject INSIDE an empty member counts too, at its own offset (0.198; `ccl_empty_subs/2`, clang's EmptySubobjectMap):
  `struct T { [[no_unique_address]] E e; [[no_unique_address]] H h; }` lays h at 1, H's E in the way at 0, where it lay at 0
  in one byte. AN EMPTY BASE IS IN THE WAY TOO (0.199, lowering 112): it lies at offset 0 and takes no byte, and the
  class's tag carries it as the layout marker `empty_sub(T)` (`cpp_empty_base_align/3`), which seeds the walk's empty
  subobjects (`ccl_empty_seed/2`, and `ccl_empty_subs/2` of a class over one); a `[[no_unique_address]]` member of its
  type and a PLAIN member of an empty class of its type step past it, as clang's EmptySubobjectMap has them, and a
  member's offset and `offsetof` take the layout over the tag's own list, its markers in (`ccl_offset_member_of/4`,
  `cpp_offsetof/4`): `struct X : E { [[no_unique_address]] E e; }` is 2 bytes, e at 1, `struct Z : E { E e; }` too, and
  `struct R : E { virtual void v(); [[no_unique_address]] E e; }` 16 bytes, e at 8, where each laid e at 0 a byte or 8
  smaller than clang++. `nuaempty.cpp`, `emptybase.cpp` (C++20). (0.96, 0.198, 0.199)
- An empty marked member has no LLVM element. Its map entry is `m(N, empty(Off), T, empty)`, and `ir_member_slot`
  addresses it by byte offset (`getelementptr inbounds i8`). (0.96)

### Base sub-objects

- A first base that is neither virtual nor empty is the `$base` member at offset 0; `this` is never adjusted for it.
  (0.34) THE TABLE POINTER COMES FIRST, though (the Itanium ABI 2.4 I; 0.135): a class that introduces its table has no
  primary base -- none of its bases has a table, or `cpp_primary_first/3` would have moved that one to the front -- and its
  own pointer lies at offset 0, its bases after it (`cpp_vptr_first/3` in `cpp_base_layout/4`; a class over a virtual first
  base too since 0.172, where it kept its order: `Z : virtual A, B` laid B at 0 and the pointer at 8, clang the pointer at
  0, B at 8). `struct D : B { virtual void f(); int x; }` over `struct B { int b; }` lays B at 8 and x at 12 in
  sixteen bytes, as clang does; B lay at 0, the pointer at 8 and x at 16 in twenty-four. Its base is then no longer at
  offset 0: the type information is a vmi one, and an implicit destructor destroys the base where it lies. (0.135, 0.172)
- A later base with storage is its own sub-object, `$base$2`, `$base$3` ... (`cpp_extra_bases_`, `'$cpp_base_slot'`),
  after the first base and before the own members ([class.derived]). It is built and destroyed with the first base
  (`cpp_extra_inits`, `cpp_dtor_body`) and found by `cpp_base_scope` and `ir_base_route`. `std::tuple` and `std::bind`
  are built so. `multibase.cpp`. (0.88)
- A LATER VIRTUAL BASE (0.172; refused as `multiple_inheritance` from 0.88 to 0.171): `X : virtual A, virtual W`, `Y : B,
  virtual A`, and a virtual first base beside a non-virtual dynamic base, `X : virtual A, R1`, whose virtual first base is no
  primary (the Itanium ABI's II.1b: `cpp_primary_first/3` moves R1 first and shares its table pointer). The Virtual bases
  and the diamond topic has the layout. (0.88, 0.172)
- The PRIMARY base is laid out first (the Itanium ABI): where the first base written has no table and a later
  non-virtual one has, the first such is moved to the front at registration (`cpp_primary_first/3`), the bases
  written before it follow it, and the class's table pointer is in it. The bases are still constructed in the order
  written and destroyed in the reverse (`'$cpp_primary_moved'(C, K)`, `cpp_bases_in_order/4` over one group of
  calls per later base, a base with nothing to call giving an empty group). Why: refused by name since 0.108,
  `polymorphic_base_after_a_plain_one`. `primarybase.cpp`, `primarybase2.cpp`. A NEARLY EMPTY VIRTUAL BASE is the primary
  where no non-virtual base has a table (0.174; the Virtual bases topic): moved first, built first, and put back in its
  written place in the type information. (0.112, 0.174)
- A pointer to a derived class converts to its base by the base's offset (`ir_convert`; `ir_base_path`,
  `ir_base_route`, `ir_base_hops`), and a null pointer stays null ([conv.ptr]/3; `nullbase.cpp`). A reference binds the
  same way at a local, a parameter and a cast (`ir_ref_to`, `ir_ref_hops`). (0.72, 0.99)
- A POINTER OR A REFERENCE TO A BASE CONVERTS DOWN to the derived class by the same offset, subtracted
  ([expr.static.cast]/2, /11; 0.134; `ir_down_offset/3` along a route of non-virtual bases, `ir_ref_hops_down/4` for the
  cast to a reference): `static_cast<D *>(pb)` over the second base of `struct D : A, B` kept pb and read D's members
  four bytes off -- a silent wrong answer since a later base had a sub-object of its own (0.88). No static_cast goes down
  from a virtual base, and none is converted here. A null pointer stays null. `downcast.cpp`.
- A cast to a reference is a conversion of its own ([expr.static.cast]): `ir_ref_to` makes the operand-to-target
  conversion (`ir_ref_cast`), then the binding's (`ir_ref_hops`). `basecast.cpp`. Else tuple's
  `L1::sw(static_cast<L1 &>(o))` swapped the wrong leaf. (0.90)

### Virtual functions and vtables

- A class's slots (`cpp_slots/5`, in `cls/6`) are its primary table's as the Itanium ABI lays it (2.5.2, clang's
  AddMethods; 0.177): the primary base's, then each virtual function the class declares that overrides none of them, in
  the order declared -- one marked `virtual`, or one that overrides a function of any other base at any depth, a virtual
  first base that is no primary, a later base or a virtual base a path holds (`cpp_overrides_base/4`), virtual without
  the word -- a destructor virtual by its word or by a base's at its own place, and the implicit destructor LAST
  (`cpp_implicit_dtor_slots/4`). Before 0.177 an override of a virtual first base's function was no slot (`C : virtual
  A` overriding A's g had g at none and h at 2, clang's g at 0 and h at 1), the destructor's pair over a virtual base
  went first, and a destructor virtual by a later base was no slot, so a delete through the class ran no derived
  destructor. A slot is named `M.K` or `op.<word>.K` (`cpp_slot_name`): `__base::__clone()` and `__clone(__base *)` are
  two slots. Its result type is resolved in its class (`cpp_slot_ret`). `vslotorder.cpp`, `vslotptr.cpp`. (0.72, 0.88,
  0.110, 0.177)
- TWO VIRTUAL OVERLOADS OF ONE NAME AND ONE ARITY ARE TWO SLOTS (0.134), in declaration order as the Itanium table has
  them: K is the arity for the first virtual of a name and arity and `A_I` for the I-th (`cpp_slot_key/4`,
  `cpp_slot_arity/2`). A method overrides the one slot of its name and arity, unless it is marked `virtual` and its
  parameter types surely differ (a new overload), and where several slots share them, the one whose parameter types are
  its own (`cpp_overridden_slot/3`, `cpp_params_agree/2`; a type that cannot be compared agrees, so only a sure
  difference makes an overload). The implementation a slot names is found the same way (`cpp_slot_method/6` in
  `cpp_slot_impl`, `cpp_slot_def`, `cpp_slot_pure`), and so is the slot of a member's address (`cpp_method_slot_key/4`).
  Why: libc++'s `money_put` has `do_put(..., long double)` and `do_put(..., const string_type &)`, `num_put` eight
  `do_put` of four parameters and `num_get` eleven `do_get` of five; keyed by the arity, the second overload took the
  first's slot, the table had one slot too few, and `std::put_money` of a string dispatched to the `long double` one --
  LLVM refused the `sitofp` of a struct. `virtualoverload.cpp`, `stdmoney.cpp`.
- A virtual destructor, by `virtual`, by `override` or by a base's virtual destructor (0.177), takes two slots,
  `'$dtor'` and `'$dtor_del'` (`cpp_own_slots`): Itanium's complete and deleting destructors, the second the deleting
  destructor since 0.202 (it held the complete one: the new, delete and placement new topic). A virtual call into an
  object that the shipped library made indexes that object's own table. `vdtordefault.cpp`, `vdtorlater.cpp`. (0.72,
  0.177, 0.202)
- The class that introduces the slots has a `'$vptr'` to `struct C.vt` (`cpp_vt_struct`): a function pointer per slot
  over the owner's `this` (`cpp_vt_owner/2`), a `dying` `this` for the destructor slots. The vptr comes first, ahead of
  the base sub-objects (0.135, the Base sub-objects topic). (0.34, 0.72, 0.135)
- The table `C.vtable` has the Itanium shape `{ [$vbo,] $off, $ti, $vt }` (`cpp_vtable`): the virtual base offset where
  needed (`vptr[-3]`, or further from the slots, after the vcall offsets of a nearly empty primary virtual base, 0.174 --
  a virtual base's own table its vcall offsets after them, 0.175),
  the offset to top (`vptr[-2]`), the type_info (`vptr[-1]`), and the slots, where the vptr points. Each slot holds the
  most derived implementation (`cpp_primary_entry`, `cpp_slot_def`, `cpp_slot_impl/4`, `cpp_dtor/2`); a pure slot that
  nothing overrides holds null. (0.34, 0.108, 0.110, 0.174)
- Every constructor, the implicit one too, stores the primary vptr after the base's constructor, then each secondary
  one (`cpp_vptr_store/3`). A destructor stores the same tables FIRST ([class.cdtor]/4) and ends with the bases'
  destructors (`cpp_dtor_body`). Why: without the store a virtual call in a base's destructor reached the derived
  class's override, whose members were already destroyed (`~A() { f(); }` under a T called T::f). A diamond path's
  base variant (`.nv`) stores the tables of the VTT it is handed instead, nothing where it is handed null (0.172; the
  Virtual bases topic). `dtorvt.cpp`. (0.112) `ir_gconst` takes a function's or a global's address for a table, and a
  global's member's address for a VTT's entry (0.172: `&D.ctvtable<J>.$vt`, a `getelementptr` constant), and the check
  counts `&global` static (`ck_static_value`). (0.34, 0.108, 0.112, 0.172)
- `p->m(a)` of a slot dispatches through the vptr, cast to the object's own `struct C.vt` (`cpp_dispatch/5`); the tables
  are laid out base first. `o.m(a)` dispatches only for a reference or `*p` (`cpp_static_object/1`). A bare `m(a)` and a
  virtual `operator()` dispatch too. A virtual of a base that the class does not name uses that base's table
  (`cpp_hops_class`). `delete` goes through a virtual destructor's slot (`cpp_destroy`). A call dispatches through the
  slot of the method it CHOSE (`cpp_slot_call/5`, 0.134): its name and its own arity -- a call that leaves a defaulted
  argument out has fewer arguments, and `p->f(3)` over `virtual int f(int a, int b = 2)` found no slot of one parameter
  and called the base's f statically -- and, where several slots share them, the one whose parameter types are the
  method's, as declared under its mangled name. `virtualdefault.cpp`. (0.34, 0.72, 0.88, 0.110, 0.134)
- AN OVERRIDE OF A VIRTUAL BASE'S SLOT DISPATCHES THROUGH THAT BASE (0.139; `cpp_vbase_slot_call/6`, on the three roads: `o.m()`,
  `p->m()`, a bare `m()`): a class over a virtual base has a table of its own for its own NEW virtual functions, and an
  override of the virtual base's is no slot of it, so `p->f()` with `const L *p` to an `M` -- `struct L : virtual V`
  overriding V's `f`, M overriding it again -- took the static road and called `L::f`, a silent wrong answer since 0.72. The
  object is converted to the virtual base and the call goes through its table, whose entry is the final overrider (a
  thunk moving `this` to it). `vbcall.cpp`. (0.139)
- `cpp_abstract_class/1` is the one test for an abstract class: a slot with no implementation or a pure one
  (`cpp_slot_pure`). A complete object of it refuses `pure_virtual` (`cpp_not_abstract`; `test/cpp/abstract.cpp`); a
  base sub-object is still built ([class.abstract]/6; `'$cpp_base_ctor'`), as libc++'s `__shared_weak_count` needs.
  `__is_abstract` asks the same test (`abstracttrait.cpp`). (0.99, 0.112)

### Multiple polymorphic bases and thunks

- A later polymorphic base keeps its own vptr in its sub-object (`'$cpp_poly_extra'`), to a secondary table
  `C.vtable<S>` (`cpp_secondary_table`). Its prefix holds minus the sub-object's offset and the class's type_info. Its
  slots are the base's implementations or thunks `C.thunk<S>.<slot>` that move `this` back and call the override
  (`cpp_thunk_entry`, `cpp_mk_thunk`). A thunk is `'$cpp_libfn'`; the check walks the override. `multibase2.cpp`,
  `multibase3.cpp`. (0.108)
- A class derived from such a class makes its own secondary tables for those sub-objects, one `$base` hop further in
  (`cpp_inherit_poly_extras`, `'$cpp_poly_path'`). `thunkdeep.cpp`. (0.110)
- A SECONDARY OR CONSTRUCTION TABLE IS TYPED BY ITS SUB-OBJECT'S OWN SLOTS (0.172; `cpp_slots_vt/3`): the struct `N.vt` of
  the sub-object's class N where N has slots, else its table owner's. A base that shares its primary base's pointer and adds
  virtual functions of its own had its table typed by the primary base's struct, one slot short, and LLVM's constant could
  not hold it: `D : X, P` over `P : PB` with `virtual int h()` was refused since 0.108,
  `item(declaration('D.vtable$base$2'))`. `secslots.cpp`. (0.108, 0.172)
- `delete` through a later polymorphic base calls the deleting destructor through that base's table, whose entry is a
  thunk that moves `this` to the complete object (`cpp_thunk_entry`, 0.202); `::delete` of one frees the complete object,
  found by the offset to top before the destructor runs (`cpp_delete`, `delete_poly/3`). (0.108, 0.202)

### Virtual bases and the diamond

- A class with a virtual first base (`'$cpp_vbase'`) is laid out as a complete object: its own vptr, its own members,
  the shared `$base` last (`cpp_base_layout`), but for a nearly empty one, the class's primary at its own address (the
  bullet below, 0.174). Its own table starts empty: an override of the base's function is a slot of it, and the base's
  virtual destructor makes the class's virtual, its slots where the class declares it or, implicit, last (0.177; they
  went first, `cpp_vbase_dtor_slots`); with none written the class gets the implicit one (`cpp_implicit_dtor_needed`).
  `basic_ostream : virtual basic_ios`; `virtualbase.cpp`. (0.72, 0.174, 0.177)
- EVERY CLASS WITH A VIRTUAL BASE HAS A TABLE OF ITS OWN (0.160; the Itanium ABI's dynamic class, `cpp_has_table/1`: one
  with slots, or one whose primary chain holds a virtual base, `cpp_primary_vbase/2`), a class with no virtual function
  among them -- the tables, their stores and the primary base are decided by that test, a virtual call, `typeid` and
  `dynamic_cast` by `cpp_polymorphic/1` as before -- and it reaches the base through the table (`cpp_vbase_dynamic`):
  until 0.160 such a class had no table, the base stayed where the class laid it, and a diamond over it was refused by
  name. Its struct carries `virtual_base`, or `virtual_base_of(T)` in its `.nv` form (`ccl_vbase_kind/2`);
  `ir_member_slot` adds the offset at `vptr[-3]` (-24), and `cpp_vbase_offset` writes it into every table. The complete
  object builds and destroys the base at its own place (`$base!`, `cpp_class_base_place`). A polymorphic virtual base
  holds this class's secondary table. libc++'s streams are read through the shipped tables the same way. AN EMPTY
  VIRTUAL BASE has no sub-object (an empty base takes no place, the Object layout topic), and the table's offset for it
  is the complete object's own place, 0 for the primary table (0.163; `cpp_vbase_offset/4`'s first clause), as clang
  lays it where nothing else of its type is there (the Itanium ABI's II.3): `offsetof(EB, $base)` named no member, and
  every class over an empty virtual base was refused (`global_init`) from 0.160 to 0.162. `vbasertti.cpp`,
  `vbaseedge.cpp`. (0.110, 0.160, 0.163)
- EVERY CLASS OVER A VIRTUAL BASE IS LAID OUT AS THE ITANIUM ABI LAYS IT (2.4 II; 0.163): its non-virtual part is the
  same in every context and its virtual base lies at the end of the COMPLETE object. A class whose one non-virtual base
  holds a virtual base V -- a class over a virtual base, or a holder itself -- is a HOLDER of V (`cpp_path_holder/3`,
  `cpp_holder_paths/3`; a class with several bases of which one holds V, `cpp_diamond_paths`' second clause): that base is
  its `.nv` form, the class's own members follow it, and V is its own `$vb`, last; a holder's `.nv` form is the holder
  without its `$vb` (`cpp_nv_form/3`), and every class with a `.nv` form has its base-variant twins
  (`cpp_has_nv_form/1`, `cpp_nv_twin`), which build and destroy no virtual base and store no table. A holder has no
  table pointer of its own: its pointer is its base's, a `$base` further in, and a store into a sub-object's pointer --
  a secondary table's, a construction table's -- names it where the sub-object's class lays it (`cpp_vptr_at/3`; `P2.nv`
  has no `$vptr`). The complete object builds V first -- with its OWN initializer of V, or V's default constructor
  ([class.base.init]/13: a base's initializer of a virtual base is ignored where the base is not the most derived class)
  -- then stores its tables and builds its paths by their base-variant constructors. Until 0.163 such a class embedded
  its base whole, V inside it: `struct D : B { int d; }` over `B : virtual V` was [B (its table pointer, its members,
  V), d], where clang lays [B's table pointer and members, d, V], and `D d;` built V with B's initializer. A CLASS HOLDS
  EVERY VIRTUAL BASE OF ITS PATHS (0.171; the ABI's 2.4 III, in inheritance graph order; `cpp_holder_paths/3`,
  `'$cpp_vb_holder'(C, V)` a fact for each, in the order a depth-first walk of its bases meets them): each base that has virtual bases -- one path or several,
  one virtual base or several -- is its `.nv` form, and the class lays them all at its end, `$vb`, `$vb$2` ...
  (`cpp_vb_name/3`), builds them first and destroys them last in the reverse (`cpp_vb_calls/5`), copies each from the
  source's -- BUILT IN THE STANDARD'S ORDER ([class.base.init]/13; `cpp_vb_build_order/2` over `cpp_vb_post/2`, 0.173): a
  depth-first left-to-right walk of the bases, each base's own virtual bases before it, where the layout's walk puts a base
  before its own (`cpp_vbases_walk/2`): `X : B, virtual V` over `V : virtual A` lays V, then A, and builds A, then V, as
  clang's `vbases()` and its LayoutVirtualBases have them (the two orders agree for every shape before 0.173); its tables carry one vbase offset a slot, -24 - 8I for the I-th of the sub-object's virtual
  bases in the ABI's order (`cpp_vbase_offsets/4`, `cpp_vb_slots/2`, the fields `$vbo`, `$vbo$1` ...), a later base's
  own sub-objects with tables get the class's tables (`cpp_inherit_later_poly_extras/1`), and each held polymorphic
  base its own table and construction tables (`cpp_held_poly_extras/1`). `struct H1 : Q1, R1` over `Q1 : virtual A` and
  `R1 : virtual W` embedded both whole, A inside Q1 and W inside R1, where clang lays [Q1, R1, h1, A, W], and a diamond
  over the two, `D : H1, H2`, was refused, `virtual_base_by_two_paths`. A slot's FINAL OVERRIDER where no first-base
  chain reaches it is the most derived implementation among all the bases (`cpp_final_overrider/4`, asked by
  `cpp_final_impl/5` and the construction tables): W's `fw` that only the second path's `R2` overrides was W's own in
  every table of D. `vbasetwo.cpp`, `vbasetwopoly.cpp`. An EMPTY virtual base reached through a path is held too, with
  no member (0.173; `cpp_holder_paths/3`): it lies at the object's own address, the ABI's II.3, and is built and destroyed
  there, its place a cast through `void *` that takes no base route (`cpp_vb_place/3`): reached through a table, it was
  read before any table was stored, a crash over libc++ 21's link. The class kept such a path whole until 0.173, and a
  later virtual base beside it was refused (`virtual_base_laid_otherwise`). The type information's `__diamond_shaped_mask` is set where a virtual base is reached twice below
  the class, as clang sets it (`cpp_diamond_shaped/1`), and a holder of one path is no diamond. `vbaselayout.cpp`,
  `diamonddeep.cpp`, `vbaseedge.cpp` (an empty virtual base, a holder's tail padding taken by a derived member, a copy
  and an assignment of a holder's sub-object, a program class over `std::ostringstream`), `streamlay.cpp` (the streams'
  sizes and where their `basic_ios` lies, clang's over libc++ 18 and 21), `lvbemptypath.cpp`. (0.163, 0.171, 0.172, 0.173)
