  base([own], [char]))`), so `ck_own_type/1` looks in both places. `move(E)` is a node. (M3)
- An owner is linear: every path consumes it exactly once. `free`, `fclose` and `realloc` consume their first argument
  (`ck_consumes/2`). So does a callee whose i-th parameter is `own`, named or read off a function pointer's type as
  `params(Ps)` (`ck_fn_params/2`). `move(p)`, `return p` and a `defer` that frees `p` consume it too. A consumed owner
  may own again by assignment. `test/c/run/owners.c`, `own_struct.c`. (M3)
- The state is `st(Frames)`, innermost first, and a frame is `fr([Key-State ...], Defers)`. `ck_stmt/3` threads it;
  `dead` marks a path that ended. An owner is `live`, `null` (free, move and overwrite are fine), `unset` (no value
  yet, or a field of a struct from malloc), `moved` or `partial`. Other keys hold `borrow(P)`, `dangling(P)`,
  `anchor`, `loose`, `array` or `none`. (M3)
- A join (`ck_merge/3`) keeps equal states. `null` beside `live` is `live`. `null` or `unset` beside `moved` is `moved`.
  `unset` beside `null` is `unset`. `dangling` wins, `borrow` beats `loose`, two borrows keep the one that dangles first
  (`ck_first_to_dangle/3`): a local's before a parameter's or static storage's (0.216; `ck_short_lived/1`: a pointer
  that borrowed a parameter on one path and a local on the other left the function, accepted;
  `test/c/safe/borrow_join.c`), of two locals the inner one (0.217), else the first, an anchor beside a borrow is the
  borrow (0.216: a library object anchored on one path that holds a borrow on the other), and `none` gives the other
  side. Any other pair is `partial`, which is refused on use and counts as a leak. A JOIN KEEPS A KEY THAT ONE SIDE MADE
  IN AN OUTER FRAME (0.217; `ck_only_in/3` in `ck_merge_frames/3`): what a local holds, declared from inside a branch or
  a loop's body in the frame of the local whose storage it is, was lost where the join took the other side's keys alone
  (`test/cpp/librowstore.cpp`). (M3, 0.216, 0.217)
- A scope's end runs its defers last first (`ck_run_defers/3`). Then `ck_leaks/2` demands each owner consumed
  (`owner_leaked`; a loose pointer is `unconsumed`). Then every borrow of the closing frame's keys dangles
  (`ck_scope_end/2`). A `return` does the same for every frame. (M3)
- A loop may not consume an owner from outside it, unless the iteration owns it again by its end
  (`ck_no_moves_across/3`, `move_in_loop`). `break` and `continue` close the frames inside the loop and join its exits
  (`'$ck_loops'`). A `switch` merges its entry state at each case label. (M3)
- A `goto` IS AN EDGE OF THE FLOW (0.133; `ck_walk_body`, `'$ck_bpath'`, `'$ck_fwd'`, `'$ck_back'`, `'$ck_seed'`): every
  frame the check pushes has an id, and a label is where a goto's state -- the frames it leaves closed, their defers run,
  their owners consumed or leaked, their borrows dangling, as a `break` closes them -- joins the state that falls
  through. A FORWARD goto's state waits for its label; a BACKWARD one, the label walked already, is closed down to the
  label's frames, and where the label's frame is one of its own, that frame loses what was declared since the label
  (jumping back past a declaration ends it: its owner must be consumed, its defers run); its state joins the label's on
  the NEXT walk: the function is walked again until no label's state changes, at most eight times (else `not_checked`),
  as a loop's state settles. An owner freed and taken again (`retry:`) settles; one left live and taken again is
  `owner_overwritten`; one live where a goto leaves its scope is `owner_leaked`. The code after a label that only a goto
  reaches is walked now (a dead state had skipped it). A goto whose label no walk reached is `not_checked`. Fixtures:
  `test/c/run/gotoown.c`; refused, `test/c/safe/gotoleak.c` and `gotooverwrite.c`. Until 0.133 any goto in a function
  with owners was `goto_with_owners`. (M3, 0.133)
- A GOTO INTO A BLOCK, OR OVER A DECLARATION, IS FOLLOWED (0.138; C 6.8.6.1 allows both but into a VLA's scope;
  `ck_skipped/4`, `ck_defers_agree/2`): the frames it enters are new to it, and at the label every owner the
  fall-through holds and the edge does not -- its declaration skipped -- is `unset` on that edge, so a merge with a live
  owner is `partial` (refused on use, as `use_after_move`, and at the scope's end), one with null `unset`, and the code
  after the label must give it a value before it frees it. A skipped plain pointer that holds fresh memory, and a skipped
  own array, would be garbage to free: `goto_with_owners`. Every path to a label has run the same defers of each frame
  it shares with the label, else `goto_over_defer`: the defer (or a C++ local's destructor, a defer of the desugaring)
  runs at its scope's end on every path, the skipped one too -- `{ if (k) goto out; std::string s = "x"; out:; }`
  destroyed a string never built, where clang++ refuses the jump. A backward goto into a block ends what the frame it
  shares with the label declared since the label (the label keeps the keys and defers of each frame, `lab(LP, KDs)`).
  Until 0.138 a goto into a block or over an owner's declaration was `goto_with_owners` where an owner lived.
  `test/c/run/gotoin.c`; refused, `test/c/safe/gotoskip.c` and `gotoskipdefer.c`, `test/cpp/gotopastdtor.cpp`. (0.138)
- `ck_consume/6` consumes by its `How`. `free` needs the own fields consumed first (`owner_leaked` names the field).
  `move` needs them live or null (`owner_unset`, `use_after_move`) and moves them along. Then the owner's borrows
  dangle (`ck_dangle/3`). (M3)
- A null test refines an owner and its own fields (`ck_refine/4`, `ck_set_null/3`). `!p` and `p == NULL` make them
  null on the then path; `p` and `p != NULL` do so on the else path. (M3)
- A statement expression's last value is consumed when it is an owner. That is how `clone`'s copy leaves its block.
  (M3)

### Owners inside structs

- An owner is a KEY: a name or a path atom (`'p->name'`, `'c.inner.name'`; `ck_path/2`). `ck_var_fields/3` declares a
  variable's own fields with it: `->` under an own pointer, `.` in a struct by value, recursing into members held by
  value. The base comes first, so a leak names the base. An own pointer member is one key; what it points to is not
  opened. (M3)
- A struct's birth sets its own fields (`ck_alloc_mode/2`, `ck_set_fields/5`). malloc and realloc give `unset`, calloc
  gives `null`, and any other call or a move gives `live`. (M3)
- `ck_into_own/6` assigns an own slot. It takes an owner moved in with its fields (`ck_transfer/5`), a null or a fresh
  value. A borrow is `borrow_stored`, unless it borrows a loose pointer: the slot then takes that memory over
  (`ck_retarget/4`). A live owner assigned is `owner_overwritten`. An owner from an own FIELD has complete fields
  (`ck_complete_rest/4`). Fields move or fill only for a struct held BY VALUE (`ck_by_value/1`). (M3)
- `ck_into_plain/6` assigns a plain slot. An owner is `owner_stored`. A borrow is `borrow_stored`, unless it borrows an
  anchor or static storage; an anchor's borrow is held where the slot is a local's own storage and `borrow_stored` where
  the slot outlives the function since 0.217 (What a local's storage holds, below). A fresh non-static value or a loose
  pointer is `untied`. (M3, 0.217)
- `ck_fill/6` gives a struct by value a whole value. The fields move over from a struct, come item by item from a list
  (`ck_init_slots/5`), or are all live from a call. (M3)
- A struct with owners handed BY VALUE hands them to the callee's copy, as a copy does. They move at the call
  (`ck_args_/5`, `ck_param_by_value/2`). The by-value parameter owns them and must consume them (`ck_param_owners/2`).
  `move(E)` of such a struct moves its fields (`ck_expr(move)`, `ck_kind(move(E))`). `test/c/safe/by_value_move.c`,
  `test/c/run/own_fields.c`. (0.40)

### Borrows and parameters

- A BORROW is a value whose type carries a pointer (`ck_carries_type/1`), taken from what `ck_borrows_from/3` traces to
  an owner: a name, `+` or `-`, a cast, `&p[i]`, `&p->x`, a path through `->` `.` `[]` `*`, or another borrow. It is
  `N-borrow(P)`. Once P is consumed it is `dangling(P)`, and a use is `borrow_after_move`. An assignment from anything
  else unbinds it. `test/c/run/borrows.c`. (M3)
- A plain pointer or array PARAMETER is a borrow of the caller's, tagged with its own name: `N-borrow(N)`
  (`'$ck_params'`). The callee reads it, passes it on and returns it; it never stores, frees or moves it. A borrow
  handed where the callee consumes is `borrow_consumed` (`ck_args_/5`). A parameter assigned anew is a plain local
  from there. `test/c/run/params.c`, `test/c/safe/param_*.c`. (M3)
- The own fields of the struct that a plain pointer parameter points to stay the struct's (`'$ck_borrowed'`). The
  callee may free and replace them, and they are exempt from leaks. They must be live or null at every return
  (`ck_complete_owners/2`, `borrow_incomplete`). (M3)
- Such a field returned as a plain pointer, from a function whose result is not `own`, is a borrow out and stays the
  caller's (`ck_consume_or_use/3`, first clause), as `c_str` is. (0.41)
- A return (`ck_no_escape/2`) checks a value whose type carries a pointer, or a closure. A loose pointer and static
  storage may leave. With a result tie, only what lies within it leaves (`tie_mismatch`); without one, a borrow of a
  pointer or reference parameter's referent or of a global. A PARAMETER BY VALUE IS THE CALLEE'S OWN STORAGE (0.217;
  `ck_param_storage/1` in `ck_short_lived/1` and `ck_ret_borrow/5`): its address returned is `borrow_escapes` -- `int
  *f(int n) { return &n; }` was accepted, the parameter counted as the caller's (`test/c/safe/param_addr_escapes.c`).
  Any other borrow is `borrow_escapes`. A conditional returns either arm, a comma its right side. (M3, 0.44, 0.217)
- THE ADDRESS OF A POINTER OR ARRAY PARAMETER IS A BORROW OF THE PARAMETER'S OWN STORAGE (0.219; `ck_borrows_from/3`'s
  clause for `addr(id(N))`, `ck_param_self/1` in `ck_short_lived/1`), keyed `&p` apart from p, which keys what p points
  to, the caller's, and anchored in the function's outer frame (`ck_param_selves/2`): a return of it is `borrow_escapes`
  (`ownership(borrow_escapes,&p)`), a store where it outlives the function `borrow_stored`, and a local may hold it and
  hand it to a call. `int **f(int *p) { return &p; }` answered p's referent and was accepted.
  `test/c/safe/param_ptr_addr_escapes.c`, `test/c/run/paramaddrok.c`. (0.219)
- A copy of a null pointer, or of a local with no ownership state, is `null` (`ck_plain_copy/2` in `ck_kind/3`). In a
  declaration this holds only for a pointer-typed local, so `int x = n` makes no owner. `test/c/run/nullcopy.c`.
  (0.99, 0.100)
- A value that lives as long as the program is never fresh (`ck_static_value/1`): a narrow or wide string literal,
  `&global`, a global array or function, arithmetic on one, a conditional of two. So a vtable store is no fresh value.
  So is a pointer that the C library answers from its own static storage (C17 7.11.1.1, 7.11.2.1, 7.22.4.6, 7.24.6.2,
  7.27.3; 0.201; `ck_library_static/1`): `getenv`, `setlocale`, `localeconv`, `strerror`, `asctime`, `ctime`, `gmtime`
  and `localtime` answer an object the library keeps for the whole run, which a later call may overwrite and the program
  never frees, and clang's `__builtin_FILE()`, `__builtin_FILE_NAME()` and `__builtin_FUNCTION()` a literal. Each was
  fresh memory, `plain pointer not consumed`. `cwrap.c`, `srcbuiltins.c`. (0.34, 0.93, 0.201)
- A C LIBRARY FUNCTION WHOSE POINTER RESULT LIES IN ITS FIRST ARGUMENT'S OBJECT is a borrow of what that argument borrows,
  static where it is (C17 7.24.2, 7.24.3, 7.24.5, 7.24.6.1, 7.29.4; C23 7.26.2.2; `ck_library_borrow/1` in
  `ck_borrows_from/3` and `ck_static_value/1`): the copies, the concatenations and `memset` answer the destination, the
  searches (`memchr`, `strchr`, `strrchr`, `strpbrk`, `strstr` and their wide forms) a place in the object searched or
  null, `memccpy` one in the destination; POSIX's `stpcpy` and `stpncpy` and glibc's `mempcpy`, `memrchr`, `rawmemchr`
  and `strchrnul` too, and clang's `__builtin_` spelling of each. Each was fresh memory: `char *e = memccpy(buf, s, ',',
  n)` was `plain pointer not consumed`. `stdc23.c`. (0.206)
- A function pointer and a pointer to member are code, which the check never follows (`ck_is_pointer_type/1`,
  `ck_carries_/1`). Else `int (*f)(int) = c ? a : b` was a loose pointer. (0.100)

### What a local's storage holds

- WHAT A LOCAL'S STORAGE HOLDS IS KEPT UNDER KEYS OF ITS OWN (0.217; `ck_hold_key/6`, `ck_held_key/3`,
  `ck_declare_under/5`): the borrow stored in a pointer, a pointer member or a view under its own path (`q`, `s.p`,
  `s.sv`), and what a library container or an array holds, or its elements hold, under `$held` below it (`v.$held`,
  `s.v.$held`, `a.$held`) -- each key in the state frame of the local whose storage it is, so it ends with that local's
  scope. The holder's own key stays its storage's: `&s`, `v.begin()` and a reference bound to v borrow the local itself
  and dangle when it ends, and what it holds dangles when the held local ends. Until 0.217 C kept a local's address in a
  member with no state at all, and a library object's own key took the borrow it was handed (0.216), so `it = v.begin()`
  over `std::vector<int *> v{&x}` borrowed x, not v, and an iterator or a pointer into v used after v ended was accepted
  (`test/cpp/libiterdangle.cpp`, `libptrdangle.cpp`; `test/c/safe/field_dangles.c`, `array_dangles.c`; refused).
- A HOLDER'S VALUE CARRIES WHAT IT HOLDS (0.217; `ck_held_borrow/3`, `ck_holder/1` over `'$ck_holders'`, in
  `ck_borrows_from/3` on a holder and on an array's element): the borrow that dangles first of all it holds, so a
  return, a copy and a library object handed it obey the borrow rules: `struct S mk(void) { int x = 1; struct S s; s.p =
  &x; return s; }` is `borrow_escapes` (`field_escapes.c`, `nested_field.c`, `struct_copy_escapes.c`;
  `test/cpp/libmemberview.cpp`). A READ OF A HOLDER WHOLE -- copied, handed on, returned, a library member called on it
  -- reads what it holds, a dangling borrow `borrow_after_move` (`ck_held_read/2`), and a member's read reads what that
  member holds, not its siblings' (`ck_base_read/3`, `ck_lval_use/3`): `*s.p` after x's block is refused, `s.n` is not.
- WHERE A STORE LANDS (0.217; `ck_where/3` over `ck_resolve/3` and `ck_root/3`): a place is followed to the storage it
  names -- a local reference to the place it was bound to, a call's result among them (`ck_ref_bind/2` keeps every
  binding: `for (auto &row : g) row.push_back(&b)` stores in g, `test/cpp/librowstore.cpp`); a local pointer to the
  local it borrows where the types agree (`ck_points_to/3`: `p->f` over `p = &s` is `s.f`, `p[i]` over `p = a` is
  `a[i]`, a pointer into a library container is in the container; `field_via_ptr.c`); an element a library member
  answers, to its holder, and through an iterator or a view to what that borrows (`ck_lib_holder/3`) -- and is `local`,
  a local's own storage by value, a parameter by value's among them; `out`, storage that outlives the function, through
  a pointer or a reference parameter, `this`, a global or a static; or `unknown`, through a pointer the check does not
  follow. 0.216's `ck_lib_where/2` answered for a library member's object alone, and followed no local pointer and no
  call's result.
- C'S PLAIN SLOT (0.217; `ck_into_plain/6`, `ck_anchor_stored/5`): an anchored local's address stored where the slot is
  a local's own storage is held there; where the slot outlives the function -- through a pointer parameter, a global,
  `*pp` -- it is `borrow_stored` (`store_out_param.c`, `store_global.c`, `store_through_pp.c`); through a pointer the
  check does not follow it is accepted, as C has had it. An initializer's slot lands in the variable it initializes, a
  static's outliving the function (`ck_init_where/3`; `init_escapes.c`). Until 0.217 an anchor's borrow went into any
  slot: `void put(struct S *s) { int x = 1; s->p = &x; }` compiled, the finding of 0.216's probes. A C++ slot through a
  reference, whose type the walk did not know, is refused a local's address too and is otherwise unchecked as before
  (`ck_ref_slot/5`; `test/cpp/refparamfield.cpp`); a library value assigned to a member or an element is held as a
  library member's store is (`ck_into_lib_slot/5`: `s.sv = str`). `test/c/run/fieldsok.c` builds what the rules let C
  keep and prints clang's and gcc's output.
- OF SEVERAL BORROWS, THE ONE THAT DANGLES FIRST (0.217; `ck_first_to_dangle/3`, `ck_first_of/2`): of a join's, a
  holder's, what a library member is handed -- a local's before a parameter's or static storage's (0.216), and of two
  locals the inner one, whose scope ends first (`ck_inner_of/2`): a vector given `&a` and then an inner block's `&b`
  kept a's, and was used after b's end unseen (`test/cpp/libtwolocals.cpp`).
- THE ADDRESS OF A LOCAL IS A BORROW OF THE LOCAL (0.217; `ck_borrows_from/3` on `addr(id(N))`): of an anchored one, an
  owner's slot, and one that holds a borrow -- a pointer, a view, an iterator. `&p` over `int *p = q` answered what p
  points to, so `int **f(int *q) { int *p = q; return &p; }` and the address of a local view of a static string returned
  were accepted, each a dead local's address (`test/c/safe/addr_escapes.c`, `test/cpp/addrview.cpp`, refused). A pointer
  parameter's address still answers its referent: the parameter's key stands for the caller's object (Not done).

### Ties

- `x tie y` says that x lives within y. The reader puts `tie(y)` in x's outermost qualifiers (`ccl_add_tie/3`,
  `ccl_tie_of/2`). `'$ck_ties'` holds Key-Root for each tie: a local's, a parameter's, or a field's per instance
  (`ck_note_tie/2`; dropped when the key is declared again). A tie to nothing declared before, or to itself, is
  `tie_unknown`. (M3; the word `tie` since 0.109)
- A tied plain value is `borrow(Root)` whatever its type (`ck_var_tie/4`). The root is what y borrows when y is itself
  a borrow. Field ties go in member order (`ck_field_ties/5`), so a tie to a later member is `tie_unknown`. Parameter
  ties come after the owners and name earlier parameters only (`ck_param_ties/4`). (M3)
- A tied OWNER keeps its state. Consuming its root while it lives is `tie_outlived` (`ck_tied_consumed/3`). It moves
  only into a slot within its tie (`ck_tie_kept/4`, `tie_escapes`), in `ck_into_own`, `ck_args_` and `ck_no_escape`.
  (M3)
- A slot under a tied base is tied to the base's root (`ck_tied_to/2`, `ck_base_path/2`). `ck_into_tied/6` gives it a
  borrow within the root, a null or a fresh value; anything else is `tie_mismatch` (`ck_within/3`). A member tied to
  an earlier member is the one place a borrow may be stored. (M3)
- Direction: a slot tied to y takes a value whose root outlives y. An owner tied to y moves only into a slot within y.
  A value rooted at a field counts as rooted at its holder. Nothing ends loose memory or static storage. (M3)
- A result tie (`'$ck_ret_tie'`) binds both sides. The callee's returns must lie within it, and the caller's variable
  borrows the argument (`ck_call_tie/3`). A parameter tie is checked at every call (`ck_arg_ties/3`). (M3)
- A result tie may name a static local of the function (`ck_body_static/2`) or a global. The root is then
  `static(Name)`: nothing ends it, and freeing it is `borrow_consumed`. `test/c/run/statics.c`. (M3)
- A tie to a plain local, `&x` of one, or a local array used as a pointer ANCHORS the local (`ck_anchor/3`;
  `ck_anchor_addrs/3` runs before an expression statement, an initializer and a return). The anchor is `Y-anchor` in
  the state frame of Y's symbol frame (`ck_declare_at/4`). Nothing consumes it, it ends with its scope, and its
  borrows may sit in plain slots, as C has them. A static local is never anchored (`'$ck_statics'`). An array member of
  a local struct anchors the struct. `test/c/run/tie.c`, `clone.c`, the eight `test/c/safe/tie_*.c`. (M3, 0.108)

### Loose pointers: every pointer has an ownership path

- Owner's rule: every pointer has an ownership path, or the program is refused. There is no warning channel: `untied`
  and `unconsumed` are errors (owner's decision). (M3, 0.14)
- A plain pointer local given a fresh value is `N-loose`, a root for borrows (`ck_borrow_source/3`). A value is fresh
  when it is not none, an initializer list, null, static, rooted under an unfollowed reference, or a `ck_va_value/1`
  form (`ck_fresh_value/1`). (M3)
- `free`, `fclose`, `realloc` and an own parameter consume a loose pointer (`ck_consume_loose/3`), and its borrows
  dangle. A `return` takes it (`ck_loose_taken/3`), and an own slot takes it over (`ck_retarget/4`). Left at a scope's
  end or a return, or overwritten, it is `unconsumed`. A rebind lands in the variable's own frame (`ck_declare_at/4`).
  `test/c/safe/unconsumed.c`. (M3)
- `untied` ("no owner behind") is a slot the check cannot follow, given a fresh value or a loose pointer: a struct by
  value (`ck_no_owner_behind/4`), or a field, an element, `*p`, a global or an initializer item (`ck_into_plain/6`,
  named by `ck_slot_label/4`). `test/c/safe/untied.c`. (M3)
- `ck_va_value/1` lists what is never fresh: a value read by `va_arg` (the caller's), a C99 compound literal (the
  block's object), a `dynamic_cast`'s result, an exception's storage, a coroutine's frame, promise or noop handle.
  (0.108)

### Own arrays and their drains

- Own arrays (owner's rule: a constant bound, or nothing). `own node *C[4]` is ONE key in state `array`
  (`'$ck_arrays'`, `ck_note_array/1`, `ck_own_elem/2`). It is readable, a root for borrows, exempt from leaks, and
  never consumed by the check: the lowering drains it. (M3)
- An element is an own slot with no key (`ck_into_own(none, ...)`). It takes an owner, a null or a fresh value, never
  a borrow. `move(C[i])` is `fresh`. Moving, freeing or overwriting an element dangles the array's borrows. (M3)
- An own array is zeroed at birth: by calloc, an initializer or a call. One from malloc or realloc is `array_unset`,
  and a local own array needs an initializer. (M3)
- `ck_type_rules/3` checks each local and parameter. `ck_bounds_ok/3` refuses `own_unbounded`: an own pointer behind a
  plain pointer, or an own array with no constant bound. An own-array parameter is `own_unbounded` too
  (`ck_param_ties/4`). `ck_array_struct_ok/3` refuses `own_array_untagged`, since the drain is named by the tag.
  `own_array_by_value` refuses such a struct declared, copied (`ck_no_array_copy/3`), passed or returned by value: a
  copy would own the elements twice. (M3)
- The one other bound is a struct's LAST member `own T *a[n]`, with `n` an earlier integer member (`ck_members_ok/3`).
  It is a flexible member of no bytes, `[0 x T]`. The developer allocates `sizeof(s) + k * sizeof(T *)` and sets `n`.
  A bound is any constant expression (`ccl_const_eval/2`), alike in the layout, the LLVM type and the check. (M3)
- The drains keep every element null or owned. `ir_drain_functions/1` makes `function(0, static, void,
  ccl_drain_<tag>, [x], ...)` for each tagged struct in `'$ccl_tags'` with an own array (`ck_has_own_array/1`; in the
  buckets' order, `ccl_tab_list/2`, so a program with two such structs has the two functions in that order). Its
  body is a `for` per array path (`ir_drain_loop/4`: `if (a[i]) { ccl_drain_T(a[i]); drain_free(a[i]); }`), recursive
  through the element's struct. The drains are noted (`ccl_items_note/1`) and lowered after the units. A flexible
  member's drain loops to `arrow(x, n)` (`ir_array_bound/4`). (M3)
- `free(E)` of such a struct is `({ drain(E); drain_free(E); })` (`ir_drain_free/2`). `a[i] = R` frees the old element
  first (`ir_elem_assign/3`). `move(a[i])` nulls the slot. An element handed to a consumer is `move`d
  (`ir_moved_args/3`). A local own array's drain is a defer of its scope (`ir_array_defers/2`). (M3)
- `test/c/run/btree.c` (`own node *C[4]`) and `btree_del.c` (`own node *C[nc]`, with deletion) are the ownership test
  case, and `leaks` finds nothing in them. `slots.c` gates a local own array, `flex.c` a flexible member. The `own_*`,
  `flex_unbounded` and `array_unset` programs in `test/c/safe/` are refused. (M3)

### What the C++ forms mean to the check

- The check sees the desugared C. `scoped(_, N)` is `id(N)`, a C++ cast is its operand, and a range-for over an array
  is its `for` (`ccl_for_each_as_for/2`). (0.32)
- A reference is the pointer it is (`ck_ref_params/2`, `ck_ref_decl/5`). A reference parameter is a borrow. A local
  bound to an lvalue borrows `addr(Init)`; one bound to a call has no state. The place a local reference is bound to is
  kept for the function (`ck_ref_bind/2`, `ck_ref_bound/2`; 0.216): a store through it lands in the place (What a
  local's storage holds), and since 0.217 every binding is kept, a call's result among them. (0.32, 0.216, 0.217)
- A BY-VALUE PARAMETER OF A CLASS WITH A DESTRUCTOR IS THE CALLEE'S OBJECT TO THE CHECK (0.207; `ck_param_dtors/3` in
  `ck_function/5`): the caller destroys it since 0.207 (the Classes topic), and the callee's code has no defer of its
  destructor; the walk takes one at the body's head all the same, as the desugaring's own defer was before, so its
  owners may be moved from (`push(T x) { v.push_back(move(x)); }`) and are consumed at every exit. With no defer, `int
  len(Name n)` over a class with an `own` member was `owner leaked` (`copies.cpp`); as a borrow, as a reference
  parameter is, the move was `move of a non-owner` (`bag.cpp`, `member.cpp`).
- `'$ck_refs'` names the function's references, and a use of one is a use of its referent: `x = v` is `*x = v`, and `&x`
  is the pointer held. `r.f` is keyed `r->f` (`ck_path/2`). A reference result is a borrow out (`'$ck_ret'`,
  `ck_no_escape/2`); a reference to a local is `borrow_escapes`, a parameter by value among them since 0.217 (`int
  &f(int n) { return n; }`, `test/cpp/byvalref.cpp`). (0.32, 0.44, 0.217)
- Every `delete` consumes as `free`: plain, `[]`, polymorphic, and past an array cookie -- `dealloc/3` after its
  destructor's walk (0.202). `new` is fresh. A new-expression's block is the allocation function's bytes
  (`ck_alloc_mode/2` on `alloc(Mode, _, _)`: `garbage` for a struct's own fields `unset`, a zeroed block `null`; the
  arguments of the call are read), a statement expression `$new...` borrows what its allocation borrows (a placement
  allocation function tied to its argument, below), and `new C(args)` is complete. `ir_cpp_prelude/0` declares `free`
  and the replaceable allocation functions before the check when the file did not (`malloc` and `calloc` before 0.202).
  (0.32, 0.37, 0.108, 0.202)
- A USUAL DEALLOCATION FUNCTION'S FIRST PARAMETER IS AN OWNER (0.202; `cpp_alloc_own_params/4`): the global and the
  class-specific `operator delete` and `operator delete[]` of the shapes [basic.stc.dynamic.deallocation]/3 names take
  the block they give back, which their body frees -- `void operator delete(void *p) noexcept { std::free(p); }` was
  `borrow_consumed`. A placement deallocation function's parameter is as the program writes it. A TIE TO A REFERENCE
  PARAMETER borrows the argument's object (`ck_call_tie/3`, an `addr` of the argument): `void *operator new(std::size_t,
  Arena &a) tie a` hands out a block within the arena, the caller's pointer a borrow of it. `placealloc.cpp`. (0.202)
- The desugaring marks a constructor's `this` `[fresh]` and a destructor's `[dying]` (`cpp_this_type/4`), and
  `ck_this_marker/2` reads the marks. Under `fresh` the own fields start `unset` (`ck_param_owners/2`) and must be live
  or null at each return (`ck_complete_owners/2`). Under `dying` they are exempt (`'$ck_dying_fields'`).
  `test/cpp/run/btree.cpp`. (0.37)
- `this` HANDED OUT OF A CONSTRUCTOR (0.133; `ck_this_handed_unset/5` in `ck_args_`): a function given `this` -- a method
  called in the body, a helper, `register(this)` -- takes the object as complete, its owners live or null, and may read
  or free one that holds garbage. Where an argument is `this` or a member of it, in a constructor (the `fresh` mark), and
  the callee's parameter is no constructor's or destructor's `this` (a base's or a member's constructor initializes what
  it is given), every own field under it must hold a value already: an unset one is `owner_unset`. What the callee does
  with the pointer is its own check's: there `this` is a borrow, as any plain pointer parameter is. `Q::Q() {
  look(this); buf = (char *) malloc(4); }` was accepted and wrote through garbage: `test/cpp/thisunset.cpp`, refused.
  (0.37, 0.133)
- The caller of a destructor takes the object's own fields as moved; the caller of a constructor takes them as live
  (`ck_args_/5`: `ck_dying_param/2`, `ck_fresh_param/2`, `ck_own_under/3`). `ck_arg_base/2` takes any path, and
  `ck_pointee_fields/3` recurses into members held by value, so a member's constructor and destructor update its
  fields. (0.37, 0.41)
- The library's functions are not checked (0.45's decision, which the owner confirmed at 0.190): libc++ keeps raw
  pointers by its own discipline. `cpp_as_lib/2` marks each function a library walk emits `'$cpp_libfn'(Name)`; a
  library template's origin is `'$cpp_lib'(N)`. `ck_items/1` skips them (`cpp_library_function/1`), and compiler-made
  thunks too. The program's own functions and its templates' instances are checked. (0.45, 0.108)
- A library class's VALUE is opaque to the owners (`ck_carries_/1` via `ck_library_class/1` -> `cpp_lib_class/1`). A
  nested class of a library class is the library's. So a map iterator's node pointer is not followed, and a library
  object is never loose memory nor `untied`. Such a value may be moved (`ck_moves_library/1`): `auto r = std::move(q)`
  over a `unique_ptr`. What it BORROWS is followed since 0.216 (below). (0.79, 0.84, 0.86, 0.216)
- A LIBRARY OBJECT THAT HOLDS BORROWS (0.216, the owner's decision of 0.190; `ck_holds_lib_borrow/1`, in
  `ck_borrowing_type/1` beside a pointer's and a closure's): an instance whose template arguments carry a pointer, a
  reference, a closure or such an object -- `std::vector<int *>`, `std::pair<int *, int>`, `std::map<int, int *>`, a
  vector's iterator over its raw pointers, `std::vector<std::vector<int *>>` --, a view or a holder of a callable by its
  nature (`ck_lib_view/1`: `basic_string_view`, `span`, `reference_wrapper`, `function`, `move_only_function`,
  `copyable_function`, `function_ref`, `ref_view`, `mdspan`), an array of them, and a class of the program's that holds
  one by value. A `std::string` or a `std::vector<int>` holds none. Each instance's answer is kept for the run
  (`ck_lib_borrowing/1`), `no` while it is asked: `struct Node { std::vector<Node> kids; }` asks itself.
- A LIBRARY OBJECT BORROWS WHAT IT IS HANDED (0.216; `ck_lib_store/4`, after a call's arguments are walked in
  `ck_expr/3`): a library member's call on such an object -- its constructor, `push_back`, `insert`, `emplace`,
  `operator=`, and an assignment through the reference `operator[]` or `at` answers (`ck_expr/3` on `assign('=',
  call(...), R)`) -- stores its arguments' borrows (`ck_lib_handed/4`: an initializer list's items for the list, the
  object's own borrow left out, the one that dangles first), joined to what the object held as a join keeps them
  (`ck_lib_more/3`) and held under the object's own `$held` key since 0.217 (`ck_lib_store_into/6`; What a local's
  storage holds), where 0.216 made the object's own key the borrow: returning the object obeys the borrow rules
  (`borrow_escapes`), and what it holds dangles where that local's scope ends. A const member, and the lookups and
  erasures by their names (`find`, `count`, `contains`, `lower_bound`, `upper_bound`, `equal_range`, `erase`, and since
  0.217 `at`, `rfind`, the `find_first_of` family, `starts_with`, `ends_with`, `compare`, `remove`, `remove_if` and
  `extract`), store nothing (`ck_lib_no_store/1`), and an assignment through `at` stores the value, not the key; a free
  function's arguments are not its objects (`ck_lib_member/1`): `std::copy(a.begin(), a.end(), std::back_inserter(b))`
  stores nothing in a, and what the free functions that store do is below (0.217). `int x = 5; std::vector<int *> v;
  v.push_back(&x); return v;` and `return std::function<int()>([&x] { return x; });` compiled and ran, each handing out
  a dead local; `test/cpp/libvec.cpp`, `libmap.cpp`, `libstruct.cpp`, `libbyval.cpp`, refused.
- WHERE A LIBRARY OBJECT'S STORE LANDS (0.216, 0.217; `ck_where/3`, the topic What a local's storage holds): in a local
  object -- a local's own, a member of a local struct, an element of a local array, a by-value parameter, reached by
  name, through a local reference or a local pointer that borrows it, or as the holder of an element a member answers
  --, which holds the borrow; in one that outlives the function -- reached through a reference or a pointer parameter,
  `this`, a global, a static --, where a borrow of this function's own local is `borrow_stored` (`libstored.cpp`,
  `libmember.cpp`, refused) and a parameter's borrow or static storage may go, as they may leave by a return; or nowhere
  the check follows, through a pointer it does not follow. A local reference is the place it was bound to, so `auto &r =
  s.v; r.push_back(&x);` stores into s, `for (auto &row : g) row.push_back(&x)` into g since 0.217 (`librowstore.cpp`,
  refused), and one bound to a reference parameter stores out.
- A MEMBER THAT REPLACES WHAT ITS OBJECT HOLDS (0.216; `ck_lib_replacing/4`, `ck_lib_replace/6`, `ck_unhold/3`):
  `operator=`, `assign`, `clear` and `reset` read no old borrow of the object, a dangling one among them, and the object
  holds what the member is handed -- read where it held its old value, so `sv = sv.substr(1)` borrows what sv borrowed
  -- or nothing. A view given a new string after the old one died, and a vector cleared and refilled in a loop, were
  `use of a borrow after its owner was consumed`. A TRIVIAL ASSIGNMENT of such an object, the desugaring's plain
  `assign` (`sv = s`), rebinds it as a pointer's does (`ck_borrowing_type/1` in the `assign` clause of `ck_expr/3`;
  `libassign.cpp`, refused). A library object's destructor reads nothing it holds (`ck_lib_dtor/1`).
- WHAT A LIBRARY OBJECT'S VALUE CARRIES OUT (0.216; `ck_borrows_from/3`): one made in a block -- the desugaring's `$tmp`
  or `$ret`, declared and built there by the library: `std::string_view(buf)`, `std::function<int()>([&x] {...})`, a
  by-value parameter moved out by `return v` -- borrows what its members are handed there. A FREE LIBRARY FUNCTION'S
  RESULT OVER AN OBJECT IT TAKES BY REFERENCE BORROWS THAT OBJECT where the object holds no borrow of its own
  (`ck_ref_object/3`): `Del *d = std::get_deleter<Del>(sp)` points into sp's control block, where it was fresh memory,
  `plain pointer not consumed`; `std::ref(x)` refers to x (`libref.cpp`, refused); `std::begin(v)` into v. A LIBRARY
  FUNCTION'S RESULT OVER A CONTAINER IT TAKES BY LVALUE REFERENCE BORROWS THE CONTAINER, never what it holds (0.217;
  `ck_lib_container_arg/3`): `std::begin(v)` over a `std::vector<int *>` is an iterator into v. A view of a local string
  (`libview.cpp`) and an iterator into a local vector (`libiter.cpp`) are a member's results, the clause on `call(id(F),
  [addr(E)|_])` below.
- AN INITIALIZER LIST'S ARRAY HANDS ITS ITEMS TO THE LIBRARY OBJECT (0.216; `ck_il_slot/1` in `ck_into_plain/6`): a
  borrow in the desugaring's `$il` array is the object's to hold (`ck_lib_handed/4`), never `borrow_stored`:
  `std::vector<int *> v{p}` over a parameter p was refused. Loose memory there is still `untied`. `libborrow.cpp`, and
  `libborrow2.cpp` since 0.217, build what the rules above let through and print clang++'s output over libc++ and
  libstdc++.
- A FREE LIBRARY FUNCTION THAT STORES (0.217; `ck_lib_free_store/4`), known by its template's name, the instance's name
  up to its first key (`ck_lib_base_name/2`): `std::swap(a, b)` and `std::exchange(o, n)` give each object what the
  other held; `std::fill`, `fill_n`, `replace`, `replace_if`, `uninitialized_fill` and `uninitialized_fill_n` put their
  value's borrow in the range's container; `std::copy` and its kin -- `copy_n`, `copy_if`, `copy_backward`, `move`,
  `move_backward`, `reverse_copy`, `unique_copy`, the `replace_copy` and `remove_copy` forms, the `uninitialized_`
  copies and moves, `rotate_copy`, `merge` and the set operations -- put what the source ranges' containers hold in the
  destination's (`ck_lib_container_of/3`: the object of a member's iterator, of `std::back_inserter`'s and
  `std::begin`'s, an array, what an iterator or a pointer borrows). `std::swap(a, b)` over a vector holding `&x` and
  another returned, `std::fill(v.begin(), v.end(), &x)` and a copy into a back inserter stored nothing until 0.217
  (`test/cpp/freeswap.cpp`, `freefill.cpp`, `freecopy.cpp`, refused).
- WHAT A FUNCTION OF THE PROGRAM STORES OF ITS PARAMETERS, ITS CALL STORES (0.217; `ck_flows/1`, `ck_flow_store/4`):
  before the walk, over the program's own functions, a store of a parameter's value that the function itself accepts --
  a library member's (`items.push_back(w)`), a library value's (`sv = v` over a view member) -- into an object or a slot
  reached through another parameter that is a pointer or a reference is a flow `flow(F, J, I)`, and one into a global's
  or a static's object a flow `flow(F, J, out(G))` (`ck_flow_target/5`, `ck_flow_root/3`, `ck_flow_slot_root/3`,
  `ck_flow_out_slot/4` over the body's own names, `ck_body_locals/2`); the flows are closed over the calls among the
  functions, eight rounds at most (`ck_flows_close/4`). A call of a function with a flow holds, in what the caller hands
  for the holder, the borrow of what it hands for the stored one, as a library member's store does (`ck_flow_apply/6`),
  and a borrow of the caller's local handed to a flow out is `borrow_stored`: `Registry r; r.add(&w); return r;` and `V
  w; w.set(s); return w;` are `borrow_escapes`, `r.add(&w)` over a reference parameter r and `reg(&x)` over `void
  reg(int *p) { g.push_back(p); }` `borrow_stored`; until 0.217 the call stored nothing. A PLAIN POINTER'S STORE NEEDS
  NO FLOW, nor does C: a pointer parameter's borrow stored anywhere -- a member through `this` or another parameter,
  `*pp`, a reference's referent, a global -- is `borrow_stored` in the function itself (`ck_into_plain/6`), as it was
  before 0.217. Fixtures: `flowmember.cpp`, `flowwrap.cpp`, `flowfree.cpp`, `flowview.cpp`, `flowout.cpp`,
  `flowglobalvec.cpp`, `flowstaticlocal.cpp`; `test/cpp/run/flowstores.cpp` builds what the flows let through. A VALUE
  COMPUTED FROM A PARAMETER IS STORED AS THE PARAMETER IS (0.221; `ck_flow_value/3`, `ck_flow_pointee/1`): a pointer or
  an iterator moved within what it points into by an integer (`p + n`, `n + p`, `p - n`; `ck_flow_ptr_operand/2`: `b -
  a` of two pointers is a number, which borrows nothing -- `n = (int) (b - a)` made a flow of b into `*this`, and
  `sfinaedefs.cpp` was refused in 0.221's gate) and a place in a pointer parameter's pointee (`&p->f`, `&p[i]`, `&*p`),
  which no flow took: `out.push_back(&p->v)` over the caller's `&s` let `s` escape with `out`, and `out.push_back(p +
  1)` over a local array alike. `flowarith.cpp`, `flowarith2.cpp` (refused), `test/cpp/run/flowarithok.cpp`.
- A POINTER TO CONST THAT A C++ LIBRARY FUNCTION RETURNS FROM NO POINTER ARGUMENT is the library's own storage, static to
  the check (`ck_static_value/1`, `ck_pointer_arg/1`; 0.138): `const time_zone *ny = locate_zone("America/New_York");`
  was fresh memory, `plain pointer not consumed`, where the zone lives in the database libc++ keeps for the whole run. A
  pointer to const cannot be freed, and what the function does is the library's discipline. `tzone.cpp`.
- A class's TABLE POINTER, `$vptr`, is static storage, never memory the check follows (`ck_carries_/1`; 0.127). Why: `V v
  = V();` of a polymorphic class was refused `untied`, a struct by value carrying a pointer given a fresh value. A store
  into it is no assignment the check follows either (0.172; `ck_vptr_slot/1`, the first `assign` clause of `ck_expr/3`,
  which only uses the place and walks the value): a base variant stores the tables its `$vtt` names, a value read through
  a parameter, which the check followed as a borrow stored in the object. (0.127, 0.172)
- A plain pointer that a library function returns over an object's address (`call(id(F), [addr(E)|_])`) is a borrow of
  the object's root (`ck_borrows_from/3` -> `ck_borrow_of/3`), never loose: `std::array`'s iterators. A borrow of a
  library-class local may be consumed (`ck_library_root/1` in `ck_args_/5`): `delete u.release()`.
  `test/cpp/run/stduniqueptr.cpp`. (0.91, 0.94)
- A library STATIC function's pointer result is a borrow of the object it takes by reference (`ck_borrows_from` on
  `call(id(F), [nullptr|As])`, the leading null being the static's `this`; `ck_ref_object/3`): `allocator_traits<A>::
  allocate(a, n)` borrows `a`. A library function's pointer result borrows what its pointer arguments borrow
  (`call(id(F), Args)`): `std::construct_at(p + 2, 42)` returns `p + 2`. `stdallocator.cpp`, `stduninit.cpp`
  (`-std=c++20`: `construct_at`, `destroy`, `destroy_n`, `destroy_at`, `uninitialized_copy`, `_fill`, `_fill_n`,
  `_move`, `_default_construct`, `_value_construct_n`). A direct `allocate` was refused as a loose pointer until 0.117.
  (0.117)
- An address under a reference that the check does not follow is no fresh value (`ck_ref_rooted/1`):
  `const auto &[k, v] = *it` binds a plain value. (0.79)
- A closure is a compound literal of its captures, and it borrows what they borrow (`ck_borrows_from/3` on
  `compound_lit`; `ck_borrowing_type/1` at an initializer and a return). Returning one that holds `&x` of a local is
  `borrow_escapes`; a `[this]` closure may leave. `test/cpp/run/closurescope.cpp`; `test/cpp/escape.cpp` is refused.
  (0.100)
- A closure's `'$this'` slot is walked (`ck_init_slots_/6`), and a bound reference member is a plain walk
  (`ck_stmt(expr(_, bind_ref(_, E)))`): the check follows neither object. It follows a closure where it is made, and
  since 0.216 one a `std::function` holds, a library object that holds borrows. (0.59, 0.61, 0.216)
- A `try` checks its body, then each handler, and merges them (`ck_catches/4`). A HANDLER IS ENTERED FROM ANY POINT OF
  ITS TRY'S BODY (0.193; `ck_try_body/4`, `ck_try_note/1`): it starts from the join of the body's entry state, its exit
  and the state before each statement of the body, each cut to the try's own frames, so an owner the body consumed is
  `partial` in the handler and its use there refused (`test/cpp/tryowner.cpp`); it started from the entry state alone,
  and the handler freed again an owner the body had freed before the call that threw. A `try` that is only a noexcept
  function's terminate guard is checked as its body.
  `if consteval` checks the run-time branch (`ck_stmt(ifce)`). `co_return` exits as a return does. A `dynamic_cast`
  borrows what its operand borrows. `[[assume(e)]]` only reads `e`. (0.93, 0.108)
- A HANDLER'S PARAMETER HAS A FRAME OF ITS OWN in the state as in the symbol table (0.201; `ck_catches/4`): the two are
  pushed together. AN EXIT RUNS A FRAME'S DEFERS UNDER THAT FRAME'S SYMBOL TABLE (0.201; `ck_in_state_scope/2` in
  `ck_exit_frames/2` and `ck_close_to/3`): a `return`, a `break` or a `goto` closes the state's frames one by one while
  the symbol table keeps the walk's own, so a defer of an outer frame that anchors its local -- `&h` of a destructor's
  call, the local's first anchor where an aggregate's braces made it -- put the anchor in a state frame too deep or in
  none; the table is cut to the frame's while its defers run, and is the walk's again afterwards, however they end.
  Each was a check that failed with no word, over 0.200's library too: `H h{1}; try { throw 5; } catch (int e) {
  return e; }` and `H h{1}; for (...) { H d{2}; if (c) return 3; }`. A constructor's cleanup of what it has built,
  `eh_cleanup/2` (the Exceptions topic), is nothing to the check. `throwexit.cpp`. (0.201)

- `&*p` borrows what p borrows (0.132): a reference bound to `*it`, which every `for (auto &&x : r)` over raw-pointer
  iterators makes (std::array, std::string_view, the empty and single views), was fresh memory, `plain pointer not
  consumed`. `arrayfwd.cpp`.
- `return std::move(x);` WITH A REFERENCE RESULT IS A CAST ([expr.static.cast]; 0.132; a `ck_stmt(return(L, move(E)))`
  clause): `T &&` bound to x, which stays the caller's; nothing moves, and the reference leaves as any other does. It was
  refused `move_of_non_owner` for a reference parameter.

### What is refused, by name

- A refusal is `error(ownership(Kind, Name, Form), where(Function, line(L)))`. `dr_diag/3` and `dr_kind/2` word it:
  `unconsumed` reads "plain pointer not consumed", `untied` "no owner behind". The kinds: `use_after_move`,
  `owner_unset`, `borrow_after_move`, `borrow_escapes`, `borrow_stored`, `borrow_consumed`, `borrow_incomplete`,
  `owner_stored`, `owner_leaked`, `owner_overwritten`, `move_in_loop`, `move_of_non_owner`, `goto_with_owners`,
  `goto_over_defer`, `tie_unknown`, `tie_outlived`, `tie_escapes`, `tie_mismatch`, `own_unbounded`, `own_array_by_value`,
  `own_array_untagged`, `array_unset`, `unconsumed`, `untied`, `not_checked`. (M3)
- The kinds not met above: `use_after_move` is a consumed owner used, freed or passed again, the double free.
  `owner_unset` is an owner used before it got a value. `move_of_non_owner` is `move` of no owner and no library value.
  `goto_with_owners` is a `goto` over the declaration of a plain pointer that holds fresh memory or of an own array
  (0.138; until then, into a block or over any owner's declaration where an owner lived, 0.133). `goto_over_defer` is a
  `goto` over a `defer` or a C++ local with a destructor (0.138). `not_checked` is a form the walk cannot follow: a range-for over a non-array, a `continue` in a switch
  with no loop, a goto whose label no walk reached, a body whose labels' states do not settle in eight walks. (M3, 0.133)
- AN ASM OUTPUT THAT CARRIES A POINTER IS REFUSED BY NAME (0.215; `ck_asm_outs/1`): an asm statement's inputs are read
  and its outputs written, as an expression's operands are (`ck_asm_ops/3`), and an output whose value carries a pointer
  (`ck_carries_type/1`: a pointer, an array of them, a struct holding one) throws `not_lowered(asm_pointer_output)`,
  since the safe part follows no pointer that an asm makes. Basic asm names no operand. The driver gate's check. (0.215)
- A LIBRARY OBJECT'S BORROW IS REFUSED AS A POINTER'S (0.216): `borrow_escapes` where the object leaves the function,
  `borrow_stored` where one that outlives the function is handed a borrow of its local, `borrow_after_move` where it is
  used after that local's scope (the topic above). The C++ gate's eleven `test/cpp/lib*.cpp`, and its eighteen of 0.217
  (the C++ gate topic).
- WHAT A LOCAL'S STORAGE HOLDS IS REFUSED AS A POINTER'S BORROW (0.217; the topic What a local's storage holds):
  `borrow_escapes` where the holder leaves the function -- a struct, an array, a library object a function filled, and a
  local's own address --, `borrow_stored` where a local's address is stored, directly or by a function the program
  calls, in a slot that outlives the function, `borrow_after_move` where what a holder holds is read after the held
  local's scope. The C gate's twelve: `store_out_param.c`, `store_global.c`, `store_through_pp.c`, `field_escapes.c`,
  `field_via_ptr.c`, `field_dangles.c`, `nested_field.c`, `init_escapes.c`, `struct_copy_escapes.c`,
  `param_addr_escapes.c`, `array_dangles.c`, `addr_escapes.c`.
- A statement form the check does not know throws `not_lowered(F)` from the last `ck_stmt` clause. Every
  `test/c/safe/NAME.c` is refused with the error its `.expect` names (`test/compile.pl`). (M3, 0.32)

## The lowering

### The pipeline

- `ccl_ir_units/2` builds the symbol table from the units (`ccl_items_note/1`). In C++ it desugars them
  (`ccl_cpp_units/2`), builds the table again, and runs `ir_cpp_prelude/0`. Then come the check
  (`ccl_check_noted/1`), the drains, every item, and the text (`ir_assemble/1`). A phase that merely fails names
  itself: `ir_fail(phase(desugaring | check | lowering))`. (M2, 0.53)
- Each item is lowered inside `\+ \+` (`ir_items/1`). A function's text goes to a global of its own (`'$ir_fdef:K'`,
  `ir_add_fdef/1`). An item that merely fails is `ir_fail(item(W))` (`ir_item_name/2`). An error inside an item carries
  the item (`ir_item_error/2`: `item(W, raised(E))`); a `not_lowered` passes as it is, and the C++ trace prints it
  with the whole item (`item_failed(X, I)`). (0.54, 0.80)
- `ir_fail(What)` throws `error(not_lowered(What), Where)`. A C++ form that the desugaring removes is refused by name
  if one arrives: in `ir_item` (`operator`, `member_of_class`, `class`, `constructor`, `destructor`, `method`,
  `template`), `ir_expr` (`lambda`, `throw`) and `ir_base` (`class`, `auto`). Namespace and `extern_c` items lower
  their items; `using` lowers nothing. (0.32)
- The module text is the struct types, the strings, the globals and the functions, then a `declare` line for each
  external used (an intrinsic's line raw). (M2)
- A SYMBOL PAST ASCII IS QUOTED (0.196; `ir_sym_text/2`): a function's, a global's, a struct type's and a type
  information's name with a character past ASCII is LLVM's quoted name, its UTF-8 bytes escaped, as clang spells it --
  `@"caf\C3\A9"`, `%"struct.Gr\C3\B6\C3\9Fe"`, `@"_ZTIN3\C3\B1s7Gr\C3\B6\C3\9FeE"` -- and an ASCII name stays bare. A
  name's text in the IR -- `__func__`, a type information's name, a contract's message -- is its UTF-8 bytes, its array
  as long as they are (`ccl_atom_bytes/2`, `ccl_byte_length/2`): cocolog 2 counts an atom's characters. A LOCAL'S, A
  PARAMETER'S AND A LABEL'S NAME past ASCII in a register is `.u` and its bytes in hex (`ir_reg_name/2`: `%.uCEBB.4` for
  `λ`, the parameter `ñ`'s `%.uC3B1.addr`, the label `é`'s `L..uC3A9`), since a register takes suffixes that a quoted name cannot and
  no C name starts with a dot; nothing reads a register's name (a variable's is its DILocalVariable's). LLVM refused
  `%λ.4` (`expected instruction opcode`), met by `identutf8.c`. (0.196)
- The lowering reads seven qualifiers only: `own` (moves, drains), `thread_local` (`ir_tls/1`), `aligned(E)` and a
  typedef's `taligned(E)` (`ir_aligned_q/2`, `ir_talign_low/2`), a place's `ualign(K)` (`ir_ualign_q/2`, 0.203),
  `'_Atomic'` (`ir_atomic_q/1`) and `volatile` (`ir_volatile_q/1`, 0.201, below). `const` changes nothing. Nothing reads
  `tie(Y)`, so a tie costs the lowering and the layout nothing. (M3, 0.99, 0.201)
- A VOLATILE OBJECT IS READ AND WRITTEN AS THE ABSTRACT MACHINE DOES (C 6.7.3/7, [dcl.type.cv]/5; 0.201;
  `ir_volatile_q/1`, `ir_load_op/2` in `ir_load_or_decay/4` and the load of a name, a clause of `ir_store_slot/4`): each
  load and each store through a slot of a volatile-qualified type -- a scalar, a pointer's own `volatile`, a struct
  whole, an array's element -- is LLVM's `load volatile` or `store volatile`, which no pass removes, merges or moves
  past another, and an alloca with one is never promoted to a register. The qualifier was read and dropped: at `-O1`
  `volatile double z = 0.0; 1.0 / z` was folded and raised no exception, a division after `fesetround` was rounded at
  compile time, and a volatile local changed between `setjmp` and `longjmp` lost its value. A MEMBER OF A VOLATILE
  OBJECT IS VOLATILE (C 6.5.2.3/3, [expr.ref]/6.2; 0.203; `ir_member_slot/5`, `ir_add_volatile/2`), a bitfield's run
  too, a union's member alike: `s.x = 1` over `volatile struct S s` is a volatile store, where 0.201 gave the object
  whole and not its members. `cwrap.c`, `cwrap.cpp`, `volmember.c`. (0.201, 0.203)
- `ccl_lowering_version/1` (`ccl_ir.pl`) is part of every stored IR's signature (`dr_ir/3`) and of `KB.version`
  (`Reader.Lowering`). Bump it for EVERY change to what the check or the lowering emits, however small. Else the store
  serves the old IR. (M4, 0.103)

### Per-function state and values

- Globals hold a function's state, and `ir_function/7` resets them: `'$ir_body'` (the lines, reversed),
  `'$ir_allocas'` (the entry block's), `'$ir_env'` (frames of `Name-loc(Addr, Type)`), `'$ir_defers'`, `'$ir_loops'`
  (the break and continue targets, with the defer depth) and `'$ir_term'`. (M2)
- Locals are allocas in the entry block, which `mem2reg` lifts. A struct or union alloca is aligned as C aligns it,
  and `aligned(E)` raises the alignment (`ir_alloca_typed/2`). `ir_ins/1` opens a dead block after a terminator, so
  every block ends once. (M2, 0.99)
- A function that falls off its end returns its result's zero (`ir_zero/2`); `main` returns 0. A function item with no
  body is a prototype, and its `declare` comes from the externals a call names. (M2, 0.54)
- `ir_expr/4` gives a value, its resolved C type and its LLVM type (owner's request, 2026-09-06: the LLVM type travels
  with the value, and no consumer derives it again from the C type). A decayed array is `ptr` (`ir_value_ll/2`).
  `ir_lval/4` gives a slot with the same two types. `ir_load_slot/4`, `ir_store_slot/4`, `ir_convert/6`,
  `ir_binary/8` and `ir_arith_op/4` take the LLVM type; `ir_cond/2` makes an `i1`. The /3 forms and `ir_convert/4` are
  wrappers. (2026-09-06)
- `ir_type/2` is cached per type term (`'$ir_tcache'`). A pointer, a reference and a function are `ptr`; an array is
  `[N x T]`, or `[0 x T]` without a constant bound. (M2)
- Signed integer arithmetic is `nsw`, and every address is `getelementptr inbounds` (`ir_arith_op/4`, `ir_step/6`). C
  leaves signed overflow and addresses past the object undefined. So LLVM widens loop counters and drops the sign
  extensions before an index. (2026-09-05)
- AN ASSIGNMENT'S RIGHT OPERAND IS EVALUATED FIRST, then its place ([expr.ass]/1, C++17; 0.197): `a[i++] = i`, `*f() = g()`
  and `x += y()` -- a compound assignment reads its left operand after the right one -- in C as clang orders them too (C
  leaves the order unspecified, 6.5.16/3). The lowering evaluated the place first: `v[f()] = g()` called f before g, where
  clang++ calls g first. The check walks the right operand first in its assignment clauses (`ck_expr/3`), so an owner that
  the right side moves is moved before the left side's place is read. An overloaded assignment operator's operands are
  sequenced as the built-in's ([over.match.oper]/2): the right one is evaluated first into a local `$rhs` where the
  operator's second parameter is a reference, a pointer or an arithmetic value (`cpp_rhs_first/2`; an operand with no side
  effect, `cpp_fixed_operand/1`, keeps the call), and since 0.198 where it takes a class by value (`cpp_rhs_first/2`'s
  second clause): the argument's temporary is built first and the object bound after it, a reference `$lhs`, the temporary
  handed on in place -- `left() = right();` over `S &operator=(S)` called left() first, and `left() = lref();` copied
  `lref()`'s object after it called left(). `test/c/run/evalorder.c`, `test/cpp/run/evalorder.cpp`, `assignbyval.cpp`.
- `int(N)` is `i32`, or `long` past 32 bits; `uint`, `long` and `ulong` keep their suffix's type, but a `uint` past
  UINT_MAX is an `unsigned long` and a `long(big(A))` past LONG_MAX an `unsigned long`, as the inference has them (0.201,
  the Integer literals topic: `i32 4294967296` was 0). A `big(Atom)` past 2^60 is spelled as written (`ir_big_text/2`;
  `u0x...` for hex). A character literal is a `char` in C++ and an `int`
  in C. `__func__` and `__FUNCTION__` are the function's name, and C's `__PRETTY_FUNCTION__` its signature as clang
  spells it (`ir_c_pretty/1`, 0.166). (0.42, 0.78, 0.94, 0.108, 0.166, 0.201)
- A double prints as LLVM's hex (`ir_double/2`). A floating global is spelled for its own type (`ir_fp_const/3`): a
  float as the double hex of its value rounded to a float, `x86_fp80` in the `0xK` form, `_Float16` as `half`. (M2,
  0.108)
- A floating constant folds as the target computes it (0.132): a subnormal double is spelled on the 2^-1074 grid
  (`ir_double/2`; the exponent was taken past -1022 and the bits lost), an infinity as the format's own
  (`ccl_float_infinite/1`), a cast to `float` or `_Float16` in an initializer rounds to that type before the value goes
  on (`ir_fp_to/3`: `double d = (float) 0.1;` is 0.100000001490116, as clang has it; past the type's range its
  infinity), and a division by zero is the signed infinity. A tie rounds to the even value (0.154; `ir_round_even/2` in
  `ir_round_bits/5`): `round/1` takes a tie away from zero, so `float g = 16777217.0;` was 16777218 and `_Float16 h =
  2049.0;` 2050 at file scope, where clang has 16777216 and 2048 (a local was right: its constant is LLVM's to round).
  `test/c/run/fpconst.c`. (0.132, 0.154)
- A NEGATIVE ZERO, AN INFINITY AND A NaN IN A FLOATING CONSTANT are folded as clang folds them (0.143). A negative zero
  keeps its sign (`ir_double`, `ir_x87`, `ir_quad` over `ir_neg_zero/1`, the sign read off the text cocolog writes,
  `-0.0`, since it has no `copysign/2`): `double g = -0.0;`, a static's, an array's item, `0.0 * -1.0`, a float and a
  long double were +0.0. A constant divided by a negative zero is the infinity of the other sign. `INFINITY`, `HUGE_VAL`
  and `NAN`, the builtins behind them, fold in a global's initializer (`ir_fp_builtin_value/3`), which refused them
  (`global_init(call(id('__builtin_nanf'), ...))`). An invalid operation -- `0.0 / 0.0`, `1e999 - 1e999`, `0.0 *
  INFINITY` -- is the positive quiet NaN, a NaN operand gives itself, a negation flips a NaN's sign; the fold carries a
  NaN as `nan(S)`, since cocolog writes no NaN's sign, and spells it by `ir_fp_nan_text/3` (`ir_fp_nan/1`). No NaN
  reaches `ir_double/2`, whose first test, `F =:= 0.0`, took one for a zero through cocolog 2.1.1, whose `=:=` held for
  a NaN against any number. `test/c/run/negzero.c`, `fpspecial.c` (both on aarch64 too). Lowering 82. A DOUBLE'S `+ - *
  /` IS FOLDED ON THE LONG DOUBLE'S EXACT ROAD since 0.158 (`ir_fp_op/4` over `ir_x_op/4` and `ir_fp_round_to/3`): each
  operand converted to a double first, the exact result rounded once, as IEEE 754 has it, its infinities, NaNs and
  signed zeros `ir_x_op/4`'s; it was the engine's own float arithmetic, which raises at an infinity, at a NaN and at a
  division by a float zero since cocolog 2.2.0. Two integers keep the integer arithmetic the fold had where the integer
  evaluator gave up (`ir_fp_op_/4`). On 2.1.0 the two roads give the same IR for the 80 C run fixtures. (0.143, 0.158)
- A local shadows an enumerator: `ir_expr(id(N))` asks `ir_lookup/2` before `ccl_enum_value/2`. An enumerator is a
  literal of its value (0.160): an int, or a value no int holds the type its literal has. Else an enumerator of libc++'s
  `<format>`, `__ptr`, replaced a parameter. `test/c/run/enumshadow.c`, `test/cpp/run/enumshadow.cpp`. (0.94, 0.160)
- `ir_convert/6` tries, in order: a reference read through, where a reference to a function is its address ([conv.func])
  and a reference to an array the array's, which decays ([conv.array]; 0.167: libc++'s `__invoke` writes
  `static_cast<_Args &&>(__args)`, and over a literal's `const char (&)[5]` the cast's value was loaded whole, an
  `inttoptr` of `[5 x i8]`); a class pointer to its base by the base's offset, null kept null by a `select`
  ([conv.ptr]/3; `nullbase.cpp`); a member-function pointer's `adj` grown by a base's offset; a complex value; the
  scalar rules. (0.61, 0.72, 0.84, 0.99, 0.108, 0.167)
- The scalar rules first convert to `bool` or `_Bool` (`ir_to_bool/4`): `icmp ne`, `fcmp une`, or a member-function
  pointer's `ptr` against null, then `zext` to `i8`. `bool` and `char8_t` are `i8`. (0.32, 0.108)

### Control flow and defer

- `defer` is scope-bound and static, with no runtime (owner's rule). `ir_defer_push/1` registers a body in its scope's
  frame. `ir_run_defers/1` inlines the bodies last first: at a block's end, at `break` and `continue` (the frames inside
  the loop), and at `return` (every frame, after the value is computed). A statement expression runs its own block's
  defers. A `goto` runs the defers of the scopes it leaves (0.133, below). Each body runs under the bodies not run yet
  and under the tries that enclose its frame (`ir_run_exit/2`, 0.201: the Exceptions topic), and a body pushed as
  `eh_only(B)` runs only in a landing pad (`ir_run_bodies/1`, 0.201). (M2, 0.201)
- A GOTO RUNS THE DEFERS OF THE SCOPES IT LEAVES (0.133; [stmt.jump]/2: leaving a block by any jump destroys its
  objects; the language's `defer` runs at every exit of its scope; `ir_goto/3`, `ir_label_here/2`): each frame the
  lowering pushes has an id (`ir_bpath_push`, `'$ir_bpath'`), and a label records its path and how many defers its own
  frame holds (`'$ir_labels'`). A goto to a label already lowered (backward) runs the frames from its own down to the one
  it shares with the label and, where the label's frame is one of its own, the defers that frame gained since the label
  (`retry: std::string s = f(); ... goto retry;` jumps back past s, which dies; `ir_run_since_label/2`). A goto to a label
  still ahead branches to a block of its own (`'$ir_fwd'`), emitted where the label is lowered, which runs those frames
  under the goto's own scope -- its locals, its defers -- then branches on (`ir_trampolines/3`). A goto from scopes with
  no defer branches straight to its label. It was a bare branch: `goto out;` from a block skipped a C++ local's
  destructor and a `defer`. `test/c/run/gotodefer.c`, `test/cpp/run/gotodtor.cpp`. (0.133)
- A GOTO INTO A BLOCK (0.138): a label records the defers and the VLAs of each of its frames (`lab(LP, Counts, Vlas)`), a
  forward goto the same of its own (`'$ir_fwdk'`); a jump over a defer of the frame it shares with the label, or into a
  frame that holds one before the label, is `goto_over_defer(L)` (the check refuses it where it walks; this covers a
  defer in code only a goto skips), and a jump into the scope of a VLA `goto_into_vla(L)` (C 6.8.6.1/1, as clang
  refuses it: the array's size was never computed; `ir_skip_check/5`). A backward goto into a block runs the defers its
  shared frame gained since the label, as one in the label's own frame does. (0.138)
- A conditional is a `phi` of its arms in their usual type -- in C++ the arms' own type where both are of ONE arithmetic
  type (`ccl_cond_arith/3`, 0.127) -- and void arms have no phi ([expr.cond]/2; `ir_expr(cond)`'s first clause, which
  tests the first arm). Else LLVM refused `phi void` in libc++ 18's string algorithms. `test/cpp/run/voidcond.cpp`.
  (0.95, 0.127)
- A conditional of a pointer and the literal zero is the POINTER, in C and C++ (`ir_expr(cond)`: both arms arithmetic
  give the usual conversion, else the null constant's arm takes the other arm's pointer type). The phi was `i32` and the
  address went through it truncated: `deque::begin()` returned a pointer whose high half was gone.
  `test/c/run/condnull.c` (the safe part refuses a plain pointer stored in a struct, so the program keeps its pointers
  in locals). (0.117)
- A conditional over two lvalues is an lvalue whose address is the phi of the arms' addresses ([expr.cond]/4;
  `ir_lvalue_form/1`, `ir_lval(cond)`). Else `std::min(a, b).c_str()` read a dead temporary.
  `test/cpp/run/condlvalue.cpp`. (0.92)
- `&&` and `||` branch and join in a `phi i1`. A comparison, `!`, `&&` and `||` give C's `int` (`ir_bool/2`) and C++'s
  `bool`, an `i8` (`ir_truth/4`, the inference's `ccl_truth_type/1`; 0.127). (M2, 0.127)
- An ENUMERATOR is a prvalue (`ir_lvalue_form(id(N))` over `ir_enumerator/1`): bound to `const Color &` it takes the
  temporary C++ materializes. Why: `v.push_back(Green)` bound it through `ir_lval` and it was `undeclared`. (0.127)
- A `switch` COMPARES AT ITS CONDITION'S PROMOTED TYPE (C 6.8.4.2/5, [stmt.switch]/2; 0.201; `ir_switch_type/3`,
  `ir_case_value/3`, `ir_case_lines/4` over `ccl_const_eval/2`): the integer promotions on its value, each case's
  constant converted to that type. It finds its cases at the top level of its block (`ir_switch_cases/3`). Every switch
  was an `i32` one: `switch (x)` of `long x = 0x100000001` took `case 1:`, and a case of `18446744073709551615ULL`
  raised a type error. `littype.c`. (M2, 0.201)
- A range-for over an array is `for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) { T x = xs[i]; S }` for both passes
  (`ccl_for_each_as_for/2`); `auto &` and `auto &&` bind a reference. Any other range-for that reaches the lowering is
  `range_for_over_non_array`. (0.32)

### References, temporaries, moves and new (C++)

- A reference is a pointer bound once. A local's slot holds the address (`ir_locals/2` through `ir_ref_to/3`), and a
  use loads it first (`ir_ref_slot/4`). A reference parameter takes the argument's address (`ir_args_/4`). A reference
  result returns the address (`ir_stmt(return)`, `ir_lval(call)`) and is read through for a value (`ir_expr(call)`).
  (0.32) A reference to an array bound to a string literal holds the literal's own global (0.167; `ir_ref_to/3`'s first
  clause over `ir_string_literal/1`), where it held a temporary pointer to it.
- `ir_ref_of/2` gives what a reference binds: an lvalue's address (through `ir_slot_addr/2`), the operand of `move(E)`
  or of a cast to a reference, or a call's reference result. A call's value or any other prvalue gets the temporary
  C++ materializes, as `v.push_back(1)` needs. (0.50, 0.58, 0.83)
- A cast to a reference is a bind, never a value conversion: its value is the address (`ir_expr(cast(T, E))` ->
  `ir_ref_to/3`). The cast's own base offset applies first (`ir_ref_cast/3`), then the binding's (`ir_ref_hops/4`).
  Else `static_cast<_Tp &&>(__t)`, `std::forward`'s body, made an `inttoptr`. `test/cpp/run/stdvector.cpp`,
  `basecast.cpp`. A CAST TO A REFERENCE TO A SCALAR -- arithmetic, enumeration, pointer -- has the scalar's value where a
  value is wanted ([expr.type]/1; 0.201; `ir_scalar_referent/1`), and a binding takes the operand's address as before
  (`ir_ref_of/2`, `ir_ref_to/3`, `ir_lval/4`, a reference result's `return`): `static_cast<int &&>(x) + 1` was the
  address, `not_a_pointer`, a condition over one tested the address, and an ellipsis argument passed it. `xvcast.cpp`.
  (0.61, 0.90, 0.201)
- A function bound to a reference to a pointer converts first, and the reference binds the temporary pointer
  ([conv.func]; `ir_ref_to/3`). Else libc++'s `__tuple_leaf` loaded code bytes. `test/cpp/run/fnrefptr.cpp`. (0.100)
- A POINTER OPERAND THAT IS A REFERENCE TO A POINTER IS READ THROUGH (`ir_ptr_operand/3`, asked by the lvalue forms of `*e`,
  `e[i]` and `e->m`; 0.126): `*static_cast<A0 &&>(a0)` with `A0` `Pt *` -- the cast to a reference is a bind (the bullet
  above), so its value is the ADDRESS of the pointer and its type `Pt *&&`, and `ir_elem` found no pointer in it
  (`not_a_pointer(rref(...))`). A named reference or a call's reference result is read through where it is made, so only a
  cast met it. libc++ 18's `__invoke` for a data member pointer and an object given by pointer is written so,
  `(*static_cast<_A0 &&>(__a0)).*__f`. `memptrqual.cpp`. (0.126)
- A reference to an arithmetic type bound to an arithmetic expression of ANOTHER LLVM type -- or a `bool` to a
  non-`bool` -- binds a TEMPORARY of the referent's type, converted from the value ([dcl.init.ref]/5.4;
  `ir_ref_converts/3`, `ir_ref_convert/3`, tried first by `ir_ref_to/3`; a reference MEMBER bound in a constructor goes
  through the same door, `ir_bind_into/3`). Types of one LLVM type share the lvalue's address, as before. Why:
  `std::max<size_t>(2 * n, 1)` hands the int `1` to a `const size_t &`, and the temporary was as wide as the int, four
  bytes read as eight; `std::deque` asked for a map of 8589934593 pointers and crashed at its first growth. `const
  size_t &r = 3;` alike. `refwiden.cpp`, `stddeque.cpp`. (0.117)
- A call whose result is a reference to an ARRAY is the array's address, which decays (`ir_expr(call)`, 0.117): libc++'s
  `static auto &__pow() { return __table<>::__pow10_32; }` is added to (`__pow() + 1`), and the whole `[10 x i32]` had
  been loaded (`type(unknown)` at the lowering). `autoref.cpp`.
- A prvalue used as a place gets a temporary (`ir_lval(call(...))`): `end()[-1]`, `f().x`. A statement expression that
  ends with a place is a place (`ir_lvalue_form/1`). So a reference binds the temporary
  `({ C $tmp; ctor(&$tmp); $tmp; })` itself, not a copy. (0.60, 0.62)
- A reference member holds an address and is read through (`ir_ref_member/4`). Binding one stores the address into the
  slot (`ir_bind_ref/2`). (0.36, 0.61)
- `move(E)` is E, with two exceptions. An own array's element is loaded and its slot nulled. A struct lvalue with own
  fields has them nulled behind it, nested structs too (`ir_null_own_fields/2`, `ir_has_own_fields/1`), so its
  destructor frees nothing. (M3, 0.40)
- A new-expression's block is `alloc(Mode, T, Call)` (0.202): the allocation function's call, then, for `zeroed(Size)`,
  an `llvm.memset` of Size bytes over the block, for `nzeroed(Size)` the same where the block is not null
  (`ir_zero_bytes/2`). A delete-expression is `dealloc(Destroy, Free, X)`: where X is not null, Destroy, the drain of
  the pointee's own arrays (`ir_dealloc_drain/1`), then Free. `delete_poly/3`, `::delete` of a class with a virtual
  destructor, takes the complete object through `vptr[-2]` before the destructor runs through the table, then gives it
  to the global function, the aligned one where the class asks for it. A `new` or a `delete` that reaches the lowering
  as it is takes the global functions (`ir_new/3`: `new T`, `new T(v)` of a type with no constructor, `new T[n]`), and a
  `new` that still needs a constructor is `new_with_constructor(T)`. They were malloc and free. (0.32, 0.108, 0.202)
- The drains are in the safe part above. Exceptions (`invoke`, landing pads), RTTI (libc++abi), coroutines
  (`llvm.coro.*`) and contracts lower as their own section says. (0.108)

- A REFERENCE MEMBER OF AN AGGREGATE BINDS ITS ITEM ([dcl.init.aggr]/4.2, [dcl.init.ref]; `ir_init_sub/4` over
  `ir_bind_into`; 0.121): the slot holds the item's address, as a constructor's member initializer stores it
  (`ir_bind_ref`); the item was loaded and converted to a pointer, an `inttoptr` of a struct. libc++ 18's
  `__value_visitor<_Visitor>{std::forward<_Visitor>(__visitor)}` of `std::visit` has `_Visitor &&` as its one member.
  The item a CLOSURE gives its reference member is the captured object's address already (`cpp_closure_value`, `[&x]`
  and `[this]`) and is stored as it is (`ir_address_item/2`, by type). `varvisit.cpp`. (0.121)

- A PRVALUE IS CONSTRUCTED IN THE OBJECT IT INITIALIZES (C++17, [class.copy.elision]/1; 0.121). The desugaring hands a
  fresh temporary on as the statement expression that built it, its declaration inside the block and its name last
  (`$tmp...`, and `$ret...` for a local moved into the result of a function); the lowering takes the declaration out and
  binds the name to the object's address (`ir_prvalue_block/4`, `ir_take_tmp_decl/4`, `ir_in_place/4`), for a local's
  initializer (`ir_init/3`), a `return` through the hidden result pointer (`ir_stmt(return)`, over `%agg.result`) and an
  aggregate member (`cpp_prvalue_in_place`). A CALL that returns the object's class through the hidden pointer gets the
  object's address as its result (`ir_sret_call/2`; the global `'$ir_sret_into'`, read and cleared by `ir_call_` and
  initialized in `ir_reset`, since `ccl_global/3` ignores a default): `std::map<int, int> m = build();` and `return
  build();`. Why: built in a slot of its own and copied bitwise, a class that holds its own address (a map's end node, a
  list's sentinel, a `std::function`'s small buffer) pointed into the dead slot -- three defects of 0.120 and before
  (`std::function<int(int)> f = std::function<int(int)>(g)` freed an invalid pointer, `return std::list<int>{1, 2, 3};`
  and a `std::map` returned by value corrupted their first growth, `std::map<int, int> m = build();` iterated for ever).
  `prvalueinplace.cpp`. (0.121) So is a STATEMENT'S TEMPORARY that such a call gives its value (0.192; `ir_stmt_` on
  `expr(L, assign('=', id(N), R))` for a desugarer's `$tmp...` and `ir_sret_call(R, T)`): the desugaring declares a
  temporary of a class with a destructor by the statement and gives it its value by `$tmp = f()` (`cpp_temp_call/3`, a
  call returning a class by value, called: `make(3)(4)`), and the assignment copied it bitwise from the call's own slot --
  `std::function<int(int)> ha(); ... ha()(5)` called through a pointer into that slot, and the destructor freed the
  stack (`free(): invalid pointer`, measured over 0.191). No other assignment of a class takes this road: a program's
  `x = f()` may alias x in f, and is copied as clang copies it. `tempsret.cpp`. (0.192)
- A CLASS PRVALUE HANDED TO A BY-VALUE PARAMETER IS THE PARAMETER ([class.copy.elision]/1; 0.197; `ir_arg_in_place/4` in
  `ir_args_/5`): where the parameter crosses by invisible reference (the Itanium ABI's `indirect`), the temporary the
  desugaring made (`$tmp...`), the copy it made for an lvalue (`$copy...`) and a call that returns the class through the
  hidden pointer are built where the callee reads them, and their address is the argument. Each was built in a slot of
  its own and copied bitwise into a second one, so `sum(l)` over `int sum(std::list<int>)` walked a sentinel left in the
  first slot for ever, and `call(g, 6)` over a `std::function` parameter freed an invalid pointer (0.196 too).
  `byvalself.cpp`. The object is the caller's to destroy since 0.207 (the desugaring's `cpp_byval_arg/3`): a temporary
  of its statement, and a conditional of two such temporaries is passed as the address of the one its arm built
  (`ir_stmt_temp_arm/1`), where the arms were built in place into a slot of the lowering's own that nothing destroyed
  once the callee no longer did.
- A NAMED RETURN VALUE IS THE RESULT OBJECT (0.199; the desugaring's `cpp_nrvo/3`, the Copies topic of Classes): a local
  that the desugaring declares with the storage `nrvo` lives at `%agg.result` where the function returns its class
  through the hidden pointer, its initializer built there (`ir_locals/2`), and a return of it is `ret void` after the
  defers (`ir_stmt_/1`); elsewhere it is a local of its own, as before. A free function's `nxif(E, Sto)` storage is its
  storage to the lowering (`ir_item/1`).

### Statics, globals and initializers

- The layout of a struct, a union and a bitfield, a member's slot, an empty value and the call ABI are rules of the
  object layout (the section "Object layout and the ABI"); the rules below are the lowering's own.
- A static local is `@fn.name.K = internal global` (`ir_static_locals/1`), or `internal thread_local global`. A
  `thread_local` global is `thread_local global` (`ir_tls/1`). `linkonce` storage is `linkonce_odr global` for a
  global and `define linkonce_odr` for a function. (M2b, 0.35, 0.93)
- A global's constant (`ir_gconst/3`): a struct over its shape, with bitfield runs packed into `c"..."` bytes
  (`ir_gstruct/3`); a union in its given member's literal type, padded (`ir_gunion/4`); a designated list made
  positional (`ccl_init_norm`), a hole `init([])`. A bitfield's value is read by `ir_gbit_value/2`: a hole is 0 and a
  braced scalar its one item (`test/c/run/bitdesig.c`), and packed exactly at any width (0.155, the Object layout
  topic). An empty class's temporary is its constant, and a scalar `T{}`
  is its zero. A char array from a shorter literal is zero-filled to its bound (`ir_str_tail/3`;
  `test/cpp/run/staticbase.cpp`). (M2b, 0.72, 0.79, 0.108, 0.112)
- A HOLDER'S TYPE FOLLOWS ITS CONSTANTS' TYPES (0.203; C 6.7.9/17, as clang types it; `ir_gconst_typed/4`,
  `ir_gconst_t/5`): a union's constant has the literal type of the member given, a packed union's an LLVM packed struct
  of it, and a struct or an array that holds a constant of another type than its element's is LLVM's packed literal
  struct of its constants' types, the padding before each explicit at the offset its named type has (`ir_gstruct_t/5`,
  `ir_gnat_padded/5`); else the named type. `static struct S g = { 1, { .i = 5 }, 2 };` over a union of a char, an int
  and a long long was `{ i64 } { i32 5, ... }`, which LLVM refused, so a static table of tagged unions did not build (a
  defect of 0.202 and before). A packed struct's constant is LLVM's packed one. `test/c/run/gunion.c`, `packunion.c`.
  (0.203)
- A wide literal, or a pointer into one, is a pointer's global constant (`ir_wide_lit`: `wstr` and `u32str` i32,
  `u16str` i16, through `ir_wstring`); an array of wide characters is not taken here. (0.115)
- A FLOATING global's fold (`ir_fp_value/2`) takes a cast to an integer type as the truncation and the wrap it is
  (`ir_fp_cast/3`: `(double) (int) 2.5` was 2.5, the cast passed over) and an integer past 2^60 as a double
  (`ccl_w_float/2`: `double d = (double) ((__int128) 1 << 100)` was refused); an INTEGER global from a floating initializer
  converts (C 6.3.1.4; `ir_int_of_float/3`): `int g = 2.5;` and `unsigned __int128 g = 3e38;` were spelled as a double's hex,
  which LLVM refuses for an integer, and `int g = -2.5;` was refused, `global_init`. `test/c/run/floatglobal.c`. (0.129)
- AN INTEGER OPERATION IN A FLOATING GLOBAL'S FOLD IS AN INTEGER OPERATION (C 6.3.1.8; 0.154): an operand whose type is an
  integer type is the integer evaluator's value of the whole operand (`ccl_const_eval/2`: its type's arithmetic, its
  wrap, its unsigned rules), exact, maybe big(_), and converted once where a floating operand meets it or the global's
  type takes it (`ir_fp_cast/3` and `ir_fp_const/3` round an integer to a float or a half once, never through a double).
  The four operations were done in doubles and in cocolog's 61-bit integers: `double g = 0x0FFFFFFFFFFFFFFFLL +
  0x0FFFFFFFFFFFFFFFLL;` was -2.0 (the sum wrapped), `-1u` was -1.0, `(1ULL << 63) + (1ULL << 63)` 2^64 where C wraps it
  to 0, and `((__int128) 1 << 64) + 2048 + 1` rounded twice. An operand the integer evaluator cannot fold keeps the old
  road. `test/c/run/fpintexpr.c`. (0.154)
- A LONG DOUBLE IN A GLOBAL'S FOLD (0.154) is `bv(Sign, T, Lsb)`, exactly T x 2^Lsb on an x87's or a quad's grid: a
  literal's text rounded once (`ir_ld_value/2`), an integer or a double converted to it exactly or rounded once
  (`ir_fp_exact/2` takes any value apart into x(Sign, M, E), `inf(S)` or `nan(S)`; `ir_fp_round_to/3` rounds to an LLVM
  type's format), and its arithmetic exact, then rounded once (`ir_ld_op/4` over `ir_x_op/4`: a sum at the smaller
  exponent, a product, a quotient to 116 bits and a sticky rest; IEEE's infinities, NaNs and signed zeros), as clang folds
  `1.0L / 3.0L` and `0.1L * 3`. A cast to an integer type truncates the exact value (`ir_fp_int/3`: `unsigned long long g =
  18446744073709551615.0L;`, a bool its test), one to a double, a float or a half rounds from it (never through a double),
  and `ir_fp_const/3` spells it for the global's own type. A CAST TO A DOUBLE OR A LONG DOUBLE makes a value of that type:
  `double g = (double) 1 / 3;` kept the integer 1, and the division was an integer one, 0. An integer past
  2^60 stays big(_) through a cast to an integer type and converts where it is used (`ir_fp_num/2`, the nearest double in
