  a double's operation). An OPERAND IS CONVERTED TO THE LONG DOUBLE FIRST (C 6.3.1.8; `ir_ld_operand/3`): an integer past
  the format's bits rounds there, so `(((__int128) 1 << 64) + 1) * 3.0L` is 3 x 2^64, as clang folds it, never the exact
  product rounded once. A SUM OF FAR OPERANDS is no 32,000-bit alignment (`ir_x_far/5`): where the smaller lies wholly
  below the unit u of the larger's bits made 120, more than any format keeps, the sum is the larger plus or minus u/2,
  which rounds as the exact sum does (every rounding boundary near it is a multiple of u); `LDBL_MAX + LDBL_TRUE_MIN` took
  3.7 s and `1.0L + 1e-4900L` 0.97 s of CPU, now under a millisecond. `test/c/run/ldconst.c`. (0.154)
- A POINTER GLOBAL FROM AN INTEGER CONSTANT (0.179; C 6.3.2.3/3 and /5, 6.6/9; `ir_gconst/3` over `ir_gint_const/2`):
  a null pointer constant is `null` -- `0`, `0L`, `0ll`, `NULL` as our `stddef.h` spells it, `(void *) 0`, `(int *) 0`,
  `(long) 0` -- any other integer constant the address it names, `inttoptr`, and a pointer constant cast to another
  pointer type that constant. `int *p = 0;` was `global ptr 0`, which LLVM refused, and `int *p = NULL;` was refused,
  `global_init`: no fixture held a pointer global given an initializer.
  AN ARRAY'S BOUND IS A CONSTANT EXPRESSION wherever the lowering reads it (`ir_arr_count/2`): a global's constant, the
  call ABI's leaves and the debug subrange took a literal alone, and `long b[1 + 1] = { 7, 16 };` at file scope was
  refused, as `long long b[2ll]` was since `2ll` reads as a cast. `test/c/run/ptrglobal.c`. (0.179)
- AN ADDRESS CONSTANT (C17 6.6/9, [expr.const]; 0.208; `ir_gaddr/3` over `ir_glval/4`, `ir_gconst/3`'s last clause): a
  pointer global, a pointer element of an array global and a struct global's pointer member initialized with a static
  object's address -- an array's or a member array's name decayed, `&arr[3]`, `&sarr[1].m[2]`, a row `m2[1]`, and an
  integer constant added or taken, `arr + 2`, `4 + arr`, `&arr[6] - 1`, `m2 + 2` -- is that object's symbol and a byte
  offset, `getelementptr inbounds (i8, ptr @arr, i64 8)`; a static local's initializer too. Each was refused,
  `global_init`, where only `&x`, `&x.m`, a literal and a function's address were taken: `int *p = arr;` and `char *q =
  buf;` at file scope did not compile. `test/c/run/addrconst.c`. (0.208)
- Brace elision ([dcl.init.aggr]/15, and C's own rule): an array member given a non-braced item takes as many of the
  following items as it has elements, while more items than members remain (`ir_init_items/4`, `ir_elide_take/4`; a
  global's through `ir_gelide/4`), or where a scalar item meets an array of scalars (`ccl_elided_item/2`, 0.164; the
  Aggregates topic), and a struct or union member and an array's element given a scalar (0.194, the same topic). Every
  `std::array` initializer needs it. (0.91, 0.110, 0.164, 0.194)
- A local aggregate initializer stores `zeroinitializer`, then its items (`ir_init/3`). A braced list on a scalar is
  its one value or the type's zero; more items are `initializer_of_a_scalar(T)`. The scalar test takes the resolver's
  first answer, else `int arr[9] = {}` became a `sext`. An item with no member names its type, `initializer(I, ST)`.
  An unsized array takes its size from its initializer (`ir_sized_type/4`). (0.54, 0.93, 0.99)
- A char array from a string is zero-filled past the literal (C11 6.7.9/21; `ir_init_zero/2`). A wide one stores its
  decoded code points (`ir_init_chars/4`). `test/c/run/wstr_alignas.c`. (0.99)

### Decimal floating types

- C23's `_Decimal32`, `_Decimal64` and `_Decimal128` run as gcc builds them (0.129; read and sized since 0.93, refused by
  name until 0.129). A value is its BID encoding (IEEE 754-2008's binary integer decimal) CARRIED in LLVM as a `float`, a
  `double` and an `fp128` (`ir_base` through `ir_dec_ll/2`) -- never computed on as one -- so the SysV ABI passes it
  where gcc does, in an SSE register, the `fp128` in one. Every operation is a call of libgcc's decimal runtime, which `cc`
  links (`ir_dec_call/5` declares each): `+ - * /` are `__bid_add<k>3` ... (k `sd`, `dd` or `td`; `ir_dec_arith/6`,
  another operator refused, `decimal_operator(Op)`); a comparison is `__bid_<eq|ne|lt|le|gt|ge><k>2`, whose long answer's
  sign tells (`ir_dec_cmp/6`); a truth test is the `ne` against the carrier's zero, whose all-zero bits are a decimal zero
  (`ir_dec_nonzero/4`, in `ir_cond/2` and `ir_to_bool/4`); `++` and `--` add the kind's one (`ir_step_`); a negation flips
  the sign bit, as gcc does (`ir_dec_negate/4`). (0.129)
- The conversions (`ir_dec_convert/6`, a clause of `ir_convert/6`): between decimal kinds `__bid_extend<f><t>2` and
  `__bid_trunc<f><t>2`; to and from an integer the width's routine, `si` for 32 bits and below (`__bid_floatsidd`,
  `__bid_fixunsddsi` ...) and `di` for 64, a 128-bit integer through the compiler's own helpers (below); to and from a
  standard floating type `sf`, `df`, `xf` (a `_Float16` through a float), named `extend` or `trunc` by the formats' widths
  -- between formats of one width a decimal truncates to binary and a binary extends to decimal, as libgcc names them;
  to a bool the test. (0.129)
- A 128-BIT INTEGER CONVERTS TO AND FROM A DECIMAL (0.137): libgcc has no `__bid_floattidd` nor `__bid_fixddti`, and
  gcc's own link of such a conversion fails. The routines are the compiler's, written in C (`module/bidrt.c`) and
  compiled by cicilang itself into IR text (`library/ccl_bidrt.pl`, generated, `ccl_bidrt_text(Name, Text)`); the first
  such conversion of a module notes every function of it, internal, and the declarations of the libgcc routines they
  call (`ir_dec_rt128/0`, loaded once by `ir_bidrt_ready/0` as the Unicode table is), so two objects that convert link.
  `__ccl_bid_float[uns]ti<k>` rounds the integer's magnitude ONCE, half to even, to the kind's digits in integer
  arithmetic, then builds the value from a 64-bit conversion and exact products by ten; `__ccl_bid_fix[uns]<k>ti`
  decodes the BID coefficient and exponent and scales toward zero. A `_BitInt` of 65 to 128 bits widens to `i128` first;
  one PAST 128 bits goes through the runtime's limb routines (0.160; `__ccl_bid_floatbitint<k>`,
  `__ccl_bid_fix<k>bitint`, over its 64-bit limbs the least first and its width, negative for a signed one, as libgcc's
  own `_BitInt` conversions take them, which libgcc 13 does not have): to a decimal the magnitude divided by ten while
  it passes 128 bits, the digits taken off kept for the one rounding; from one the coefficient scaled into the limbs
  toward zero and the bits past the width dropped. It was refused, `decimal_conversion(From, To)`.
  `test/c/run/decbitint.c`, the values Python's `decimal` module's (no gcc here reads a `_BitInt` with the decimal
  types). They are a runtime of the compiler, as libgcc's, and no part of the standard library. `test/c/run/dec128.c`
  (gcc's build over the same helpers, the values checked against Python's `decimal`; on aarch64 under qemu too). (0.137,
  0.160)
- A literal is encoded here, exactly (`ir_dec_literal/3`): its text's digits and exponent (`ir_dec_parse/3`), rounded half
  to even past the kind's precision (7, 16, 34 digits; `ir_dec_round_to/5`), an exponent past the greatest clamped by
  padding with zeros where the coefficient holds them, else an infinity, one past the least rounded away (`ir_dec_fit/3`),
  then the short form (the biased exponent above the coefficient) or the long one (`11`, the exponent, the coefficient's
  low bits under an implied `100`; `ir_dec_bits/3`), spelled `bitcast (i64 N to double)` with N the pattern read signed.
  A decimal GLOBAL's constant folds as gcc folds it (0.132; IEEE 754-2008, C23 6.3.1.4, 6.3.1.5; `ir_dec_fold/3`): a
  literal of any decimal kind re-encoded in its own, a negation, an integer; `+`, `-`, `*` and `/` at the operation's
  type, the wider decimal one, each operand converted to it and the exact result rounded half to even to its digits (a
  sum at the smaller exponent, a product at the exponents' sum, a quotient exact at the preferred exponent where it can
  be, else to the type's digits with a sticky digit; `ir_dec_op/5`); a cast rounds to its type; a BINARY floating
  constant converted to a decimal type by gcc's own steps (its text of the value to 57 digits with the trailing zeros
  cropped to `d.d`, then a `_Decimal128`, then the type's digits; `ir_dec_exact/2`); a decimal constant as a binary
  floating global, the nearest value on the format's grid, ties to even, a subnormal one included (`ir_dec_binary/2`:
  `float`, `double`, `half`, the x87 and the quad formats by their bits). AN INFINITY, A NaN AND A DIVISION BY ZERO fold
  as gcc folds them (0.137; IEEE 754-2008 7.2, 7.3; `ir_dec_special/9`, the fourth field of `d/4` `yes` for an infinity and
  `nan` for a NaN): a NaN of a NaN, `inf - inf`, `inf x 0`, `0 / 0` and `inf / inf`, positive, `0x7c` in its top byte; an
  infinity of an infinity with a finite value and of a nonzero value divided by zero, its sign the operands'; a finite
  value divided by an infinity a zero at the least exponent; a negation flips the sign of either; as a binary global the
  format's own infinity or quiet NaN (`ir_dec_special_value/3`, `ir_fp_nan_text/3`). `test/c/run/decspecial.c`. A LONG
  DOUBLE constant converted to a decimal type takes gcc's steps from its own exact value (0.154; `ir_dec_fold_/2` over
  `ir_long_double_type/1`, `bv/3` in `ir_dec_exact/2`): `_Decimal128 d = LDBL_MIN;`, `0.1L`, `1.0L / 3.0L`; it was refused,
  `decimal_constant(E)`, while the literal held a double's value. gcc's 57 digits are made from the value's top 60 to 62
  digits and a sticky digit (`ir_dec_binary_digits/4`), since the expansion of an x87's `LDBL_MIN` has 11,500 digits. The
  driver gate compares the bits of twelve such globals with gcc's build (`test/c/link/decld.c`; no gcc with decimal types
  is a skip line). A quotient's bits are divided past the divisor's top bits in one shift and a value far past a format's
  range is told by its exponent alone, so `long double x = 1e-4940dl;` folds in milliseconds. `test/c/run/decfold.c`
  (gcc's output). (0.129, 0.132, 0.154)
- The inference (`library/ccl_infer.pl`): `ccl_is_decimal/1`, `ccl_decimal_kind/2`; a decimal is arithmetic and no
  standard floating type (`ccl_is_float/1` stays false); the usual arithmetic conversions take the wider decimal type
  where either operand is decimal, an integer converted to it (C23 6.3.1.8; `ccl_decimal_usual/3`); a decimal is never
  promoted. A decimal member of an aggregate is an SSE leaf, a `_Decimal128` SSE and SSEUP, one `fp128` piece in one
  register (`ir_leaves/3`, `ir_eightbytes/4`, the register budget and `va_arg`'s register area): the driver gate passes
  values, structs and a variadic call both ways against gcc-built code. `test/c/run/decimal.c` (gcc's output; clang has no
  decimal types). (0.129)

### long double, _Complex, _BitInt and wide characters

- `long double` on x86-64 is `x86_fp80` (`ccl_long_double(x87)`), 16 bytes aligned 16, its constants in `0xK` hex.
  On Linux aarch64 it is an IEEE quad (`ccl_long_double(quad)`, 0.131): `fp128`, 16 bytes aligned 16, its constants in
  `0xL` hex (`ir_quad/2` from a double, `ir_dec_binary_bits_text/5` from the bits: the low 64 bits, then the sign, the 15
  exponent bits and the fraction's top 48), its arithmetic libgcc's soft quad routines, its complex runtime `__multc3` and
  `__divtc3`, a decimal's conversions `tf` (`__bid_extendddtf`); on Apple's arm64 a `double`. An HFA of quads is in the
  SIMD registers. `test/c/run/ldouble.c`, `test/cpp/run/ldouble.cpp`. (0.108, 0.131)
- A LONG DOUBLE LITERAL IS ITS TEXT ROUNDED ONCE TO THE LONG DOUBLE'S OWN FORMAT (0.154; `ir_ld_value/2`), to nearest, ties
  to even, as clang reads it: an x87's 64 significant bits, a quad's 113, the format's subnormals and infinity
  (`ir_fp_inf_bits/6` names the format by its LLVM type). A decimal text is its digits times 5^E times 2^E, or divided by
  5^-E and 2^-E, made exactly and rounded on the magnitude's limbs (`ir_dec_binary_bits/7` over `ir_mag_round/8`, the
  rounding a decimal constant has had since 0.132); a hex text is its digits times two to its exponent (`ir_ld_hex/3`). In a
  function the value is the constant (`ir_expr(ldbl(A))`, GNU's `imagl(A)` the `{ 0, value }` of a complex long double);
  in a global's fold it is `bv(Sign, T, Lsb)` (the Statics topic). It was the double nearest the text: the double's 53
  bits widened, `LDBL_MAX` the largest double. The limbs, not `ccl_w_*/3`, carry the work: those spell each result past 2^60
  as its decimal digits, and over them `LDBL_MAX`'s 16,000 bits took 3.4 s, `LDBL_MIN` 1.3 s, where they take 0.03 s and
  0.05 s of CPU.
  `test/c/run/ldconst.c` (on aarch64 too, against clang's quad), `test/cpp/run/ldlimits.cpp`. Lowering 83. (0.154)
- PLAIN `char` AND `wchar_t` ARE UNSIGNED ON LINUX AARCH64 (0.131; `ccl_char_unsigned/0`, `ccl_plain_char_unsigned/1`,
  asked by `ccl_int_rank/3` and `ir_signed_/1`): `(char) 200` is 200 there, a comparison and a constant fold alike.
- `_Complex T` is `{ E, E }` over its real type (`ccl_complex_real/2`; a bare `_Complex` is a double), twice the real's
  size and aligned as one. `ir_complex_elem/2` covers `double`, `x86_fp80`, `float`, `i64`, `i32`, `i16` and `i8`. The
  usual arithmetic conversions give the complex of the common real type (`ccl_complex_usual/3`). (0.100, 0.103)
- A complex conversion is decided by the C types (`ccl_is_complex/1` in `ir_complex_convert/6`), never by the LLVM
  shape: an ABI piece `{ i64, i64 }` is no complex. A real becomes a complex with a zero imaginary part; a complex
  becomes a real by its real part. (0.100, 0.103)
- `+` and `-` work per component, `==` and `!=` compare both components, and negation negates both. A floating `*` or
  `/` calls the Annex G runtime, which recovers the infinities (`ir_complex_rt/8`). An integer one uses the textbook
  formulas and divides with `sdiv` or `udiv` (`ir_complex_op/9`), as clang does:

  | Type | Helpers | Value type |
  |---|---|---|
  | complex double | `__muldc3`, `__divdc3` | `{ double, double }` |
  | complex float | `__mulsc3`, `__divsc3` | `<2 x float>` |
  | complex long double | `__mulxc3`, `__divxc3` | `{ x86_fp80, x86_fp80 }` |

  (0.101, 0.103, 0.108)
- An imaginary literal (`imag`, `imagf`, `imagi(Specs, N)`) is the constant `{ 0, F }` of its type. A global's
  complex constant is spelled per component (`ir_complex_text/3`, `ir_imag_const/2`; a `big(A)` through
  `ir_big_text/2`). `__builtin_complex(x, y)`, C11's `CMPLX`, builds one. `test/c/run/complex.c`, `complex2.c`,
  `complex3.c`. (0.100, 0.101, 0.104)
- `__real__ z` and `__imag__ z` are values and places: a component's address inside the complex (`ir_complex_slot/5`).
  The imaginary part of a real as a place is `imaginary_part_of_a_real_as_a_place`, as clang refuses it (`expression is
  not assignable`). A complex crosses a call as its
  components (`ir_leaves/3`): SSE leaves for a floating one, INTEGER for an integer one, X87 and X87UP for a long
  double one. (0.100, 0.101, 0.108)
- `_BitInt(N)` is exactly `iN` (`ir_base`), sized by the psABI: the smallest of 1, 2, 4 or 8 bytes up to 64 bits, and
  whole eightbytes aligned 8 past that. (0.93)
- `wchar_t` is a signed `i32`, `char16_t` an unsigned `i16` and `char32_t` an unsigned `i32` (LP64). A wide string
  literal is a constant of its decoded code points (`ir_wstring/3`, `ir_utf8_decode/2`). `sizeof` of a string literal
  is its array's bytes, one element per code point for a wide one (`ccl_literal_bytes/2`). (0.92, 0.93, 0.103)

### Atomics

- The `__atomic_*` builtins are LLVM's own instructions, never calls (`ir_atomic_rmw/3`). `__atomic_<op>_fetch` is an
  `atomicrmw` followed by the op on the old value; `__atomic_fetch_<op>` answers the old value; `__atomic_exchange_n`
  is `xchg`. `__atomic_load_n` and `__atomic_store_n` carry the order and the type's alignment. The thread fence is a
  `fence`, the signal fence a `fence syncscope("singlethread")`. libc++'s `shared_ptr` counts its owners so. (0.86)
- GCC'S GENERIC ATOMIC BUILTINS (0.194): `__atomic_load(p, ret, mo)`, `__atomic_store(p, val, mo)`,
  `__atomic_exchange(p, val, ret, mo)` and `__atomic_compare_exchange(p, expected, desired, weak, success, failure)`
  move an object of any type through pointers, where the `_n` forms take and give values; libc++ 21's atomic_ref is
  written on them, and they were `undeclared`. As clang lowers them: an object whose size is a lock-free width and whose
  type is aligned to it moves as the integer of its size, by the instructions of the `_n` forms (`ir_atomic_int/3`:
  `load atomic i64`, a `cmpxchg` of two `i64` loaded through the pointers, the old value stored to `*expected`); any
  other is the call of libatomic's generic routine of that name, its size first, the orders as the program gives them at
  run time (`ir_atomic_lib/6`: `__atomic_load(i64 8, ptr, ptr, i32 5)`), which the link takes with `-latomic`, as
  clang's does. The alignment is the type's own, a typedef's `taligned(E)` and an `aligned(E)` kept (0.205;
  `ir_atomic_plain/2` took every qualifier off): an atomic_ref of a 4-byte struct of alignment 2, raised to 4 by its
  `_Aligned_Tp`, called libatomic's routine, a link error with no `-latomic` (`atomicrefalign.cpp`, `atomicalign.cpp`).
  A weak flag that does not fold asks the strong instruction, which never fails spuriously. Their types are the
  inference's (`void`, the exchange's `bool`). `atomicgen.c`, `atomicref.cpp` (C++20, libc++ 21).
- GCC'S LOCK-FREE QUESTIONS (0.194): `__atomic_always_lock_free(size, ptr)` is a constant (`ccl_const_eval/2` over
  `ccl_lock_free_answer/3`): 1 for a lock-free width -- 1, 2, 4 and 8 bytes, 16 on aarch64 too (its pair loads and
  stores; `ccl_lock_free_width/1`), where x86-64's default CPU has no 16-byte compare-and-swap -- whose pointer is null
  or points to a type aligned to the size at least, as clang answers, 0 else; in C++ a pointer that is no null constant
  is answered by the desugaring over its desugared form (`cpp_builtin_call/3`), since the raw form of libc++ 21's
  `std::addressof(__get_aligner_instance<...>::__instance)` is typed by addressof's own signature, `_Tp *`, and the raw
  fold of atomic_ref's static `is_always_lock_free` answered 0. `__atomic_is_lock_free(size, ptr)` asks the pointer's
  alignment at run time where its type does not tell, and `__c11_atomic_is_lock_free` answers 16 bytes on aarch64.
  `lockfree.c`.
- The memory order is the constant the header spells, in clang's numbering (`ir_atomic_order/2`): 0 is `monotonic`, 1
  and 2 `acquire`, 3 `release`, 4 `acq_rel`, 5 `seq_cst`. An order that does not fold is `seq_cst`. (0.86)
- The `__c11_atomic_*` builtins are the same instructions (`ir_c11_rmw/2`; load, store and the fences as above; init a
  plain store). Compare-exchange, strong or weak, is a `cmpxchg` that stores the old value to `*expected`; its failure
  order is never a release (`ir_cmpxchg_fail/2`). `is_lock_free` answers 1 up to 8 bytes (and 16 on aarch64, 0.194). The compiler's own
  `library/include/stdatomic.h` and libc++'s `<atomic>` are written on them. `test/c/run/atomic.c`. (0.99)
- An `_Atomic` object loads and stores `seq_cst` (`ir_load_slot/4`, `ir_store_slot/4` over `ir_atomic_q/1`). An
  integer `x++` or `--x` (`ir_step/6`) and `+=`, `-=`, `&=`, `|=`, `^=` are one `atomicrmw` each (C11 6.7.3, 7.17.7).
  (0.99)
- EVERY OTHER READ-MODIFY-WRITE OF AN `_Atomic` OBJECT IS ONE COMPARE-EXCHANGE LOOP (C17 6.5.16.2/3, 6.5.2.4/2; 0.208;
  `ir_atomic_loop/6` from the compound assignment of `ir_expr/4` and from `ir_step_/6`, over `ir_cas_ll/2`), as clang's:
  `*=`, `/=`, `%=`, `<<=` and `>>=` on an integer, `*=` and `/=` on a floating object, the integer of its bits to
  `cmpxchg`, a pointer's `++` and `--`, and every one of an x86 `long double`, through libatomic's
  `__atomic_compare_exchange` over two sixteen-byte temporaries, the desired one zeroed first. The object is loaded
  once, the new value computed from the old and exchanged where the object still holds the old, else the loop goes again
  from what the exchange found; the expected temporary holds the object's own bytes, so a `long double`'s padding
  compares equal. Each was a load and a store, another thread's write between them lost. AN ATOMIC POINTER IS ATOMIC
  (`ir_atomic_q/1` takes `ptr(Q, _)` too): `_Atomic(int *)` resolves to a pointer whose qualifiers hold `_Atomic`, and
  its loads, stores and steps were plain. `test/c/run/atomrmw.c` (clang's 17 `cmpxchg` and one `atomicrmw`),
  `atomldbl.c`. (0.208)
- A compound assignment and an increment take their place ONCE ([expr.ass]/6, C 6.5.16.2/3): `ir_lval` first, the
  atomic test asked of the slot after (`ir_step_/6`). Why: the `_Atomic` road was a clause of its own that took the
  place to decide, a lowering emits as it goes and backtracking undoes no instruction, so `slot() += 5` called slot
  twice (since 0.99). `test/c/run/oncetarget.c`, `oncetarget.cpp`. (0.112)
- A FLOATING OBJECT'S ATOMIC ADDITION AND SUBTRACTION ARE `atomicrmw fadd` AND `fsub` (0.206; `ir_rmw_fp/3` on the
  `__atomic_*` and `__c11_*` roads, on an `_Atomic` compound assignment, C17 6.5.16.2/3, and on its increments and
  decrements, `ir_step_/6`, C17 6.5.2.4, as clang's -- a `float`, a `double`, a `_Float16` and aarch64's `long double`,
  `fp128`): C++20's `std::atomic<float>::fetch_add` is `__c11_atomic_fetch_add` over a float, and LLVM refused `atomicrmw
  add` of one (`operand must be an integer`); `x += 1.5f` and `x++` on an `_Atomic float` were a load and a store, two
  atomic accesses and no atomic step. `ftmatomic20.cpp`, `test/c/run/atomicfp.c`.
- AN x86 `_Atomic long double` MOVES THROUGH LIBATOMIC'S GENERIC ROUTINE (0.206; the last `_Atomic` clauses of
  `ir_load_slot/4` and `ir_store_slot/4` over `ir_atomic_lib/6`, sixteen bytes, sequentially consistent, through a
  temporary), as clang's does: `load atomic x86_fp80` LLVM refused, its 80 bits no power of two
  (`ir_atomic_scalar_ll/1` takes `float`, `double`, `half` and `fp128` only), and the link names `-latomic` (0.208, the
  driver topic). Its `x++` and `+=` are a compare-exchange loop since 0.208 (above). `atomldbl.c`.
- AN ATOMIC OBJECT OF CLASS TYPE MOVES AS THE INTEGER OF ITS SIZE (0.206; `ir_atomic_int/3` on the `__atomic_load_n` and
  `__atomic_store_n` roads, through a temporary, and in `ir_load_slot/4` and `ir_store_slot/4` for an `_Atomic` one):
  where its size is a lock-free width and its type aligned to it, as the generic builtins move it, else libatomic's
  routine. `std::atomic<Pt>` of `struct Pt { int x, y; }` was `load atomic %struct.Pt`, which LLVM refused. The scalar
  types an atomic load and store take as they are -- an integer, a floating type, a pointer -- are
  `ir_atomic_scalar_ll/1`'s. `ftmatomic20.cpp`. ANY OTHER `_Atomic` OBJECT, of a size that is no lock-free width, loads
  and stores through libatomic's routines (0.208; the last `_Atomic` clauses of `ir_load_slot/4` and `ir_store_slot/4`,
  the x86 `long double`'s made general): `r = g` and `c = e` over an `_Atomic` struct of 20 or 12 bytes were a plain
  load and store. C11'S EXCHANGE AND COMPARE-EXCHANGE TAKE ANY TYPE (0.208; GCC's generic forms' bodies as
  `ir_atomic_xchg_mem/5` and `ir_atomic_cas_mem/8`, over temporaries of the values): `atomicrmw xchg` and `cmpxchg` take
  an integer or a pointer only, and a struct's `atomic_exchange`, a float's `compare_exchange_strong` and an x86 `long
  double`'s `fetch_add` (a compare-exchange loop, above) were IR that LLVM refused. An integer's and a pointer's
  compare-exchange keep their one `cmpxchg`. `atomodd.c`, `atomic208.cpp`.
- A POINTER'S ATOMIC ADDITION AND SUBTRACTION ARE ONE `atomicrmw` OVER AN i64 (0.208; `ir_atomic_ptr_rmw/9` on the
  `__c11_*` and the `__atomic_*` roads, `ir_atomic_ptr_place/1` asking the type before anything is emitted): the delta
  in elements for C11's builtin, as clang scales it, in bytes for GCC's, as GCC has it, the result back through
  `inttoptr`; libc++'s `atomic<T *>::fetch_add`, `++` and `+=` were `atomicrmw add ptr, ptr`, which LLVM refused
  (`operand must be an integer`). `atomic208.cpp`.
- AN ATOMIC TYPE OF A POWER-OF-TWO SIZE UP TO 16 BYTES IS ALIGNED AT ITS SIZE (C17 6.2.5/27: its alignment need not be
  the unqualified type's; clang's rule; 0.206; `ccl_size_align/3`'s first clause, and `ir_atomic_plain/2` keeps
  `_Atomic`): libc++'s `std::atomic<T>` holds an `_Atomic(T)`, and `std::atomic<Pt>` was aligned at 4, its loads
  libatomic's routine, which the link did not find; clang's are one 8-byte instruction. ANOTHER SIZE KEEPS THE TYPE'S
  OWN LAYOUT, as gcc's does (0.208): clang rounds a size up to sixteen bytes to a power of two and aligns it so, gcc
  does not, and clang's compare-exchange then compares the padding -- over `_Atomic struct { int i[3]; }` clang 18
  leaves `*expected` as it was when the exchange fails and clang 21 fails the first exchange, and over libc++ 18 and 21
  `std::atomic<S12>`'s compare_exchange_strong fails where C++20 ignores padding bits (P0528); gcc's answers and this
  compiler's are the standards' (`atomodd.c`, `atomic208.cpp`; the Findings). `ftmatomic20.cpp`.

### Vector types

- A vector is LLVM's own `<N x T>` (`ir_base`), a bool ext vector `<N x i1>` (0.162; the VECTOR TYPES block of
  `library/ccl_ir.pl`, `ir_vec_*`). The arithmetic, bitwise and shift operators work lane by lane, as clang's do --
  `add`, never `add nsw`, a lane wraps (`ir_vec_binary/10`) --, a scalar operand converted to the element and SPLATTED
  (`insertelement`, `shufflevector ... zeroinitializer`; `ir_vec_side/8`); a comparison is the lanes' `icmp` or `fcmp`
  and the `sext` of its `<N x i1>` to the mask (`ir_vec_cmp/10`); `-v` and `~v` lane by lane (`fneg`, `sub` from zero,
  `xor` with all ones); a bool vector takes `& | ^` and `~`, its lanes bits. A lane is a place: an element's address in
  the vector (`ir_lval(index)`), a bool vector's lane loaded and stored through the whole vector (`vlane/3`: load,
  `extractelement` or `insertelement`, store) and no address (`address_of_a_bool_vector_lane`). A braced initializer
  fills the lanes in order from zero, `[i] = x` moving the lane (`ir_vec_init_value/3`); a global's constant is `<i32 1,
  i32 2, i32 0, i32 0>` (`ir_vec_gconst/3`). A vector converts to a vector of the same size by its bits and a scalar to
  a vector by a splat (`ir_vec_convert/6`); anything else is `vector_conversion(From, To)`, and a vector used as a
  condition `vector_condition(Op)`. (0.162)
- The vector builtins (0.162): `__builtin_convertvector(v, T)` converts lane by lane, a bool lane from its truth and to
  0 or 1 (`ir_vec_elem_convert/6`); `__builtin_shufflevector(a, b, i...)` is `shufflevector` over folded indices, -1 a
  `poison` lane (`vector_shuffle_index` for another); `__builtin_reduce_add`, `mul`, `and`, `or`, `xor`, `max` and `min`
  are `llvm.vector.reduce.*` of the lanes, a signed or an unsigned `max` and `min` by the element, `fmax` and `fmin` for
  a floating one (`ir_vec_reduce_name/4`; `vector_reduce(Op, T)` for an integer reduction of floats), a bool vector's
  answer a `bool`. libc++ 21's `__all_of` is `__builtin_reduce_and(__builtin_convertvector(v, __simd_vector<bool, N>))`.
  (0.162)
- A vector crosses a call as clang passes it, measured on both machines (`ir_vec_abi/8`, `ir_vec_leaves/5`): on SysV one
  of 4 bytes or fewer in an INTEGER register as `iN`, one of 8 in an SSE register as a `double` -- a `<1 x double>` in
  memory as an argument and in `xmm0` as a result --, one of 16 in one SSE register as itself (`<1 x i128>` as `<2 x
  i64>`), a larger one in memory as an argument and as itself as a result; as a member of an aggregate its eightbytes
  are SSE (a 16-byte one SSE and SSEUP: `struct { v4sf v; }` is `<4 x float>`). On AAPCS64 a legal vector -- 8 bytes, or
  16 with more than one lane, lanes a power of two, no bool -- in a SIMD register as itself, any other of 4 bytes or
  fewer as `i32`, of 8 as `<2 x i32>`, of 16 as `<4 x i32>`, a larger one by reference; a result of 16 bytes or fewer as
  itself, a larger one through the hidden pointer; a struct of up to four vectors of one type is an HVA in SIMD
  registers (`ir_hfa/3`). `va_arg` of a vector takes the same classes (the SSE area on SysV, the SIMD area on AAPCS64).
  gcc and clang differ on aarch64 for a 4-byte vector RESULT, and this is clang's; the gates' link checks use the
  vectors on which both agree. The driver gate and the cross gate (`test/c/link/vec_*.c`). (0.162)
- The debug information describes a vector as DWARF's `DW_TAG_array_type` with `DIFlagVector` over its lanes, as clang
  does (`ir_dbg_type_text`). (0.162)

### VLAs

- A VLA is allocated where it is declared: `alloca EL, i64 Total, align 16` in the body. Its bounds are evaluated once
  (C11 6.7.6.2/5) and kept in the local's type, `arr(vla(Reg), E)`. A VLA with `= {}` is zeroed (C23 6.7.10,
  `llvm.memset` over the kept bytes, `ir_locals`); any other initializer is `vla_initialized(N)`, as C23 6.7.10 has it and
  clang refuses it (`variable-sized object may not be initialized`). `test/c/run/vlaempty.c` (`-std=c23`). (0.93, 0.99,
  0.117)
- `sizeof` of a VLA local reads the kept bounds (`ir_vla_expr_type/2`, `ir_vla_bytes/2`). A VLA of a VLA is one
  allocation, and row `a[i]` lies at i times the row's bytes (`ir_lval(index)`). `test/c/run/vla_nested.c`. A VLA type
  that no local holds multiplies the bound read at the `sizeof`. (0.99)
- A VARIABLY MODIFIED PARAMETER'S BOUNDS ARE EVALUATED ON ENTRY (C 6.9.1/10; 0.197; `ir_vm_params/1`): `int a[n][n]` is the
  pointer `int (*a)[n]`, and its bounds are kept in the parameter's type, `ptr(Q, arr(vla(Reg), E))`, so `a[i]` steps i rows
  of the bytes they make and `sizeof(a[0])` and `sizeof(*a)` read them. The row's LLVM type was `[0 x i32]`, and every row
  lay at a[0]. `test/c/run/c17forms.c`.

### Builtins

- The bit builtins answer an `int` to the inference too (`ccl_bit_builtin/2`, the one table, which the lowering's
  `ir_bit_builtin/2` reads; 0.129): `c ? 64 + __builtin_clzll(x) : __builtin_clzll(y)` had no type, in C as in C++, and the
  lowering refused it, `type(unknown)` -- libc++'s `__libcpp_clz(__uint128_t)` is written so. `test/c/run/bitcond.c`.
- The bit builtins are LLVM's intrinsics at the argument's own width (`ir_bit_builtin/2`): `__builtin_clz*`, `ctz*`,
  `popcount*`, and the generic `g` forms with their value for zero. A zero argument is defined, and the result is an
  `int`. The intrinsic's `declare` is a raw line, since `i1` has no C spelling. Every integer width is one
  (`ir_bit_width/2`): an `unsigned __int128` is `i128` and an `unsigned _BitInt(N)` its own `iN` -- libc++ 21's
  `__countl_zero` calls `__builtin_clzg` on an `unsigned __int128` (libc++ 18 splits it into two 64-bit calls), and the
  gate over libc++ 21 found the widths 8 to 64 only, eight fixtures RED. `bitwide.c`, `bit128.cpp`. (0.73, 0.129)
- THE BYTE SWAPS `__builtin_bswap16`, `32`, `64` and `128` ARE `llvm.bswap.iN` (0.206; `ccl_bswap_builtin/3`, one table,
  which the inference, the lowering's `ir_call/4` and the desugaring's evaluator read): each answers the unsigned integer
  of its width, its argument converted to that width first, and a constant 16- or 32-bit swap folds in a constant
  expression (`cpp_bswap_bits/3`). C++23's `std::byteswap` is written on them; they were undeclared. `ftm23.cpp`.
- The overflow builtins (`__builtin_add_overflow` and kin, `ccl_overflow_builtin/2`) compute the exact result in
  `i128` over operands widened by their own signedness (`ir_widen128/4`). They store the truncated result and answer
  whether it lost anything. C23's `<stdckdint.h>` is written on them. (0.93)
- `__builtin_unreachable()` is `unreachable`, and `[[assume(e)]]` calls `llvm.assume`. (0.93)
- A FUNCTION THAT RETURNS TWICE IS DECLARED SO, as clang declares it (0.201; `ir_returns_twice/1` in `ir_declares`):
  `setjmp`, `_setjmp`, `sigsetjmp`, `__sigsetjmp`, `savectx`, `vfork` and `getcontext` carry LLVM's `returns_twice`, which
  tells the optimizer that the call returns a second time. A local changed between the two returns keeps its value only
  where it is `volatile` (C 7.13.2.1/3, the qualifiers topic above): `cwrap.c` at `-O1`, whose locals are volatile, prints
  clang's answers with the attribute and without it. `cwrap.c`, `cwrap.cpp`. (0.201)
- `va_start`, `va_end` and `va_copy` are the `llvm.va_*` intrinsics (`ir_va_intrinsic/3`); on x86-64 `va_arg` of a
  scalar is LLVM's own instruction. `va_arg` of a struct, a union, a complex, an `__int128` or an x87 `long double` is
  expanded here on x86-64 (psABI 3.5.7; `ir_va_arg_aggregate/4`, `ir_piece_classes/5`, `ir_va_fetch/7`,
  `ir_va_overflow/4`): every eightbyte of the type comes from the register save area by its class (`gp_offset` /
  `fp_offset`) when they all fit, else the whole value from `overflow_arg_area`, aligned to 8 or 16 and advanced; a
  long double is X87, always the overflow area (0.131: LLVM's own `va_arg` read it wrong, and every argument after it).
- ON LINUX AARCH64 `va_arg` OF EVERY TYPE IS EXPANDED HERE (AAPCS64 B.4, as clang does; `ir_va_arg_aapcs/4`, 0.131): the
  va_list is `{ __stack, __gr_top, __vr_top, __gr_offs, __vr_offs }`, and LLVM's own `va_arg` takes Apple's `char *`. A
  floating scalar or an HFA comes from the SIMD registers' save area (`__vr_offs`, 16 bytes a register, an HFA's members
  one register each, gathered into a temporary, `ir_va_hfa_copy/6`), anything else from the general registers'
  (`__gr_offs`, 8 a register, a 16-aligned value from an even one), a composite past 16 bytes as the pointer it came by;
  an offset already 0 or more, or taken past 0, sends it to `__stack` (aligned 16 where the type needs it, moved on by
  its size rounded up to 8), and the registers it took are not given back. ON APPLE'S ARM64 (0.160;
  `ir_va_arg_darwin/4`, as clang's EmitDarwinVAArg) every variadic argument lies on the stack in 8-byte slots, a value
  aligned past 8 rounds the pointer up to its alignment first, the pointer moves on by the size rounded up to 8, a
  composite past 16 bytes that is no HFA came by a pointer, and an empty record takes no slot; a scalar is LLVM's own
  `va_arg`. Its va_list is a `char *` OBJECT, whose ADDRESS `va_arg`, `va_start`, `va_end` and `va_copy` take
  (`ir_va_list_addr/2`), where the pointer's value had been taken for the address; an aggregate was refused by name,
  `va_arg_of_aggregate`. No Apple machine is here: the driver gate compiles `test/c/link/va_darwin.c` for
  arm64-apple-macos with clang and with cicilang, retargets both texts to this host and runs them over one buffer laid
  out as Apple lays the arguments out (`va_darwin_main.c`), and the scalar forms are clang's text. `__builtin_va_list`
  is the ABI's type (`ccl_va_list_type/2`): `unsigned long[3]` on x86-64, `[4]` on AAPCS64, `char *` on Apple's arm64.
  `test/c/run/varargs.c`, `vaaggregate.c`. (0.108, 0.117, 0.160)
- `__builtin_inf`, `huge_val` and `nan`, in double, float and long double forms (a quad's too, 0.131), are constants (`ir_float_builtin/4`),
  as glibc's `INFINITY`, `NAN` and `HUGE_VAL` need. `__builtin_isnan`, `isinf`, `isinf_sign`, `isfinite`, `isnormal`
  and `signbit` are `fcmp` or bit tests that answer an `int` (`ir_fp_class/1`). (0.101, 0.108) C23's SIGNALING NaNs,
  `__builtin_nans`, `nansf` and `nansl` (`FLT_SNAN` and kin), are constants of the quiet bit clear and the bit below it
  set, as clang spells them (0.194; `ir_float_builtin/4`, `ir_fp_snan_text/3`), and a global's fold carries one as
  `snan(S)`: a negation flips its sign, an operation or a conversion gives the quiet NaN (IEEE 754 6.2), as gcc folds it.
  `__builtin_flt_rounds()` is LLVM's `llvm.get.rounding`, `<float.h>`'s `FLT_ROUNDS` (0.194). `c23float.c`.
- `__builtin_classify_type(e)` (GCC's; 0.194) is the class of e's type, an integer constant with clang's numbers and e
  never evaluated (`ccl_type_class/2` in `library/ccl_infer.pl`, the desugaring's `cpp_builtin_call/3` over the
  argument's type, the lowering's `ir_call/4`): void 0, an integer 1 (a character type, and an enum in C), an enum in
  C++ 3, a bool 4, a pointer, an array or a function 5, a pointer to a data member 7, a real floating type 8 (a decimal
  one too), a complex type 9, a struct, a class or a pointer to a member function 12, a union 13, a `_BitInt` 18, a
  vector 19. glibc's `<tgmath.h>` asks it where the compiler is no GCC 8. `tgmath.c`.
- libc++'s memory builtins become the C library's `memcpy`, `memmove` and `memset` in the desugaring;
  `ir_cpp_prelude/0` declares them when the file did not. (0.60)

### GNU's inline assembly

- A FILE-SCOPE ASM IS THE MODULE'S (0.215; `ir_module_asm/1`): each line of its text is a `module asm "..."` line at the
  module's head (`'$ir_masm'`, `ir_assemble/1`), as clang emits it, a last newline making no empty line. `gnuasm.c`
  defines an object so on each host, `gnuasm.cpp` in a linkage block and in a namespace. (0.215)
- AN ASM STATEMENT IS A CALL OF AN INLINE ASM, as clang lowers it (0.215; `ir_asm/1`). Basic asm is its text with `$`
  doubled (`ir_asm_dollars/2`), a side effect, its constraints the target's implicit clobbers alone. Extended asm's
  template takes `%N` and `%[name]` as `$N`, `%mN` and `%m[name]` as `${N:m}`, `%=` as `${:uid}`, `%%` as `%` and `$` as
  `$$` (`ir_asm_tpl/3`). Its constraints are the outputs' -- a register output `=` and its letters, the call's result,
  one value or a struct of them stored to their places (`ir_asm_stores/4`); an output whose constraint allows memory
  (`m`, `o`, `V`, `<`, `>`, `g`, and `Q` on AArch64) `=*` and its letters over the output's address, `ptr
  elementtype(T)` -- then the inputs' -- a tie by number as written and by `[name]` as the output's number, one that
  allows only memory `*` over its address, else a value, `g` as `imr` (`ir_asm_letters/2`) -- then each in-out output's
  input: its number and its value loaded where it allows a register (`+rm` and `+g` too), `*` over the same address
  where it allows only memory (`ir_asm_ties/3`) -- then the clobbers, `~{name}` with a leading `%` dropped
  (`ir_asm_clobbers/2`), and on x86-64 `~{dirflag},~{fpsr},~{flags}` (`ir_asm_implicit/1`; none on AArch64). x86's `a`,
  `b`, `c`, `d`, `S` and `D` are `{ax}` and kin (`ir_asm_x86_reg/2`), and A REGISTER VARIABLE'S OPERAND ITS OWN
  REGISTER, as clang's AddVariableConstraints has it (`ir_asm_regvar/2`): a local given an asm label -- `register long
  r10 asm("r10")`, a system call's argument -- is `{r10}` where a register is asked, an in-out one's input too unless it
  is early-clobbered; it was the register LLVM chose. It is `sideeffect` where `volatile` says so or it has no output.
  `asm goto` is refused by name, `asm_goto` (the driver gate's check). The probes held each form's text to clang's
  (`=r,0,r`, `=*rm,0`, `=*m,*m`, `=r,=r,0,1`, `={ax},={dx}`, `={eax},{eax}`, `${0:w}`): `gnuasm.c`'s 26 asm lines are
  clang's on both machines, and it prints what clang's and gcc's builds print on x86-64 and on aarch64 Linux under qemu.
  Lowering 123. `gnuasm.c`, `gnuasm.cpp`, which the cross gate runs too. (0.215)

### Debug information (`-g`)

- Under the driver's `debug` option (`'$ccl_debug'` = `file(Path)`, `'$ccl_debug_kind'`, the Driver topic) the lowering
  writes DWARF 5 (0.128, 0.130). A function the program defines gets a `distinct !DISubprogram` with its name, its
  scope, its line, its type and the one file (`ir_dbg_begin/5`, from `ir_function/7`; the line from the item,
  `'$ir_fn_line'`), and EVERY instruction of its body a `!DILocation` of the line of the statement being lowered
  (`'$ir_line'`; the function's own line before the first statement) in the current scope: `ir_ins/1`, `ir_end/1` and
  the fall-through branch of `ir_block/1` append `, !dbg !N` (`ir_dbg_parts/2`). LLVM's verifier asks a location of
  every call in a function that has a subprogram, and of an inlinable call in particular, so no instruction of the body
  is left without one. A location is made once per line, column, scope and function (`'$ir_dbg_locs'`, `at(Line, Column,
  Scope, Ref)`). A declaration sets the line too (`ir_stmt(declaration(L, ...))`): its initializer's calls are its own.
  (0.128, 0.161)
- A DEFINITION A C HEADER MAKES IS DESCRIBED IN ITS HEADER (0.213; `ir_dbg_def_file/2` over `'$ir_hfile'/2`, which
  `ir_header_defs/2` notes): its subprogram, its lexical blocks, its variables and its static locals name a `DIFile` of
  the header (`ir_dbg_hfile/2`, made once a header, `'$ir_dbg_hfiles'`; `'$ir_dbg_file'` the current function's), and so
  does a header's object, at the header's line; they named the unit's file at the header's line. The driver gate's check
  reads it back with `llvm-dwarfdump`. A C++ program's own header's functions name the unit's file still. (0.213)
- A STATEMENT'S COLUMN (0.161): every instruction of a statement has the column where the statement begins on its line,
  the one clang gives its first instruction or its last: a declaration's at its first declared NAME (the store, and the
  variable's `llvm.dbg.declare` at its name's column: a parameter's on the function's line), a call statement's at its
  callee (a method's at its object), an assignment's at its left side, an `if`'s at its condition's first name, a
  loop's, a `switch`'s, a `return`'s and a jump's at its keyword (`ir_stmt_anchor/2`, which `ir_stmt/1` sets before the
  statement is lowered, every `ir_stmt` clause being `ir_stmt_/1`'s). The anchor is found in the line's text -- the
  debug file's lines, read once a build (`ir_dbg_src_line/2`) -- as a whole word, from the column of the statement
  before it on that line, else from the line's start (`ir_dbg_col/2`; `ir_line/1` asks it under `-g` only), a column in
  bytes, as clang counts; a statement whose anchor is not there -- a name the compiler made, a destructor run at a
  closing brace -- has the column of the line's first character that is no blank (the brace). A loop's step and its
  branch back are the loop's line and column (`ir_pos/1`, `ir_pos_set/1`): they had the body's last line. clang gives
  each EXPRESSION its own column (a load at its name, an operation at its operator), so its line table has more rows
  than this compiler's; the driver gate holds every row of a program's to one clang's table has for that line. Every
  location was column 1.
- THE PROLOGUE HAS NO LOCATION (0.130): the parameters' stores (`ir_run_lines/1` under `'$ir_dbg_prologue'`) carry no
  `!dbg`, as clang's have none, since LLVM puts the prologue's end, where a debugger stops at a breakpoint on the
  function, at the first instruction with a location: with the function's line on the stores, gdb stopped before them
  and `info args` read garbage. The line table is clang's, row for row (the driver gate: 3 4 5 8 9 10 11). (0.130)
- THE VARIABLES (0.130): every named local and parameter of a function with a subprogram is a `DILocalVariable` of the
  scope it is declared in, declared at its place by `llvm.dbg.declare` over its slot (`ir_dbg_var/3`, from `ir_local/3`,
  which every local and parameter passes through; the call has the variable's own location, the prologue's included): a
  parameter carries its number (`arg: K`, `'$ir_dbg_args'`), `this` the flags `DIFlagArtificial | DIFlagObjectPointer`.
  Every global the program defines is a `DIGlobalVariableExpression` on its definition, listed by the compile unit's
  `globals:` (`ir_dbg_global/3`; a tentative definition and its definition one variable, `'$ir_dbg_gvars'`), and a
  static local one in its function's scope (`ir_dbg_static_local/3`; `ir_dbg_var/3` leaves an `@` slot to it). A name
  the compiler made (`$tmp1`, `$ret`) is not described. (0.130)
- THE TYPES (0.130), DWARF's from the C types, each described once per module (`ir_dbg_type/2` over `'$ir_dbg_types'`,
  keyed by `ir_dbg_key/2`: a tag by its kind and name and a C++ class name by its tag, so `struct point` named through a
  pointer, a typedef and itself is one type): the base types by their encoding (`ir_dbg_encoding/2`: boolean, complex,
  decimal, float, UTF, signed or unsigned char, signed, unsigned), pointers (a pointer to a function points to the shared
  `!4`), references, rvalue references, `const` and `volatile`, typedefs (not a C++ class name, which is its class),
  arrays with their `DISubrange`, structs, unions and classes with their members at their bit offsets (a bitfield
  `DIFlagBitField` with its storage offset, a base sub-object `$base`, `$base$2` ... a `DW_TAG_inheritance`, an anonymous
  member unnamed, the table pointer and the compiler's other names left out; `ir_dbg_composite/5` over
  `ccl_members_layout/4`), enums with their enumerators and their underlying type (`DIFlagEnumClass` for a scoped one,
  `ccl_scoped_enum/1`). A tag named alone takes its members from the tag table (`ir_dbg_tag_members/3`). A type's number
  is taken BEFORE its members are described, so a struct that points to itself names its own number; a type with no
  description is described by its size alone (`ir_dbg_sized/3`). (0.130)
- THE LEXICAL BLOCKS (0.130): a block of statements is a `distinct !DILexicalBlock` inside the scope around it
  (`ir_dbg_block_enter/1`, `ir_dbg_block_leave/0` around `ir_stmt(block(Is))`; its line the first statement's), which its
  variables and its instructions' locations name; the function's own body is the subprogram's scope (`'$ir_dbg_top'`).
  (0.130)
- A DESTRUCTOR RUN AT A SCOPE'S END HAS THE LINE OF THE SCOPE'S CLOSING BRACE, on every exit -- the end, a `return`, a
  `break`, a `goto` -- as clang's has (0.139): the driver names the file it compiles under `-g` (`'$ccl_scope_ends_for'`),
  and the read of that file records the line of each compound's `}` against the block's declarations and its first
  statement (`ccl_note_scope_end/2`, `'$ccl_scope_ends'`: `v(Line, Name, Close)`, `b(First, Close)`); the desugaring
  gives a local's, a lifetime-extended temporary's and a by-value parameter's destructor call that line
  (`cpp_scope_end/3`, `cpp_body_end/2`). The AST does not change, and without `-g` nothing is recorded. It had the line
  of its object's declaration, and a debugger stopped at the declaration on the way out of the scope. The driver gate's
  check, read back by `llvm-dwarfdump --debug-line`. (0.139)
- EACH FUNCTION HAS ITS TYPE (0.130): a `DISubroutineType` of its result (`null` for void) and its parameters' types
  (`ir_dbg_fn_type/3`), `flags: DIFlagPrototyped`; gdb's `ptype twice` is `int (int, const char *)` and `finish` prints
  the value returned. (0.130)
- C++'S NAMES AND SCOPES (0.130; `cpp_dbg_fn/2`, `cpp_dbg_global/2`, `cpp_dbg_class_path/3` in the desugaring, asked by
  `ir_dbg_fn_scope/3`, `ir_dbg_global_scope/3` and `ir_dbg_tag_scope/3`): this compiler's own names stay the symbols,
  and the debug information says what the source says. A method's subprogram is named as the member (a constructor the
  class's own name, the destructor `~` and it, an operator `operator+`) in its class's scope, and LLVM puts it in the
  class's description, so `ptype` lists the methods; a free function its name in its namespace's `DINamespace`
  (`ir_dbg_ns_ref/3`, one per path), a function template's instance its name and its arguments (`sum<int>`, from
  `'$cpp_dbg_targs'`, noted where the instance is emitted, `cpp_dbg_note_targs/3`; a value with its type always,
  `g<4U>`, `h<5LL>`, `s<(short)9>`, as clang names a debug entry, 0.199, `cpp_dbg_spell/2`; an enumeration's value its
  number cast to the enumeration, `X<(Color)1>`, 0.203); a free operator `operator<<`; a class its own name -- an
  instance `Buf<int, 4>` -- in its namespace or the class that holds it (`cpp_dbg_holder_tag/2`); a static data member a
  member of its class (0.133; `ir_dbg_static_members/4`: a `DW_TAG_variable` with `DIFlagStaticMember`, after the data
  members, where clang keeps the declaration order), its definition's global named as the member in the class's
  namespace and pointing at it (`declaration:`, `ir_dbg_global_scope/4`), as clang's -- it was a global named
  `Class::name`, which `ptype` did not list; a namespace's global its name in its namespace. A compiler-made global (a
  table, a type's information) is not described. The program's own namespaces are `'$cpp_dbg_ns'(Name, Path)`, noted by
  `cpp_ns_resolve/2` under `-g`; a header's come from `cpp_hdr_ns/2`. gdb: `break shapes::Buf<int, 4>::get`, `break
  Counter::bump` (both overloads), `bt` with the qualified names, `print *this`, `ptype sq` with its base and its
  methods, `print k` as `shapes::Kind::square`, a `std::vector<int>` and a `std::string` printed member by member.
  (0.130)
- A LIBRARY function (`cpp_library_function/1`) gets no subprogram: its lines are a header's, and the table names one
  file. A function without a subprogram has no location on any instruction and no variable. (0.128)
- `ir_assemble/1` appends the module's own metadata (`ir_dbg_module/1`): `!0` the `DICompileUnit` (language
  `DW_LANG_C11` or `DW_LANG_C_plus_plus_14`, producer `cicilang <version>`, `emissionKind: FullDebug` or, under
  `debug(lines)`, `LineTablesOnly`, the globals, `nameTableKind: None` as clang has it on Linux, so gdb meets no
  `.debug_names` it ignores), `!1` and `!2` the two module flags LLVM asks (`Dwarf Version` 5, `Debug Info Version` 3),
  `!3` the `DIFile` (the base name and the directory of the absolute path), `!4` the type a function pointer points to
  and every subprogram has under `debug(lines)`, then the rest from `!5` on (`'$ir_dbg_md'`, `'$ir_dbg_n'`). A name or a
  path is escaped for a metadata string (`ir_dbg_escape/2`). Under `debug(lines)` (`ir_dbg_full/0` false) nothing but
  the subprograms, the blocks and the locations is made. (0.128, 0.130)
- THE MACROS (0.134; `-fdebug-macro`): `ccl_pp_macro_trace/2` preprocesses the file standalone, its includes in place
  as `-E` runs them, and records each `#define` and `#undef` at its line and each file it enters and leaves, entered at
  the line of the `#include` (`pp_mt_note/1`, a global per event, `'$pp_mt:N'`, since a list would be copied whole at
  each one; a guarded header included again is not entered, as clang's is not; a run that stops keeps what it saw). The
  lowering makes clang's tree (`ir_dbg_macros/3`): the compile unit's `macros:` holds the main file's `DIMacroFile` --
  its definitions and, at each `#include`'s line, the `DIMacroFile` of the header it enters, a `DIFile` per header by
  its path (`ir_dbg_mfile/6`, `ir_dbg_mfile_ref/5`) -- then every predefined macro this run answers and every `-D` at
  line 0 (`ir_dbg_predef_macros/3` over `pp_predef_macro/3`, the names sorted). A name is spelled as clang spells it
  (`F(a,b)`, `F(fmt,...)`, `F(x,rest...)`, `pp_mt_define/2`) and a body with one space for each run of blanks, none at
  its ends, a literal's own blanks kept (`pp_mt_squash/2`); a macro's string escapes `"`, `\` and every code outside
  printable ASCII as LLVM's two hex digits (`ir_dbg_mesc/2`). The lines are made in one list and added at once: a libc++
  header brings thousands, and `ir_dbg_md/1` copies the whole list at each line. gdb reads them (`info macro EOF`: defined
  at `/usr/include/stdio.h:105`, included at the file's line 1; `macro expand SQ(3)`); the driver gate compares a file's
  and its header's lines with clang's object (`llvm-dwarfdump --debug-macro`). The headers' and the predefined macros are
  this compiler's own (`library/include`'s headers, its predefined table), so their counts differ a little from clang's:
  765 and 741 definitions for a program over `<stdio.h>`. (0.134)

### The embedded LLVM

- `module/ccl_llvm.cicili` is the whole back end, a cocolog module over llvm-c (owner's rule: no clang, no LLVM
  binary). It initializes every target LLVM was built with (`ccl_ll_all`, 0.131), and a `--target=TRIPLE` flag makes
  the target machine that triple's, its CPU `generic` and its features the default ones (`ccl_ll_target_flag`,
  `ccl_ll_target_triple`); without one the host's triple, CPU and features. Its surface: `ccl_llvm_version/1`, `ccl_llvm_triple/1`, `ccl_llvm_check/2` (parse and verify) and
  `ccl_llvm_compile/3`. `cicilang_compile/3` calls it through `ccl_compile/3` (`library/ccl_build.pl`); without the
  module it is `no_embedded_llvm`. (M2, M5)
- `ccl_llvm_compile/3` parses and verifies the IR in a fresh context. It sets the host's triple, CPU, features and data
  layout, runs the pass pipeline, and writes an object file, or assembly under `-S`. An LLVM error is
  `error(ccl_llvm(What), Detail)`, for example `no_target`, `passes_failed` or `emit_failed`. (M2)
- The pipeline is `default<On>` for the flag's level (`ccl_llvm_pipeline`). When the flags name no level the module
  takes `-O1`; the driver passes `-O0` unless an `-O` flag is given. (M2)
- At `-O0` the pipeline is `default<O0>,globaldce`. `default<O0>` holds CoroSplit, which every coroutine needs.
  `globaldce` drops the `linkonce_odr` instances that nothing calls, such as libc++'s `iter_move` over
  `__projected_impl`, whose operator the library never defines. (0.108, 0.109)
- `module/build-llvm.sh` builds `library/ccl_llvm.so` with an rpath to LLVM. It links `-lLLVM-C` when `libLLVM-C.*` is
  in `llvm-config --libdir` (Homebrew), else `-lLLVM` (Debian, Ubuntu). Rebuild it after a change to
  `module/ccl_llvm.cicili` and after a cocolog update. (0.87)

## Time and memory

### Memory: every unit of work inside `\+ \+`

- cocolog reclaimed the heap only on backtracking before 1.8.36, and its collector ran inside no nested engine before
  1.9.4 (findings below). So each unit of work runs inside `\+ \+` and passes
  its result out through a global or a fact: a preprocessed file (`pp_include_file`, its output under `'$pp_out:N'`,
  spliced by `pp_finish`), a parsed item (`ccl_externals/4`: the item and the count of its tokens pass through
  `'$ccl_item'`, and `ccl_skip` restores the position), a gate check (`test/reader.pl`, `test/cpp.pl`). Why: a
  `std::vector<int>` build restarted the owner's machine. (0.46, 0.184)
- Large text is built a hundred items at a time, each chunk inside `\+ \+` (`ccl_ast_chunks`, `ccl_sum_chunks`).
  (0.71)
- `ck_items` scopes each checked function and `ir_items` each lowered item. A function's text is a global of its own
  (`'$ir_fdef:K'`, `ir_add_fdef/1`), never a list copied at each addition. (0.80)
- Each emission road of the desugaring runs inside `\+ \+`: `cpp_instantiate_class_` (an instance's whole body),
  `cpp_make_lazy`, `cpp_use_fn`, `cpp_instantiate_function_`, `cpp_make_member`, `cpp_nested_class`, `cpp_hdr_load`,
  `cpp_implicit_copy_ctor`, `cpp_implicit_assign`. Their facts and globals survive. (0.68, 0.80)
- A candidate's check runs inside `\+ \+` where the arguments and the explicit template arguments are ground
  (`cpp_candidate_check/5`, on the free, member and constructor roads); only the bindings come out, through
  `'$cpp_cand_out'`. (0.109)
- A goal that writes a global runs under `once/1` where a search can ask it again: `nb_setval/2` survives
  backtracking, and a `findall` once registered one temporary twice. (0.80)
- `cpp_spend/1` refuses `instantiation_budget` past 6000 loads and instances (3000 until 0.133); `cpp_deeper/1` refuses
  `instantiation_depth` past a nesting of 120. Why: a runaway instantiation took the machine's memory. (0.44, 0.133)

### Tables: a global is copied, a fact is indexed

- `nb_getval/2` and `nb_setval/2` copy the whole term (a read as one block since cocolog 1.12.1, and the copy of a
  GROUND value shared until a backtrack past its first read: the Findings' costs). So `ccl_items_note/1` sets each table
  once per unit tree (per-item writes were quadratic), and the file scope is its own table (`'$ccl_gscope'`, in buckets
  since 0.120, below): `'$ccl_scope'` holds only the open frames, and `ccl_declare/2` and `ccl_declared/2` never copy
  the headers' names.
- The globals are set once per process (`ccl_ensure_globals/0`) and read bare. `ccl_global/3` calls it first, so code
  that the initialization reaches reads with a bare `nb_current(K, V)` (`ccl_set_has/2`, `ccl_set_new_bucket/2`); else
  the initialization re-enters itself. A global that may be unset is read with `nb_current/2` (cocolog 1.12.0), which
  fails there in one inference, never with `catch(nb_getval(K, V), _, fail)`, a catch frame a read: 0.149 changed the
  156 such reads of the library and the gates (7 of them with a default in the recovery, now in an else), the answers
  the same, since every key the library makes is an atom (a key that is no atom raises `type_error(atom, K)` where the
  catch failed). A `catch/3` stays only where a call can
  throw (`time_file/2`, `proc_run/4`, a macro call, a candidate check), never around a hot read. (0.46, 0.149)
- A name set that the parser asks at every identifier is held in buckets, a global each (`ccl_set_has/2`,
  `ccl_set_add/2`, `ccl_set_new/3` over `'$ccl_envs'`, `'$ccl_tmpls'`, `'$ccl_ftmpls'`, and since 0.188 the no-throw
  names `'$ccl_nxs'`). A bucket's key is the name's
  first and last character and its length modulo 7, taken from its list of characters (`ccl_set_bucket/3`:
  `atom_chars/2`, `last/2` and `length/2`, a step each, 0.187; two calls of `sub_atom/5`, clauses over `between/3`
  since cocolog 2.5.0, took 0.68 s where they take 0.39 s for 240,000 keys, the count a read of `<thread>`'s
  flattened text asks). THE SET IS THE WHOLE RECORD (0.187): a list of every name stood beside each set until 0.186,
  for the snapshots, and each name added or taken away copied it whole -- a template's parameters joined the env and
  left it at the item's end, 12,397 copies of the env's list, 0.89 s of that read. A snapshot is the set's names
  (`ccl_set_list/2`, `ccl_env_names/1`), a rebuild puts them back (`ccl_env_put/1`, `ccl_templates_put/1`), and the
  names new to the env are logged as they join (`ccl_env_log/1`, the log cleared at each item of the item loop), so
  that a template head's leave takes away those logged after its mark (`ccl_env_since/2`). A deep grammar rule passes
  `genv` for the global env (`ccl_env_member/2`). A C++ tag is noted without its bodies (`ccl_slim_members/2`,
  `ccl_sum_slim/2`). (0.46, 0.187, 0.188)
- THREE TABLES ARE BUCKETED (0.120): the file scope `'$ccl_gscope'`, the typedefs `'$ccl_typedefs'` and the tags
  `'$ccl_tags'` are 128 globals each, `P_0` to `P_127` (`ccl_tab_g/3`), and an entry lives in the bucket its key's
  characters hash to (`ccl_tab_bucket/2`; a key that is no atom, a method defined out of its class, is in bucket 0,
  which the file scope keeps none of since 0.188, the symbol table's topic). A
  write or a lookup copies ONE bucket, 150 entries at 20,000 names: `ccl_tab_add/2` (one entry, or a bulk grouped by
  bucket), `ccl_tab_find/3` (by key), `ccl_tab_member/3`, `ccl_tab_list/2` (every entry, the buckets concatenated, for a
  reader that wants them all), `ccl_tab_reset/1`, and `ccl_tab_save/2` with `ccl_tab_restore/2` (a nested read's save and
  restore keep the buckets, `ccl_with_file/2`). Inside a bucket the order is the old list's, newest first, so the first
  entry that unifies is the one the single list gave; ACROSS buckets there is no order, and a caller with an UNBOUND key
  gets the first bucket's (every caller asks with the name). The drain functions follow `ccl_tab_list`, which is why the
  lowering version moved. `ck_declare_at/4` asks the open frames and the file scope apart for the same reason (the file
  scope is the LAST frame). Why: 800 file-scope declarations into 3,000 names and 6,000 lookups were 6 of the 15 CPU
  seconds of a `std::vector` build, and one write was 40 ms at 20,000 names. (0.120, 0.188)
- SEVEN OF THE DESUGARING'S REGISTRIES, lists in a global until 0.119, are facts (0.120): the class typedefs
  `'$cpp_ctype'(Class, Name, Type)`, the enclosing classes `'$cpp_encl'(Nested, Enclosing)`, the static initializers
  `'$cpp_sinit'(Class, Name, Init)`, the lazy library classes `'$cpp_lazy_c'(Class)`, the destructors defined out of their
  class `'$cpp_dtor_def'(Class)`, the names that keep C linkage `'$cpp_cname'(Name)` and the functions' default arguments
  `'$cpp_dflt'(Name, Defaults)`. A fact is found by its first argument and copies only what it answers. They are written
  NEWEST FIRST (`asserta`) and a lookup takes the first match (the cut), as `memberchk/2` did on the lists. The class
  typedefs alone were copied 38,777 times in a `std::vector` build (1.5 of its 9.6 s), and the heap those copies leave is
  what a nested engine does not collect. `test/cpp.pl` sets `'$cpp_encl'` for its mangler check. (0.120)
- The C++ registries that hold bodies are facts, cleared in `cpp_register_units/1`: `'$cpp_cls'`, `'$cpp_clsl'`,
  `'$cpp_tmpl'`, `'$cpp_spec'`, `'$cpp_mt'`, `'$cpp_inst'`, `'$cpp_out'`, `'$cpp_hdr'`, and the concepts,
  `'$cpp_concept'(N, concept(TPs, E))`. C's tables stay globals (a clause is a store row under `--embed`); C++ runs
  `--local`. (0.44, 0.112, 0.120)
- THE LIGHT CLASS RECORD (0.120): a class's record `'$cpp_cls'(C, cls(Base, Data, Members, Statics, Defaults, Slots))` is
  97% its members (every method with its body), so a lookup that wanted only the base copied the whole class:
  `cpp_base_scope/2` alone asked 44,764 times in a `std::vector` build, 2.6 of its 9.6 s. `cpp_class_put/2` writes beside
  the record `'$cpp_clsl'(C, cls(Base, Data, Statics, Defaults, Slots))` (a hundredth of the size), `cpp_class_l/2` answers
  it (a class not registered yet is asked of `cpp_class/2`, which loads it), and every caller whose members field was `_`
  asks that one. A caller that wants the members still asks `cpp_class/2`.
- THE MEMBERS A CLASS ONLY DECLARES (0.153): `cpp_shipped_member/5`, which the mangler asks of every member it names
  (does the shipped library define it?), copied the class's whole record to walk its members, and it answers no almost
  always; 0.152's time view found it (Finding a cost). `cpp_class_put/2` writes beside the light record a fact for each
  constructor and method whose body is `none`, `'$cpp_decl'(C, ctor | method(Name), Qualifiers, Parameters)`, in the
  order the class declares them; the record's replacement takes them away with it, and `cpp_register_units/1` clears
  them. The predicate asks `cpp_class_l/2` (which loads a class not registered yet, as `cpp_class/2` did), then the
  facts: it gives the answers it gave, in the same order, and the IR of 34 C++ fixtures is the same, byte for byte, over
  the two libraries. Three shapes were measured first, 1000 classes of 60 declarations each: the whole record 93 us a
  lookup, one list a class 17.5 us, one fact a member 6.2 us. Over the four library builds of 0.152's finding, the least
  of three runs each: the predicate 0.71 s where it took 8.93 s, the copies of a record through `cpp_class/2` 56,464
  where they were 102,737 (0.78 s against 7.57 s), and with `counter.cpp` the five builds 50.09 s where they took
  58.02 s; the 34 fixtures 275.7 s where they took 385.1 s, one run each, a string's and a stream's build near half
  (`stdstringstream.cpp` 38.1 s against 68.6 s).
- Per-process state is a global, never a dynamic clause (`'$ccl_reading'`, `'$ccl_macro_files'`, `'$ccl_unit_paths'`):
  a dynamic predicate persists under `--embed`.
- No header's macro table is parsed whole: a macro reaches a preprocessor run by name, on first use
  (`pp_outer_macro/3`, `pp_header_macro/3`). In C++ it is a fact, `'$ccl_hml'(Name, Path, raw(Line))`, parsed when
  asked (`pp_raw_macro/4`); in C it is the store's row under its name (`ccl_kb_macro/5`).

### Caches of the symbol table

- `ccl_cached(Cache, Key, Value, Goal)` keeps the Key-Value pairs found so far in one global, for a term key and a
  small value: layouts (`'$ccl_laycache'`), `ir_type/2` (`'$ir_tcache'`), `ir_abi/2` (`'$ir_abicache'`). A CACHED ANSWER
  IS ONE ANSWER (0.178): the goal of a miss runs under `once/1`, in both forms, as a hit gives one value. A caller that
  backtracked into a first ask got the goal's next answer, and the cache kept that one for every later ask: a struct's
  layout, which has an answer for each member it may skip, laid `I : virtual A` out without A, eight bytes for 24, where
  `cpp_vprim_inside/1` tested the size after the ask. (0.178)
- `ccl_cached_named(Prefix, Name, Value, Goal)` keeps a global per name and an index of the names, for a large value:
  typedefs (`'$ccl_td:'`), tags (`'$ccl_tag:'`), struct forms (`'$ccl_ts:'`), resolutions (`'$ccl_r:'`), the file
  scope (`'$ccl_g:'`), `ck_has_own_array/1` (`'$ck_oa:'`), a summary's tables (`'$ccl_sumload:'`), the asm labels
  (`'$ccl_asm:'`, 0.194). THE INDEX IS A GLOBAL THAT NO NAME'S OWN IS (0.194; `ccl_cache_index/2`): `'$ccl_cidx'` and the
  prefix, where a name's global is the prefix and the name. It was the prefix and `names`, the global of the name `names`
  too: the first ask of that name wrote its value there and the index over it, and every later ask answered the index, a
  list. A typedef, a tag or a file-scope name `names` asked twice took the list as its type, since 2026-09-06 (`typedef
  int names;` refused `phase(check)`, a class `names` lowered as `type([names])`), and a C global `names` took it as its
  asm label at 0.194, whose lowering asks the label of every global (`memory.c` in the compile gate's one process).
  `test/c/run/cachenames.c`, `test/cpp/run/cachenames.cpp`.
- `ccl_tables_changed/0` empties the small caches and the index of each `ccl_named_caches/1` prefix wherever a table
  is written (the noters, a summary's note, `ccl_scope_init/0`, `ccl_with_file/2`'s restore). `ccl_sum_forget/1`
  empties `'$ccl_sumload:'`.
- A miss is remembered as `'$ccl_miss'` for the `ccl_caches_misses/1` prefixes (`'$ccl_tag:'`, `'$ccl_td:'`,
  `'$ccl_ts:'`, `'$ccl_g:'`), only for an atom name asked with the value unbound. `ccl_gdeclare/1` marks each
  remembered name it declares `'$ccl_recheck'` (`ccl_gdeclare_recheck/1`), so the next ask looks again. Why:
  `cpp_path_class(std, _)` copied the whole tags table at every `std::` call. (0.112)
- A cached predicate is not re-entrant: both forms read the cache once before the goal and write it after, so a nested
  ask on the same cache is lost (a recomputation). An entry's computation never asks its own cache: it takes the
  `_nocache` form or asks nothing (`ccl_empty_layout/1` over `ccl_no_data_members/1`). (0.89)
- Ask a cached predicate with the output unbound, then compare: on a miss a bound output reaches the goal
  (`ir_type(T, x86_fp80)` met `ir_base`'s throwing last clause). Write `ir_type(T, LL), LL == x86_fp80`. (0.108)
- Answer by shape first: `ccl_resolve_type/2` takes a plain specifier list in one head and sends `base` to
  `ccl_resolve_base/3`; `ck_own_array_type/1` answers an array, a pointer or a plain type in one head each.
- A summary is parsed once per process (`ccl_sum_terms/2` into `'$ccl_sum:<File>'`, forgotten by `ccl_sum_write/4`),
  split once (`ccl_sum_load/7`), and its names added to the sets (`ccl_add_envs/1`, `ccl_note_templates/1`).
- `time_file/2` is never memoized: a memo served a touched file stale inside one gate process.

### Memos of the C++ desugaring

- An instance asked for again answers its name only (`'$cpp_iname'(N, Args, Name)`, the arguments compared with `==`).
  Why: a clause retrieval copies what it answers, here a template's whole item. (0.64)
- A function template's candidate set is made once per name (`cpp_fn_candidates/2`, `cands(N, Cands)` in
  `'$cpp_fncands:F'`, each key computed once by `cpp_fn_merge_defaults/3`), and again only where the count N of its
  templates moves. Why: each call of `std::get` (96 definitions) rebuilt it. (0.97)
- ONE FUNCTION TEMPLATE DECLARED TWICE IS ONE CANDIDATE (`cpp_dedupe_candidates/2`, `cpp_same_candidate/2`, `cpp_unlined/2`; the
  set is made once per name, above): a header's items come from every summary that flattened it, and `<format>` and
  `<string>` each hold libc++ 21's `back_inserter`, so a program that read both had it TWICE under one name. Alike means
  the same template head, storage, result, name, parameters and variadic mark and the same body once the line of each
  statement is set aside (`cpp_line_functor/1` lists the forms that carry one; a form the list lacks compares unequal and
  keeps both copies, as before); a declaration is alike to a declaration only. Why: the second copy is tried after the
  first, and when the first candidate's check refuses and leaves its instance half made -- `back_insert_iterator<void>`,
  whose `operator=(const typename _Container::value_type &)` cannot be declared; a class's name is recorded before its body
  registers and a refusal leaves it, which later asks of the NAME rely on (the views at libc++ 21 need it) -- the second is
  answered the name, holds, and emits a constructor of a class that was never made: `not lowered yet:
  typedef(back_insert_iterator.void)`. Forgetting the half-made instance instead was tried (0.126) and broke `viewchain`
  and `viewsall`: a registration that refuses and is asked again refuses again, where the name had been answered. A
  reduction needs libc++ 21 (`formatton.cpp`: `format_to_n` with `<string>` read first). (0.97, 0.126)
- The holding set is remembered per call shape (`cpp_holding_set/6`, `cpp_call_shape/5`, `hs(Hs, FirstRefusal)` in
  `'$cpp_hs:<key>'`): the name, the explicit arguments' VALUES (`cpp_targ_value`), each argument and its type, the
  template count, `'$cpp_class_ctx'`. An untypable argument disables it. Why by value: `get<__indx>` in libc++'s
  `__mu` differs per instantiation (`stdbind`). (0.97)
- A concept's satisfaction (`'$cpp_ccm'(C, Args, yes | no)` in `cpp_concept_holds/2`, cached as C++ caches it,
  [temp.constr.atomic]) and a variable template's value (`'$cpp_vtm'(N, Args, E)` in `cpp_instantiate_variable/3`) are
  remembered per ground arguments. Why: libc++'s ranges ask the same ones thousands of times. (0.112)
- The partial ordering's comparisons are tests under `once/1` (`cpp_most_special_fn/3`, `cpp_most_special/3`), and
  `cpp_fn_more_special/2` runs its prefix under `once`. Why: a comparison failing under `\+` retried every alternative
  before it, 4^k + 1 comparisons for k parameters. (0.95, 0.99)
- A library template's instance and a lazy library class emit only the members the program names
  (`cpp_lazy_instance/2`, `cpp_use_member/2`); a lazy polymorphic class emits only its slot implementations
  (`cpp_slot_fns/6`). The program's own templates stay eager, for the safe part. (0.52, 0.72)
- Measured at noise and taken out: a memo of the choice among the holding set (0.97), a kind pre-filter (0.98).

### The reader, the lowering and the processes

- The lexer that runs is native (`ccl_lex_native/6`, chosen once by a probe into `'$ccl_lexer'`), about 600 times
  faster than the DCG, which stays the specification and the fallback.
- The grammar chooses a clause by one look at the next token (`ccl_peek//2`, `ccl_unary_//3`, `ccl_primary_//3`,
  `ccl_postfix_p//3`), and one precedence-climbing rule reads the binary levels (`ccl_binary//2` over `ccl_binop/2`;
  owner's rule: a pattern is written once). Why: trying every alternative cost 30 token matches a token, against 8.
  Since 0.187 one look also tells an attribute (`ccl_gnu_attr//0`: `[`, `alignas` or a word of `ccl_attr_word/1`,
  asked 419,449 times in a read of `<thread>`'s flattened text, 0.57 s where it takes 0.06 s), the end of the
  specifiers (the first clause of `ccl_specs//8`, before 27 others: 1.35 s where it takes 0.79 s) and a qualified name
  of one identifier, which two clauses read only to test it (`ccl_qname_ahead//1`); with the sets as the whole record
  (above) and an out-of-class definition's name read once, that read takes 13.0 s and 115.0 million steps where it
  took 20.5 s and 164.3 million, its tree the same, byte for byte. Since 0.188 one look takes a specifier's keyword
  -- a storage word but `auto`, a qualifier but `_Atomic` and `constexpr`, a basic type (`ccl_spec_fast/2`) -- and a
  type's name of one word (`ccl_specs_type//7`), where a word went down the clauses one after another to the one that
  took it, the fifteenth for `int`: `ccl_specs/10`'s retries 0.70 s of a cold read of `<thread>` over libc++ 21, 0.23 s
  since. With the file scope's atoms, the no-throw set, the directive mark, the float walk and the text as atoms (each
  in its topic), the flat read takes 11.3 s and 98.7 million steps; that cold read 17.3 s and 170.3 million where
  0.187's library takes 22.0 s and 211.7 million, the trees the same, byte for byte. (0.187, 0.188)
- Text goes through builtins: `atomic_list_concat/3` splits a file, `atom_codes/2` and `memberchk/2` test a line, and
  only a line that needs it is walked code by code (`pp_clean/3`). On a hot path `sub_atom/5` has every position
  bound: since cocolog 2.5.0 it is clauses over `between/3`, and with its start free it tries every start (0.184: the
  test of a line for a raw string's `R"` took 26 us a line of 80 characters, where the split by it takes 0.7 us,
  `pp_raw_join/5`; a name's last character 8 us, where at its own position it takes 1 us, `ccl_set_bucket/3`; the cold
  read of `<thread>`'s text 27.3 s to 20.2 s, `between/3` 7.83 million steps to 1.05 million). (0.184)
- A read is linear in its items: the item loop counts the tokens an item took, never the length of the rest of the
  file (`ccl_item_length/3`, the C reader's topic). Until 0.183 that length, a walk of the rest of the file for each
  item and each body, was 58 % of a cold read of `<thread>`'s text. (0.184)
- A C++ library header is flattened and read once, never raw: raw, `<sstream>`'s headers each failed and were
  preprocessed in turn, for ten minutes.
- The lowering caches `ir_type/2` and `ir_abi/2` per type term; `ir_expr/4` carries the LLVM type beside the C type;
  `ir_join/3` is `atomic_list_concat/3`.
- The inference is at its floor. The check's cost is `ck_expr`'s walk, a `ck_in` lookup per node over the threaded
  `st(Frames)`; a further cut is a redesign (a state table per function, or the lookups in C).
- The host's arch and OS come from the module (`ccl_host_arch/1`, `ccl_host_os/1`), `uname` only without it. A build's
  only spawns are the link (`ccl_sh/3`), for a C++ summary `mkdir -p` (`ccl_sum_dir_ready`), and, for two or more cold
  library headers of a C++ build, a cocolog for each (0.188, the driver's topic).
- `bin/cicilang` forks about six times, where it forked twenty: every `$(...)` and every pipe is a fork.

### Finding a cost

- `test/prof.sh` (0.148, 0.152) says where a build's steps and its time go, from windows of its run recorded under
  `library(flow/debug)` (its topic): the calls by predicate, the steps, the callers, the goals asked more than once, and
  since cocolog 1.13.3 each predicate's inclusive and self time. It needs no scratch copy of the library. Its time is a
  sample of the run; the timers below measure a cost it names over the whole run. Its first reading (0.152) moved a cost
  from where the count put it: in `stdvector.cpp`'s windows `cpp_shipped_member/5` held 26.6 % of the inferences, nearly
  all of them `member/2` steps of a walk, and 33 % of the time, four fifths of it 295 single inferences that copy a
  class's record. 0.153 took the copy out (the Tables topic). The next reading of `stdvector.cpp`, 17.1 million
  inferences, has 41 copies of a record where there were 295, and outside the embedded LLVM's compile (46.7 ms of the
  windows' 76.3 ms) and the load of its module (12.0 ms), no predicate's own time reaches 1 ms: `dr_take/4` 1.0 ms,
  `between/3` 0.9 ms, `member/2` 0.8 ms. The RUN view's first reading (0.156, cocolog 1.15.0) is the whole build, 2.816
  s untraced: the copies of terms lead -- `findall/3` 381 ms (13.5 %), `nb_setval/2` 210 ms (7.4 %, 148,385 calls),
  `nb_getval/2` 91 ms (3.2 %) -- then `ensure_loaded/1` 125 ms (4 calls, the files the build loads), `member/2` 98 ms
  with its retries, `between/3` 85 ms, `memberchk/2` 75 ms, `cpp_type/2` 77 ms (nearly all of it retries) and the
  embedded LLVM's compile 35 ms; nothing is taken up yet. (0.148, 0.152, 0.153, 0.156)
- The memory trace is in the code: `cpp_mem/1` and `ir_mem/1` give `kb(Heap, Store)`
  (`statistics(globalused | store_used)`) on every `'$cpp_trace'` line (`cpp_trace_mem/1`, each spend), at each phase
  (`phase(check | lowering | assemble)`) and per lowered item (`lower(Item, Mem)`); `stmt_out(S)` shows the program's
  statements. Call cocolog directly: `bin/cicilang`'s filter drops the trace lines. (0.80)
- The breadcrumb is a stack of eight frames (`cpp_where/2`, `'$cpp_wstack'`), kept only under `'$cpp_trace'`, since it
  is entered at every statement: `class`, `fn`, `load`, `member`, `sig`, `subst`, `body`, `auto`, `call`, `args`,
  `stmt`, `scope`. `cpp_refuse/2` prints `refuse(What, in(Stack))`, and an instance keyed by a free name prints
  `free_name_instance(N, A, ctx(C), making(M), from(Stack))`: such an instance can run to the cap. (0.87, 0.93)
- Rank time by CPU per trace line: a scratch copy stamps `statistics(cputime, T)` on each line, and a script sums the
  gap after each line by its functor. A count of one event (per comparison, per deduction) then names an exponential
  that switching rules off one at a time could not. (0.95, 0.99)
- A FLAT PROFILE, made by a script (0.120; cocolog has no profiler, and the script is session scratch, not in the
  repository): a scratch copy of `ccl_cpp.pl` and `ccl_infer.pl` in which every rule and fact begins with a goal that stamps
  `statistics(cputime, T)` and adds the time since the last stamp to the clause entered BEFORE it, the stamp taken again as
  the goal ends so that the instrument's own cost is not charged, and a dump after a CPU limit. A clause is charged for what
  runs after it is entered and before the next one is -- its own goals, the builtins it calls, the callees that are not
  instrumented -- so a builtin's copying (`nb_getval/2`) is its CALLER's. The overhead is a factor of three; the ranking is
  the work's. On a `std::vector` build, `cpp_class/2` was 19% and `cpp_class_typedef/4` 12%, the rest flat. A smear names a
  region, not a line: timers in situ around the suspected reads (`statistics(cputime)` before and after, summed in a
  global) then measured the copies themselves -- the class record 68,075 times, 2.61 s; the class typedefs 38,777 times,
  1.23 s; the enclosing classes 29,700 times, 0.06 s -- and a count of one predicate per CALL SITE (`cpp_base_scope/2`
  alone, 44,764 times) named who asked. The dump comes at the CPU limit whatever the program is doing, so it serves a build
  that does not end as well as one that does.
- Rank memory by event: sum the heap stamps by the event before each growth. Trace at a LOW cap to see what is in
  flight when the memory goes; spends against distinct instances tell breadth from a loop. A loop grows to the cap and
  raises nothing, so each failing candidate step traces itself (`ctor_candidate`, `ctor_no`, `member_refused`,
  `sig_failed(F, Step)`). (0.64, 0.68, 0.109)
- Rank every predicate's calls before touching a pass: a scratch library first on `COCOLOG_LIBRARY`, every rule HEAD
  wrapped by a counter (heads only: renamed calls bypass the wrapper).
- Attribute time with stubs, ten runs deep: one clause stubbed in a scratch library
  (`ck_anchor_addrs(_, St, St) :- !.`), the pass run ten times in one process. A stub must be SEEN to succeed: one
