  that failed fast read as the cost.
- Take the phases apart before guessing: the read alone (`cicilang++ -fsyntax-only`), then `ccl_cpp_units` alone. Why:
  the serial gates' seven hours were one cold read done twice, on one core of four. (0.64, 0.105)
- Measure against a baseline: probes that differ by one line, beside one that calls nothing; a fix that breaks it is a
  wrong edit. A bad thing in a trace is not THE cost until the CPU time says so. A dominant cost hides the rest, so
  measure again after each fix. A rise can be right, where work had been skipped. (0.65, 0.68, 0.92, 0.95)

## Findings about the neighbours and the instruments

### cocolog, Cicili, the installer and the host

- cocolog collects the heap since 1.8.36 (`coco_heap_gc`, a sliding mark-compact, the trail with it): between two
  steps of the outermost engine, when it is the only engine running on the machine and its host turned it on (the
  `query` host does), and since 1.9.4 inside a nested engine too -- `findall/3`, `forall/2`, `aggregate_all/3`, a
  search a builtin starts -- once that search has grown by the floor itself (`coco_gc_nested_begin`; a load's goal only
  where its caller vouched, cocolog's own notes). Measured at 0.161 on 2.2.5: a deterministic loop that makes a 41-cell
  term at each turn and keeps none, thirty million turns (some 9.8 GB of cells), peaks at 42 MB with 536 collections at
  the top, inside `findall/3` and inside `forall/2` alike, about 13 s each. It runs between steps only, so a module's C
  frame never holds a moved cell: the
  native lexer and the embedded LLVM are safe. Before it, the heap came back on backtracking only (on 1.2.12 thirty
  million-integer lists built deterministically took 521 MB, and 42 MB inside `\+ \+`): hence the `\+ \+` scoping
  above, which still serves the work inside a `findall/3`. Measured on the `std::format` build, warm: 1.8.1 peaked
  at 2882 MB, 1.8.38 at 591 MB. After a cocolog update the modules are rebuilt (`module/build.sh`,
  `module/build-llvm.sh`, and cocolog's `os` and `process` modules); 1.8.36 to 1.8.41 left the SDK's ABI unchanged.
  (0.46, 0.112, 0.114)

- SINCE 2.3.0 (`ee0073a`) A CALL SEES THE CLAUSES THAT STOOD WHEN IT BEGAN, ISO's logical update view, as swipl's: an
  assert or a retract while a call is open on its predicate moves nothing that call has still to try, and a new call
  sees the clauses as they are. Through 2.2.5 a retry read the live clause list: measured at 0.182, `forall(q(K),
  retract(q(K)))` over five clauses left two on 2.2.5 and none on 2.11.0. The library's loops that write a table read
  another, or test the one they write by a new call (`\+ '$cpp_lvb'(C, N, _)` in the generator before the
  `assertz/1`), and its registries are read whole by `findall/3` before they are cleared (`cpp_flush_instances/2`), so
  each answers alike under either view. (0.182)
- SINCE 2.5.0 THE NUMBER READERS TAKE THE WHOLE TEXT (measured at 0.182): `atom_number('12abc', N)` and
  `atom_number('12 ', N)` fail, `number_codes(N, "12 ")` raises `syntax_error(illegal_number)` and `number_string(N, "
  42 ")` fails, where 2.2.5 read the number at the text's front (12, 12, 12 and 42); a leading blank is still taken
  (`atom_number(' 12', 12)`), and `1r3` reads as a rational (`atom_number('1r3', 1r3)`, 1 on 2.2.5). Each call of them
  in the library and the gates passes the digits of one number and no `r` -- a name's numbered part (`'$anon'`, `$A`,
  an arity, `llvm-NN`), an IR type's width, a decimal literal's exponent, a pp-number's digits, and the DCG lexer's
  float text, which it makes whole (`1.` is read as `1.0`) -- so nothing moves; the reader gate's `k84` compares the two
  lexers token for token. (0.182)
- cocolog counts text in CHARACTERS since 2.0.0, as SWI does, where 1.13.0 to 1.15.0 counted bytes unless a program
  asked for characters (the flag `text_units`, 1.13.0): bytes are asked for by `:- set_prolog_flag(text_units,
  bytes).`, or `COCOLOG_TEXT_UNITS=bytes` for a whole run, and give 1.x's answers. In characters `atom_length/2`,
  `atom_codes/2`, `sub_atom/5`, `char_code/2` and the reader's `0'c` count code points (`atom_length('café', N)` is 4,
  `atom_codes('é', Cs)` `[233]`), and a module that hands codes back asks the run's units (`coco_m_codes_of`). cicilang
  answers alike in both: the native lexer takes a line as its bytes and hands its tokens back as atoms and lists of
  byte codes, which it makes itself, and the passes work on what it gives. Measured at 0.151 under
  `COCOLOG_TEXT_UNITS=characters`, the flag answering `characters` inside a `#cocolog` block: a program of narrow and
  wide strings with `\u` and `\N{...}` built and printed clang's answers, `-E` spelled the same text as in bytes, and
  the reader and compile gates over a fresh store were GREEN; since 0.157 every gate runs in characters, and the whole
  chain of 0.157 is GREEN on 2.1.0, the C++ side's first run in them. A `#cocolog` block or a `.pl` macro file runs in
  the run's units: one that counts text past ASCII asks `current_prolog_flag(text_units, U)`. (0.151, 0.157)
- Through 1.10.27 cocolog's build exhausted the 1 GB heap that Debian's and Ubuntu's SBCL 2.2.9 starts with, while
  Cicili transpiled `cocolog.cicili` (`Heap exhausted during garbage collection`, then `GC invariant lost, file
  "gencgc.c"`), and a `make modules` after the failed `make` skipped the flow tables with no word of why. Since 1.10.28
  a plain `make` gives SBCL 4096 MB (`tools/cc/sbcl`; `COCO_SBCL_HEAP=N` for another size), and `make modules` names
  why it skips anything. Our own `module/build.sh` fits the default heap. (0.140, 0.142)
- Since cocolog 1.10.17 an error nothing caught is followed, on stderr, by where it was raised; `bin/cicilang`'s filter
  drops those lines, so call cocolog directly to read them (`--no-backtrace` turns them off). (0.140)
- Through 1.10.27 cocolog WROTE A FLOAT WITH 15 DIGITS, `%.15g`: a 16- or 17-digit double written and read was another
  double, the largest double read back as an infinity, and an infinity was `inf.0`, which its own reader refused. Since
  1.10.28 it writes a float as SWI 9 does, the fewest digits that read back as the same double (`0.30000000000000004`,
  `1.0e+22`, `5.0e-324`, `100000000000000.0`, `1.0Inf`, `1.5NaN`; a NaN's sign is never written), reads `1.0Inf` and
  `1.5NaN` back, and keeps the sign of `-0.0` in its reader and in `-/1`; `copysign/2` and `atan2/2` are no functions,
  `sign(-0.0)` is `0.0`, a float divided by zero was an infinity (it raises `zero_divisor` since 2.2.0), and through
  2.1.1 `=:=` held for a NaN against any number, 0.0 among them (`<` and `>` held for none), where since 2.1.2 a NaN is
  unordered, only `=\=` holding of it, as SWI's. Every store write here still freezes its floats to integers (the store
  topic, 0.132), exact under either writer and over a store written before. (0.132, 0.142, 0.158)
- cocolog was at 1.9.1 from 0.117 (it was 1.8.41; ZiguratIP is rebuilt first, then cocolog, then both modules here). The
  baseline of that step was 0.116 over 1.9.1, all seven gates GREEN, so the engine's compiled-control stages (1.8.55,
  1.8.57, 1.9.1: one dispatch per functor, an index on any argument) changed nothing cicilang relies on. cocolog's own
  reader refuses an integer literal past 61 bits since 1.8.50 (past 64 bits since 2.0.0); cicilang writes none
  (`big(Atom)`). (0.117)
- Since cocolog 1.8.39 a load directive that loads nothing says so, in SWI's two lines (`ERROR: ... source_sink
  `library(X)' does not exist`, then `Warning: ... Goal (directive) failed`), and the load goes on; it was silent
  before. cicilang's directives name only libraries that exist (`process`, `os`, its own), and every `ensure_loaded/1`
  of a cache file asks `exists_file/1` first, so no run prints them. A missing `os` or `process` module now prints them;
  `bin/cicilang`'s filter drops the lines. 1.8.40 and 1.8.41 add the translation library (`library/reasoning/`), which
  cicilang does not load. (0.114)
- The store compacts itself since cocolog 1.2.13: once 32 MB or more of cells are dead and outnumber the live ones, a
  safe point copies the reachable terms to a fresh array (sized at the live length since 1.2.14). `garbage_collect/0`
  forces it; `statistics(store_used, B)` reads it. It is the process's array, not the disk. Before it, `nb_setval`
  overwrites left most of a build's store dead. (0.79, 0.84)
- On disk a process that writes a predicate rewrites all of it, about 360 bytes per row it holds (500 measured here);
  a read-only process adds nothing. Dead rows stay until `cocolog vacuum` (since 0.128 every 64th run of
  `bin/cicilang` and each gate vacuum the store). A write is LINEAR in its rows since ZiguratIP 1.0.1 and cocolog 2.x
  (measured at 0.161 on 2.2.5: one process asserting 10,000 to 640,000 rows of one predicate into a fresh store took 148
  ms to 8.8 s, the commit at its end included, twice the time for twice the rows, some 385 bytes a row on disk, and a
  read back 43 ms to 2.9 s); it was quadratic past about 30,000 rows at 1.2.16. A LATER process that adds one row to a
  predicate of N rows still rewrites all of it: 1.0 s and 15 MB more on disk at 40,000 rows, 3.9 s and 61 MB at 160,000,
  where a row of another predicate costs 27 to 45 ms and nothing on disk. So
  the AST cache is one predicate per file (`'$ccl_items:<Path>'`), no C++ header enters the store (`cicilang++` runs
  `--no-kb`), and the store is stamped `Reader.Lowering` and started afresh when a version moves (`kb_prepare`,
  `ccl_kb_prepare`).
- A writer killed mid-write can damage the store (`hexmap ends inside the chunk`). It is a cache:
  `rm -rf ~/.cicilang/KB ~/.cicilang/KB.version` repairs it. (0.108)
- INTEGERS ARE 64 BITS SINCE cocolog 2.0.0 (`d17fef4`): a value past 61 bits (60 since 2.5.0's four-bit cell tag) is
  boxed as a float is, and a result past 64 bits, the least integer `// -1` and a `<<` that loses a bit raise
  `evaluation_error(int_overflow)` (`1 << 63`, `10^18 * 997`), where SWI makes a bignum; a literal past the range is a
  syntax error, `atom_number/2` and `number_codes/2` fail for a numeral past it, the flag `bounded` is true and
  `max_integer` 2^63 - 1. Through 1.15.0 they were 61-bit and `is/2` wrapped in silence. cicilang leans on neither: a
  literal past 2^60 is `big(Atom)` in both lexers, the constant evaluator computes 64 bits and more over base-2^30
  limbs (`ccl_w_*`, the 64-bit arithmetic topic), and `dr_fold/4` keeps two folds under 2^31; the chain of 0.157 is
  GREEN on 2.1.0, the library unchanged.
  (0.94, 0.157) Through 1.13.7 `X >> N` and `X << N` took N modulo 64, as the machine's shift does (measured at 0.154
  and 0.155 on 1.13.3): `1 >> 64` was 1, `1 >> 128` 1, `255 >> 64` 255 and `1 >> -1` 0, where SWI answers 0, 0, 0 and 2,
  and `1 << 64` 1 and `1 << 65` 2, where the 61-bit wrap of the true value is 0: cocolog shifted two C `i64` values
  (`lib/solve.cicili`'s `is/2`, `lib/kb.cicili`'s compiled arithmetic), a shift that C leaves undefined for a count past
  63 or below 0 (6.5.7/3). Told to cocolog's owner at 0.155 and answered by 1.14.0 (`52abc90`): a count past 63 gives a
  right shift the sign of its left side and a left shift 0, a negative count shifts the other way, as SWI's does (`1 >>
  -1` is 2), and a left shift goes through `u64`, in both evaluators (`coco_shift_right` and `coco_shift_left` in
  `lib/term.cicili`). `ccl_w_shr/3`'s own test of the count went with it; the bitfield masks past 60 bits are the wide
  arithmetic's, since a 61-bit integer holds none of them (the Object layout topic). Through 1.14.0 a shift of a float
  or by one raised `type_error(integer, P)` with the loaded file's path as P (the culprit was heap cell 0, cocolog's
  owner says); since 1.15.0 P is the value, as SWI's is (`1.5 >> 1` and `1 >> (1.0 + 0.5)` raise `type_error(integer,
  1.5)`). cicilang shifts no float. (0.154, 0.155, 0.156)
- THROUGH 1.15.0 `compare/3` ORDERED TWO INTEGERS AS DOUBLES (measured at 0.156 on 1.14.0 and 1.15.0, the same on
  every kept build back to 1.10.22; cocolog's owner named it first): two integers that differed only below a double's
  53 bits were equal to the standard order -- `9007199254740993 == 9007199254740992` held, `@<` and `@>` both failed,
  and `sort/2`, `setof/3` and `list_to_ord_set/2` kept one of the two -- where unification, `memberchk/2`, the
  arithmetic comparisons and a clause's selection by its first argument were right. cicilang met it where it compares
  two integers by the standard order: `ccl_w_cmp/3` answers by `compare/3` for two integers, and every comparison of
  the constant folder goes through it (`ccl_const_op/4`); the C++ desugaring compares argument lists with `==` (the
  instance memo `'$cpp_iname'`, the variable template memo `'$cpp_vtm'`, the concept memo `'$cpp_ccm'`,
  `cpp_same_value/2`). Four probes against clang gave wrong answers with no message: with `A` `9007199254740993LL` and
  `B` `9007199254740992LL`, the enum value `(A > B)` was 0 and `(A == B)` 1, `char b[(A > B) + 1]` had 1 byte, a valid
  `_Static_assert(A != B, "")` was refused and `#if A == B` took its `#error`; in C++ `V<B>` was given `V<A>`'s
  instance, a specialization written for A was taken for B, a variable template answered A's value for B and `if
  constexpr (A == B)` took its first branch. Told to cocolog's owner at 0.156 and mended by 2.0.0, which orders two
  integers exactly (an integer and a float as doubles, the float first when equal, swipl 9.0.4's): on 2.1.0 the four
  probes print clang's answers, the library unchanged (0.157). Since 2.1.0 `=@=/2`, `\=@=/2` and `subsumes_term/2` are
  SWI's (`=@=` and `\=@=` operators at 700 xfx); the memos' keys hold no variable, so `==` and `=@=` answer alike
  there. (0.156, 0.157)
- THROUGH 2.1.0 UNIFICATION, `==/2` AND `compare/3` TOOK `0.0` AND `-0.0` AS EQUAL (measured at 0.157, alike on 1.15.0
  and 2.1.0): `0.0 = -0.0` and `0.0 == -0.0` held, `compare/3` gave `=`, `sort/2` kept one of the two, and a fact whose
  first argument is `0.0` answered a call with `-0.0` and the reverse; two NaNs computed apart did not unify, while `==`
  held and `compare/3` gave `=`, and a fact keyed by a NaN answered nothing. Since 2.1.1 (`a7a5841`) floats are told
  apart by their bits, as swipl 9.0.4's are: `0.0 = -0.0` and `0.0 == -0.0` fail (measured at 0.158 on 2.2.0), a head's
  `p(0.0)` takes no `p(-0.0)`, a NaN unifies with itself, and in the standard order a NaN comes first and two zeros or
  two NaNs go by their bits; arithmetic still compares numbers (`0.0 =:= -0.0` holds). cicilang leans on neither: the
  lowering tests a zero with `=:=` and reads its sign off the text cocolog writes (`ir_neg_zero/1`), a folded value
  keeps its sign in a field of its own (`x/3`, `bv/3`), and a NaN travels as `nan(S)`, never as a float. One place
  waits: the store's freeze writes every zero `'$fl'(0, 0)` (`ccl_float_parts/3`), so a stored `-0.0` would come back
  `0.0`; no read holds one, since a literal has no sign and a minus is a node of its own. Two clause heads of the
  library hold a float constant, each asked with that argument free: `ccl_binop('<=>', 7.5)`, a precedence the grammar
  compares by arithmetic (0.157 said no head held one), and `ccl_float_infinity(1.0Inf)` (0.158); no float is compared
  as a term. (0.157, 0.158)
- SINCE 2.2.0 (`2b7df28`) A FLOAT THAT IS NO NUMBER RAISES, as swipl 9.0.4's `check_float()` does at its float flags'
  defaults (cocolog has no flags): an arithmetic function -- `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`, `**`, `^`, `sqrt/1`, the
  transcendentals, `exp/1`, `log/1`, `float/1` -- whose float result is a NaN raises `evaluation_error(undefined)` and
  an infinity `float_overflow`, and each float OPERAND is checked first, so arithmetic on an infinity raises (`1.0Inf *
  1.0`, `float(1.0Inf)`); a number divided by a float zero raises `zero_divisor` (`0.0 / 0.0` `undefined`); `log(0.0)`
  raises `float_overflow`; `X ** 0` is the integer 1, `2.0 ** 0` too; `truncate/1` and its kin hand a NaN or an infinity
  back; a comparison, `abs/1`, `sign/1` and unary `-` and `+` are not checked, and an underflow is a number (`1.0e-300 *
  1.0e-300` is `0.0`). 0.157's library failed on it in three ways, measured: the freeze of the largest double raised
  (`ccl_float_parts/3` told an infinity by `F =:= F * 2`), so reader check `k93` failed and no C++ summary of a header
  whose AST holds `__DBL_MAX__` -- `<vector>`, through `<limits>` -- was written, and every build read it cold
  (`stdvector.cpp` 71 s a build, where 0.158 takes 63 s cold and 2.7 s warm); six C run fixtures stopped at `not lowered
  yet: item(declaration(G), raised(error(evaluation_error(float_overflow), _)))` (`decfold`, `fpconst`, `fpspecial`,
  `hexfloat`, `ldconst`, `negzero`: an infinity made by `1.0e308 * 10.0`, tested by `F * 2`, or met by the fold's own
  arithmetic); and three ran until their cap (`complex`, `complex2`, `fpintexpr`): `ir_fp_const/3` takes an integer by
  rounding it to the format and asking itself again, and `0 * 2.0 ** 0` is the integer 0, so a floating global's integer
  zero -- `double g = 0;`, the imaginary part of `double _Complex g = 2.0;` -- went round for ever. cicilang leans on
  none of it since 0.158: an infinity is told by a comparison with the largest double (`ccl_float_infinite/1`), never by
  `F =:= F * 2`, and made from its text, the fact `ccl_float_infinity(1.0Inf)`, never by `1.0e308 * 10.0`, and unary
  minus negates it; a double's exponent estimate is held to -1074 to 1023 (`ccl_float_norm/4`: `floor(log(X) / log(2))`
  is 1024 for the largest double, and `2.0 ** 1024` raises); a power of two that scales an integer takes the integer as
  a float (`float(T) * 2.0 ** L`: the store's thaw, `ir_fp_bits_value/5`, `ir_round_bits/5` and the three decimal
  conversions); a value that may be a float is made one with no arithmetic on it, itself where it is one, else
  `float(X)` of the integer (`ir_fp_float/2`), never `X * 1.0`; the fold of a double's `+ - * /` takes the long double's
  exact road (the Lowering's bullet of a negative zero); and the DCG lexer's hex float takes an overflow as the infinity
  (`ccl_hex_scale/3`). On 2.1.0 the repaired library gives the old one's IR, byte for byte, for the 80 C run fixtures
  and 13 C++ ones, and on 2.2.0 the IR it gives on 2.1.0 for the 80. (0.158)
- Through 1.10.27 a refused allocation was a WRONG ANSWER: the `oom` flag was set at eleven growth sites and read only
  by the compaction, which declined and kept the store; new terms then aliased cell 0, the query answered `false.`,
  printed `ERROR: ?-: Unknown message: _G0` and exited 1, and the heap and the choice stack ended the run with an `out
  of memory` that nothing could catch. Since 1.10.28 a refused allocation raises `error(resource_error(memory), _)`
  (SWI's `Not enough resources: memory`), which `catch/3` takes: a catch-all here (`catch(G, _, fail)`) takes it as it
  takes any error, and the run goes on. No run here has met it: the caps kill a run first (a watchdog over the RSS,
  never `ulimit -v`). A gate that dies of the MACHINE's memory runs clean alone; `test/cpp.sh` then prints `RED: the gate
  did not finish (query exit N)` and the raw tail. (0.84, 0.142)
- Fixed in cocolog 1.1.0: a `catch/3` whose goal succeeded stayed live for a later `throw/1`; a throw in
  `findall/forall/aggregate_all` escaped its catch; `atomic_list_concat` segfaulted on an unbound element and failed
  past 8 KB. Kept as habit: every `catch/3` under `once/1` or as a condition, a raising loop written as recursion,
  `new/3` checking its initial values first. The first habit still pays (measured at 0.149, on 1.11.10 and 1.12.1): a
  `catch/3` whose goal succeeded leaves a choice point, so a deterministic recursion of a million bare
  `catch(nb_getval(K, V), _, fail)` took 1.0 s and kept 295 MB of heap and 24 MB of trail, under `once/1` 0.21 s and
  32 MB, where `nb_current(K, V)` and a bare `nb_getval/2` took 0.2 s and kept 13 MB. 37 of the library's 153 reads
  that 0.149 replaced stood bare in a clause body (`ccl_set_has/2`'s, asked at every identifier, among them), the rest
  in a condition, under `\+` or under `once/1`; the builds measured at 0.149 show no change, since a cut or a caller's
  condition soon drops such a choice point. The catch alone, measured at 0.151 on 1.13.0 and on 1.12.1 alike: a million
  bare `catch(atom(a), _, fail)` kept 208 MB of heap and 8 MB of trail in 0.8 s, under `once/1` 10 MB in 0.19 s,
  followed by a cut 24 MB in 0.25 s, and a plain `atom(a)` nothing; told to cocolog's owner at 0.151. Since 1.13.4 a
  catch whose goal exited with nothing above it to retry takes its frame with it: measured at 0.155, the bare loop takes
  0.16 to 0.19 s and keeps 18 MB of heap and no trail on 1.14.0, where 1.13.3 took 0.81 to 0.94 s and kept 208 MB and
  8 MB. The habit stays, and costs nothing.
- Fixed in cocolog 1.2.0: a clause over a store row (about 8 KB; no limit under `--local`) silently lost every clause
  of its predicate. It now raises `resource_error(clause_length)`, which the writers catch to leave the file uncached
  (`ccl_kb_store_items`, `dr_ir_store`). Nothing large goes in one clause: a row per item, IR chunks of 3500
  characters, a row per dependency under `'$dep'`.
- Fixed in cocolog 1.2.2 (7f6a1ac): a first call probed the store at a cost growing with it. The stamp and the
  one-process gates stay, for the dead rows.
- `term_to_atom/2` with T bound, even partly, WRITES T and compares the texts
  (`term_to_atom(mnames(Ns), 'mnames([a])')` fails): parse into a fresh variable. Through 1.10.5 it read at most 8191
  characters (`char buf[8192]`, then `type_error(atom, A)`), so a summary's `tag(...)` line for a big class (`pair`,
  `tuple`, `optional`, `variant`, `basic_string`, `vector` ...) was dropped silently, until 0.112 wrote such a term to
  the `.big.pl` beside the summary. Since 1.10.6 it reads text of any length (an atom of 13,897 characters read back at
  1.10.22, 0.140); the `.big.pl` stays as it is.
- Through 1.10.27 an infinity was written `inf.0`, which cocolog's reader refused (`its clauses would not consult`, no
  line), so every literal past a double was clamped to the largest double (`ccl_finite_float/2`). (0.55, 0.142)
- The reader refused, naming no line, `is` as a plain atom argument, a quoted atom holding `"` and
  `append([declaration(...)] , Ifs, B0)`, and through 1.11.8 a load named no place (`run` said a byte offset, `-s` `its
  clauses would not consult`): such a file was bisected by its clauses, or by each hunk alone onto HEAD. Since 1.11.9 a
  syntax error in a load says where and why, in SWI's shape, from `run` and from a query's load alike: `ERROR:
  bad.pl:2:15: Syntax error: expected a term` (the column from 0, in bytes), `ERROR: ?-: use_module:
  /path/bad.pl:2:15: Syntax error: ...`. (0.93, 0.148)
- Through 1.11.7 `atom_chars/2` and `number_chars/2`, joining a list, crashed the process (SIGSEGV, exit 139) where
  its first or second element was no one-byte character, and failed silently on a list of 4096 or more; since 1.11.8
  they raise `type_error(character, X)` or `instantiation_error` and join any length. A character is one byte: a
  non-ASCII letter in such a list is an error, where SWI takes it. No file of cicilang calls either. (0.148)
- `cocolog --embed run FILE goal` consults FILE into the store, and a module's clauses do not reach the knowledge base
  (1.2.18): a gate program is loaded by `ensure_loaded/1` from a `query` (`reader_main`, `compile_main`, `cpp_main`).
  Every dynamic predicate asserted at run time persists under `--embed`. A second `ensure_loaded/1` replaces a file's
  clauses, which stay in the process, unstored.
- Seventy goal-carrying facts consulted into a store segfaulted once, and cocolog cannot reproduce it: the gate checks
  are clauses (`k1 :- check(Name, Goal).`).
- Builtins at 1.8.1, again at 1.10.22 (0.140) and at 1.10.28 (0.142). `current_predicate/1` answers for a file the
  program loads by its path (`-s FILE`, `ensure_loaded/1`, `use_module/1` of a file) since 1.10.28, and for no
  library's (`library(X)`) nor a builtin; it names no file, so a macro file's heads still come from `ccl_pl_clauses/2`.
  `predicate_property/2` is new at 1.10.28 (a control construct, `built_in`, `foreign`, `dynamic`,
  `number_of_clauses/1`; nothing for a `.so` module's predicates). Absent: `consult/1` as a goal, `load_files/2`,
  `flag/3`, `recorda/2`, `prolog_load_context/2`, `term_expansion`. `open/3` and `stream_position/2` are `library(stream)`'s (a module `make modules` builds), and
  `read_term/3` answers `term_position` since 1.10.7. Present: `abolish/1`, `clause/2`, `retract/1`, `nb_setval/2`, `b_getval/2`, `dynamic/1`,
  `read_file_to_codes/2`, `phrase/2,3`, `number_codes/2`, `statistics/2` (cputime, inferences, globalused, trailused,
  atoms, functors, store_used), `get_time/1` (microseconds); since 1.12.0 `nb_current/2`, `setarg/3` and
  `nb_setarg/3` (which no file of cicilang calls; on a value that a ground read shares, since 1.12.1, they change the
  global itself, so a term read from a global is copied first); since 2.0.0 `string_bytes/3` (a text's UTF-8 bytes),
  and since 2.1.0 `=@=/2`, `\=@=/2` and `subsumes_term/2`; `current_prolog_flag/2` answers ten flags, by name only
  (an unbound flag enumerates none): `executable`, `argv`, `os_argv`, `double_quotes`, since 1.13.0 `text_units`, and
  since 2.0.0 `bounded`, `max_integer`, `min_integer`, `max_tagged_integer` and `min_tagged_integer` (the cell's
  2^60 - 1 and -2^60). `time_file/2` answers whole seconds.
- `nb_getval/2` of an unset global throws an existence error. `nb_current(K, V)` (1.12.0) fails there in one inference;
  a bound K that is no atom raises `type_error(atom, K)`, and an unbound K enumerates the globals, so a key is made
  bound before the read. A global that may be unset is read through `ccl_global/3` (with a default) or `nb_current/2`
  (0.149), never through a `catch/3` around `nb_getval/2`.
- The query loop asks for a second answer, so an entry point is under `once/1` (`ccl_drive/2`). It reads standard
  input, so a background run gets `< /dev/null` and a pool job runs with `/dev/null` (`test/parlib.sh`): one job
  swallowed the queued job lines. (0.46, 0.106)
- Costs: `nb_getval/2` and `nb_setval/2` copy the whole term (0.63 ms for 5,000 pairs at 1.8.1), and so does a clause
  retrieval. Since 1.12.1 a read copies the value as one block, and a ground value read again with no backtrack between
  is the copy already made; measured at 0.149 over a global of 3,000 pairs `k(N)-v(N, abc)`: 25 µs a read after a
  backtrack where 1.11.10 took 163 µs, 0.4 µs a read again where it took 189 µs, and a value with a variable 23 µs a
  read after a backtrack. A global that is not there costs `nb_current/2` 0.04 µs and a `catch/3` around `nb_getval/2`
  0.36 µs (each over the 0.15 µs a step of an empty failure-driven loop). `memberchk/2` 0.15 µs a step; a fact among
  5,000 found by its first argument 3 µs, asserted 2 µs (under `--embed` a store row, indexed by an ATOM first argument,
  not `dep(I)`), where a global per name costs 25 µs; a predicate call about 5 µs; `catch/3` grows with the terms bound
  in it (37 ms against 0.3 ms bare); a code walk about 1 µs a code; `sub_atom/5` with a free position about 150 µs; a
  spawn 0.14 s and a shell fork 10 ms on macOS; the DCG lexer 0.15 ms a token whatever its clauses.
- The module SDK builds no compound: `coco_make/4` (lib/term.cicili, behind `coco_m_machine`) does. `coco_m_error/3`
  returns the predicate's ANSWER, not a status: a raising helper hands it back through an out parameter and returns 0,
  else its caller walks on into LLVM with a null module.
- The DCG translates `->` and `*->` in a body. `( A, ! ; B )` in a DCG body cuts the WHOLE clause, so it serves only a
  choice that decides the clause; an optional word is `( X ; [] )`. A misplaced cut once killed every inline function.
- A predicate whose name and arity are a nonterminal's plus two IS that nonterminal: `ccl_init_items/3` joined
  `ccl_init_items//1` and raised `Arguments are not sufficiently instantiated`, no line. Look a name up at its arity
  and at the DCG's. (0.93)
- `memberchk/2` on an open list binds its tail: never on an open accumulator. `atom_concat/3` on a compound throws: a
  name that may be compound is guarded with `atom(N)` (the noters, `ccl_resolve_base/3`, the mangler). (0.32)
- `::` is xfy: `a::b::c(X)` reads `a::(b::c(X))`; the objects layer has a `Recv::(Inner::Msg)` clause.
- The lexers write `"`, `'` and `\` as the codes 34, 39 and 92, since `0'"` and `0''` read badly in an older cocolog;
  the 1.8.1 reader takes any character after `0'`, not yet checked by a run.
- Cicili: a function is defined above every function that names it, else the transpiler says `unknown symbol: NAME`.
  (0.93)
- Cicili's module pattern: a C function outside Cicili's std is declared
  `(decl) (func Name ((Type arg) ...) (out Type))` with one-token types (`LLVMBool`, `char **`); `unsigned` needs an
  alias (`(@define (code "uint_t unsigned"))`). A header's enum constant or `static inline` goes behind a one-line raw
  C helper (`(code "static T ccl_ll_x(...) {...}")`, declared with `(decl)`). `(cof p)` is `*p`, `(? c a b)` the
  conditional, `(cond ...)` a chain; a `let` initializer that is no call is `(T x . nil)` then `(set x ...)`; no
  parameter is named `asm`.
- cocolog's installer took `ZIGURATIP_HOME=${ZIGURATIP_HOME:-$ZIGURATIP/home}`: an inherited value beat the caller's
  `ZIGURATIP`, nothing linked, and the completeness check audited the OTHER tree. Since cocolog 1.2.16 it refuses
  (`INSTALL RED: ZIGURATIP and ZIGURATIP_HOME name different trees`); `make EMBED=0` builds a store-less cocolog.
  (0.87)
- macOS's memory counters read LOW: a realloc moved by copy-on-write remap drops its pages from `/usr/bin/time -l` and
  ps's RSS until touched, so identical runs read 1.7 to 3.5 GB. The high reading is honest; Linux has neither effect.
  Ask `statistics/2` from inside (`cpp_mem/1`, `ir_mem/1`); a ps-RSS watchdog under-protects there. macOS does not
  enforce `ulimit -v`. (0.46, 0.79)
- On Linux a container's memory ceiling is set outside: `/sys/fs/cgroup/memory.max` reads `max` inside, and the OOM
  killer takes the biggest process. When a gate dies silent, run `dmesg | grep -i "killed process"` first. (0.87)
- dash, the Linux `/bin/sh`, has no `jobs -r`: the pool tracks its children by PID with `kill -0` (`test/parlib.sh`).
  (0.105)
- sh has no local variables: a helper's variable is its caller's, so each helper a pool job calls uses names no job
  uses (`_nd_cond`, `_nd_f`, `_nd_r` in `ccl_needs_met`). A MISSING verdict is the tell. (0.107)
- The Unicode name table comes from Perl's `Unicode::UCD` (`module/gen-uninames.pl`): python3's `unicodedata` is
  Unicode 14.0.0 and lists no alias, and the proxy refuses unicode.org. `charprop` is slow per Hangul syllable, so
  those names come from the Jamo tables. (0.104)
- COCOLOG'S `sub_atom/5` SEEKING A SUBSTRING WITH ITS PLACE UNBOUND IS QUADRATIC in the atom's length (2.11.6, 0.208:
  0.09 s over 10 KB, 0.84 s over 40 KB, 5.5 s over 100 KB, the substring absent), where `atomic_list_concat/3` split at
  the same string takes no measurable time. 0.208's libatomic test asked an IR's text so, and the compile gate went from
  29 s to 86 s, and the cross gate's build of `stdvariant.cpp` for aarch64 did not end in 23 minutes; the test splits
  the text (`ccl_ir_has/2`). Every other `sub_atom/5` of the library seeks in a name or a path. Raised with cocolog's
  owner and mended in cocolog 2.12.0: 0.001 s over 100 KB, 0.009 s over 1 MB; the split stays, as fast and plainer.
  (0.208, 0.209)

### Measurement and the instruments

- An instrument that answers without measuring the thing asked answers confidently and wrongly. The tell is an answer
  that came too cheaply, or at all when what makes it had just failed. Absence is evidence only on a channel known to
  carry a presence (macOS's counters, the installer's check, a sleeping clock, a stale binary, a filtered write, a
  missing runner's old log, a self-matching waiter). (0.88, 0.92)
- A wall clock counts a sleeping laptop. Compare timings only over windows known awake
  (`pmset -g log | awk '$4=="Sleep"||$4=="DarkWake"'`), and use CPU time where a number must mean something. A real
  slowdown is even; a sleep leaves the progress in bursts. (0.88)
- Change ONE variable and compare with the same fixture built on the COMMITTED library (a scratch copy of
  `git show HEAD:library/X.pl` first on `COCOLOG_LIBRARY`, its own HOME), alone and over the same cache. Measure
  BEFORE changing: a cap's bound is not a value. Name a cause only after measuring it; a number that looks right, or a
  probe of another road, measures nothing. (0.89, 0.92, 0.94)
- Run-to-run noise is up to a fifth on the owner's machine: only interleaved minimums of generated code mean anything,
  and a gate run again after an engine change claims nothing from its numbers. A gate's average moves with the box,
  the library version and the fixtures added: compare it on one box only. (0.90, 0.97)
- Every cocolog run has a memory cap and a time cap, a small fixture included (owner's rule), and a cap kills the
  whole tree: coreutils' `timeout -s KILL` signals the group it leads. A perl `alarm` kills only what it execs, so
  around `bin/cicilang++` (a shell) cocolog runs on. A watchdog put after a `#` on its line never runs. (0.46, 0.90,
  0.93)
- A memory watchdog sums every `cocolog ... query` on the box and kills them all past its cap (the session's
  `watch.sh`; `test/parlib.sh`'s pool past its hard cap). So: one guarded run at a time, or a cap of the sum. A probe
  beside a gate dies with it, and a "crash" may be that kill line above the verdict. A gate's watchdog follows the
  gate's process, never "any cocolog"; a probe watches its own process group. (0.93, 0.94)
- A waiter whose pattern matches its own shell waits for ever (`pgrep -f "cocolog ..."`): write `[c]ocolog`, or watch
  the RESULT file. (0.92)
- A KILLED GATE LEAVES ITS TEMPORARY DIRECTORY (`mktemp -d`: the `trap` does not run on SIGKILL), and a watcher that takes
  the last of `ls -d /tmp/cicilang-cpp-*/res` reads the dead run's verdicts as the live one's: it reported eight FAIL
  lines, all of the stopped first run of 0.118, while the live run had none. Take the newest (`ls -dt`), or remove the
  dead directory first; the gate's own log is the verdict. (0.119)
- After a reader-version bump every summary is cold: the next run flattens its headers in-process and peaks far above
  the steady state, and a run killed then writes no summary. A RED or a "regression" that comes with a bump is a cold
  cache until a warm run says otherwise; warm outside the gates (`test/libcxx.sh`). A mixed-age cache inflates a
  fixture, and a stale one reads as a fresh defect. (0.61, 0.89, 0.95, 0.105)
- A grammar or index edit WITHIN one reader version leaves the summaries of the older edit VALID (same key): a probe of
  the new edit runs over a HOME of its own, or the version is bumped. Over the old cache, `deque` missed its
  out-of-class statics (a link error, then a segmentation fault) and `<thread>` its operator, after both were fixed.
  (0.117)
- A COPIED HOME IS NO WARM HOME (0.156): a summary's `.big.pl` names its `.sum` by the absolute path
  (`'$ccl_sum_big'(File, I, T)`), so in a HOME copied to another path every summary that holds a big term is no longer
  valid and its header is read again (`<vector>`: 88 s where a warm build takes 3 s). Warm a HOME where it stays, and
  give a probe a HOME of its own, warmed there.
- Remove what a run can be served: a probe's HOME first (a leftover summary is served and nothing reaches the index),
  the binary before the build (a failed build ran the last one under its heading), and bump the lowering version with
  every change to what is emitted (`dr_ir/3` serves the stored IR). (0.44, 0.89, 0.103)
- Filtered output reads as silence. `bin/cicilang`'s filter keeps diagnostics and the `cicilang: ` and `unit(` lines:
  a debug `write/1` in the library shows only with a `cicilang: ` prefix, or with cocolog called directly. The link
  diagnostic keeps ld's first line only: link by hand to see the symbol. (0.90, 0.93)
- A flag that skips the stage under test passes for unrelated reasons: `cicilang++ -fsyntax-only` skips the
  desugaring, the check and the lowering, so it passes where a build fails and a probe inside them prints nothing.
  Instrument under `-S -emit-llvm`. (0.87, 0.103)
- A partial read is silent: `ccl_read_unit` takes it, and the symptom shows far away (`undeclared(printf)`). Find the
  stop with the census: `cicilang++ -E f.cpp -o flat.cpp`, then `sh test/census.sh flat.cpp` (`CCL_CENSUS_STD=20` for
  a level) prints the stop line, the farthest line, their tokens and a functor histogram. Bisect by census cuts. If
  the declaration alone compiles, the reader stopped short. To compare two grammars, call cocolog directly, the other
  library under its own HOME (`test/census.sh` puts this tree's library first). (0.44, 0.87, 0.93, 0.109)
- A step that merely fails lies: make each failure a named refusal and trace it (a half-registered class made every
  later lookup wrong, 0.46). A write allowed to fail never fails silently (`ast_not_written`, 0.71). A recovery that
  traces an error and then succeeds makes it a success (a valid summary with no AST, 0.106). A `catch` that maps an
  `existence_error` to failure leaves no refusal in the trace; a tracing `catch` on a scratch copy names it (0.98).
- A refusal that should fire and does not says the work was SKIPPED (0.69). A swallowed refusal hides: trace it
  (`refuse(What, in(W))`, `alias_refused`). A removed predicate still called is an existence error that the driver
  reports as the compiled FILE's error (0.83).
- A breadcrumb is scoped and stacked: an unscoped one names the last thing entered, a one-frame one the ask itself
  (0.65, 0.87). A trace prints refusals, caught ones too, so a refusal in a log is no cause (0.91). It never prints a
  choice: for a wrong pick read the emitted IR per function (`-S -emit-llvm`). A missing definition is a name in the
  trace (`implicit_copy(...)`) with no `lower(function(...))` after it. A refusal's NAME is a symptom: grep the AST
  beside a summary (`<name>-<fold>.ast.pl`) for the shape. (0.93, 0.94)
- Cut each defect to a reproduction of ten to twenty lines that fails in a second (0.87, 0.94). Take the cheapest
  evidence first: write the deduced `auto` type out (0.91); print the constants or traits a road turns on beside
  clang++'s (0.94). A passing reduction can mean the probe is wrong (a file-scope typedef where libc++ has a
  class-scope one; 0.92, 0.104). Stacked defects hide each other until the front one moves; one defect seen twice is
  one (0.91).
- An expectation comes from an independent compiler: clang or clang++, or the C mirror for the B-tree
  (`bench/btree/btree_cicilang.c`, `-O1`, 20000 keys). A self-consistent error passes the program's own fixtures (a
  mangling that agrees with itself, `std::string` at 40 bytes against libc++'s 24), so measure against clang++'s
  symbols, the shipped library's export list (`nm`) and clang++'s sizes and offsets. `nm -u` names what the link will
  refuse. Measure an assumption before relying on it (a hidden stream member's `inline` mark). (0.37, 0.55, 0.75,
  0.86)
- The gates run no leak checker: a fixture over owners is checked by hand (`leaks` and MallocScribble on macOS,
  valgrind on Linux). (0.41)
- A gate finds what probes do not: run the gate the change touches. A change to one overload rule is worth only the
  gate it passes, since the rules interact ("not an lvalue" is not "an rvalue"). (0.68, 0.91, 0.94)
- A gate that ends early reads like one that passed the rest: a truncated FAIL list is no pass list. A restart under a
  gate leaves no verdict (the log is written at the end): run it again alone. A missing runner's old log read as
  GREEN: a loop over gates takes each runner's EXIT STATUS, never a log it did not see written. (0.90, 0.93, 0.101)
- Identical numbers where they must differ are a tell: equal item counts across levels meant one read was served (the
  unit cache is keyed by path and level since 0.99). An order-only failure can then fail alone, a bad read STORED as
  the AST: reproduce in the gate's order in one process and read the store's rows (0.99). Measure a tool's coverage
  before believing it; its log names the list it ran (0.96).
- Every gate check has its own name and number: two clauses of one name both run, by backtracking.
- A clause's head is part of its answer: a body that computes a new result must reach the head (`cpp_lambda_`).
  (0.101)
- Look a variable up before giving it: a `findall` reused the head's `PT`, and every defaulted `<=>` answered "equal".
  When a step adds an argument to a predicate, read the clauses of that predicate for its name first: `ir_args_/5` got a
  register state `R0`, and an older clause that used `R0` for a resolved reference type failed silently, for every
  reference handed to a by-value aggregate (`refbyvalue.cpp`). (0.103, 0.117)
- Carry a lesson to every predicate that asks the same question (`ccl_class_size` and `ccl_empty_layout`). A shape is
  no test: refusing `typedef X X` by its spelling broke `allocator_traits`, where a guard per (class, name) fixed
  both. (0.86, 0.89)
- The passes rebuild the symbol table from the top-level items (`ccl_items_note/1`): what the reader notes only inside
  a body is lost to them unless the bulk noter collects it. (0.43)
- An instrument can break what it measures: markers on `user_error`, which cocolog lacks, failed the write they
  watched. (0.106)
- A string in an `.ll` file carries its length in its type (`[19 x i8]` in `proof/forty2.ll`): edit both. (0.100)
- THE FLOW TOOLS (cocolog 1.10.14 and later; `make modules` writes their tables). `library(flow/chart)` reads a
  program from one call pattern, runs nothing, and gives its findings at file, line and column (`flow_graph/3`,
  `flow_findings/2`; `cocolog -s $COCOLOG/tools/flow/chart.pl -- SPEC FILE BASE` also writes BASE.svg and BASE.xml).
  `library(flow/debug)` records the last steps of a run (`flow_debug/4`: a probe, then a replay, each a child
  cocolog) and reads back why a call failed (`flow_why/3`, `flow_why_call/4`, `flow_why_raised/3`,
  `flow_why_furthest/2`). 0.140 used them by hand and found the two predicates written twice (written once since 0.141);
  since 0.144 they are two instruments of this repository, the flow gate (`test/flow.sh`) and `test/why.sh`, each in
  its topic. What 0.144 needed of them went to cocolog's owner in thirteen items, and 1.11.4 answers each (0.146):
  - The chart reads ONE file and is given the rest as `load(Files)`; the charted file is stubbed out of the library
    path, else its clauses are read twice. A project's own C predicates are `modules(Files)`, the modules' Cicili
    sources, and the tables a program declares as it runs count as declared where they are declared with a written
    name (`dynamic/1`, an assert, one level of a declarer such as `cpp_reset/1`) in the files the chart reads, follows
    through `load(Files)`, or reaches from the modules' Prolog halves; 0.144 wrote both as files of its own. A helper of
    ours never takes the prefix `flow_`: `flow_trim/2` joined the library's own and the chart failed far from it, and
    since 1.11.4 a file the chart reads that does so is refused by name.
  - Its false findings at 1.11.3 are gone at 1.11.4: `format(atom(A), ...)` binds A, text made from text binds every
    argument (`atomic_list_concat/3`'s split), and a call that nothing answers under a `catch/3` that takes its error is
    a warning. The false `instantiation` of a `catch/3`'s catcher inside its recovery (0.140) is gone since 1.10.28, and
    `ccl_cpp.pl`, which did not end in 30 min at 1.10.22, is charted in 46 s.
  - The debugger explains every call of a predicate with clauses under `own(all)` (the default explains a call with a
    panel on the chart, and for a program loaded from a top file every call is a library's); `flow_why_raised/3` gives
    the path of the exception that ended a run and the failure it answered, and `flow_why_furthest/2` steps past an
    explicit `fail/0`. A cache on disk that the probe writes and the replay reads makes the two runs diverge, which
    1.11.4 says with both ends: build once first.
  - 1.11.7 answered the three points of 0.146: `flow_why_raised/3`'s answers `chose(C)` -- the branch a choice took to
    the raise and every condition it ran, builtins included, so a refusal's deciding builtin is named and the rule
    0.146 kept for it went -- and `caught(K)` -- the error a catch took where the raise is in its recovery --, a
    `throw/1` placed on its box, and the clash check held to the library in every loaded file. Two limits met at 0.148,
    each worked round in `test/why.sh` (its topic): the clauses an exception ended are read from the program's files as
    the source's directives load them, and a compiled module's Prolog half (`library(cicilang)`'s) is not reached, so
    the top file names our files in a skipped `:- if(fail).` block; and `caught(K)` names only a catch whose call the
    window recorded, so the driver's report sites keep taking no error under the why flag (`dr_catch/3`).
  - 1.11.10: `svg(false)` and `xml(false)` (no document; a window costs its matching), the profile's views
    (`callers(C)`, `repeats(R)`, `flow_steps_text/2`), `flow_debug_windows/4` (windows along one run, each in a
    cocolog of its own, J at a time; `flow_profile_merge/4` adds them up), and a large window recorded about three
    times faster; `test/prof.sh` is built on them (its topic). The debugger's children -- the probe, the replay, a
    window's cocolog -- run in a process group or a session of their own (cocolog's process module: `posix_spawn` with
    `SETPGROUP` or `SETSID`), so a cap that sums or kills a process group misses them; ours sum and kill the process
    tree (0.148). A window of 20000 steps costs about 12 s and 300 MB a C++ build at 1.11.10, the documents left
    out.
  - 1.13.3 (0.152, the owner's request): `time(T)`, where a window's TIME went -- each predicate's calls and its
    inclusive and self time in nanoseconds, the most inclusive first, the control constructs' share and the collections
    apart (`flow_time_text/2`; `flow_profile_merge/5` adds windows' up; `profile=time` from the shell). The probe runs
    under a clock read at the top of every inference of the window (`'$trace_window'/4`'s `time(F, K)`), untraced, and
    the replay says whose each inference was; a clause's leading guards read 0, their time their call's, and
    `findall/3`'s copying is its own. A reading costs some 30 to 35 ns, measured as the probe starts and taken off; a
    run that does not ask pays nothing. `test/prof.sh` prints it as its TIME view (its topic).
  - 1.13.6 and 1.13.7 (0.155): the clock's unit is a STEP in `library(flow/debug)`'s words and in each view, which
    says how many of its steps were inferences (a call of `true/0` or `=/2` is a step and no inference); the time view
    charges a retry to the retried predicate, marks a load `(one call: P %)` -- a row whose largest call holds most of
    its inclusive time, at least ten times its other calls' mean -- and writes each window's profile under
    `windows=N`; `flow_why_furthest/2` goes into the call that spent the most steps before it failed, not into the
    clause's last call that did not exit. Over 1.14.0 `test/why.sh` gives `abstract.cpp`'s 19 calls and branch as at
    0.148, and `test/prof.sh` its views, each saying how many of its steps were inferences (`stdvector.cpp`: 114,719
    of 120,000).
  - 1.15.0 (0.156), our two wishes of 0.152: each time-view row ends ` @W:S`, the window and the step of its largest
    call (`at(From-To, Step)` in the term), so that a small window recorded around S reads that call with its
    arguments, and the load mark `(one call: P %)` counts a predicate's outermost calls only; and `flow_run_time/3`
    (`flow_run_time_text/2`; `profile=run` on `tools/flow/debug.pl`) runs the probe alone under a clock read at every
    step from the first -- no window, no replay -- each step's time charged to its goal's predicate and a retry's to
    the predicate retried, the clock's own cost (some 38 ns a reading here) taken off each row, a control construct a
    row of its own, and a guard a clause runs as it is entered no step the clock reads (`is/2` so run has no row of
    its own). A run that asks for neither clock pays nothing. `test/prof.sh` prints it as its RUN view (its topic).
  - 2.0.0 (0.157): a finding's column and a drawn width count a character past ASCII as the run's units say, where a
    continuation byte took a column of its own; the flow gate's keys hold no column, and its 125 keys are 1.15.0's.
    (0.140, 0.144, 0.146, 0.148, 0.152, 0.155, 0.156, 0.157)
- The session's tools are not in the repository: `probe.sh` (time and memory caps over its own process group),
  `trace.sh` (cocolog with `'$cpp_trace'` on), `fx.sh` (removes the binary, builds, compares as the gate does),
  `guard.sh` and `watch.sh` (a query or a gate under the summing watchdog). A new session writes them again. The first
  question a trace of a failed build answered, which call gave up, is `test/why.sh`'s since 0.144, in the repository.
  (0.93, 0.144)
- THE REFERENCE COMPILERS DISAGREE OVER AN `_Atomic` OBJECT OF A SIZE THAT IS NO POWER OF TWO (0.208), and two of them
  answer wrongly: clang rounds `_Atomic struct { int i[3]; }` up to sixteen bytes aligned at sixteen, gcc keeps twelve
  aligned at four, and clang's compare-exchange compares the four bytes of padding -- clang 18 leaves `*expected` as it
  was when the exchange fails, and clang 21 fails an exchange whose values are equal; clang++ over libc++ 18 and 21 lays
  `std::atomic<S12>` so, and its `compare_exchange_strong` fails where C++20 ignores padding bits (P0528), while clang++
  over libstdc++ answers as the standard does; g++ over libstdc++ never ends `std::atomic<long double>::fetch_add`, its
  loop comparing padding that the expected copy does not hold. This compiler takes gcc's layout and the standards'
  answers, and the fixtures hold those: `atomodd.c` gcc's output, `atomic208.cpp` clang++'s over libstdc++. (0.208)

## What runs

### Hosts

- macOS on x86-64 (Apple's SDK, Homebrew's LLVM, libc++ 21) is the first host. The seven gates last ran there at
  0.90, all GREEN (cocolog 1.2.18). The fixtures added since 0.93 have run on Linux only.
- Ubuntu 24.04 on x86_64 (clang and LLVM 18, glibc, libc++ 18 and 21) is a host since 0.87. Every gate but the C++ one
  is GREEN there since 0.93, and all seven since 0.95. Every step from 0.93 on is gated there, but the save points
  0.112, 0.113, 0.117, 0.122 to 0.125, 0.130, 0.131 and 0.143 (0.143's C gates and cross gate ran, its libc++ gates did
  not; the others were gated by the steps after them). The last full run is 0.221's, before its commit, over cocolog
  2.12.0 (the Findings), on its work tree, over fresh HOMEs: over libc++ 18 all nine GREEN (the flow gate's one finding
  in 91 s, reader 4 s, compile 23 s, driver 19 s, objects 4 s, proof, the cross gate in 284 s with its C++ part for
  aarch64, the library read in 443 s (203 other headers warmed), the C++ gate in 1209 s with 826 of 836 fixtures ok,
  the skips are `atomicref`, `atomicrefalign`, `ftm23b`, `ftm26b`, `joinwith`, `stdflatmap`, `stdoptionalref`,
  `tzone`, `vbaseof` and `zipadjacent`, the two units, the 30 refusals, the 35 of the safe part and the eight static
  assertions); over libc++ 21 the library read (the phase 390 s) and the C++ gate (about 1261 s, 834 of 836 ok,
  the skips `stdoptionalref` and `zipadjacent`) GREEN -- the C gates do not read libc++. The headers' reads, summed,
  took 1618 s over 226 over libc++ 18 and 1432 s over 21; the fixtures' builds 3963 s over 826 and 4165 s over
  834. The chains of 0.165 to 0.203 and of 0.205 to 0.219 are in HISTORY.md, 0.166 to 0.204 and 0.206 to 0.220;
  0.221's runs after its commit. Two libc++ passes are one gate: `LLVM=/usr/lib/llvm-18` and
  `LLVM=/usr/lib/llvm-21` choose the tree the chain reads and links. libc++ 22 (the newest tree, which a run without
  `$LLVM` reads) is no gate: 0.182 built its vector and its C++23 views by hand (`zipadjacent.cpp`, which its `.needs`
  skips over 18 and 21), and `stdoptionalref` passes there. The run before 0.121's (0.118, 0.119) found, over 0.117, two
  defects and one stale check of `test/cpp.pl` (c20, above).
- The host sets the predefined macros (`ccl_host_os/1` and `ccl_host_arch/1` in the module), the inclusion path
  (Debian's `/usr/lib/llvm-NN`, the multiarch directory) and the link (`-lc++` and `-lm` on Linux) (0.87, 0.93, 0.100).
- A struct passed or returned by value crosses a call as clang's x86-64 code expects, in both directions, with the
  register budget of SysV 3.2.3 (`test/driver.sh` over `test/c/link/abi_main.c` and `abi_helper.c`) (M3, 0.117).
- `long double` is x87's 80-bit type on x86-64, an IEEE quad on Linux aarch64 and a double on Apple's arm64
  (`ccl_long_double/1`; `test/c/run/ldouble.c`, `test/cpp/run/ldouble.cpp`) (0.108, 0.131).
- LINUX ON AARCH64 IS A TARGET (0.131): `cicilang --target=aarch64-linux-gnu` builds C for it on this x86-64 box, and
  the cross gate runs every C fixture and the ABI checks under qemu against clang's and gcc's builds; and C++ over that
  machine's libc++ 18 under the sysroot since 0.161: 25 C++ fixtures and the three C++ ABI checks against clang++.

### libc++ headers read whole

- `test/libcxx.sh` reads each header in its own process and asserts that it reads whole, to at least a minimum item
  count (`test/readhdr.pl`, libc++ 18's counts) (0.105, 0.109):
  C++17 `<vector>`, `<string>`, `<iostream>`, `<map>`, `<set>`, `<unordered_map>`, `<unordered_set>`, `<optional>`,
  `<memory>`, `<functional>`, `<tuple>`; C++20 `<compare>`, `<vector>`, `<string>`, `<iostream>`, `<set>`, `<map>`,
  `<unordered_map>`, `<unordered_set>`, `<ranges>`; C++23 `<optional>`, `<string>`; C++26 `<optional>`.
- The same pass reads every other header that the fixtures and Cicili's C++ files include, at each fixture's level
  (`ccl_union`: `<algorithm>`, `<array>`, `<atomic>`, `<concepts>`, `<coroutine>`, `<iterator>`, `<iomanip>`,
  `<type_traits>`, `<sstream>` and others). It writes their summaries for the C++ gate and does not assert them whole
  (0.105).

### libc++ modules that compile and run

- Nothing of the standard library is the compiler's own (owner's rule, 0.41). libc++ compiles from its own headers, and
  each fixture `test/cpp/run/NAME.cpp` prints clang++'s output, `NAME.expect`.
- `<random>` (`stdrandom`: `mt19937`, `mt19937_64` and `minstd_rand` through the uniform and Bernoulli distributions and
  `std::shuffle`) and `std::valarray` (`stdvalarray`: arithmetic through its expression templates, a slice, `sum`, `max`)
  (0.136). A stream's tie (`stdtie`: a read of `cin` flushes `cout`, counted by a buffer's syncs) (0.136).
- Streams (`<iostream>`, `<istream>`, `<ostream>`, `<iomanip>`): `stdcout`, `stdendl`, `stdcin`, `stdgetline`,
  `stdget`, `stdws`, `stdistream`, `stdistream2`, `stdostream`, `stdmanip`. `cout`, `cin`, `cerr` and `clog` are the
  shipped library's objects. A fixture reads its input from `NAME.stdin` (0.73-0.78). The wide streams `wcout`,
  `wostringstream`, `wistringstream` (`stdwstream`); `seekg`, `tellg`, `seekp`, `tellp` (`stdseek`); `cin >> long
  double` (`stdcinld`) (0.115); the rvalue-stream `getline`, `getline` with a delimiter and `sync_with_stdio(false)`
  (`stdstreammisc`) (0.117). Since 0.134: the money and time facets, `put_money` and `get_money` of a `long double` and of
  a string, `put_time` and `get_time` (`stdmoney`); the exceptions mask set and read back (`stdiosexc`); the padding of
  an inserter through the ostreambuf_iterator overload of `__pad_and_output` (`stdpadout`).
- `std::wofstream`, `std::wifstream` and `std::wfstream` (`stdwfstream`, 0.134); `std::filesystem`'s `path`
  (`stdfspath`: decomposition, `/`, `replace_extension`, comparison) and its operations (`stdfsops`:
  `temp_directory_path`, `create_directories`, `exists`, `is_directory`, `file_size`, a range-for over a
  `directory_iterator`, `remove_all`) (0.134).
- `std::stringstream` and `std::wstringstream` (`stdstringstream`: libc++'s basic_iostream is a diamond over basic_ios;
  extraction and insertion through the one object, the `istream &`, `ostream &`, `iostream &` and `ios &` references,
  `getline` with a delimiter, `std::ws`, `tellp`, `rdbuf()` inserted); `std::ofstream`, `std::ifstream` and
  `std::fstream` (`stdfstream`: write, read back by `getline` and `>>`, append, rewrite through an fstream, seek, a file
  that is not there, `open` and `close`); a program class derived from `std::ostream` and from `std::iostream` over its
  own streambuf (`streamderived`) (0.117).

### Benchmarks

- `bench/btree/run.sh`: the B-tree at `-O3` beats Rust's BTreeSet on insert and search and ties it on deletion
  (owner's goal, 2026-09-05; a million keys, min of 11: 94/90/62/92/66 ms against 107/96/60/95/63). Its node holds a
  bounded own array, its key scan is branchless, and deletion fixes only a node left short.

## Not done

### The owner's decisions of 0.190, in the order they are done

The four questions put to the owner at 0.190, each answered by the recommendation it was given, each a step of its own,
are done: the first, RTTI in libc++ on by default, at 0.191, the second, exceptions in libc++ on by default, at 0.193
(the Configuration chosen through the macros topic), the third, the safe part at the library's boundary, at 0.216 (the
safe part's topic of what the C++ forms mean to the check), and the fourth, the C++ IR cache, at 0.221 (the IR cache
topic): a C++ build keeps each file's IR as a file beside the summaries, and the gates build uncached. A store for it
comes only after parallel writes to one store are measured.

### The audit of C17 to C23 and C++17 to C++26, in the order it is done

The owner asked at 0.193 for every form and every library facility of the C and C++ levels the compiler takes, up to
C++26, to be done. The audit's gaps are steps of their own, a group a step; each moves into its topic when it is done.
The first group, the platform and the preprocessor, is 0.194's (clang's predefined macros on Linux, asm labels, brace
elision into records, C23's enums, `<tgmath.h>`, C23's headers, GCC's atomic builtins, `alignas` before a declaration);
the second, the program's own file-scope constants, is 0.195's (the Constant evaluation topic: C17's, C23's and C++'s, a
C23 block's `constexpr`, a local constant its block's own); the third, the lexers, is 0.196's (the Lexers topic: the
`u8` literals of C23 and C++20, UTF-8 and multi-character constants in a character literal, adjacent prefixed string
literals, identifiers past ASCII and universal character names in them); the fourth, C++'s core language, is 0.197's,
0.198's and 0.199's (0.197: the order of evaluation, `explicit(bool)`, the implicit moves, `decltype((x))`, a constant's
initializer manifestly constant-evaluated, parenthesized aggregate initialization, template parameter objects, a lambda
made in a lambda one class, a class prvalue handed by value in place and one bound to a reference parameter destroyed,
and C's variably modified parameters; 0.198: noexcept in the type system, an init-capture pack, an immediate function

   Coroutines topic). NO DEFECT (0.221): a construction table keeps the complete destructor in both destructor slots, so
   a delete through the table while a base-variant sub-object is built would keep the block, where clang's table deletes
   through the base's deleting destructor at the base's size -- and a delete of an object whose construction has not
   finished is undefined ([basic.life]/6.1: a pointer to an object whose lifetime has not started, of a class with a
   non-trivial destructor, as the operand of a delete-expression; its lifetime starts when its initialization is
   complete, [basic.life]/1), so no program can tell the two tables apart.

   configuration is one for the file, so a header included before a `__STDC_WANT_*` or `_LIBCPP_*` definition is read
   under it too, and a late `_LIBCPP_*` name that libc++'s `__config` reads once
   (`_LIBCPP_ENABLE_CXX17_REMOVED_FEATURES`, `_LIBCPP_ENABLE_EXPERIMENTAL`) reaches the headers where clang++'s does
   not; a local header's `_LIBCPP_*` names, and a `__STDC_WANT_*` name that glibc does not ask, configure no header's
   read; a file that defines such a name after its first system `#include` is read at every build (the C store topic); a
   header that the program's own header includes reads `NDEBUG` as its table has it (under `-DNDEBUG` an `#undef NDEBUG`
   before `<assert.h>` asserts again since 0.221, the topic of the user's file and the headers' macros). `asm goto` is
   refused by name (`asm_goto`), and so is an asm output that carries a pointer (`asm_pointer_output`, the safe part's);
   a register variable's register is the operand's only, as an asm operand. macOS is not measured: Apple's libc chooses
   its names by `_ANSI_SOURCE`, `_POSIX_C_SOURCE` and `_DARWIN_C_SOURCE`, its headers' reads under the ISO modes are no
   gate's, and `gnuasm.c` and `gnuasm.cpp` name its sections and its symbols' underscore without a run there.

### C++ language

- NAMES ACROSS THE HEADERS' READS AND THE PROGRAM'S, WHAT 0.221 LEFT (0.218's to 0.221's probes): a read keys apart only
  the names that collide in it; 0.218, 0.219 and 0.221 take a qualified and an unqualified CLASS name to its own
  namespace's items -- the class's own namespace among them where a function or an object of the name stands in another
  -- and a call qualified by std to std's functions and objects (the namespaces' bullets of the libc++ topic). FUNCTIONS
  of one name in two namespaces across the reads stay one overload set: over the summaries of libc++ 18 and 21, 20
  operators (std's beside std::chrono's, std::filesystem's and std::pmr's) and 16 and 19 math functions (std's complex
  overloads beside std::__math's), which C++ joins too, by argument-dependent lookup and libc++'s own
  using-declarations, and internal helpers it does not -- libc++ 18's `__transform`, `__fill`, `__vprint_unicode` and
  `__vprint_nonunicode`, libc++ 21's `__fill`, each of std and of std::__formatter or std::__print -- where the
  arguments' types choose. THE PROGRAM'S GLOBAL FUNCTIONS are hidden from a call qualified by std (0.221), not from an
  unqualified call in a library template, where C++ finds them only by argument-dependent lookup. ARGUMENT-DEPENDENT
  LOOKUP of a keyed name asks the classes of the arguments, of their pointees, of their templates' arguments and their
  bases (0.221), not a function type's parameters and result, a member pointer's class or a template template argument's
  namespace ([basic.lookup.argdep]/3). (0.218, 0.219, 0.221)
- A library class's consteval constructor's check runs at compile time since 0.164 where the evaluator takes it (the
  Constant evaluation topic: `basic_format_string`'s format parse); a check it cannot take leaves the format string to
  the library's run-time parser, which no check of the format fixtures does since 0.168 (over libc++ 18 and 21). A
  library's other consteval functions run at run time, as before -- their values are the same, and only a call that is
  no constant expression would differ, which libc++'s own calls are not (0.110, 0.164, 0.168); the program's own fold
  (0.99, 0.112). `std::source_location::current()` is answered since 0.166.
- A later virtual base or a path whose virtual bases cannot be laid as a `.nv` form is refused by name,
  `virtual_base_over_virtual_base(C, V)` or `virtual_base_laid_otherwise(C, P)`; since 0.173 no shape the probes tried
  meets either -- a later virtual base with virtual bases of its own (`X : B, virtual V` over `V : virtual A`) and a path
  that reaches an empty virtual base further in (`X : P, virtual A` over `P : Q` and `Q : virtual E`), each refused at
  0.172, build as clang lays them. A NEARLY EMPTY virtual base is the primary base since 0.174 (the Itanium ABI's II.1b),
  the one clang chooses since 0.175, a stolen one and one further in since 0.176, and a holder lays it where a base
  sub-object takes it as its primary, and one whose own virtual bases lie outside it since 0.178 (`C : virtual I` over
  `I : virtual A`, A with data). A primary table's slots are in the ABI's order since 0.177. Since 0.171
  every class over virtual bases through its paths has the Itanium layout, since 0.172 every class with a later virtual
  base too, since 0.173 one whose later virtual base has virtual bases of its own, and every base-variant sub-object at
  any depth is built under construction tables of its own, its secondary pointers among them (0.110, 0.117, 0.160,
  0.163, 0.171, 0.172, 0.173, 0.174, 0.175, 0.176, 0.177, 0.178).

### libc++ modules

- Range views: `filter`, `transform`, `reverse`, `iota`, `take`, `drop`, `take_while`, `keys`, `values` and their chain
  run, alone and in one program (0.115), and since 0.132 `empty`, `single`, `counted`, `chunk_by`, `common`, `zip`,
  `elements`, `drop_while`, `as_rvalue`, `repeat`, `join`, `split`, `lazy_split` and `ranges::to`, and since 0.133 `join_with`
  at libc++ 21. The other C++23 views are in neither libc++ 18 nor 21 (their `__ranges/` has no `adjacent`, `chunk`,
  `slide`, `stride`, `enumerate`, `cartesian_product`, `as_const`); libc++ 22 has `adjacent`, `pairwise`,
  `zip_transform` and `adjacent_transform`, which run since 0.182 (`zipadjacent.cpp`, built over libc++ 22 by hand: no
  gate reads that tree). The read of its `<ranges>` was never the cost (25 s and 184 MB alone at 0.182): the
  desugaring of any `std::vector` over libc++ 22 ran past the cap (0.136, 0.180), which 0.182 mended (the template
  template parameters' and the member alias templates' topics). `chunk`, `slide`, `stride`, `enumerate`,
  `cartesian_product` and `as_const` are in none of the three trees.
- `std::format` runs (`stdformat.cpp`, 0.112), its format string checked at compile time since 0.164 (`fmtcheck.cpp`;
  `fmtindex.cpp` and `fmttype.cpp` refused with the library's message), where the evaluator takes the check (the
  Constant evaluation topic); a check it cannot take is the library's own parser's at run time. `vformat`, a formatter
  the program specializes, the wide format and `std::print` run (0.115), range and tuple formatting (0.133) and chrono
  formatting (0.136, `fmtchrono.cpp`). Time points, the calendar types and `hh_mm_ss` format since 0.137
  (`fmtchrono2.cpp`), and time zones, libc++'s experimental part, run under `-fexperimental-library` since 0.138
  (`tzone.cpp`: a zone by name, its offsets and abbreviations in winter and in summer, a local time; libc++ 21, whose
  database reads the box's `/usr/share/zoneinfo/tzdata.zi`).
- `optional<T &>` needs libc++ 22 (`stdoptionalref.needs`; 21.1.8 has none). `bad_optional_access` is caught since
  0.193 (`ehlib.cpp`), libc++ in its exceptions configuration; under `-fno-exceptions` it aborts with the message, as
  it did from 0.82 to 0.192.
- `std::atomic<shared_ptr<T>>` (C++20, P0718) is in none of libc++ 18, 21 and 22: clang++ refuses
  `std::atomic<std::shared_ptr<int>>` over each tree (22's `<version>` leaves `__cpp_lib_atomic_shared_ptr` out, and
  `std::atomic<T>` asserts that T is trivially copyable), so there is nothing of the library to compile (0.86, 0.128,
  0.182). `<atomic>`'s `wait`, `notify_one` and `notify_all` run at C++20 (`stdatomic20.cpp`, 0.117). A program's own
  calls of `std::uninitialized_copy`, `std::construct_at`, the `destroy_*` algorithms and `allocator_traits` run
  (`stduninit.cpp`, `stdallocator.cpp`, 0.117).
- `std::stringstream`, `std::wstringstream`, `std::ofstream`, `std::ifstream` and `std::fstream` run (0.117), and since
  0.134 the wide file streams and `std::filesystem`'s `path` and operations, and since 0.137 the rest of it that a program
  uses most: `recursive_directory_iterator`, permissions, `last_write_time` read and set, `space`, `copy_file`, `rename`,
  `remove_all` (`fsrest.cpp`).
- `<random>` and `std::valarray` run since 0.136 (`stdrandom.cpp`, `stdvalarray.cpp`). `std::bit_cast` runs since the
  builtin is answered (`stdbitcast.cpp`, C++20). `<chrono>`: durations, clocks and time points run, with their literals

  `std::mutex` run (`stdthread.cpp`), and `std::from_chars` and `std::to_chars` of integers (`stdcharconv.cpp`).
- `std::variant` and `std::visit` run (0.121): the converting constructor and assignment, `in_place_index` and

### ABI and hosts

- AAPCS64 is proven on Linux (the cross gate under qemu, 0.131), not on Apple's arm64, whose variadic calls and long
  double differ: no Apple machine is on this box, and its expansion of an aggregate's `va_arg` is checked against
  clang's on this host alone (0.160).
- The Itanium mangler spells a function type, a pointer to one, an array and a pointer to member as a parameter
  (0.117; `c37`), every builtin type (0.136; `c44`) and a vector type (0.162; `c46`). A type that none of its clauses
  names keeps this compiler's own name, and the link names it. No shipped symbol needs one (measured at 0.186): the
  symbols that libc++ 18's, 21's and 22's `libc++.so.1` and their `libc++abi.so.1` export, and the 27 that libc++ 21's
  `libc++experimental.a` defines strongly, use no form the mangler lacks -- a pack expansion `Dp`, a `decltype` `DT` or
  `Dt`, an ABI tag `B`, a closure `Ul`, an unnamed type `Ut`, an expression `X`, an external name `L_Z` as an argument
  (the archive's weak definitions that do are instances of the headers' inline templates, which a program compiles).
- macOS has not run the gates since 0.90, so every rule made since 0.91 is gated on Linux and libc++ 18 only.

### The safe part

- A library header's functions are not checked (`cpp_library_function/1`, `'$cpp_libfn'`): 0.45's decision, which the
  owner confirmed at 0.190; in C, a library header's function that the unit uses and lowers with it is not either
  (`ck_library_fn/1`, `'$ir_hlib'/1`; 0.212), and the program's own header's are checked as its file's are. What a
  library object holds is followed since 0.216, and what a local's storage holds, where a store lands and what a
  function of the program stores since 0.217 (the safe part's topics), with these limits: a store through a pointer the
  check does not follow -- a call's result, an own pointer's pointee, a pointer member (`s.p->q = &x`), a local pointer
  whose type is not the borrowed local's -- is accepted; a flow is found by the forms alone: a value computed from a
  parameter is followed since 0.221 (`p + n`, `p - n`, `&p->f`, `&p[i]`, `&*p`), but a store through a pointer the
  function computes, or into an object reached through a pointer member, is none, and a copy constructor's member stores
  carry nothing; a container, an array and a whole struct each hold one `$held` key, so what one element or one member
  of a copy holds is what all of them hold; a free library function stores by its template's name, the swaps, fills and
  copies of `<algorithm>` and `<utility>`, and any other stores nothing; a slot reached through a reference whose type
  the walk does not know is checked for a local's address only; a lookup is known by its member's name, and another
  non-const member's argument counts as stored. A pointer parameter's address is the parameter's own storage since 0.219
  (the safe part's topic of borrows and parameters).
- A direct `std::allocator::allocate` and `allocator_traits<A>::allocate(a, n)` are accepted: a library member's or
  static function's plain pointer result borrows the object it takes by reference (`ck_borrows_from`, 0.91, 0.117;
  `stdallocator.cpp`).
- An owner live across a call that may throw, outside every `try`, is not followed on the unwinding path (0.193:
  libc++'s calls throw now): the unwinding runs the defers and the destructors of the scopes it leaves, and an owner
  that none of them frees leaks, as a raw pointer does in C++. The language's remedy is a `defer`, which runs on every
  exit, the unwinding included; no rule asks for one. Whether one asks for it -- an owner live across a call that may
  throw refused without a `defer` -- is a rule of the language, the owner's to make (0.221's record). Inside a `try`, a
  handler is entered from any point of its body (the safe part's topic).

### Tools and performance

- `bin/cicilang` accepts and ignores `-W`, `-f...` and `-pedantic` (owner's rule: clang's arguments, no new flags).
  `-D` and `-U` define and undefine (0.112), and `-fexperimental-library` turns libc++'s experimental part on (0.138); a
  run with any of them keeps no C store.
- `-g` (0.130) leaves out what clang's has beyond the variables, the types and the scopes: a location has its
  STATEMENT's column (0.161), where clang gives each expression its own -- that would need a column in every token and
  every node of the tree, which the reader has not (a token is `tok(Kind, Value, Line)`). A destructor at a scope's end
  has the closing brace's line since 0.139. The macros are described under `-fdebug-macro` (0.134; `-g3` alone describes
  none in either compiler).
- A C++ read never uses the store: `cicilang++` runs `--no-kb` (M5), its cache the summary and the AST beside it (0.35,
  0.45). The reason written then, a store write quadratic past about 30,000 rows, is gone (linear on cocolog 2.2.5,
  measured at 0.161: the Findings); a process that adds a row to a predicate still rewrites all of it, which one
  predicate per file serves. The owner decided at 0.190 that a C++ build keeps its IR as files beside the summaries,
  which it does since 0.221 (the IR cache topic).
- The check's cost is its expression walk. The next cut needs the state as a per-function table, or the lookups in C
  (2026-09-06).
- A call under a `try` or a scope with defers is an `invoke` whatever its callee (`ir_invoke_needed`): one declared
  noexcept, a C function among them, gets a landing pad it never uses. libc++'s exceptions configuration (0.193) made
  every C++ program's calls so: eight warm builds take 5.2 % more CPU than 0.192's, and the IR of `stdstringstream.cpp`
  is 42 % larger (256 invokes), of `stdvector.cpp` 14 % (42). A plain call needs two things the lowering has not
  (0.221's record): the callee's noexcept -- a declared function's own type carries none (reader 150: the suffix is the
  declaration's, `ccl_own_fn_nx`), and the program's noexcept definitions and the summaries' `nothrow` names are the
  desugaring's tables -- and a terminate guard in a LIBRARY function's noexcept body, which only the program's have
  (`cpp_nx_wrap`): without it a plain call lets an exception that breaks the callee's noexcept pass the caller's
  cleanups.
- A C++ build's time was its first deductions and its instantiations (0.98), and, found at 0.120, the COPIES of the
  desugaring's own tables and class records (the Time and memory topic): the slowest fixture, `viewsall.cpp`, took 1760 s
  of the C++ gate's 2400 s cap in the gate's pool at 0.115 and 1357 s at 0.118, and takes 211 s now; the sum of the 388
  fixtures' builds went from 11,775 s to 2,936 s, the gate from 2989 s to 908 s over four lanes, its pool's peak from 9034
  MB to 1675 MB (0.120). What is left is mostly the reader's own cold flattening of a header, 2.4 to 2.7 times faster
  since 0.184 (its item loop: the 114 headers' reads summed 4313 s over libc++ 18 in 0.181's chain), 1.5 times faster
  again since 0.187 (the sets as the whole record and the grammar's looks: 1349 s in 0.187's chain, 1802 s in 0.186's)
  and faster again since 0.188 (999 s in 0.188's chain; seven headers' texts read in 71.9 s where 0.186's library read
  them in 133.7 s and 0.187's in 90.0 s, the trees the same); and since 0.188 a build's cold headers are read by
  processes of their own, at once (the driver's topic). In 0.188's chain the slowest builds were `fmtrange` (109 s over
  libc++ 18) and `fmtchrono2` (97 s over 21), `viewsall` 72 s and 76 s, and the 600 and 602 builds summed 2638 s and
  2701 s over four lanes (0.120, 0.184, 0.187, 0.188, 0.189).
- The flow gate charts the ten hand-written files of `library/` and the nine gate programs of `test/` (0.161): the two
  generated tables (`ccl_bidrt.pl`, `ccl_uninames.pl`) are loaded, not charted. `test/why.sh` is no gate.
